set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)

set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

# `conduitscope version`'s own reported build type -- see version.hpp.in below. CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE
# is meaningless for a multi-config generator (Visual Studio, Xcode: CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES is
# set instead, and the actual configuration is picked at BUILD time via --config, not here at
# configure time), so it's always empty in that case -- confirmed on a real Windows/MSVC build,
# which without this fallback reports "conduitscope 0.3.3  [MSVC ..., Windows,  build, ...]" (note
# the double space where an empty CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE left a hole). "multi-config" is honest about why
# no single value is available here, rather than guessing a config that may not be the one actually
# built.
if(CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
  set(CONDUITSCOPE_REPORTED_BUILD_TYPE "multi-config")
else()
  set(CONDUITSCOPE_REPORTED_BUILD_TYPE "${CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE}")
endif()

# The version `conduitscope version` reports is PROJECT_VERSION above by
# default (bumped by hand alongside each release), but the release CI job
# (.github/workflows/ci.yml's `release` job) overrides it explicitly from
# the pushed git tag via -DCONDUITSCOPE_VERSION_OVERRIDE=X.Y.Z, so the
# published binary's own reported version can never drift from the tag it
# was actually built from even if this line is forgotten before tagging.
set(CONDUITSCOPE_REPORTED_VERSION "${PROJECT_VERSION}")
if(CONDUITSCOPE_VERSION_OVERRIDE)
  set(CONDUITSCOPE_REPORTED_VERSION "${CONDUITSCOPE_VERSION_OVERRIDE}")
endif()

# Embeds the project version / compiler / build type into the binary so
# `conduitscope version` can report exactly what it's running, without
# depending on git being present (this groundwork checkout may or may not be
# a git repo yet).
configure_file(
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include/conduitscope/version.hpp.in"
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated/conduitscope/version.hpp"
  @ONLY
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional live-capture support (libpcap on Linux, the Npcap SDK on Windows). This is the ONE
# exception to the project's otherwise zero-external-dependency design (see README.md's "Why
# offline pcap files" section) -- and it stays optional even where it's found: when neither is
# present, conduitscope_core still builds exactly as it always has, and live_capture.cpp's stub
# implementation (see its own comment) makes `-i/--interface` and `conduitscope interfaces` fail
# with a clear message instead of not existing at all.
#
# CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_LIVE_CAPTURE lets a builder opt out of even searching (e.g. a packager who
# wants a guaranteed-dependency-free build regardless of what happens to be installed on the build
# machine); it defaults on since the search itself is harmless when nothing is found.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
option(CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_LIVE_CAPTURE
  "Search for libpcap (Linux) / the Npcap SDK (Windows) and build live-capture support if found"
  ON)

set(CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP FALSE)
if(CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_LIVE_CAPTURE)
  if(WIN32)
    # The Npcap SDK (distinct from the Npcap runtime installer -- see docs/MANUAL.md's LIVE
    # CAPTURE section) ships pcap.h under Include/ and import libraries under Lib/ (32-bit) or
    # Lib/x64/ (64-bit); it has no standard install location, so NPCAP_SDK_DIR (an environment or
    # CMake variable) is how a builder points at it, alongside the common default install path.
    set(_conduitscope_npcap_sdk_dir "$ENV{NPCAP_SDK_DIR}")
    if(NOT _conduitscope_npcap_sdk_dir AND DEFINED NPCAP_SDK_DIR)
      set(_conduitscope_npcap_sdk_dir "${NPCAP_SDK_DIR}")
    endif()
    find_path(PCAP_INCLUDE_DIR pcap.h
      HINTS "${_conduitscope_npcap_sdk_dir}/Include" "C:/Npcap-SDK/Include")
    if(CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P EQUAL 8)
      set(_conduitscope_npcap_lib_subdir "Lib/x64")
    else()
      set(_conduitscope_npcap_lib_subdir "Lib")
    endif()
    find_library(PCAP_LIBRARY NAMES wpcap
      HINTS "${_conduitscope_npcap_sdk_dir}/${_conduitscope_npcap_lib_subdir}"
            "C:/Npcap-SDK/${_conduitscope_npcap_lib_subdir}")
    unset(_conduitscope_npcap_sdk_dir)
    unset(_conduitscope_npcap_lib_subdir)
  else()
    find_path(PCAP_INCLUDE_DIR pcap.h)
    find_library(PCAP_LIBRARY NAMES pcap)
  endif()

  if(PCAP_INCLUDE_DIR AND PCAP_LIBRARY)
    set(CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP TRUE)
    target_compile_definitions(conduitscope_core PUBLIC CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP=1)
    target_include_directories(conduitscope_core PRIVATE "${PCAP_INCLUDE_DIR}")
    target_link_libraries(conduitscope_core PUBLIC "${PCAP_LIBRARY}")
    if(WIN32 AND MSVC)
      # wpcap.lib above is the Npcap SDK's *build-time* import library -- the actual wpcap.dll
      # (the Npcap RUNTIME) is a separate, user-installed component (see docs/MANUAL.md's LIVE
      # CAPTURE section). Without delay-loading it, the OS loader would refuse to start
      # conduitscope.exe AT ALL -- even for a plain offline `decode` that never touches a single
      # pcap function -- on any Windows machine that has this binary but not the Npcap runtime
      # installed (this is also what was hanging the release-windows CI job's ctest step: every
      # test process, including ones with nothing to do with live capture, failed to start).
      # /DELAYLOAD defers resolving wpcap.dll until the first actual pcap_*() call -- i.e. only
      # when live capture is genuinely used (see live_capture.cpp's ensure_pcap_runtime_available
      # for the friendly error if it's missing at that point) -- so everything else keeps working
      # with zero extra runtime dependency.
      target_link_libraries(conduitscope_core PUBLIC delayimp.lib)
      target_link_options(conduitscope_core PUBLIC "/DELAYLOAD:wpcap.dll")
    endif()
    message(STATUS "conduitscope: live capture ENABLED (found ${PCAP_LIBRARY})")
  else()
    message(STATUS "conduitscope: live capture DISABLED (libpcap/Npcap SDK not found -- "
                    "'-i/--interface' and 'interfaces' will report this clearly at runtime; "
                    "everything else is unaffected)")
  endif()
else()
  message(STATUS "conduitscope: live capture DISABLED (CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_LIVE_CAPTURE=OFF)")
endif()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional TLS decryption support (OpenSSL's libcrypto) -- ROADMAP item 150, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
# Mirrors CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_LIVE_CAPTURE immediately above exactly: an optional dependency this
# project otherwise has none of (see README.md's "Why offline pcap files" section, and
# tls_decrypt.hpp's own file header comment for why OpenSSL specifically, rather than extending
# this codebase's existing hand-rolled QUIC-only crypto quartet -- ROADMAP item 139/patch295
# finding F7). When OpenSSL isn't found (or this option is turned off), conduitscope_core still
# builds exactly as it always has -- tls_decrypt.cpp's own stub implementation (see its own
# #else branch) makes --tls-keylog/DSB-sourced decryption of MQTTS/FOXS/WinRM-over-HTTPS report
# "unavailable" instead of not existing at all, and every OTHER feature (detection-only ClientHello/
# SNI tagging for those three ports, and everything else in this codebase) is completely
# unaffected either way.
option(CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_TLS_DECRYPT
  "Search for OpenSSL and build --tls-keylog/pcapng-DSB TLS decryption support if found"
  ON)

set(CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_OPENSSL FALSE)
if(CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_TLS_DECRYPT)
  find_package(OpenSSL QUIET)
  if(OpenSSL_FOUND)
    set(CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_OPENSSL TRUE)
    target_compile_definitions(conduitscope_core PUBLIC CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_OPENSSL=1)
    target_link_libraries(conduitscope_core PUBLIC OpenSSL::Crypto)
    message(STATUS "conduitscope: TLS decryption ENABLED (found OpenSSL ${OPENSSL_VERSION})")
  else()
    message(STATUS "conduitscope: TLS decryption DISABLED (OpenSSL not found -- --tls-keylog/"
                    "pcapng-DSB decryption of MQTTS/FOXS/WinRM-over-HTTPS will report this "
                    "clearly at runtime; everything else, including this capture file reader's "
                    "own DSB parsing, is unaffected)")
  endif()
else()
  message(STATUS "conduitscope: TLS decryption DISABLED (CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_TLS_DECRYPT=OFF)")
endif()

# CLI11 is vendored as a single header under third_party/ specifically so this
# project has ZERO external dependencies to install on either platform -- no
# vcpkg/conan/apt package needed, just a C++17 compiler and CMake.
add_executable(conduitscope src/cli_main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(conduitscope PRIVATE conduitscope_core)
target_include_directories(conduitscope PRIVATE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/third_party/CLI11")

if(MSVC)
  target_compile_options(conduitscope PRIVATE /W4 /permissive-)
else()
  target_compile_options(conduitscope PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic)
endif()

install(TARGETS conduitscope RUNTIME DESTINATION bin)
if(UNIX)
  install(FILES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/man/conduitscope.1" DESTINATION share/man/man1)
endif()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Crypto primitives self-tests (sha256.*, hkdf.*, aes128.*, aes128_gcm.*) -- see
# tools/crypto_selftest.cpp's own file header for why this exists and why it is always built
# (not gated behind CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_FUZZING or any other opt-in flag, unlike the libFuzzer
# harnesses below): quic.cpp's Initial-packet decryption depends on every one of these being
# correct, and a subtle bug here would silently corrupt QUIC decryption rather than crash loudly.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_executable(crypto_selftest tools/crypto_selftest.cpp)
target_link_libraries(crypto_selftest PRIVATE conduitscope_core)

enable_testing()

add_test(NAME crypto_primitives_self_test COMMAND crypto_selftest)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Protocol result type safety self-test -- see tools/protocol_result_selftest.cpp's own file
# header for the full rationale (finding 3, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-
# patch160.md: ProtocolResult::as<T>() used to be an entirely unchecked static_cast, silent UB on
# a protocol_id<->T mismatch). Same "always built, no opt-in flag" posture as crypto_selftest
# above -- this needs no separate toolchain either, and the bug it guards against lives in this
# codebase's own source (a future decoder migration getting an id()<->T association wrong), not in
# anything a pcap fixture could exercise, so a dedicated small executable is the right shape here
# too, not a CLI-driven CTest case.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_executable(protocol_result_selftest tools/protocol_result_selftest.cpp)
target_link_libraries(protocol_result_selftest PRIVATE conduitscope_core)

add_test(NAME protocol_result_type_safety_self_test COMMAND protocol_result_selftest)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ResourceLimits scoping self-test -- see tools/resource_limits_selftest.cpp's own file header for
# the full rationale (checks 1-4: finding 5, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-
# patch160.md: ResourceLimits used to be plain process-global mutable state -- two differently-
# configured Decoder instances, interleaved on one thread or run concurrently on separate threads,
# would race over the same global configuration. checks 5-6: finding 3, docs/reviews/2026-09-
# chatgpt-security-review-patch209.md: max_active_flows=0/max_flow_state_entries=0 is now
# normalized to "no cap" by set_resource_limits, rather than the old undefined behavior/cap-
# violating-by-one-entry each caused). Same "always built, no opt-in flag" posture as
# crypto_selftest/protocol_result_selftest above -- the scenarios these guard against can never be
# constructed through the `conduitscope` CLI itself (it only ever builds one Decoder per process,
# and its own build_resource_limits already maps a `--max-active-flows 0`/`--max-flow-state-
# entries 0` argument to "flag not passed" before a ResourceLimits value is ever built), so no
# CLI-driven CTest case could exercise either; a dedicated small executable against the library API
# directly is the only way.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_executable(resource_limits_selftest tools/resource_limits_selftest.cpp)
# The only target in this build that uses std::thread directly (check 4's genuine cross-thread
# concurrency test) -- find_package(Threads) is scoped to just this one target's link line rather
# than added globally, since nothing else here needs it.
find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(resource_limits_selftest PRIVATE conduitscope_core Threads::Threads)

add_test(NAME resource_limits_scoping_self_test
  COMMAND resource_limits_selftest
          "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap"
          "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_active_flows.pcap"
          "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Live capture drop-statistics self-test -- see tools/live_capture_stats_selftest.cpp's own file
# header for the full rationale (ROADMAP item 118, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-
# patch257.md section 4, "Detection completeness": "Packet loss... must be distinguishable from a
# clean capture with no findings"). Same "always built, no opt-in flag, needs no libpcap/Npcap SDK
# itself" posture as crypto_selftest/protocol_result_selftest above -- format_live_capture_drop_
# reason (live_capture.hpp) has no pcap.h dependency at all, so this links and runs identically
# whether or not THIS build has CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP defined. A real OS-level pcap_stats() drop
# can't be constructed on demand through the CLI/CTest the way resource_limits_selftest's own
# --max-* scenarios can -- a dedicated executable against the library API directly, exercising
# just the pure decision+wording logic, is the only way.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_executable(live_capture_stats_selftest tools/live_capture_stats_selftest.cpp)
target_link_libraries(live_capture_stats_selftest PRIVATE conduitscope_core)

add_test(NAME live_capture_drop_statistics_self_test COMMAND live_capture_stats_selftest)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Detect export-format invariants self-test -- see tools/detect_export_invariants_selftest.cpp's
# own file header for the full rationale (ROADMAP item 119, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-
# review-patch257.md section 3.B, "Four-axis detection model": "establish explicit invariants in
# the finding data model and test them across JSON, CEF, LEEF, syslog... verify that a format
# conversion cannot silently upgrade a heuristic finding into a confirmed finding or change the
# underlying severity judgment"). A dedicated executable, not more pcap-fixture CTest entries,
# because the thing under test (every evidence x novelty x severity combination this engine's own
# type system allows, 18 in total) is a property of the DATA MODEL, not of any one capture -- no
# real pcap fixture exercises more than a handful of these 18 combinations (today's only Heuristic-
# evidence finding source, RemoteAccessChannel, only ever carries Moderate severity), so a
# synthetic DetectionReport built directly against the struct is the only way to cover the full
# cross-product and prove the four export writers never let one axis's value leak into another's,
# or drift between formats.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_executable(detect_export_invariants_selftest tools/detect_export_invariants_selftest.cpp)
target_link_libraries(detect_export_invariants_selftest PRIVATE conduitscope_core)

add_test(NAME detect_export_format_invariants_self_test COMMAND detect_export_invariants_selftest)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RotatingPcapWriter rotation/retention self-test -- see tools/rotating_pcap_writer_selftest.cpp's
# own file header for the full rationale (Grok review item 5, docs/reviews/2026-09-grok-ics-ot-
# improvement-areas.md: "runs for weeks... rotates captures, does not fill the disk" -- see
# docs/design/sensor-mode.md for the full design record). Same "always built, no opt-in flag"
# posture as the selftests above -- exact byte-boundary/retention-eviction correctness across many
# synthetic packets is far more reliably and quickly proven directly against the library API than
# through a CLI-driven CTest case timing real captured traffic.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_executable(rotating_pcap_writer_selftest tools/rotating_pcap_writer_selftest.cpp)
target_link_libraries(rotating_pcap_writer_selftest PRIVATE conduitscope_core)

set(_conduitscope_rotating_pcap_writer_selftest_scratch_dir
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/rotating_pcap_writer_selftest_scratch")
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${_conduitscope_rotating_pcap_writer_selftest_scratch_dir}")

add_test(NAME rotating_pcap_writer_rotation_and_retention_self_test
  COMMAND rotating_pcap_writer_selftest
          "${_conduitscope_rotating_pcap_writer_selftest_scratch_dir}")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional libFuzzer harnesses (fuzz/) -- see fuzz/README.md and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's "External
# code review and engineering priorities" section for which five parsers these target and why.
# Off by default: libFuzzer is a Clang/compiler-rt feature (GCC cannot build -fsanitize=fuzzer),
# and the fuzzer/sanitizer runtime is a separate OS package from the compiler itself on most
# distros (e.g. libclang-rt-<version>-dev on Debian/Ubuntu) that most builds/builders won't have
# installed -- opting in explicitly avoids failing an ordinary configure for a builder who just
# wants the CLI tool.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
option(CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_FUZZING
  "Build libFuzzer harnesses under fuzz/ (requires Clang + compiler-rt fuzzer/ASan/UBSan runtime)"
  OFF)

if(CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_FUZZING)
  if(NOT CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID STREQUAL "Clang")
    message(FATAL_ERROR
      "CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_FUZZING requires Clang (libFuzzer is a Clang/compiler-rt feature) -- "
      "reconfigure with -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++")
  endif()

  # The bugs this pass exists to find mostly live INSIDE conduitscope_core's own parsing code
  # (decoder.cpp, dnp3.cpp, cotp.cpp, s7comm.cpp, mqtt.cpp, ...), not in a fuzz harness's few
  # lines -- ASan/UBSan only instrument the translation units they're applied to, so the library
  # itself needs these flags too, not just the fuzz_* executables below. This is also, for free,
  # exactly the "ASan/UBSan folded into the same CI matrix" half of docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's adopted
  # plan: any CTest case (not only the fuzz_*_corpus_regression ones added below) run against a
  # CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_FUZZING=ON build -- including the `conduitscope` CLI binary itself, which
  # also links conduitscope_core and therefore also carries this instrumentation in this
  # configuration -- is already running under ASan/UBSan. PUBLIC on the link options so they
  # propagate to every consumer of conduitscope_core (the CLI executable and every fuzz_*
  # target), since each of those is a separate final link that also needs the sanitizer runtime.
  target_compile_options(conduitscope_core PRIVATE -fsanitize=address,undefined -g -O1)
  target_link_options(conduitscope_core PUBLIC -fsanitize=address,undefined)

  # Every harness below is one .cpp defining LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput, linked straight against the
  # same (now sanitizer-instrumented) conduitscope_core the real CLI links against -- no parsing
  # logic is duplicated in fuzz/. -fsanitize=fuzzer adds libFuzzer's own main() and coverage
  # instrumentation on top, for this target's one small harness file.
  function(add_conduitscope_fuzzer name)
    set(target "fuzz_${name}")
    add_executable(${target} "fuzz/fuzz_${name}.cpp")
    target_link_libraries(${target} PRIVATE conduitscope_core)
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined -g -O1)
    target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE -fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined)

    set(corpus_dir "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/fuzz/corpus/${name}")
    if(EXISTS "${corpus_dir}")
      # A short, bounded run over this target's own seed corpus -- a regression check ("a fuzz
      # corpus catching regressions", per docs/DEVELOPMENT.md), not a real fuzzing campaign. For
      # an actual campaign, run the built binary directly with -max_total_time/-jobs -- see
      # fuzz/README.md.
      add_test(NAME "fuzz_${name}_corpus_regression"
        COMMAND ${target} "${corpus_dir}" -max_total_time=10 -max_len=8192)
      set_tests_properties("fuzz_${name}_corpus_regression" PROPERTIES
        TIMEOUT 60
        LABELS "fuzz")
    endif()
  endfunction()

  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(pcap_reader)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(packet_decode)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(dnp3)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(cotp_s7comm)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(mqtt)
  # Second wave, added after the original five-target plan: the next four highest hand-rolled-
  # parsing-complexity OT/ICS protocols -- see each fuzz_*.cpp's own file header for why. bacnet
  # already has a confirmed track record (fuzz_packet_decode found a real signed-left-shift UB in
  # bacnet.cpp before this dedicated harness existed); iec104/enip/s7comm_plus are the next-most
  # structurally complex parsers in this codebase (self-describing per-type ASDU objects, CIP
  # EPATH/service-code recursion, and an unofficial, community-reverse-engineered object model,
  # respectively).
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(bacnet)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(iec104)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(enip)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(s7comm_plus)
  # Third wave: eight more dedicated harnesses -- five GateKind::TcpPort decoders parsed
  # directly off a raw TCP payload on a specific port (dcom/dicom/fox/ge_srtp/winrm), the two
  # AMQP wire formats sharing one TCP port and one connection-preamble parser (amqp091/
  # amqp10 -- each harness also drives amqp_common.hpp own try_parse_amqp_preamble directly,
  # since neither frame-level entry point reaches it on its own; see fuzz_amqp091.cpp own file
  # header for the full amqp_common decision, and why no separate fuzz_amqp_common target was
  # added), and the DNS-over-HTTPS TLS-SNI detector (tls_sni). See each fuzz_*.cpp own file
  # header for the exact entry point(s) and reasoning.
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(dcom)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(dicom)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(fox)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(ge_srtp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(winrm)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(amqp091)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(amqp10)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(tls_sni)
  # Fourth wave: the eight GateKind::IpProtocol decoders dispatched directly off the IP payload
  # by protocol number, no TCP/UDP header involved. See each fuzz_*.cpp own file header for the
  # exact entry point and, for icmpv6/igrp, the extra context (pseudo-header addresses / source
  # IP) each one needs beyond a bare ByteSpan.
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(icmp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(icmpv6)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(igmp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(igrp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(ospf)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(pim)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(vrrp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(eigrp)
  # Fifth wave: eleven more UDP/EtherType-gated decoders. bsap/coap/dhcpv6/dns/hsrp/nbns/rip/rmcp
  # are single-UDP-payload entry points; cclink_ie exposes four narrow (parser, expected-kind)
  # combinations fuzzed unconditionally in one harness; powerlink is dual-gated (EtherType 0x88AB
  # and UDP port 3819) but funnels through one shared try_parse_powerlink entry point, so its
  # corpus (not its call count) is what carries the dual coverage; quic loops several
  # representative (src_port, dst_port, extra_ports) combinations against try_recognize_quic
  # since QUIC has no single fixed port. See each fuzz_*.cpp own file header for details.
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(bsap)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(cclink_ie)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(coap)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(dhcpv6)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(dns)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(hsrp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(nbns)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(powerlink)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(quic)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(rip)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(rmcp)
  # Sixth wave: thirteen GateKind::TcpPortIndependent decoders (including modbus itself, which --
  # somewhat surprisingly -- was never in the original five-target plan despite being one of the
  # most foundational protocols in this codebase) plus six dual TCP+UDP protocol modules
  # (codesys/ffhse/fins/hartip/kerberos/melsec -- see each fuzz_*.cpp own file header for whether
  # that module's TCP and UDP sides converge on one shared parse function or are genuinely
  # distinct entry points) and mms, which rides the same TPKT/COTP framing s7comm does and is
  # built exactly like fuzz_cotp_s7comm.cpp's own two-stage shape.
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(bgp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(ldap)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(modbus)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(opcua)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(smb)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(twincat)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(codesys)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(ffhse)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(fins)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(hartip)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(kerberos)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(melsec)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(mms)
  # Seventh wave: the thirteen remaining GateKind::EtherType decoders (the fourth wave covered
  # GateKind::IpProtocol; this covers the rest of the raw-EtherType-gated set). cdp and stp are
  # not dispatched off a plain EtherType at all -- both ride 802.2 LLC/SNIC framing (CDP: DSAP=
  # SSAP=0xAA, OUI 00:00:0C, PID 0x2000; STP: DSAP=SSAP=0x42, Control=0x03) on top of an Ethernet
  # frame with a length field instead of an EtherType, so their harnesses fuzz the LLC-stripped
  # payload the same way an EtherType-gated one fuzzes the EtherType payload. slow_protocols is a
  # single try_parse_slow_protocols entry point that internally dispatches LACP/Marker/OAM by its
  # own Subtype byte, not three separate entries. pppoe's entry point takes a second bool
  # parameter (is_session_ethertype, for PPPoE Discovery vs. Session) looped over both values. See
  # each fuzz_*.cpp own file header for the exact entry point and sample-fixture source.
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(arp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(cdp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(eapol)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(ethercat)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(goose)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(homeplug_av)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(lldp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(mpls)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(pppoe)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(profinet)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(slow_protocols)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(stp)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(sv)
  # Eighth wave: the six GateKind::LinkType decoders -- non-Ethernet captures (SocketCAN,
  # IEEE 802.15.4) where the captured frame itself, not an EtherType/IP-protocol/TCP-or-UDP
  # payload, is what a try_parse_X(ByteSpan) expects. devicenet and canopen are, like j1939 and
  # zigbee, two-stage entry points (try_parse_X(const CanSocketcanFrame&), confirmed directly
  # against src/devicenet.cpp and src/canopen.cpp) built on top of a parsed CAN frame rather than
  # raw bytes -- each harness parses the fuzzer input as a SocketCAN frame first via
  # try_parse_can_socketcan, exactly as decoder.cpp itself does, before handing it to the
  # second-stage parser.
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(can_socketcan)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(canopen)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(devicenet)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(ieee802154)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(j1939)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(zigbee)
  # Ninth wave: the Windows Active Directory / DCE-RPC suite -- the generic connection-oriented
  # DCE/RPC PDU reader (dcerpc) plus the five named-pipe-riding interfaces built on top of it
  # (netlogon/samr/lsarpc/srvsvc/wkssvc share smb.hpp's pipe dispatch; drsuapi likewise) and the
  # NTLMSSP authentication-blob scanner (ntlm), which is reached from several different transports
  # rather than one gated entry point. Seed corpora for the five RPC interfaces were extracted by
  # "dogfooding" this project's own already-correct decode path (try_parse_smb ->
  # parse_dcerpc_chain -> per-interface classification by UUID) against real captured SMB2
  # traffic, rather than hand-slicing NDR-encoded bytes, to guarantee every seed is a genuine,
  # boundary-correct stub payload. See each fuzz_*.cpp own file header for its exact entry point.
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(dcerpc)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(ntlm)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(netlogon)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(samr)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(lsarpc)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(srvsvc)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(wkssvc)
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(drsuapi)
  # UMAS (umas.hpp/cpp, Grok gap #4 Phase 5) -- reachable transitively through fuzz_modbus's own
  # try_parse_modbus_tcp (base_fc == 0x5A dispatches to decode_umas, modbus.cpp), but this
  # dedicated harness calls decode_umas directly so every iteration lands on UMAS-specific code
  # instead of ~1/128th of them -- see fuzz_umas.cpp's own file header comment. Particularly worth
  # a dedicated pass since UMAS is this codebase's first protocol decoded entirely from
  # unofficial, reverse-engineered sources (umas.hpp's own header comment), with no official
  # spec's own edge cases already anticipated.
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(umas)
  # -Y/--display-filter (display_filter.hpp/display_filter_parser.cpp) -- this codebase's first
  # hand-rolled TEXT parser over untrusted-shaped input, rather than a binary wire-format decoder;
  # see fuzz_display_filter.cpp's own file header for why it needs no DecodedPacket at all.
  add_conduitscope_fuzzer(display_filter)
endif()

# The response packet's logical payload is 23 bytes -- over the 16-byte data-link block size --
# so this is also the regression guard for the multi-block CRC reassembly logic: if it mis-skips
# a block CRC, the object headers below would decode to garbage or fail to decode at all.

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "object 0: g1v2 \\(Binary Input\\) qualifier=0x00 range=0-2 -- 3 point\\(s\\), 3 byte\\(s\\) of object data")

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)

# CROB command decode: control byte 0x43 = trip/close Close(1), control code Latch On(3);
# on_time=1000ms, off_time=0ms, status=0 (Success). High security relevance -- this is literally
# how DNP3 issues output commands, so getting every field named correctly matters.

set_tests_properties(dnp3_crob_value_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "idx=7: code=Latch On tc=Close queue/clear=0x00 count=1 on_time=1000ms off_time=0ms status=Success")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cross-packet DNP3 fragment reassembly (packets 8-12 of sample_dnp3.pcap): a fragment split
# across multiple data-link frames arriving in SEPARATE TCP segments/pcap packets, requiring the
# per-TCP-flow state Dnp3Decoder::process_frame maintains (via
# DecodeContext::flow_state<Dnp3ReassemblyState>(FlowStateKeying::DirectionalFlow), migration
# batch 2 -- see dnp3.hpp) across decode() calls -- distinct from the same-TCP-payload frame
# coalescing (Problem A) tested above.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The FIR=1,FIN=0 starting frame (packet 8) must show only its own transport header -- nothing
# decoded yet -- plus a note that reassembly has begun and is buffering.
add_test(NAME dnp3_reassembly_start_frame_not_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_reassembly_start_frame_not_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "beginning a DNP3 fragment that spans multiple data-link frames \\(FIR=1, FIN=0, SEQ=5\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "transport: FIR=1 FIN=0 SEQ=5 \\| application")

# The FIN=1 completing frame (packet 9, a separate pcap packet from packet 8) must decode the
# full, concatenated application layer -- same CROB command as the single-frame packet 6, but
# reconstructed from two frames delivered a packet apart.
add_test(NAME dnp3_reassembly_completes_across_packets
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_reassembly_completes_across_packets PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "completed a 2-data-link-frame DNP3 fragment reassembled across separate TCP segments \\(18 application-layer byte\\(s\\) total\\)")

add_test(NAME dnp3_reassembly_completed_object_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_reassembly_completed_object_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "function=Direct Operate \\(0x05\\) objects: \\[g12v1\\].*idx=7: code=Latch On tc=Close")

add_test(NAME dnp3_reassembly_completed_function_in_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_reassembly_completed_function_in_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 9,[^}]*\"dnp3_function\": \"Direct Operate\"")

# packet 5 (FIR=1,FIN=1, same TCP flow as packet 4's never-completed start) must abandon packet
# 4's stale in-progress reassembly rather than silently merging into it.
add_test(NAME dnp3_reassembly_abandoned_by_new_complete_fragment
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_reassembly_abandoned_by_new_complete_fragment PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "a complete single-frame DNP3 fragment \\(FIR=1, FIN=1\\) arrived on this TCP flow while a previous multi-frame fragment reassembly was still in progress")

# packet 10: a FIR=0 continuation with no reassembly in progress on its flow at all (orphan) --
# must be left transport-only, with an explanatory note, never guessed at.
add_test(NAME dnp3_reassembly_orphan_continuation_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)

# packets 11-12: a sequence-number mismatch must discard the in-progress reassembly rather than
# concatenating bytes out of order.
add_test(NAME dnp3_reassembly_sequence_mismatch_discarded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_reassembly_sequence_mismatch_discarded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "continuation DNP3 data-link frame's sequence number \\(35\\) does not follow the previous frame's \\(expected 11\\)")

# packets 23-24: a duplicate/replayed data-link frame -- frame 23 begins a fragment (SEQ=20),
# frame 24 repeats the SAME SEQ=20 instead of advancing to 21 -- distinct from packets 11-12's
# arbitrary sequence JUMP above (expected 11, got 35); must be rejected the exact same way, not
# specially "recognized" as a harmless repeat. Security audit follow-up (docs/reviews/2026-09-
# chatgpt-security-review-patch257.md's "4. OT-specific security risks", item 3, "Protocol
# reassembly").
add_test(NAME dnp3_reassembly_duplicate_sequence_discarded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_reassembly_duplicate_sequence_discarded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "continuation DNP3 data-link frame's sequence number \\(20\\) does not follow the previous frame's \\(expected 21\\) -- discarding 5 already-buffered byte\\(s\\) and abandoning this fragment reassembly; application layer not decoded")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data-link CRC-16 validation (header CRC + per-block CRC, both now actually calculated and
# compared against the on-the-wire value -- see dnp3_crc16 in dnp3.cpp). tools/make_sample_pcap.py
# now gives every sample_dnp3.pcap frame a genuinely correct CRC by default (dnp3_link_frame), so
# packets 1-12 above all validate cleanly; packets 13 and 14 below are deliberately corrupted.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Packet 1: a link-layer-only control frame with no user data at all -- must still get its header
# CRC checked (block_count/block_crc_failures stay 0, there is nothing to reassemble).
add_test(NAME dnp3_no_user_data_header_crc_still_validated
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_no_user_data_header_crc_still_validated PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 1,[^}]*\"dnp3_link_crc_valid\": true,\n    \"dnp3_header_crc_valid\": true,\n    \"dnp3_block_count\": 0,\n    \"dnp3_block_crc_failures\": 0")

# Data-link source/destination address (Dnp3LinkFrame::source/destination -- 16-bit DNP3 station
# addresses, NOT IP addresses, see decoder.hpp's own dnp3_source_address/dnp3_destination_address
# comment) surfaced to JSON output: packet 1 is master(1)->outstation(1024), packet 3 is the
# reverse direction, outstation(1024)->master(1) -- confirms both fields render correctly, and
# that the direction actually flips with the real traffic direction rather than being a fixed pair.
add_test(NAME dnp3_source_destination_address_master_to_outstation
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_source_destination_address_master_to_outstation PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 1,[^}]*\"dnp3_source_address\": 1,\n    \"dnp3_destination_address\": 1024,")

add_test(NAME dnp3_source_destination_address_outstation_to_master
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_source_destination_address_outstation_to_master PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 3,[^}]*\"dnp3_source_address\": 1024,\n    \"dnp3_destination_address\": 1,")

# Packet 2: single-block Read Class 0 request -- one valid block.
add_test(NAME dnp3_read_class0_crc_valid_single_block
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_read_class0_crc_valid_single_block PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 2,[^}]*\"dnp3_link_crc_valid\": true,\n    \"dnp3_header_crc_valid\": true,\n    \"dnp3_block_count\": 1,\n    \"dnp3_block_crc_failures\": 0")

# Packet 3: the 23-byte multi-block Response -- two valid blocks, exercising the multi-block CRC
# path (block boundary at 16 bytes) with genuinely correct CRCs, not just correct block placement.
add_test(NAME dnp3_multiblock_response_crc_valid_two_blocks
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_multiblock_response_crc_valid_two_blocks PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 3,[^}]*\"dnp3_link_crc_valid\": true,\n    \"dnp3_header_crc_valid\": true,\n    \"dnp3_block_count\": 2,\n    \"dnp3_block_crc_failures\": 0")

# Packet 13: the same Read Class 0 request as packet 2, but with a deliberately corrupted header
# CRC. The specific calculated-vs-declared note must appear, AND the application layer -- which a
# bad HEADER crc has no bearing on -- must still decode exactly as it does for packet 2, proving
# a CRC failure never stops decoding (this codebase's consistent degrade-gracefully philosophy).
add_test(NAME dnp3_bad_header_crc_noted_and_still_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_bad_header_crc_noted_and_still_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "function=Read \\(0x01\\) objects: \\[g60v1\\][^\n]*\n *note: header CRC mismatch: calculated 0x[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f], frame declares 0x[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]")

add_test(NAME dnp3_bad_header_crc_fields_in_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_bad_header_crc_fields_in_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 13,[^}]*\"dnp3_link_crc_valid\": false,\n    \"dnp3_header_crc_valid\": false,\n    \"dnp3_block_count\": 1,\n    \"dnp3_block_crc_failures\": 0")

# Packet 14: the same 23-byte multi-block Response as packet 3, but with ONLY block 2's CRC
# corrupted (block 1's CRC and the header CRC are both left correct) -- confirms per-block
# granularity, and that object headers still decode from the (structurally untouched) bytes.
add_test(NAME dnp3_bad_block_crc_noted_and_objects_still_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_bad_block_crc_noted_and_objects_still_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "block 2 CRC mismatch \\(7 data byte\\(s\\)\\): calculated 0x[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f], frame declares 0x[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]\n.*object 0: g1v2 \\(Binary Input\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "block 1 CRC mismatch")

add_test(NAME dnp3_bad_block_crc_fields_in_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dnp3_bad_block_crc_fields_in_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 14,[^}]*\"dnp3_link_crc_valid\": false,\n    \"dnp3_header_crc_valid\": true,\n    \"dnp3_block_count\": 2,\n    \"dnp3_block_crc_failures\": 1")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Phase 5 (docs/design/asset-inventory-real-record.md): Device Attributes (group 0, IEEE 1815)
# decode + identity correlation. Packets 15-22 of sample_dnp3.pcap -- see
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py's own per-packet comments for the full byte-level rationale.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Packet 15: a plain Read request for g0v252 (Device Manufacturer's Name) carries NO object data
# on the wire (dnp3.hpp's file header comment on the request/response asymmetry) -- confirms the

# Packet 16: the matching single-attribute Response -- has_device_identity=true,
# device_manufacturer_name="Acme Controls", every other device_* field absent (only the fields
# actually present are ever emitted -- see write_dnp3_json_fields's own comment).

# Packet 17: a Response bundling all five recognized identity attributes -- confirms every field
# promotes correctly in one fragment, and the "device-identity(...)" summary suffix (mirroring

# Packet 18: g0v252 declared as Data Type Code 0x05 (OSTR) instead of VSTR -- not decoded by this
# groundwork release (same gap Wireshark's own packet-dnp.c dissector has), and critically NOT
# promoted (a non-VSTR value on an identity variation is never treated as identity).

set_tests_properties(dnp3_device_attribute_unsupported_data_type_not_promoted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 18,[^}]*\"dnp3_has_device_identity\": false,")

# Packet 19: a non-identity variation (g0v221, "Number of analog outputs") decoded as UINT --

# Packet 20: a non-zero index prefix (qualifier 0x17) on group 0, variation 255 (List of
# Attribute Variations) -- the "bundling format... not decoded" bailout, distinct from the plain

# Packet 21: g0v252 declares a 20-byte VSTR length but only 5 bytes actually remain (truncated
# capture) -- the truncation note names the exact declared-vs-available counts, and nothing is

# Packet 22: variation 0 (the bare "Device Attributes Group and null variation" placeholder) --
# the variation-0/254/255 bailout, distinct from the index-prefix bailout in packet 20 (this one

# Inventory wiring: packet 17's Response (192.168.1.10, the outstation) carries all five

# Real-world confirmation, independent of the synthetic fixture above: a genuine capture's own
# CRC bytes (computed by a real DNP3 stack, not by tools/make_sample_pcap.py) must validate --

# Same, but for a link-layer-only control frame (Request Link Status carries no user data) --
# regression guard for the "no user data" path specifically, since that's the one case where
# Dnp3Decoder::process_frame is never called at all (see dnp3.cpp) and the crc fields must still

add_test(NAME real_dnp3_request_link_status_crc_valid_with_no_user_data

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# General TCP stream reassembly (Decoder::reassemble_tcp_payload / tcp_reassembly_) -- a single
# PDU/frame's own bytes split across TCP segments, one flow-level layer below DNP3's own
# application-fragment reassembly tested above. tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap, scenarios A-F.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A) Modbus response ADU split across two TCP segments: the first segment alone must show only
# "buffering", never a modbus decode; the second must complete it correctly.
add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_modbus_first_segment_buffers
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_modbus_first_segment_buffers PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "buffering a Modbus/TCP PDU/frame split across TCP segments 502->51600: 15 of 29 declared byte\\(s\\)")

# [^#] rather than a bare .* binds the match to one packet's own block of output (every packet's
# block starts with a line beginning "#<index>", and nothing inside a block contains '#') -- .*
# alone would span the WHOLE command output across every packet, so a later, unrelated packet's
# text (several other scenarios below decode to this same "response: 20 data byte(s) = 00 00 00
# 01..." text, being built from the same register values) could satisfy it just as well, proving
# nothing about which packet actually produced it. Same technique already used for the JSON
# per-object checks above (there bounded by '}' instead of '#').
add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_modbus_completes
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_modbus_completes PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "response: 20 data byte\\(s\\) = 00 00 00 01 00 02 00 03 00 04 00 05 00 06 00 07 00 08 00 09[^#]*reassembled a Modbus/TCP PDU/frame from 29 byte\\(s\\) spanning 2 TCP segments")

# B) A complete single-data-link-frame DNP3 fragment split mid-*header* across two TCP segments.
add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_dnp3_link_layer_completes
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_dnp3_link_layer_completes PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "function=Read \\(0x01\\) objects: \\[g60v1\\][^#]*reassembled a DNP3 data-link PDU/frame from 18 byte\\(s\\) spanning 2 TCP segments")

# C) A TPKT/S7comm Setup Communication request split across two TCP segments.
add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_tpkt_s7comm_completes
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_tpkt_s7comm_completes PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Setup Communication \\(negotiated PDU length=240[^#]*reassembled a TPKT/COTP PDU/frame from 25 byte\\(s\\) spanning 2 TCP segments")

# D) A TCP sequence gap abandons the in-progress reassembly, and a later, ordinary request on the
# same flow still decodes normally afterward (the abandoned state doesn't wedge the flow).
add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_gap_abandons_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_gap_abandons_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "TCP sequence gap on this flow \\(expected seq 30009, got 30509, 500 byte\\(s\\) apparently missing\\) -- abandoning an in-progress 9-byte PDU/frame reassembly")

add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_flow_recovers_after_gap
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_flow_recovers_after_gap PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "request: read 10 holding register\\(s\\) starting at address 0")

# E) A fully-duplicate retransmission mid-reassembly is ignored, not misapplied; the real
# completing segment afterward still finishes the PDU correctly.
add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_duplicate_retransmit_ignored
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_duplicate_retransmit_ignored PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "retransmitted/duplicate TCP segment 502->51604 \\(fully overlaps bytes already buffered for an in-progress 20-byte PDU/frame reassembly")

add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_completes_despite_duplicate
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_completes_despite_duplicate PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "response: 20 data byte\\(s\\) = 00 00 00 01 00 02 00 03 00 04 00 05 00 06 00 07 00 08 00 09[^#]*reassembled a Modbus/TCP PDU/frame from 29 byte\\(s\\) spanning 3 TCP segments")

# F) A partial-overlap retransmission (repeats a few already-buffered bytes, then extends past
# them with new ones) is trimmed to just its new bytes, not misaligned or duplicated.
add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_partial_overlap_trimmed
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_partial_overlap_trimmed PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "TCP segment on this flow overlaps 3 already-buffered byte\\(s\\) with identical content \\(a genuine retransmission\\) -- trimmed and only the new byte\\(s\\) appended")

add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_partial_overlap_completes_correctly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_partial_overlap_completes_correctly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "response: 20 data byte\\(s\\) = 00 00 00 01 00 02 00 03 00 04 00 05 00 06 00 07 00 08 00 09[^#]*reassembled a Modbus/TCP PDU/frame from 29 byte\\(s\\) spanning 3 TCP segments")

# G) A partial overlap whose overlapping bytes DISAGREE with what's already buffered (distinct
#    from scenario F above, whose overlap is genuine identical content) -- security audit
#    follow-up, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch257.md's "4. OT-specific
#    security risks", item 3, "Protocol reassembly". The note must say the content disagrees
#    (not the generic "likely a retransmission" wording scenario F's identical-content overlap
#    gets), and the final decode must still show the REAL register values -- proving first-
#    received-wins holds even when a later segment's own overlapping bytes actively disagree,
#    not just when they're an identical repeat.
add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_conflicting_overlap_content_flagged
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_conflicting_overlap_content_flagged PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "TCP segment on this flow overlaps 3 already-buffered byte\\(s\\) whose content disagrees with what's already buffered \\(ambiguous/conflicting data -- possibly a crafted overlap\\) -- the already-buffered byte\\(s\\) are kept for that range \\(first-received-wins\\) and only the segment's new byte\\(s\\) beyond the overlap are appended")

add_test(NAME tcp_reassembly_conflicting_overlap_first_received_wins
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tcp_reassembly_conflicting_overlap_first_received_wins PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "response: 20 data byte\\(s\\) = 00 00 00 01 00 02 00 03 00 04 00 05 00 06 00 07 00 08 00 09[^#]*reassembled a Modbus/TCP PDU/frame from 29 byte\\(s\\) spanning 3 TCP segments")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Real-world DNP3 captures (not synthetic, unlike tests/sample_dnp3.pcap above),
# sourced from github.com/automayt/ICS-pcap -- see
# tests/real_captures/dnp3/ATTRIBUTION.md for exact provenance, why these
# particular captures, and licensing notes.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(DNP3_REAL_CAPTURES
  dnp3_read
  dnp3_read_request
  dnp3_write
  dnp3_write_request
  dnp3_select_operate
  dnp3_select_operate_request
  dnp3_request_link
  dnp3_request_link_status
  dnp3_malformed
  dnp3_test_data_part1
  dnp3_test_data_part2
)
# Baseline regression guard for every one of them: real (including deliberately
# malformed/fuzzed) traffic must never crash the parser or make it exit non-zero,
# independent of whatever it does or doesn't manage to decode. CTest already
# fails a test on a non-zero exit code, so no PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION is needed
# here -- that would only test that decode ran, which the exit code already covers.
foreach(capture ${DNP3_REAL_CAPTURES})
  add_test(NAME real_dnp3_${capture}_does_not_crash
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/dnp3/${capture}.pcap" --format json)
endforeach()

add_test(NAME real_dnp3_read_class1_poll_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/dnp3/dnp3_read.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(real_dnp3_read_class1_poll_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "function=Read \\(0x01\\) objects: \\[g60v2\\]")

# Real Select/Operate CROB sequence -- confirms the field-by-field CROB decode
# (control code, trip/close, queue/clear, on/off time, status) against an
# independent DNP3 master's actual wire encoding, not just the synthetic
# fixture's one hand-constructed control byte.
add_test(NAME real_dnp3_select_operate_crob_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/dnp3/dnp3_select_operate.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(real_dnp3_select_operate_crob_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "idx=1: code=Latch On tc=NUL queue/clear=0x00 count=1 on_time=100ms off_time=100ms status=Success")

# Same CROB object, but a real operate attempt that the outstation rejected --
# confirms the IEEE 1815 control-status-code table isn't only decoding whichever
# single status value the synthetic fixture happens to use.
add_test(NAME real_dnp3_test_data_part2_crob_status_success

# Real polling session: Binary Input (bit-packed), Binary Output (byte-per-point

# `detect` against dnp3_test_data_part1.pcap -- an unplanned, welcome bonus (same discipline noted
# at real_modbus_detect_batch1_all_findings above): this real capture genuinely contains DNP3 Stop
# Application traffic, a Disable Unsolicited Responses request addressed to the reserved broadcast
# address 0xFFFF, AND a Read-request enumeration sweep spanning 5 distinct object group/variation
# combinations, giving three of Batch 2's six new patterns (docs/research/2026-09-detect-pattern-
# candidates-batch2.md's own Batch 2 section, items 7-9) real-traffic evidence rather than only a
# synthetic fixture. Confirmed via this test's own manual verification pass against the real CLI
# output before this assertion was written. Only asserts the Batch 2 finding TEXT (not the full
# report, which also carries this capture's own pre-existing dnp3-restart/dnp3-unsolicited-misuse
# findings from earlier work) -- see detect_snort_patterns_batch2_all_findings below for the full,
# exhaustively-pinned synthetic-fixture report.
add_test(NAME real_dnp3_detect_batch2_findings
  COMMAND conduitscope detect --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/dnp3/dnp3_test_data_part1.pcap")
set_tests_properties(real_dnp3_detect_batch2_findings PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[Engineering-Station Activity\\] T0861 \\(Point & Tag Identification\\).*DNP3 Read requests from this master spanned 5 distinct object group/variation combinations against this outstation within 60s -- an engineering-tool-shaped enumeration sweep rather than routine periodic polling.*\\[Protocol Misuse\\] T0855 \\(Unauthorized Command Message\\).*DNP3 Disable Unsolicited Responses addressed to reserved broadcast destination address 0xffff -- reaches every outstation on the segment at once, a single message with plant-wide blast radius\; can also be a redundant/standby master issuing a legitimate resync broadcast after a failover, or a commissioning/maintenance broadcast re-enabling unsolicited reporting plant-wide -- treat as a prompt to confirm which master should be active and why a broadcast was used, not confirmed misuse.*\\[Engineering-Station Activity\\] T0858 \\(Change Operating Mode\\).*DNP3 Stop Application request -- an outstation's application layer is being halted without a full device restart.*\\[Engineering-Station Activity\\] T0858 \\(Change Operating Mode\\).*DNP3 Stop Application request -- an outstation's application layer is being halted without a full device restart.*\\[Protocol Misuse\\] T0855 \\(Unauthorized Command Message\\).*DNP3 Stop Application addressed to reserved broadcast destination address 0xffff -- reaches every outstation on the segment at once, a single message with plant-wide blast radius\; can also be a redundant/standby master issuing a legitimate resync broadcast after a failover, or a commissioning/maintenance broadcast re-enabling unsolicited reporting plant-wide -- treat as a prompt to confirm which master should be active and why a broadcast was used, not confirmed misuse")

# Regression fixture for the IEC104-vs-Modbus detection collision found while scoping this
# feature (see try_parse_iec104_apci's header comment in iec104.hpp and the dispatch-order
# comment in decoder.cpp): an I-format APDU with N(S)=N(R)=0 whose APCI bytes also read as a
# plausible Modbus/TCP MBAP header (protocol-id==0, mbap_length==0, a non-zero "function code")
# must be classified as iec104, not modbus.
add_test(NAME iec104_wins_modbus_detection_collision
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_iec104_modbus_precedence.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(iec104_wins_modbus_detection_collision PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[iec104\\]  I-format N\\(S\\)=0 N\\(R\\)=0\; C_IC_NA_1")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Real-world IEC 60870-5-104 captures -- see tests/real_captures/iec104/ATTRIBUTION.md for
# provenance. Three sourced from public Wireshark/ICS-pcap test-capture collections (the
# Wireshark wiki's own iec104.pcap sample, a diverse 2010 simulated hydro-plant capture, and a
# 2008 dissector test file), plus the three station-address captures from Netresec's public
# Industroyer2 release -- real, attributed nation-state ICS malware traffic against a live
# IEC 104 RTU, not a synthetic or generic test vector.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(IEC104_REAL_CAPTURES
  iec104_wireshark_wiki
  iec104_090813_diverse
  iec104_test_dissect
  industroyer2_station1
  industroyer2_station2
  industroyer2_station3
)
# Same baseline regression guard as the DNP3/Modbus real-capture loops above: must never crash
# the parser or exit non-zero, independent of what it does or doesn't manage to decode.
foreach(capture ${IEC104_REAL_CAPTURES})
  add_test(NAME real_iec104_${capture}_does_not_crash
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/iec104/${capture}.pcap" --format json)
endforeach()

# 090813_diverse.pcap: a simulated hydro-plant floodgate-manipulation scenario (subject of
# Netresec's 2012 "SCADA Network Forensics with IEC-104" post) -- real command/setpoint traffic,
# not just monitoring, including the short-floating-point setpoint command (type 50) this
# decoder table covers.

# Regression: before cip_is_plausible_type_code was widened to include the >= 0x02A0 structured
# range (see that function's comment in enip.cpp), a genuine UDT Read_Tag response like the one
# above was WRONGLY rejected into the "response data does not start with a recognized CIP
# elementary type code" fallback note -- assert the structure_handle value is present AND that
# fallback note is absent for this specific response.
add_test(NAME enip_structured_type_code_not_misclassified_as_implausible
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip_string_and_structured.pcap")
set_tests_properties(enip_structured_type_code_not_misclassified_as_implausible PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "structure_handle=0x1234"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "response data does not start with a recognized CIP elementary type code")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PROFINET RT (synthetic, tests/sample_profinet.pcap): DCP (Discovery and Configuration
# Protocol) request/response exchanges and cyclic real-time IO data frames -- see
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_profinet_sample for the exact byte layout each assertion
# below is checking, and profinet.hpp's file header comment for the decoder itself. Unlike every
# other protocol above, PROFINET RT rides directly on raw Ethernet (EtherType 0x8892) -- there is
# no IP/TCP/UDP layer at all.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_test(NAME profinet_dcp_identify_request_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_profinet.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(profinet_dcp_identify_request_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[profinet\\]  DCP Identify Request xid=0x00112233")

add_test(NAME profinet_dcp_unknown_block_shown_as_raw_hex
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_profinet.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(profinet_dcp_unknown_block_shown_as_raw_hex PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: DCP block option=0xFF suboption=0xFF not decoded")

# The Identify Response: same Xid as the Request above (authoritative pairing isn't attempted by
# this decoder, but a matching Xid is still a useful correlation signal for a human reading the
# output), and all five of this decoder's value-decoded DCP block types in one PDU.
add_test(NAME profinet_dcp_identify_response_headline_fields_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_profinet.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(profinet_dcp_identify_response_headline_fields_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "DCP Identify Response-Success xid=0x00112233 name_of_station=\"plc-1\" vendor=0x002A device=0x0101")

# Regression guard for DCP block-list padding (see profinet.cpp's decode_dcp_blocks): the
# NameOfStation block above is a deliberately ODD-length string ("plc-1", 5 bytes); if the pad
# byte before the next block were handled wrong, DeviceID/DeviceRole below would misparse instead
# of decoding cleanly.
add_test(NAME profinet_dcp_response_all_blocks_decoded_in_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_profinet.pcap")
set_tests_properties(profinet_dcp_response_all_blocks_decoded_in_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"profinet_dcp_blocks\": \\[\"MACAddress=00:0C:29:AA:BB:CC\", \"IPParameter=ip=192.168.1.10 subnet=255.255.255.0 gateway=192.168.1.1\", \"NameOfStation=plc-1\", \"DeviceID=vendor=0x002A device=0x0101\", \"DeviceRole=0x01 \\[IO Device\\]\"\\]")

add_test(NAME profinet_dcp_set_request_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_profinet.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(profinet_dcp_set_request_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[profinet\\]  DCP Set Request xid=0x00445566")

# Regression guard for the OTHER (ServiceID, direction) combination that carries a 2-byte prefix
# before an Option 0x01/0x02 block's content (BlockQualifier, for a Set Request -- see
# dcp_block_prefix_len's comment in profinet.cpp): if that prefix weren't stripped, this
# IPParameter block would show as an unrecognized 14-byte blob instead of decoding cleanly.
add_test(NAME profinet_dcp_set_request_block_qualifier_stripped
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_profinet.pcap")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"profinet_dcp_blocks\": \\[\"IPParameter=ip=192.168.1.20 subnet=255.255.255.0 gateway=192.168.1.1\"\\]")

add_test(NAME profinet_dcp_hello_decoded

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "gcb04[^\n]*\n *note: header S-bit")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Real-world IEC 61850-8-1 GOOSE captures -- see tests/real_captures/goose/ATTRIBUTION.md for
# provenance. All four sourced from the same ITI/ICS-Security-Tools public pcap collection
# PROFINET RT's real fixtures came from: a GE F650 relay's own retransmission/sqNum-reset
# sequence, a single maximally-complete VLAN-tagged frame, a 451-frame bulk-validation capture,
# and a mixed MMS+GOOSE capture used as a crash-safety/non-interference check.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(GOOSE_REAL_CAPTURES
  goose_ge_f650_retransmissions
  goose_demo_full_fields
  sample_file_goose
  sample_file_mms_and_goose
)
# Same baseline regression guard as the other protocols' real-capture loops above: must never
# crash the parser or exit non-zero, independent of what it does or doesn't manage to decode.
foreach(capture ${GOOSE_REAL_CAPTURES})
  add_test(NAME real_goose_${capture}_does_not_crash
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/goose/${capture}.pcap" --format json)
endforeach()

# The F650 relay capture: sqNum counts 10, 11, 12 then RESETS to 1 while stNum stays at 1 -- a

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IEC 61850-9-2 Sampled Values (synthetic, tests/sample_sv.pcap): the ASN.1 BER-encoded SavPdu
# (noASDU + one or more ASDU elements) -- see tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_sv_sample for the
# exact byte layout each assertion below is checking, and sv.hpp's file header comment for the
# decoder itself. Like GOOSE and PROFINET RT, SV rides directly on raw Ethernet (EtherType
# 0x88BA) -- there is no IP/TCP/UDP layer at all. No real SV capture was found despite a genuine
# search (see sv.hpp's Validation paragraph), so unlike GOOSE, there is no real-capture test block
# below -- every path here is synthetic-only.

# An SV frame too short for even the fixed 8-byte APPID/Length/Reserved1/Reserved2 header must NOT
# be misdetected -- falls through to the generic "non-ip" ethertype-name-only report.
add_test(NAME sv_truncated_header_falls_back_to_non_ip
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_sv.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(sv_truncated_header_falls_back_to_non_ip PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[non-ip\\]  Ethernet frame with ethertype 0x88ba \\(IEC 61850-9-2 Sampled Values\\) \\(not IPv4\\)")

# A full 8-byte header but the byte immediately after it is not 0x60 -- must NOT be misdetected as
# SV; both this packet and the truncated-header one above fall back to the same "non-ip" report,
# so this asserts there are exactly two such lines in the whole file (no false positive elsewhere).
# A non-IP packet's src_mac/dst_mac are now shown directly on its own headline (see output.cpp's
# endpoint()) rather than needing a separate "eth ..." line below it -- write_packet() suppresses
# that line outright for a packet with no IP layer, since it would just repeat the same pair (see
# write_packet's own comment); --ether is kept on this test only to prove that suppression, not
# because it still adds anything here. Two consecutive #10/#11 non-ip lines, each carrying its own
# MAC pair inline, is what pins that down.
add_test(NAME sv_wrong_outer_tag_falls_back_to_non_ip
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_sv.pcap" --ether --format text)
set_tests_properties(sv_wrong_outer_tag_falls_back_to_non_ip PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#10  .*non-ip\\][^\n]*\n#11  .*00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc[^\n]*non-ip\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\n *eth ")

add_test(NAME sv_bogus_length_field_falls_back_to_available_bytes
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_sv.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(sv_bogus_length_field_falls_back_to_available_bytes PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SV IED5/MSVCB01 smpCnt=1 confRev=1[^\n]*\n *note: Length field \\(3\\) is implausible")

add_test(NAME sv_truncated_apdu_partial_decode_noted

set_tests_properties(sv_truncated_apdu_partial_decode_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SV appid=0x4009 noASDU=1 \\(0 ASDU\\(s\\) decoded\\)[^\n]*\n *note: SV APDU declares 200 byte\\(s\\) but only 3 remain -- decoding what's present")

add_test(NAME sv_wrong_asdu_element_tag_skipped_with_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_sv.pcap" --format text --verbose)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: seqASDU element tag=0x31 is not the expected UNIVERSAL SEQUENCE tag \\(0x30\\) -- skipped")

add_test(NAME sv_unrecognized_asdu_field_tag_noted

# Len word's Circulating bit (0x4000) -- never observed set in the real capture (see
# ATTRIBUTION.md), synthetic-only. Surfaced via ethercat_first_circulating and the per-datagram
# summary's " circulating" suffix, not the terse top-level frame summary (matching how GOOSE's own

add_test(NAME ethercat_frame_header_reserved_bit_noted

# Curated finding (4): a Controlled Node (NodeID 1, i.e. CN1) sourcing an ASnd/NMTCommand

# Curated finding (2): rogue-MN / MN-identity tracking. sample_powerlink.pcap itself (above) is
# this finding's own NEGATIVE control -- exactly one (MAC, NodeID) identity ever sources
# SoC/PReq/SoA there, so the finding must NOT appear in any of the --stats tests above (none of
# their PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION patterns match "rogue Managing Node", and CTest does not check for

# --powerlink-sdo-port -- widens (and, with an explicit --protocol powerlink, un-gates) detection
# of the SDO-over-UDP secondary path beyond its own default port (3819), mirroring --bsap-port/
# --coap-port's own "DOES gate detection" posture. sample_powerlink.pcap's own standard-port UDP
# packet (#19 above) already covers the ordinary case; packet #21 (53700->9999, not the standard
# 3819) is not reached at all in Auto mode (require_powerlink_sdo_port), so this forces
# --protocol powerlink to exercise the non-standard-port note.
add_test(NAME powerlink_sdo_udp_non_standard_port_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_powerlink.pcap" --protocol powerlink --format text --verbose)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.1.50:53700 -> 192.168.1.10:9999[^\n]*\\[powerlink\\]  POWERLINK ASnd \\(SDO\\)[^\n]*\n *note: seen on UDP port 53700->9999, which is not a configured/standard POWERLINK SDO-over-UDP port \\(3819\\)")

# With an explicit --powerlink-sdo-port matching packet #21's own non-standard port, Auto mode's
# port gate widens to admit it too (no --protocol override needed) and the "not a
# configured/standard port" note must NOT appear, since 53700 is now itself "configured/expected".
add_test(NAME powerlink_sdo_udp_extra_port_widens_detection
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_powerlink.pcap" --powerlink-sdo-port 53700 --format text --verbose)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.1.50:53700 -> 192.168.1.10:9999[^\n]*\\[powerlink\\]  POWERLINK ASnd \\(SDO\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "not a configured/standard POWERLINK")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STP/RSTP/MSTP (synthetic, tests/sample_stp.pcap): the first protocol in this codebase reached

# EtherType -- see link_layer.hpp's file header for that plumbing, and stp.hpp's file header for
# the BPDU wire format and every documented deviation/scope decision. Packet numbers in comments
# below match build_stp_sample()'s own numbered comments 1-30 in tools/make_sample_pcap.py.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2) RSTP RST BPDU (version 2) -- byte-for-byte reproduction of a real capture frame (see

# 3-4) TCN BPDU, decoded under both a classic STP (version 0) and an RSTP (version 2) Protocol

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  .*\\[stp\\]  STP Topology Change Notification \\(STP \\(802.1D\\)\\)")

# 13) MSTP MST BPDU with zero MSTI Configuration Messages (Version 3 Length exactly the 64-byte

# 14) Version 3 Length nonzero but less than the 64-byte static MST extension header -- the

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#14  .*MSTIs=2\n *note: Version 3 Length \\(2\\) is nonzero but less than the 64-byte static MST extension header -- treated as a COUNT OF MESSAGES")

# 15) Version 3 Length implies more MSTI bytes than actually remain -- decodes as many whole
# messages as fit.

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#15  .*MSTIs=1\n *note: Version 3 Length implies 32 byte\\(s\\) of MSTI Configuration Message\\(s\\) but only 16 byte\\(s\\) remain -- decoding as many whole messages as fit")

# 16) A partial trailing MSTI Configuration Message (fewer than 16 leftover bytes) is left
# undecoded and its leftover bytes are noted, not silently dropped.

# 17) Protocol Version 3 (MSTP) but too few bytes present for the MST extension's 102-byte
# minimum -- falls back to a plain RST-shaped decode, matching the reference dissector.
add_test(NAME stp_mstp_too_short_for_mst_extension_falls_back_to_rst
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_stp.pcap" --format text --verbose)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#17  .*Port=0x800A Role=Unknown\n *note: Protocol Version 3 but only 36 byte\\(s\\) present \\(need >= 102\\) -- MST extension not attempted, decoded as a plain RST BPDU")

# 18) Protocol Version 3 but Version 1 Length is nonzero -- the MST detection gate's second
# condition fails, falls back to a plain RST-shaped decode (matches the reference source exactly).
add_test(NAME stp_mstp_nonzero_version1_length_falls_back_to_rst
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_stp.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(stp_mstp_nonzero_version1_length_falls_back_to_rst PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#18  .*Port=0x800B Role=Unknown\n *note: Protocol Version 3 but Version 1 Length is 5 \\(not 0\\) -- MST extension not attempted, decoded as a plain RST BPDU \\(matches the reference source's own behavior exactly\\)")

# 19) Version 3 Length is 0 (not merely below 64) and the frame's total length matches the
# legacy/alternative MSTI Configuration Message format's own sizing rule -- named as such, but
# that alternative format is deliberately not decoded (see stp.hpp for why).
add_test(NAME stp_mstp_version3_length_zero_alt_format_named_not_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_stp.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(stp_mstp_version3_length_zero_alt_format_named_not_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#19  .*MST Config Name=\"\" \\(CIST Bridge Identifier/MSTI not decoded -- Version 3 Length is 0, see notes\\)\n *note: Version 3 Length is 0 and the frame's total length matches the legacy/alternative MSTI Configuration Message format's own sizing rule")

# 20) SPB (802.1aq, Protocol Version 4) -- named-only, not decoded, per this release's explicit
# scope decision (see stp.hpp).
add_test(NAME stp_spb_version4_named_only_not_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_stp.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(stp_spb_version4_named_only_not_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#20  .*\\[stp\\]  SPB \\(802.1aq\\), not decoded -- out of scope")

# 21-22) STP's own LLC DSAP/SSAP/Control (0x42/0x42/0x03) present, but the payload itself doesn't
# structurally parse as STP (bad Protocol Identifier; unrecognized BPDU Type) -- falls back to
# reporting the frame as a generic, unrecognized LLC frame rather than guessing.
# Same "no separate eth line for a non-IP packet" behavior sv_wrong_outer_tag_falls_back_to_non_ip
# above pins down -- --ether is kept here only to prove the suppression, not because it still adds an
# "eth ..." line between these two.
add_test(NAME stp_bad_protocol_identifier_and_bad_bpdu_type_fall_back_to_llc
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_stp.pcap" --ether --format text)
set_tests_properties(stp_bad_protocol_identifier_and_bad_bpdu_type_fall_back_to_llc PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#21  .*00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 01:80:c2:00:00:00[^\n]*\\[non-ip\\]  IEEE 802.3 LLC frame, DSAP=0x42 SSAP=0x42 Control=0x3 \\(length=38\\)\n#22  .*\\[non-ip\\]  IEEE 802.3 LLC frame, DSAP=0x42 SSAP=0x42 Control=0x3 \\(length=38\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#21[^\n]*\n *eth ")

# 23) Truncated before the common Configuration/RST BPDU body -- reported as truncated with an
# explanatory note, not decoded further.

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#23  .*\\[stp\\]  Configuration BPDU \\(truncated before the common body\\)\n *note: only 20 byte\\(s\\) present, need 35 for the common Configuration/RST BPDU body")

# 24) Common body present in full, but truncated right after it (no Version 1 Length byte at
# all) -- decoded as RST-shaped with no trailer.

# 25-28) Out-of-scope/unrecognized LLC traffic that must not crash and must not be misreported as
# STP: SNAP-encapsulated Cisco PVST+, GARP (GVRP/GMRP, which collides with STP's own DSAP/SSAP and
# is disambiguated only by destination MAC), an unrelated LLC DSAP/SSAP pair, and a length-framed
