# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DeviceNet over SocketCAN (synthetic, tests/sample_devicenet.pcap) -- LINKTYPE_CAN_SOCKETCAN
# (227), this codebase's second wholly new link layer after STP's own classic-802.3-LLC work
# above, and a wholly SEPARATE one from Ethernet (no MAC addresses, no IP layer at all -- see
# can_socketcan.hpp/devicenet.hpp's own file header comments). No real public DeviceNet/CAN
# capture was found during this feature's own research (searched github.com/ITI/ICS-Security-
# Tools and general web search for "DeviceNet pcap"/"CAN capture" -- ICS-Security-Tools' own
# pcaps/README.md lists no CAN-bus or DeviceNet capture of any kind among its protocol-organized
# captures, and no other public source turned one up either) -- synthetic-only, matching several
# other protocols already in this codebase (e.g. FOUNDATION Fieldbus HSE, per ffhse.hpp). Packet
# numbers in comments below match build_devicenet_sample()'s own numbered comments 1-33 in
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1-4) Group 1: all four named message types, with Source MAC ID extraction (id & 0x003F) and
# I/O data shown as raw byte count only (never further decoded).
add_test(NAME devicenet_group1_multicast_poll_response_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_devicenet.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(devicenet_group1_multicast_poll_response_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  .*\\[devicenet\\]  DeviceNet Group 1 \\(Slave's I/O Multicast Poll Response\\): SrcMAC=5 CAN ID=0x0305 I/O data=4 byte\\(s\\) \\(not decoded further\\)")

add_test(NAME devicenet_group1_change_of_state_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_devicenet.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(devicenet_group1_change_of_state_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2  .*DeviceNet Group 1 \\(Slave's I/O Change of State or Cyclic Message\\): SrcMAC=12 CAN ID=0x034C")

# LINKTYPE_CAN_SOCKETCAN branch), a LEGITIMATE J1939 frame in Auto mode -- so devicenet_eff_frame_
# rejected below pins --protocol devicenet explicitly, to keep testing DeviceNet's OWN EFF
# rejection in isolation from J1939's own opportunistic Auto-mode claim on the exact same bytes;
# devicenet_eff_frame_decodes_as_j1939_in_auto_mode right after it is the positive proof that Auto
# mode's own new behavior for this frame is exactly what canopen.hpp/j1939.hpp's own dispatch
# analysis says it should be.

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol devicenet --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_devicenet.pcap" --format text)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#28  .*\\[non-ip\\]  CAN frame, id=0x1ABCDEF \\[EFF -- extended 29-bit id\\] \\(not decoded -- J1939 decoding disabled by --protocol\\)")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#28  .*\\[j1939\\]  J1939 PGN 109312 Priority=0 SA=239 DA=205")

# --protocol devicenet: an ordinary Ethernet-linktype capture (sample_stp.pcap) is completely
# unaffected -- DeviceNet dispatch is gated on link_type == LINKTYPE_CAN_SOCKETCAN, checked
# BEFORE any protocol filter, so restricting to --protocol devicenet on a non-CAN capture simply
# means nothing in it is recognized as any protocol at all (every packet still decodes at the
# link layer, just with no application-layer match) -- confirms no accidental cross-link-type
# leakage either way.
add_test(NAME devicenet_protocol_filter_still_decodes_on_can_capture
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol devicenet --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_devicenet.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(devicenet_protocol_filter_still_decodes_on_can_capture PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  .*\\[devicenet\\]  DeviceNet Group 1")

add_test(NAME devicenet_protocol_filter_excludes_other_protocols_on_can_capture
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol modbus --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_devicenet.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(devicenet_protocol_filter_excludes_other_protocols_on_can_capture PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  .*\\[non-ip\\]  CAN frame, id=0x305 \\(not decoded -- DeviceNet decoding disabled by --protocol\\)")

add_test(NAME devicenet_protocol_filter_does_not_affect_ethernet_capture
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol devicenet --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_stp.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(devicenet_protocol_filter_does_not_affect_ethernet_capture PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[devicenet\\]")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CANopen (CiA 301) and SAE J1939 over SocketCAN (synthetic, combined fixture,
# tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap) -- LINKTYPE_CAN_SOCKETCAN 227, same link type as DeviceNet
# above. See can_socketcan.hpp/canopen.hpp/j1939.hpp's own file header comments for the wire
# formats and, above all, canopen.hpp's own "THE DEVICENET-VS-CANOPEN DISPATCH COLLISION" section
# for why CANopen requires an explicit --protocol canopen and never joins ProtocolFilter::Auto,
# while J1939 (a structurally disjoint, EFF-gated space) DOES join Auto right alongside DeviceNet.
# Packet numbers below match build_canopen_j1939_sample()'s own numbered comments 1-36 in
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py. All PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION text below was verified against this
# decoder's own actual output (text/json/stats, all three of --protocol canopen/j1939/devicenet
# and the plain Auto default) before being written here, per this task's own mandatory
# manually-run-and-read-real-output-first requirement.

# --------- THE DISPATCH-COLLISION PROOF (packet 1: COB-ID 0x0000, decodable 3 different ways) ----
# Packet 1 is DELIBERATELY dual-shaped: a valid CANopen NMT "Start remote node" AND a valid
# DeviceNet Group 1 "Other Group 1 Message" on the exact same bytes (see the fixture's own comment).

# (a) Auto default (no --protocol): DeviceNet wins, exactly as canopen.hpp's own header comment
# says it must -- CANopen is NOT part of Auto, so on a shared-ID-space frame like this one Auto
# mode's own opportunistic DeviceNet attempt claims it first, silently, with no ambiguity warning
# (matching how every other GateKind::LinkType collision in this codebase resolves: whichever
# decoder is tried first in the Auto ordering wins, since there is no separate "ambiguous" state).
add_test(NAME canopen_devicenet_collision_auto_mode_prefers_devicenet
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(canopen_devicenet_collision_auto_mode_prefers_devicenet PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  .*\\[devicenet\\]  DeviceNet Group 1 \\(Other Group 1 Message\\): SrcMAC=0 CAN ID=0x0000")

# (b) --protocol devicenet: same DeviceNet decode, now explicit rather than incidental.
add_test(NAME canopen_devicenet_collision_explicit_devicenet_filter
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol devicenet --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(canopen_devicenet_collision_explicit_devicenet_filter PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  .*\\[devicenet\\]  DeviceNet Group 1 \\(Other Group 1 Message\\): SrcMAC=0 CAN ID=0x0000")

# (c) --protocol canopen: ONLY under this explicit filter does the exact same bytes decode as
# CANopen instead -- the positive proof that the documented dispatch policy actually behaves the
# way canopen.hpp/decoder.cpp's own comments say it does.
add_test(NAME canopen_devicenet_collision_explicit_canopen_filter_reaches_canopen
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol canopen --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(canopen_devicenet_collision_explicit_canopen_filter_reaches_canopen PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  .*\\[canopen\\]  CANopen NMT \\(COB-ID=0x0000 FC=0x0000 Node=0\\): Start remote node \\[Node 5\\]")

# --------------------------------------- CANopen: NMT ----------------------------------------

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol canopen --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(canopen_nmt_start_remote_node_targeted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  .*\\[canopen\\]  CANopen NMT \\(COB-ID=0x0000 FC=0x0000 Node=0\\): Start remote node \\[Node 5\\]")

add_test(NAME canopen_heartbeat_pre_operational_state

# ERR/RTR rejection: proves CANopen rejects both exactly the way DeviceNet does (its own reference
# dissector's very first check), and that under --protocol canopen the fallback wording correctly
# names BOTH protocols as rejecting the frame shape (distinguishing this from the --protocol
# devicenet-only wording tested above in the DeviceNet section, which names DeviceNet alone).

# --------------------------------------- CANopen: --protocol -------------------------------------
# `--protocol canopen` can't become `info` here: Auto mode (info has no --protocol of its own)
# labels this fixture's CAN frames "devicenet", not "canopen" (see the devicenet/canopen ambiguity
# this decoder resolves via --protocol, canopen.hpp) -- only an explicit `--protocol canopen`
# relabels and decodes them as CANopen, exactly what this test needs to exist at all. With
# --stats gone from decode (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md ROADMAP item 105), this now asserts directly
# against decode's own per-packet text output instead of the old aggregate message-type
# breakdown -- arguably more direct: it confirms CANopen frames actually decode as CANopen AND
# that this fixture's J1939 frames are correctly excluded ("not decoded -- J1939 decoding
# disabled by --protocol"), which --protocol canopen's whole point is.
#
# Deliberately a single, un-skip-grouped literal per test (matching every OTHER --protocol
# canopen test on this same fixture just above/below, none of which use "(.*\n)*"), not one
# combined regex spanning from packet #1 to packet #27 via "(.*\n)*" -- an earlier version of
# this test tried that and it hung ctest itself (not the test binary, which exits fine): CMake's
# own backtracking regex engine blows up catastrophically on a multi-line skip-group when, as
# here, the literal on either side of it also recurs elsewhere in the ~38-line output (e.g.
# "CANopen NMT" appears on both #1 and #2, "id=0xCF00400" on #27/#33/#36), multiplying the
# number of backtracking paths it tries -- confirmed by reproducing the hang and then removing it.
add_test(NAME canopen_stats_message_type_breakdown
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol canopen --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap")
set_tests_properties(canopen_stats_message_type_breakdown PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[canopen\\]  CANopen NMT \\(COB-ID=0x0000 FC=0x0000 Node=0\\): Start remote node \\[Node 5\\]")

add_test(NAME canopen_protocol_filter_excludes_j1939
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol canopen --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap")
set_tests_properties(canopen_protocol_filter_excludes_j1939 PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[non-ip\\]  CAN frame, id=0xCF00400 \\[EFF -- extended 29-bit id\\] \\(not decoded -- J1939 decoding disabled by --protocol\\)")

# ============================================= J1939 =============================================
# All J1939 IDs are EFF (Extended, 29-bit) -- see j1939.hpp's own file header comment for why this
# makes J1939 a structurally disjoint gate from DeviceNet/CANopen's shared standard-ID space, and
# hence safe to include in ProtocolFilter::Auto (tested without --protocol below; the explicit
# --protocol j1939/devicenet/canopen variations are tested separately where they add coverage).

add_test(NAME j1939_eec1_broadcast_decoded_in_auto_mode
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(j1939_eec1_broadcast_decoded_in_auto_mode PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#27  .*\\[j1939\\]  J1939 PGN 61444 \\(EEC1\\) Priority=3 SA=0 \\(Engine #1\\) \\(broadcast\\) EngineSpeed=1500rpm ActualTorque=40%")

add_test(NAME j1939_et1_decoded

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol j1939 --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap")

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 32,[^\n]*\"j1939_dm1_dtcs\"")

# RTR tolerance: J1939 UNIQUELY tolerates an RTR-flagged frame (unlike DeviceNet/CANopen, which
# both reject RTR outright) -- see j1939.hpp's own "ONE FURTHER DIFFERENCE" paragraph.

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --protocol j1939 --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap" --format text)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#33  .*\\[j1939\\]  J1939 PGN 61444 \\(EEC1\\) Priority=3 SA=0 \\(Engine #1\\) \\(broadcast\\) \\[RTR -- no payload\\]")

# Negative control: EFF AND ERR both set -- ERR always wins, even though EFF is present.
add_test(NAME j1939_eff_and_err_both_set_rejected

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#34  .*\\[non-ip\\]  CAN frame, id=0xCF00400 \\[EFF -- extended 29-bit id\\] \\[ERR -- error frame\\] \\(not a valid J1939 frame shape\\)")

# Truncated payload: EEC1-shaped id but too few bytes actually captured -- clamped, and EEC1's own

# --protocol canopen must NOT reach any J1939 frame (structurally disjoint on EFF, but still worth

# --------------------------------------- J1939: info ---------------------------------------------
# CRITICALLY includes the "never buried" DM1 active-DTC headline count, matching the task's own
# explicit ask (same treatment as IPMI's own Cipher-Suite-0 headline finding). Unlike the CANopen
# test just above, `--protocol j1939` isn't needed here to get this content -- Auto mode (`info`
# has no --protocol of its own) already recognizes this fixture's J1939 frames as j1939 by
# structural signature alone (see j1939.hpp's own file header comment on why J1939's all-EFF ID
# space is structurally disjoint from DeviceNet/CANopen's, and so safe under Auto) -- so `info`
# reproduces this section identically, confirmed against this build's actual output.
add_test(NAME j1939_stats_pgn_counts_and_dm1_headline
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap")
set_tests_properties(j1939_stats_pgn_counts_and_dm1_headline PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "j1939 pgn counts:\n *59904 \\(Request\\) +1\n *61444 \\(EEC1\\) +3\n *65226 \\(DM1\\) +2\n *65262 \\(ET1\\) +1\n *65265 \\(CCVS\\) +1\n *65535 +1\n\\*\\*\\* J1939 DM1 active diagnostic trouble codes observed: 2 \\*\\*\\*")

# Auto-mode combined stats: both devicenet AND j1939 breakdowns appear together (CANopen's own
# breakdown does NOT, since it never joins Auto) -- the same collision-resolution policy visible
# in --stats form, not just per-packet text.
add_test(NAME canopen_j1939_auto_mode_stats_shows_devicenet_and_j1939_not_canopen
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_canopen_j1939.pcap")
set_tests_properties(canopen_j1939_auto_mode_stats_shows_devicenet_and_j1939_not_canopen PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "devicenet message groups:.*j1939 pgn counts:")
set_tests_properties(canopen_j1939_auto_mode_stats_shows_devicenet_and_j1939_not_canopen PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "canopen function-code/message types:")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# BACnet/IP (synthetic, tests/sample_bacnet.pcap): BVLC framing, NPDU network layer, APDU
# application layer/services over UDP port 47808 -- see tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_bacnet_sample for the exact byte layout each assertion below is checking (packet numbers
# in comments match that function's own numbered comments 1-53), and bacnet.hpp's file header
# comment for the decoder itself. Unlike EtherCAT/GOOSE/SV/PROFINET, BACnet/IP rides over UDP, so
# detection is a payload-shape gate (BVLC Type 0x81 + Function 0x00-0x0C) applied port-
# independently, mirroring CIP I/O's own opportunistic detection.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1-2) Who-Is, unrestricted and with a device-instance range.
add_test(NAME bacnet_who_is_unrestricted_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(bacnet_who_is_unrestricted_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[bacnet\\]  BVLC Original-Broadcast-NPDU Unconfirmed-Request who-Is\n")

add_test(NAME bacnet_who_is_with_range_decoded_in_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet.pcap")
set_tests_properties(bacnet_who_is_with_range_decoded_in_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"bacnet_service_name\": \"who-Is\".*\"bacnet_values\": \\[\"device-instance-range-low=100\", \"device-instance-range-high=200\"\\]")

# DLEN/DADR themselves (6-byte MAC vs. DLEN=0 broadcast-on-destination-network) aren't promoted to
# DecodedPacket/JSON -- npdu.dadr_hex only ever reaches the (currently unused-in-JSON) NPDU struct
# field -- so packets #30 and #31 (ordinary 6-byte DADR vs. DLEN=0 broadcast) are only
# distinguishable from each other via full-frame internals this decoder doesn't yet surface; both
# still decode as ordinary DEST-present NPDUs with no notes, which this asserts by requiring the
# dnet=5 shape to appear twice.

set_tests_properties(bacnet_npdu_dest_present_both_dadr_shapes_decoded PROPERTIES

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"bacnet_npdu_has_src\": true,.*\"bacnet_npdu_snet\": 7,.*\"device-object=device,999\"")

# 62-68) Cross-packet APDU segmentation reassembly (see bacnet.hpp's "Cross-packet segment
# reassembly" section and reassemble_bacnet_apdu_segment in bacnet.cpp). Three fixture scenarios,
# each spanning its own invoke-id so they can't cross-contaminate each other's reassembly state:
#   - invoke-id=60 (packets 62-63): a 2-segment Confirmed-Request ReadPropertyMultiple that
#     completes cleanly and gets the exact same value-decode a non-segmented request would.
#   - invoke-id=61 (packets 64-66): a 3-segment Complex-ACK ReadPropertyMultiple that completes
#     and, because its reassembled data is a Device-object identity read, still gets the
#     device-identity correlation promoted onto the summary/JSON fields.
#   - invoke-id=62 (packets 67-68): a sequence-number gap (segment jumps straight to
#     sequence-number 2 without an intervening 1) that must be honestly abandoned rather than
#     silently reassembled wrong -- the segment's own raw hex is all that's shown.
add_test(NAME bacnet_segment_reassembly_first_segment_in_progress_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(bacnet_segment_reassembly_first_segment_in_progress_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "invoke-id=60 readPropertyMultiple\n *note: segmented APDU:[^\n]*\n *note: continuing a segmented BACnet APDU reassembly for this \\(flow, invoke-id\\) \\(sequence-number 0\\): 9 service-data byte\\(s\\) buffered across 1 segment\\(s\\) so far, still waiting for more-follows=0")

add_test(NAME bacnet_segment_reassembly_confirmed_request_completes_and_decodes
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(bacnet_segment_reassembly_confirmed_request_completes_and_decodes PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "invoke-id=60 readPropertyMultiple \\[read-access-spec\\[0\\]-object=device,1234 \\+5 more\\]\n *note: segmented APDU:[^\n]*\n *note: completed a 2-segment BACnet APDU reassembled across separate UDP datagrams \\(18 service-data byte\\(s\\) total\\)")

add_test(NAME bacnet_segment_reassembly_complex_ack_completes_with_device_identity
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(bacnet_segment_reassembly_complex_ack_completes_with_device_identity PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "invoke-id=61 readPropertyMultiple \\[read-access-result\\[0\\]-object=device,1234 \\+10 more\\] device-identity\\(vendor=Acme Controls model=Widget 9000 firmware=3\\.2\\.1 app-sw-version=App 1\\.0\\.0 serial=SN-00012345\\)\n *note: segmented APDU:[^\n]*\n *note: completed a 3-segment BACnet APDU reassembled across separate UDP datagrams \\(92 service-data byte\\(s\\) total\\)")

add_test(NAME bacnet_segment_reassembly_sequence_gap_abandons_and_stays_raw
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(bacnet_segment_reassembly_sequence_gap_abandons_and_stays_raw PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "invoke-id=62 readPropertyMultiple\n *note: segmented APDU:[^\n]*\n *note: segmented BACnet APDU \\(sequence-number 2\\) does not continue the in-progress reassembly for this \\(flow, invoke-id\\) as expected \\(expected sequence-number 1, same PDU type/service-choice\\) -- discarding 4 already-buffered byte\\(s\\) and abandoning this reassembly\; service data not reassembled, shown above as this segment's own raw hex only")

# Security audit follow-up (docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch257.md's own "4.
# OT-specific security risks", item 3, "Protocol reassembly"): a DUPLICATE segment sequence-
# number (the second segment repeats sequence-number 0 instead of advancing to 1) rather than a
# sequence GAP -- its own dedicated fixture (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_bacnet_reassembly_adversarial_sample) since sample_bacnet.pcap itself feeds several
# exact-count tests a new exchange would perturb. Falls into the same abandon-on-any-anomaly path
# as the sequence-gap case above (bacnet.cpp's reassembly check doesn't special-case "repeats the
# last sequence-number" from "skips ahead" -- both simply aren't "the expected next
# sequence-number"), proving a replayed/duplicated segment can never silently re-merge into, or
# manufacture, a complete command either.
add_test(NAME bacnet_segment_reassembly_duplicate_sequence_discarded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet_reassembly_adversarial.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(bacnet_segment_reassembly_duplicate_sequence_discarded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "segmented BACnet APDU \\(sequence-number 0\\) does not continue the in-progress reassembly for this \\(flow, invoke-id\\) as expected \\(expected sequence-number 1, same PDU type/service-choice\\) -- discarding 4 already-buffered byte\\(s\\) and abandoning this reassembly\; service data not reassembled, shown above as this segment's own raw hex only")

# JSON mirror: bacnet_reassembly_completed/bacnet_reassembly_segment_count only ever appear on a

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HART-IP (synthetic, tests/sample_hartip.pcap): 8-byte fixed header, Session
# Initiate/Close/Keep Alive/Pass-Through message bodies, the full per-command
# value-decode dispatch table, packed-ASCII and HART-timestamp decoding, and
# the documented, deliberately-unresolved TCP Session-Initiate-vs-Modbus/TCP
# detection collision. See tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_hartip_sample
# for the exact byte layout each assertion below is checking (packet numbers
# in comments match that function's own numbered comments 1-63), and
# hartip.hpp's file header comment for the structural detection gate and the
# known collision's full explanation. JSON is pretty-printed one field per
# line, so assertions below join fields with ".*" (CMake's regex "." matches
# newlines) except where a field (e.g. hartip_values, notes) is itself a
# single-line JSON array.

add_test(NAME hartip_cmd1_request_and_response_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(hartip_cmd1_request_and_response_decoded PROPERTIES
  # "notes": [] followed by the closing "}," anchors this as the end of the *first* packet object
  # (Command 1 request) so the greedy .* that follows can't jump ahead into some later packet's
  # own "hartip_values" instead -- since -t/--time-format's own `time` field (time_format.hpp) now
  # renders directly after "notes", followed in turn by direction_source/direction_client_ip and
  # decode's own --detect-highlight fields (has_detect_finding/detect_finding_kind/
  # detect_finding_technique/detect_finding_description -- see output.cpp's JsonWriter and
  # docs/MANUAL.md's ROADMAP item 19), that anchor has to match through all seven.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"hartip_command\": 1,.*\"hartip_command_name\": \"Read Primary Variable\",.*\"notes\": \\[\\],\n *\"time\": \"[^\"]*\",\n *\"direction_source\":[^\n]*\n *\"direction_client_ip\":[^\n]*\n *\"has_detect_finding\":[^\n]*\n *\"detect_finding_kind\":[^\n]*\n *\"detect_finding_technique\":[^\n]*\n *\"detect_finding_description\":[^\n]*\n *\\},.*\"hartip_values\": \\[\"pv-units=1\", \"pv=72.500000\"\\]")

# The HART Data-Link (longitudinal/XOR) checksum: computed across Delimiter..Data inclusive and
# compared against the wire's own trailing Checksum byte -- see hartip.hpp's file header comment's
# Checksum entry and HartIpPassThrough::checksum_valid's own doc comment. A dedicated fixture
# (tests/sample_hartip_checksum.pcap, 2 packets) rather than sample_hartip.pcap itself, since every
# Pass-Through packet in that larger, widely-shared fixture now carries a genuinely correct
# checksum (fixed as part of adding this verification -- previously an unverified placeholder byte)
# and deliberately corrupting one there would perturb several existing "notes": [] assertions
# elsewhere in this file.
add_test(NAME hartip_checksum_valid_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip_checksum.pcap")
set_tests_properties(hartip_checksum_valid_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"hartip_command\": 1,.*\"hartip_command_name\": \"Read Primary Variable\",.*\"hartip_checksum\": 4,.*\"hartip_checksum_valid\": true,.*\"notes\": \\[\\]")

add_test(NAME hartip_checksum_mismatch_noted_and_invalid_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip_checksum.pcap")
set_tests_properties(hartip_checksum_mismatch_noted_and_invalid_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"hartip_command\": 1,.*\"hartip_response_code\": 0,.*\"hartip_checksum\": 42,.*\"hartip_checksum_valid\": false,.*\"notes\": \\[\"longitudinal \\(XOR\\) checksum mismatch: calculated 0xD5, frame declares 0x2A\"\\]")

add_test(NAME hartip_checksum_mismatch_noted_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip_checksum.pcap" --verbose)
set_tests_properties(hartip_checksum_mismatch_noted_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[hartip\\]  Response Pass Through ACK command=1 \\(Read Primary Variable\\) response-code=0 \\(Success\\) \\[pv-units=1 \\+1 more\\]\n *note: longitudinal \\(XOR\\) checksum mismatch: calculated 0xD5, frame declares 0x2A")

add_test(NAME hartip_checksum_valid_does_not_note_anything_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --ether --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip_checksum.pcap")
set_tests_properties(hartip_checksum_valid_does_not_note_anything_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[hartip\\]  Request Pass Through STX command=1 \\(Read Primary Variable\\)\n *eth "

# The documented, deliberately-unresolved limitation: a HART-IP Session Initiate message's own
# header (MessageID 0, Status 0) reads as a plausible Modbus/TCP MBAP header, so on TCP it is
# misclassified as Modbus/TCP "buffering, waiting for more" bytes that never arrive -- see
# hartip.hpp's "KNOWN, ACCEPTED, DOCUMENTED LIMITATION" paragraph and decoder.cpp's matching
# comments on both the declared-length chain and the TCP dispatch chain for the full explanation
# and why reordering HART-IP ahead of Modbus was tried and rejected (it regressed this project's
# own Modbus/S7comm test corpus). These three packets (a genuine Session Initiate request,
# response, and the start of a coalesced Keep Alive) are never decoded as hartip on this flow.
add_test(NAME hartip_modbus_collision_known_limitation
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(hartip_modbus_collision_known_limitation PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "52010->5094: 13 of 106 declared byte\\(s\\) seen so far across 1 segment\\(s\\) on this flow, waiting for more[^\n]*\n.*5094->52010: 13 of 106 declared byte\\(s\\) seen so far across 1 segment\\(s\\) on this flow, waiting for more[^\n]*\n.*52010->5094: 29 of 106 declared byte\\(s\\) seen so far across 2 segment\\(s\\) on this flow, waiting for more")

add_test(NAME hartip_modbus_collision_never_reports_hartip_protocol
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(hartip_modbus_collision_never_reports_hartip_protocol PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"src_port\": 52010,\n *\"dst_port\": 5094,\n *\"tcp_flags\": \"ACK,PSH\",\n *\"protocol\": \"tcp\",")

add_test(NAME hartip_tcp_pass_through_non_standard_port_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(hartip_tcp_pass_through_non_standard_port_decoded PROPERTIES

add_test(NAME hartip_stats_counted
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(hartip_stats_counted PROPERTIES
  # tcp is 4, not 3: packet #68's own fabricated TLS Application Data record (see
  # hartip_tls_record_not_misdetected_as_hartip below) correctly falls through to the generic
  # "tcp" fallback instead of being claimed by HART-IP's own weak declared-length gate.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packets: +68[^\n]*\n[^\n]*\nprotocols:\n *hartip +62\n *tcp +4\n *udp +2.*\nhartip message types:\n *Error +3\n *NAK +1\n *Request +17\n *Response +41\nhartip pass-through commands:\n")

# Regression test for a real, systematic (not occasional) collision found against a user's own
# live capture -- see hartip.cpp's own looks_like_tls_record_header and hartip.hpp's updated
# header comment. Every TLS/SSL record's own ProtocolVersion field (major byte always 0x03, minor
# byte always 0-3) satisfies HART-IP's weak MessageType/MessageID gate, so EVERY TLS record --
# not just an occasional coincidental one, unlike the Modbus/TCP collision below -- used to get
# claimed by HART-IP's own TCP reassembly and left "buffering, waiting for more" forever, since a
# real TLS record's own Length field almost never matches what HART-IP interprets as its
# MsgLength. Packet #68 is deliberately on a non-443, non-HART-IP port pair (55055/55056) to prove
# this is a content-based exclusion, not a port carve-out.
add_test(NAME hartip_tls_record_not_misdetected_as_hartip
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(hartip_tls_record_not_misdetected_as_hartip PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:55055 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:55056  \\[tcp\\]  TCP payload of 261 byte\\(s\\) on port 55055->55056"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[hartip\\][^\n]*\n *note: [^\n]*55055|buffering a HART-IP message PDU/frame split across TCP segments 55055->55056")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Real-world HART-IP capture -- see tests/real_captures/hartip/ATTRIBUTION.md for provenance: a
# genuine 116-frame, 72-second capture (automayt/ICS-pcap, fetched via GitHub's LFS media CDN)
# of a WirelessHART gateway ("wihartgw") running the same command sequence over both UDP and TCP.
# Independently cross-validated against tshark's own HART-IP dissector (see ATTRIBUTION.md) and,
# notably, this capture reproduces the documented TCP Modbus-collision limitation on genuine field
# traffic, plus a second, previously-undocumented weak-gate false-positive pattern against
# unrelated background TCP traffic -- see ATTRIBUTION.md's own two dedicated sections for both.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME real_hartip_does_not_crash
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/hartip/hart_ip.pcapng" --format json)

add_test(NAME real_hartip_stats_summary
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/hartip/hart_ip.pcapng")
set_tests_properties(real_hartip_stats_summary PROPERTIES
  # This capture's one non-TCP/non-modbus/non-hartip packet is a genuine ICMP Destination
  # Unreachable -- previously shown only as an opaque "non-tcp" count before try_parse_icmp
  # existed (see icmp.hpp/icmp.cpp); now decoded and broken out as its own "icmp" protocol line
  # plus an "icmp types:" breakdown, confirmed against this real capture.
  # tcp is 61, not 63: one of this capture's background TCP connections (port 445) is genuine SMB1
  # traffic, now correctly recognized and decoded as "smb" by smb.hpp -- see
  # real_hartip_smb_traffic_now_correctly_decoded below and ATTRIBUTION.md's own updated note; a
  # second background connection (port 443) is genuine HTTPS/TLS, now correctly recognized and
  # decoded as "https" instead of getting stuck in HART-IP's own weak-gate false-positive
  # reassembly loop forever -- see real_hartip_tls_weak_gate_false_positive_fixed below (the TLS
  # record header's own ProtocolVersion field systematically, not coincidentally, satisfies HART-
  # IP's declared-length gate, since every TLS record's major version byte is 0x03 and minor byte
  # is 0-3 -- hartip.cpp's own looks_like_tls_record_header now excludes it outright).
  # arp is 4, not "non-ip" 4: this capture's four non-IPv4 Ethernet frames are genuine ARP traffic
  # (OPER a recognized opcode) -- previously shown only as an opaque "non-ip" count before
  # try_parse_arp existed (see arp.hpp/arp.cpp), now decoded and broken out as its own "arp"
  # protocol line, the same "real feature, real capture, count moves from the generic fallback to
  # the new specific protocol" pattern the icmp/smb notes above already document.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packets: +116[^\n]*\n[^\n]*\nprotocols:\n *arp +4\n *hartip +46\n *https +1\n *icmp +1\n *modbus +2\n *smb +1\n *tcp +61\n.*hartip message types:\n *Request +23\n *Response +23\nhartip pass-through commands:\n.*icmp types:\n *Destination Unreachable +1")

# The documented TCP Session-Initiate-vs-Modbus/TCP collision (see hartip.hpp's "KNOWN, ACCEPTED,
# DOCUMENTED LIMITATION" paragraph, decoder.cpp's matching comments, and tests/sample_hartip.pcap's
# own packets 58-60) reproduced on genuine field traffic: this real TCP session's own Session
# Initiate request and response both get misclassified as Modbus/TCP, exactly as documented.
add_test(NAME real_hartip_modbus_collision_confirmed_on_real_traffic
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/hartip/hart_ip.pcapng" --format text)
set_tests_properties(real_hartip_modbus_collision_confirmed_on_real_traffic PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.0.101:49559 -> 192.168.0.10:5094 \\(hart-ip\\)  \\[modbus\\]  Unknown \\(0xd\\): Unknown \\(0xd\\)[^\n]*\n.*192.168.0.10:5094 \\(hart-ip\\) -> 192.168.0.101:49559  \\[modbus\\]  Unknown \\(0xd\\): Unknown \\(0xd\\)")

# FIXED (see ATTRIBUTION.md, and hartip.cpp's own looks_like_tls_record_header): the weak
# declared-length gate used to false-positive against unrelated background TCP traffic having
# nothing to do with HART-IP (a TLS connection elsewhere in this same real capture, port 443) --
# real-world confirmation, beyond the Modbus collision above, that hartip.hpp's own "structural
# detection gate is genuinely weak" paragraph was not overstated. This one, unlike the Modbus
# collision above (a real but occasional single-shape overlap, still accepted as a known
# limitation), turned out to be a SYSTEMATIC collision -- every TLS record's own ProtocolVersion
# field (major byte always 0x03, minor byte always 0-3 for every deployed SSLv3/TLS1.0-1.3
# record) satisfies HART-IP's own MessageType/MessageID gate essentially every time, not
# occasionally -- confirmed independently against a second real capture reported directly by a
# user (ordinary HTTPS traffic to two unrelated destinations both buffering indefinitely,
# "832 of 50656 declared byte(s)..."), which is what prompted the fix. Reported this capture's own
# port-443 connection used to get stuck in HART-IP's reassembly loop the exact same way; now
# correctly recognized and decoded as "https" instead (a genuinely reachable steady state, not
# just "buffering, waiting for more" forever). This capture's OTHER background connection (port
# 445) used to be a second instance of this same false positive too -- see
# real_hartip_smb_traffic_now_correctly_decoded below for why that one was already resolved a
# different way (smb.hpp's own decoder is tried earlier in decoder.cpp's cascade and correctly
# claims it, dispatch-ordering rather than a structural exclusion).
add_test(NAME real_hartip_tls_weak_gate_false_positive_fixed
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/hartip/hart_ip.pcapng" --format text)
set_tests_properties(real_hartip_tls_weak_gate_false_positive_fixed PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.0\\.100:50322 -> 74\\.125\\.159\\.99:443 \\(https\\)  \\[https\\]  HTTPS/TLS"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "50322->443: [0-9]+ of [0-9]+ declared byte\\(s\\) seen so far")

# AD suite phase 3 (smb.hpp): this same capture's port-445 background connection -- previously ALSO
# a HART-IP weak-gate false positive (see above) -- is genuine SMB1 (CIFS) traffic, and is now
# correctly recognized and decoded as such, curated note 1 included, since smb.hpp's own decoder
# runs earlier in decoder.cpp's TCP-port-independent cascade than HART-IP's own weak declared-length
# probe. A real-world confirmation of both this decoder's own detection gate AND of the general
# "a stronger, earlier gate resolves a weaker, later one's false positive" pattern this codebase
# already relies on elsewhere (e.g. IEC104-before-Modbus).
add_test(NAME real_hartip_smb_traffic_now_correctly_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/hartip/hart_ip.pcapng" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(real_hartip_smb_traffic_now_correctly_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "49343 -> 192.168.0.101:445 \\(microsoft-ds\\)  \\[smb\\]  SMB1 \\(CIFS\\) message[^\n]*\n *note: SMB1 \\(CIFS\\) traffic observed on this session")

# OPC UA Binary (synthetic, tests/sample_opcua.pcap): the UA-TCP connection-protocol handshake
# (Hello/Acknowledge/Error/ReverseHello), a full OpenSecureChannel/CloseSecureChannel round trip
# with SecurityPolicyUri "...#None", the GetEndpoints/FindServers discovery services, a
# CreateSession/ActivateSession/CloseSession lifecycle (including both an Anonymous and a
# cleartext-UserName/Password ActivateSession -- the latter deliberately exercising the
# "SECURITY FINDING" credential-exposure note), a Tier-2 (header-decoded, body-raw-hex) Read
# request/response pair, an entirely unrecognized service TypeId, a non-'F' chunk, a
# structurally-invalid NodeId shape (the inner try/catch regression case), a genuinely truncated
# capture (TCP-reassembly "buffering, waiting for more" path), port-independence, and coalesced
# messages. See tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_opcua_sample docstring for the full packet-by-
# packet rationale, and opcua.hpp's file header comment for the wire format each packet below
# exercises (cross-checked against the OPC Foundation's own Part4/Part6 reference documentation,
# its own published NodeIds.csv/StatusCode.csv, and python-opcua's own generated bindings -- see
# opcua.hpp's own "Sourcing" paragraph). Like every other synthetic fixture's own test block in
# this file, JSON field assertions below join adjacent fields with ".*" rather than a literal
# ", " -- this project's pretty-printed JSON puts one field per line, and CMake's own regex engine
# lets "." match newlines, so a literal ", " would never match across a line break.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # reassembly.

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_opcua.pcap")

  # A 'C' chunk begins a reassembly, then a DIFFERENT message's 'F' chunk (different
  # SecureChannelId) arrives on the same flow before any continuation -- the first is abandoned
  # (noted) and the second decodes normally on its own.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"Message channel=800002 token=6 ReadRequest\",.*\"opcua_service_name\": \"ReadRequest\",.*\"notes\": \\[\"an OPC UA chunk for a different message arrived on this TCP flow while a previous multi-chunk reassembly was still in progress \\(4 byte\\(s\\) buffered across 1 chunk\\(s\\)\\) -- the earlier, incomplete message is abandoned\"\\]")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Real-world OPC UA capture -- see tests/real_captures/opcua/ATTRIBUTION.md for provenance: two
# back-to-back OPC UA Binary (UA-TCP/Secure Conversation) sessions from Wireshark Bug 3986's own
# attachment (a 2009 dissector-freeze reproduction capture, an OPC UA conformance/fuzz-test tool
# -- Achilles Satellite -- against a reference "StackTestServer" implementation). Independently
# cross-validated against tshark's own OPC UA dissector (which needs an explicit "Decode As", since
# this capture uses non-standard TCP port 12001, not 4840 -- see ATTRIBUTION.md's own
# "Port-independent detection confirmed on real traffic" section for why that itself is a
# meaningful real-world result for this decoder's own port-independent detection gate).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME real_opcua_does_not_crash
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/opcua/opc-ua-ap-method-wireshark-freeze.pcap" --format json)

add_test(NAME real_opcua_stats_summary
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/opcua/opc-ua-ap-method-wireshark-freeze.pcap")
set_tests_properties(real_opcua_stats_summary PROPERTIES
  # Both sessions' CallRequest (TypeId 712) no longer appear under "opcua services" now that Call is
  # Tier 1: their own bodies are genuinely malformed (Achilles Satellite fuzz-test payloads -- see
  # ATTRIBUTION.md -- e.g. session 1's carries a method-id NodeId claiming a 262144-byte String with
  # only ~21 bytes actually left in the captured body), so decode_call_request_params's own bounds-
  # checked reads now correctly throw and this decoder honestly falls back to "not in this decoder's
  # dispatch table" for them, rather than the old Tier-2 behavior of labeling them "CallRequest"
  # without ever having attempted to parse their bodies at all -- see the tests below this one.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packets: +90[^\n]*\n[^\n]*\nprotocols:\n *opcua +24\n *tcp +66.*\nopcua message types:\n *Acknowledge +2\n *Error +2\n *Hello +2\n *Message +14\n *OpenSecureChannel +4\nopcua services:\n *ActivateSessionRequest +2\n *ActivateSessionResponse +2\n *CreateSessionRequest +2\n *CreateSessionResponse +2\n *GetEndpointsRequest +2\n *GetEndpointsResponse +2\n *OpenSecureChannelRequest +2\n *OpenSecureChannelResponse +2")

add_test(NAME real_opcua_port_independent_detection_on_nonstandard_port
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/opcua/opc-ua-ap-method-wireshark-freeze.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(real_opcua_port_independent_detection_on_nonstandard_port PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.41.176:58674 -> 192.168.41.212:12001  \\[opcua\\]  Hello protocol-version=0 receive-buffer-size=65535 send-buffer-size=65535 max-message-size=4000 max-chunk-count=0 endpoint-url=opc.tcp://vm-xp-steven:12001/UA/StackTestServer[^\n]*\n *note: seen on TCP port 58674->12001, which is not a configured/standard OPC UA port \\(4840\\)")

add_test(NAME real_opcua_call_request_first_session_body_rejected_as_malformed
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/opcua/opc-ua-ap-method-wireshark-freeze.pcap")
set_tests_properties(real_opcua_call_request_first_session_body_rejected_as_malformed PROPERTIES
  # This session's CallRequest (TypeId 712, reassembled from 4 TCP segments) is one of the Achilles
  # Satellite fuzz-test payloads this capture is built from (see ATTRIBUTION.md): its CallMethodRequest
  # array's own MethodId NodeId claims a String identifier 262144 bytes long with only ~21 bytes
  # actually present in the captured body. Now that Call is Tier 1, decode_call_request_params's
  # bounds-checked read_string throws, and this decoder correctly falls back to raw hex rather than
  # asserting a "CallRequest" label it was never able to verify -- see opcua.cpp's inner try/catch
  # around the service-body decode.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"Message channel=6495 token=1 \\(service type-id 712, ns=0 -- not in this decoder's dispatch table\\)\",.*\"opcua_message_size\": 5224,.*\"opcua_service_recognized\": false,.*\"opcua_service_type_id\": 712,.*\"opcua_body_shown_as_hex\": true,")

add_test(NAME real_opcua_call_request_second_session_body_rejected_as_malformed
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/opcua/opc-ua-ap-method-wireshark-freeze.pcap")
set_tests_properties(real_opcua_call_request_second_session_body_rejected_as_malformed PROPERTIES
  # This session's CallRequest carries a structurally-invalid MethodId NodeId encoding byte (shape
  # 0x07, outside the valid 0x00-0x05 range) -- the same real-world fuzz-test posture as the first
  # session above, just a different malformed field.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"Message channel=6496 token=1 \\(service type-id 712, ns=0 -- not in this decoder's dispatch table\\)\",.*\"opcua_message_size\": 110,.*\"opcua_service_recognized\": false,.*\"opcua_service_type_id\": 712,.*\"opcua_body_shown_as_hex\": true,")

add_test(NAME real_opcua_malformed_call_request_gets_error_not_response_first_session
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/opcua/opc-ua-ap-method-wireshark-freeze.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(real_opcua_malformed_call_request_gets_error_not_response_first_session PROPERTIES
  # ROADMAP item 146 (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md): 0x80020000 is now a named entry (BadInternalError) in
  # the widened 181-entry status_code_name table, where the old 20-entry table fell back to raw
  # severity+hex -- a real-world confirmation that the widened table actually gets exercised, not
  # just a synthetic-fixture claim.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[opcua\\]  Message channel=6495 token=1 \\(service type-id 712, ns=0 -- not in this decoder's dispatch table\\)[^\n]*\n.*\\[opcua\\]  Error error=BadInternalError reason=")

add_test(NAME real_opcua_malformed_call_request_gets_error_not_response_second_session
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/opcua/opc-ua-ap-method-wireshark-freeze.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(real_opcua_malformed_call_request_gets_error_not_response_second_session PROPERTIES
  # Same widened-table effect as the first session above -- 0x80070000 is now named
  # (BadDecodingError).
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[opcua\\]  Message channel=6496 token=1 \\(service type-id 712, ns=0 -- not in this decoder's dispatch table\\)[^\n]*\n.*\\[opcua\\]  Error error=BadDecodingError reason=")

add_test(NAME real_opcua_security_policy_none_both_sessions

# Real-world S7comm/COTP captures -- see tests/real_captures/s7comm/ATTRIBUTION.md
# for provenance. 14 from github.com/automayt/ICS-pcap's S7/ directory (good

# S7comm-Plus detection stub -- none of them turned out to contain real 0xB2
# traffic, see ATTRIBUTION.md for why), plus one file
# (s7comm_1200sym_real_polling.pcap) with different provenance: a small slice
# manually extracted from a much larger (140MB) real capture containing over
# a million real 0xB2 items, all decoding with zero fallbacks -- almost
# certainly the SAME real session already behind this project's original
# single-shape 0xB2 validation, not an independent new one (see
# ATTRIBUTION.md), but confirming that shape holds at full-session volume
# rather than just the handful of items originally spot-checked.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(S7COMM_REAL_CAPTURES
  s7comm_varservice_read_db1dbd0
  s7comm_varservice_cyclicdata_1s

  s7comm_varservice_libnodavedemo
  s7comm_1200sym_real_polling
)

    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/s7comm/${capture}.pcap" --format json)

add_test(NAME real_s7comm_read_db1dbd0_item_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/s7comm/s7comm_varservice_read_db1dbd0.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(real_s7comm_read_db1dbd0_item_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "item 0: DB1\\.DBB0")

# Real EOT-chaining evidence: this capture's PLC precedes almost every real Read Var response with
# a zero-byte EOT=0 "priming" COTP Data frame before the real EOT=1 frame -- see
# tests/real_captures/s7comm/ATTRIBUTION.md for how this shape was confirmed across every real
# S7comm capture checked for this project (content-free in all of them; a genuinely
# content-split real-world chain has yet to be seen -- see sample_s7comm_chaining.pcap for a
# synthetic one that does split real content). Decoder::reassemble_cotp_data_frame must
# transparently chain across it (0 buffered bytes + the real frame's own bytes = unchanged
# decoded content) rather than mishandling or crashing on it.
add_test(NAME real_s7comm_read_db1dbd0_eot_chaining_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/s7comm/s7comm_varservice_read_db1dbd0.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(real_s7comm_read_db1dbd0_eot_chaining_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "reassembled a COTP/S7comm message from 24 user-data byte\\(s\\) chained across 2 complete TPKT/COTP frames")

# The "opc_request_all_types" capture's name matches its content: a single 40-item
# GetMultiVariables request/response pair that walks nearly every S7comm-Plus datatype this
# decoder knows (Bool/USInt/Byte/Word/UDInt/UInt/DInt/DWord/Int/Timestamp/LInt/LReal/Timespan/
# ULInt/LWord/Real/SInt, plus USInt arrays) -- by far the richest real-world datatype coverage
# either capture provides, and the main reason to keep this file distinct from db3_var1_hmi
# rather than only testing one of the two.
add_test(NAME real_s7comm_plus_opc_all_types_getmultivar_40_items_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/s7comm/s7comm_plus_1511_opc_request_all_types.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(real_s7comm_plus_opc_all_types_getmultivar_40_items_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"Data: Response GetMultiVariables \\(seq=9\\) \\(40 value\\(s\\)\\)\",.*item=22: \\(Timestamp\\) = 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000.000.000Z.*item=24: \\(LReal\\) = 0.000000.*item=25: \\(Timespan\\) = 0 ns.*item=31: \\(USInt\\) Array\\[256\\]")

# Regression guard: neither real S7comm-Plus capture should ever produce a per-item decode
# error (S7CommPlusItemError) or a ParseError-triggered "decoding stopped" note -- both
# real files decode cleanly end to end with this implementation.
foreach(s7plus_capture s7comm_plus_1511_db3_var1_hmi s7comm_plus_1511_opc_request_all_types)
  add_test(NAME real_${s7plus_capture}_no_item_errors
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/s7comm/${s7plus_capture}.pcap" --format json)
  set_tests_properties(real_${s7plus_capture}_no_item_errors PROPERTIES
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "s7plus_item_errors|decoding stopped")
endforeach()

# Tier1/Tier2 split -- takeControl(19) is a real, named confirmedServiceRequest/Response

# Two complete MMS frames coalesced by the sender/OS into one TCP segment: cotp.cpp's own COTP/
# TPKT framing decodes only the first, with an honest note about the rest (see its own "possible
# pipelined TPKT frames" comment) -- this documents that known, already-labeled limitation for MMS
# specifically, matching what the same coalescing shape already does for every other single-PDU-
# per-call COTP-based protocol in this codebase.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Real-world IEC 61850 MMS captures -- see tests/real_captures/mms/ATTRIBUTION.md for provenance:
# three small captures from ITI/ICS-Security-Tools's own IEC61850/MMS pcap set (one full Session/
# Presentation/ACSE association plus a Read/conclude exchange with two genuinely malformed frames;
# two entirely-bare-MMS captures, takeControl/relinquishControl and cancelRequest), plus one much
# larger (224-frame) capture this project generated itself against a real, independent MMS stack
# (mz-automation/libiec61850) rather than against this decoder's own output -- see ATTRIBUTION.md's
# own "Independent-stack validation traffic" section. Two genuine structural-gate bugs (the
# Presentation layer's own fully-encoded-data tag being mistaken for a bogus third SPDU, and
# looks_like_bare_mms_pdu missing the 3 primitive MMSpdu alternatives) were found and fixed via
# this validation -- also documented in ATTRIBUTION.md, not just fixed silently.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(MMS_REAL_CAPTURES
  iec61850_read
  mms-takeControl
  mms-cancelRequest
  libiec61850_loopback_capture
)
foreach(capture ${MMS_REAL_CAPTURES})
  add_test(NAME real_mms_${capture}_does_not_crash
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/mms/${capture}.pcap" --format json)
endforeach()

# Sparkplug B (Eclipse Tahu), flows C/C5, port 63000/63005 -- hand-rolled protobuf decode of the

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"mqtt_topic\": \"spBv1.0/PlantA/NBIRTH/EdgeNode1\",.*\"mqtt_sparkplug_message_type\": \"NBIRTH\",.*\"mqtt_sparkplug_metrics\": \\[\"\\\\\"bdSeq\\\\\" type=UInt64 value=0\", \"\\\\\"Temperature\\\\\" type=Float value=21.500000 ts=2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z\", \"\\\\\"Running\\\\\" type=Boolean value=true ts=2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z\", \"\\\\\"Count\\\\\" type=Int32 value=-5 ts=2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z\", \"\\\\\"SerialNumber\\\\\" type=String value=\\\\\"SN-00123\\\\\" ts=2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z\", \"\\\\\"StartTime\\\\\" type=DateTime value=2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z ts=2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z\"\\]")

# The Int32 metric above (-5) is the non-obvious sign-reinterpretation test: Sparkplug's int_value
# is a raw uint32 wire value, NOT zigzag-encoded, so a negative signed value must be reinterpreted
# from its two's-complement bit pattern -- see render_sparkplug_metric's own comment on this.

add_test(NAME mqtt_sparkplug_dbirth_metrics
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_mqtt.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(mqtt_sparkplug_dbirth_metrics PROPERTIES

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flows D1/D2: SUBSCRIBE/SUBACK/UNSUBSCRIBE version-disambiguation HEURISTIC -- no CONNECT is ever
# seen on either flow, so decoder.cpp's mqtt_session_version_ map has nothing to go on and mqtt.cpp's
# own per-packet-type heuristic determines the shape (see mqtt.hpp's "Version disambiguation"
# section). D1 is v3.1.1-shaped, D2 is v5-shaped; both correctly resolve via SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE's
# stronger topic-filter-string evidence. SUBACK is documented as the weakest of the three heuristics
# (an empty/degenerate reason-code list can misresolve, since almost any byte value forms a
# "valid"-looking Properties block) -- the SUBACK responses on both flows below happen to hit exactly
# that degenerate case and resolve to v5 regardless of which flow they're on, which is expected,
# already-documented behavior, not a bug.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_test(NAME mqtt_version_heuristic_d1_v311_shape
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_mqtt.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(mqtt_version_heuristic_d1_v311_shape PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"SUBSCRIBE \\(MQTT 3.1.1\\) id=4100\",.*\"notes\": \\[\"MQTT version for this SUBSCRIBE determined via heuristic \\(only the v3.1.1-without-Properties shape parsed cleanly\\)\"\\].*\"summary\": \"UNSUBSCRIBE \\(MQTT 3.1.1\\) id=4101\",.*\"notes\": \\[\"MQTT version for this UNSUBSCRIBE determined via heuristic \\(only the v3.1.1-without-Properties shape parsed cleanly\\)\"\\]")

add_test(NAME mqtt_version_heuristic_d2_v5_shape
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_mqtt.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(mqtt_version_heuristic_d2_v5_shape PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"SUBSCRIBE \\(MQTT 5.0\\) id=4200\",.*\"notes\": \\[\"MQTT version for this SUBSCRIBE determined via heuristic \\(only the v5-with-Properties shape parsed cleanly\\)\"\\].*\"summary\": \"UNSUBSCRIBE \\(MQTT 5.0\\) id=4201\",.*\"notes\": \\[\"MQTT version for this UNSUBSCRIBE determined via heuristic \\(only the v5-with-Properties shape parsed cleanly\\)\"\\]")

add_test(NAME mqtt_version_heuristic_suback_weakest_evidence
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_mqtt.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(mqtt_version_heuristic_suback_weakest_evidence PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"SUBACK \\(MQTT 5.0\\) id=4100\",.*\"notes\": \\[\"MQTT version for this SUBACK determined via heuristic \\(a Properties block parsed cleanly within the declared Remaining Length -- the weakest-evidence heuristic of the three ambiguous MQTT packet types, see mqtt.hpp\\)\"\\]")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flow E: one PUBLISH split mid-message across two TCP segments -- Decoder::reassemble_tcp_payload,
# driven by mqtt_declared_length. No CONNECT on this flow, so the reassembled PUBLISH also carries
# the "protocol version not known" note (PUBLISH's own version ambiguity, separate from the
# SUBSCRIBE-family heuristic above).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_test(NAME mqtt_tcp_split_reassembly

# Flow F: PINGREQ + PUBACK + PINGREQ coalesced by the sender/OS into ONE TCP segment -- the

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flow G: negative/edge cases.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# An invalid QoS=3 PUBLISH (MQTT-3.3.1-4 reserves QoS to 0-2) that also happens to be missing its

# together, rather than a crash or a silent misparse.

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_mqtt.pcap" --format json)

# A CONNECT-shaped byte sequence whose Protocol Name is neither "MQTT" nor "MQIsdp" -- this MUST be
# rejected outright by the structural detection gate (the stronger CONNECT-specific check in
# try_parse_mqtt_message), not decoded as MQTT at all, and must fall all the way through to the
# generic "no protocol claimed this payload" fallback.
add_test(NAME mqtt_bogus_connect_protocol_name_rejected

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[tcp\\]  TCP payload of 16 byte\\(s\\) on port 55020->1883")

# A genuinely truncated/incomplete final packet on its own flow -- declares more Remaining Length
# than actually follows, with nothing more ever arriving in this capture -- the TCP-reassembly

# regression case.

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "buffering a MQTT packet PDU/frame split across TCP segments 55030->1883: 20 of 126 declared byte\\(s\\) seen so far across 1 segment\\(s\\) on this flow, waiting for more")

# Flow H: PINGREQ/PINGRESP on a TCP session where neither port is 1883 -- the "not a configured/

# The RedHat61 file is genuinely corrupt from its very first frame (see ATTRIBUTION.md's own byte-
# level analysis) -- this decoder must reject it with a clear error, not crash or silently misparse.
add_test(NAME real_mqtt_redhat61_corrupt_file_reports_clear_error
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/mqtt/mqtt_packets_RedHat61_tcpdump.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(real_mqtt_redhat61_corrupt_file_reports_clear_error PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: '.*mqtt_packets_RedHat61_tcpdump\\.pcap' reports an implausible captured length \\([0-9]+ bytes\\) -- the file is likely truncated or corrupt")

# Regression guard for a real bug found by tools/compare_with_tshark.py: this same corrupt file,
# read as --format json, used to leave an unterminated JSON array on stdout (the ParseError this
# file triggers partway through the read used to unwind straight past writer->end()) -- a
# structured-output consumer piping this straight into a JSON parser would get a parse error
# instead of a clean, valid (if short) array. See run_decode's own inner try/catch in cli_main.cpp
# for the fix: the output is now finalized (writer->end()) before the same error is reported.
# Before the fix, the array's closing "]" was never written at all -- its presence anywhere in
# this run's output is enough to prove writer->end() actually ran.
add_test(NAME real_mqtt_redhat61_corrupt_file_json_output_still_well_formed
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/mqtt/mqtt_packets_RedHat61_tcpdump.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(real_mqtt_redhat61_corrupt_file_json_output_still_well_formed PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\]")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TLS decryption (ROADMAP item 150, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) -- --tls-keylog / pcapng Decryption
# Secrets Blocks for MQTTS (8883)/FOXS (4911)/WinRM-over-HTTPS (5986). Every fixture below is a
# REAL TLS 1.2/1.3 session (genuine HKDF/PRF-derived keys, genuine AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305
# ciphertext -- not a hand-rolled approximation), generated independently of conduitscope's own
# tls_decrypt.cpp by tools/gen_tls_decrypt_fixtures.py (see that script's own file header for why
# it depends on the `cryptography` package rather than make_sample_pcap.py's stdlib-only
# promise). These exercise the real decoder.cpp/cli_main.cpp pipeline end to end -- ClientHello
# detection, key-log/DSB-driven decryption, epoch transition, and feeding the decrypted plaintext
# into the existing cleartext MqttDecoder/WinRmTcpDecoder/FoxDecoder -- not just tls_decrypt.cpp's
# own standalone unit-level correctness (already verified independently during development; see
# that ROADMAP item's own verification notes).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# MQTTS, TLS 1.3, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 -- the ClientHello is detection-only (no key seen yet),
# the next three packets advance the handshake/epoch-transition machinery silently, and the real
# MQTT CONNECT/CONNACK app data decrypts and feeds straight into MqttDecoder.
add_test(NAME tls_decrypt_mqtts_full_session_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tls_mqtts.pcap"
    --tls-keylog "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tls_mqtts_keylog.txt" --format text)
set_tests_properties(tls_decrypt_mqtts_full_session_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[mqtts\\]  MQTTS/TLS ClientHello \\(MQTT over TLS, port 8883\\)[^\n]*\n.*\\[mqtts\\]  MQTT over TLS \\(port 8883\\) -- TLS session in progress[^\n]*\n.*\\[mqtts\\]  MQTT over TLS \\(port 8883\\) -- TLS session in progress[^\n]*\n.*\\[mqtts\\]  MQTT over TLS \\(port 8883\\) -- TLS session in progress[^\n]*\n.*\\[mqtt\\]  CONNECT \\(MQTT 3.1.1\\)[^\n]*\n.*\\[mqtt\\]  CONNACK \\(MQTT 3.1.1\\)")

add_test(NAME tls_decrypt_mqtts_key_log_and_epoch_notes
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tls_mqtts.pcap"
    --tls-keylog "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tls_mqtts_keylog.txt" --format json)
set_tests_properties(tls_decrypt_mqtts_key_log_and_epoch_notes PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"notes\": \\[\"TLS session decrypted via key log \\(TLS 1.3, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256\\)\"\\].*\"notes\": \\[\"server direction of this TLS 1.3 session switched from handshake to application traffic keys\"\\].*\"notes\": \\[\"client direction of this TLS 1.3 session switched from handshake to application traffic keys\"\\]")

add_test(NAME tls_decrypt_mqtts_connect_decoded_with_decrypted_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tls_mqtts.pcap"
    --tls-keylog "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tls_mqtts_keylog.txt" --format json)
set_tests_properties(tls_decrypt_mqtts_connect_decoded_with_decrypted_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"CONNECT \\(MQTT 3.1.1\\)\",.*\"mqtt_values\": \\[\"ProtocolName=\\\\\"MQTT\\\\\"\", \"ProtocolLevel=4 \\(3.1.1\\)\", \"CleanSession=true\", \"WillFlag=false\", \"UsernameFlag=false\", \"PasswordFlag=false\", \"KeepAlive=60s\", \"ClientId=\\\\\"plc1-hmi-tls\\\\\"\"\\],.*\"notes\": \\[\"decrypted from MQTTS \\(TLS, port 8883\\) via --tls-keylog/pcapng DSB\"\\]")

# Absent --tls-keylog entirely, the exact same capture must stay fully opaque: the ClientHello is
# still detection-tagged (no key is needed to recognize a cleartext ClientHello record), but every
# later ciphertext-only packet falls all the way through to the generic "tcp" fallback -- nothing
# distinguishes it from any other opaque encrypted TCP stream absent a key.
add_test(NAME tls_decrypt_mqtts_without_keylog_stays_opaque
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tls_mqtts.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(tls_decrypt_mqtts_without_keylog_stays_opaque PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[mqtts\\]  MQTTS/TLS ClientHello[^\n]*\n.*\\[tcp\\]  TCP payload of [0-9]+ byte\\(s\\) on port 8883->52000"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[mqtt\\]  CONNECT")

# WinRM-over-HTTPS, TLS 1.2, TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 -- a real WS-Management Create
# request/response (the flagship "remote shell opened" finding) decrypts and feeds into

# A TLS 1.2 session negotiating a CBC suite (0xC013) this build deliberately never decrypts (RFC

# Regression guard for a real bug found by tools/compare_with_tshark.py (an automated tshark-vs-
# conduitscope comparison across this project's own fixture corpus): frame #9 of this real capture
# is a genuine Modbus "Illegal Function" exception response -- raw function-code byte 0x80, i.e.
# base function code 0 with the exception bit set. try_parse_modbus_tcp used to reject ANY base
# function code of 0, exception bit or not, so this real 9-byte MBAP frame fell through to
# HART-IP's own loose structural gate instead (which happened to also accept the same 9 bytes as a
# plausible-looking "Session Initiate" header) -- a real misclassification tshark's own dissector
# does not make. See modbus.cpp's try_parse_modbus_tcp for the fix and the full story.
#
# NOTE: frame #60 further into this same capture is a DIFFERENT, deeper, NOT-yet-fixed instance of
# HART-IP/Modbus collision on this same TCP flow -- see hartip.hpp's own "KNOWN, ACCEPTED,
# DOCUMENTED LIMITATION" section for the full story (this is its mirror image: a genuinely
# malformed Modbus segment earlier in the SAME flow, frame #6, real function-code byte 0x00 --
# correctly still rejected by the guard immediately below this one -- causes HART-IP's
# declared-length reassembly to claim the rest of that TCP flow for 22 segments before decoding it
# as a nonsensical "Session Initiate"). Deliberately not attempted here: this project already has
# a documented history of trying to resolve this exact class of collision by reordering dispatch
# and measurably regressing the Modbus/S7comm test corpus -- fixing frame #60 properly needs
# cross-protocol session-state corroboration (e.g. "this flow already showed confirmed Modbus
# traffic in the other direction"), a real design change, not a quick patch.
add_test(NAME real_modbus_illegal_function_exception_for_function_zero_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/real_captures/modbus/modbus_test_data_part2.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(real_modbus_illegal_function_exception_for_function_zero_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#9  [0-9.]+  166\\.161\\.16\\.230:502 \\(modbus\\) -> 192\\.168\\.66\\.235:2582  \\[modbus\\]  Unknown \\(0x0\\): exception response to Unknown \\(0x0\\): Illegal Function")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Chaining a single S7comm message across multiple COMPLETE TPKT/COTP frames via the EOT bit
# (Decoder::reassemble_cotp_data_frame / cotp_reassembly_) -- a different, higher layer from
# General TCP stream reassembly above: every individual TPKT frame here is itself well-formed and
# complete, but the logical S7comm message inside only decodes correctly once several are chained
# together. tests/sample_s7comm_chaining.pcap, scenarios A-B.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A) The first (EOT=0) frame alone must show only "beginning...", never an s7comm decode; the
# second (EOT=1) frame must complete it and decode the CONCATENATED bytes correctly -- the split
# lands mid-byte inside a register value itself (see the fixture's own comment), so a wrong decode
# here would mean the reassembly corrupted content, not just failed to buffer.
add_test(NAME s7comm_chaining_first_frame_buffers
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7comm_chaining.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(s7comm_chaining_first_frame_buffers PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^#]*\\[cotp\\]  beginning a COTP/S7comm message fragmented across multiple complete TPKT/COTP frames on this TCP flow \\(EOT=0\\): 21 user-data byte\\(s\\) buffered across 1 frame\\(s\\)")

add_test(NAME s7comm_chaining_completes_with_correct_values
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7comm_chaining.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(s7comm_chaining_completes_with_correct_values PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Ack_Data: Read Var \\(1 value\\(s\\): 13 ec 13 ed 13 ee 13 ef 13 f0\\)[^#]*reassembled a COTP/S7comm message from 28 user-data byte\\(s\\) chained across 2 complete TPKT/COTP frames")

# B) A Disconnect Request mid-reassembly abandons the in-progress fragment with a note rather than
# silently dropping it or splicing the Disconnect frame's own (irrelevant) bytes in.
add_test(NAME s7comm_chaining_disconnect_abandons_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7comm_chaining.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(s7comm_chaining_disconnect_abandons_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "a Disconnect Request \\(DR\\) frame arrived on this TCP flow while a COTP/S7comm fragment reassembly was still in progress \\(21 byte\\(s\\) buffered across 1 frame\\(s\\)\\) -- the earlier, incomplete fragment is abandoned")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# S7comm-Plus (0x72) -- tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap, see tools/make_sample_pcap.py's own
# build_s7commplus_sample() docstring for the full scenario list. Validated against real TIA
# Portal traffic too -- see the real_s7comm_plus_* cases above and
# tests/real_captures/s7comm/ATTRIBUTION.md's own S7comm-Plus addendum.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# GetMultiVariables request: all five item-address shapes decode_item_address branches on, in one
# request -- symbolic Merker (no extra LID), symbolic DB with a nested LID, an unrecognized IQMCT
# area code, a wholly unrecognized area1/area2 pair, and object-ID-style addressing.
add_test(NAME s7commplus_getmultivar_request_item_address_shapes
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(s7commplus_getmultivar_request_item_address_shapes PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"Data: Request GetMultiVariables \\(seq=1\\) \\(5 item\\(s\\)\\)\",.*\"s7plus_items\": \\[\"SYM-CRC=ea2db0d9, LID=M\", \"SYM-CRC=a9bc66e6, LID=DB5.10\", \"SYM-CRC=11111111, LID=Unknown IQMCT area 0x0099\", \"SYM-CRC=22222222, LID=Unknown area 0x1234/0x5678\", \"by IDs: RID=100, ID=500, ID=7\"\\]")

# GetMultiVariables response: scalar Int, Array of (signed varint) DInt, Addressarray of UInt,
# Sparsearray of Byte, a genuinely nested Struct-of-Struct with a WString leaf, LReal, Timestamp,
# Timespan, Blob, and a per-item error -- effectively every datatype/array-kind this decoder
# supports in one response.
add_test(NAME s7commplus_getmultivar_response_all_datatype_shapes
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(s7commplus_getmultivar_response_all_datatype_shapes PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "item=1: \\(Int\\) = -1234.*item=2: \\(DInt\\) Array\\[3\\] = \\[1, 2, -3\\].*item=3: \\(UInt\\) Addressarray\\[2\\] = \\[10, 20\\].*item=4: \\(Byte\\) Sparsearray = \\[0xaa, 0xbb\\].*id=315: \\(UDInt\\) = 320\; id=316: \\(Struct\\) Struct \\{ id=1826: \\(ULInt\\) = 123456789\; id=1827: \\(UDInt\\) = 42 \\}\; id=317: \\(WString\\) = ..V1.0\;6ES7 511-1AK00-0AB0.*item=6: \\(LReal\\) = 3.141593.*item=7: \\(Timestamp\\) = 2024-09-10T20:26:40.*item=8: \\(Timespan\\) = 1500000000 ns.*item=9: \\(Blob\\) = 000102030405.*item=10: Object not found \\(-12\\)")

add_test(NAME s7commplus_getmultivar_response_integrity_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(s7commplus_getmultivar_response_integrity_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"Data: Response GetMultiVariables \\(seq=1\\) \\(9 value\\(s\\)\\)\",.*\"s7plus_integrity_digest_present\": true")

# GetMultiVariables request/response via the "subscribed link" item-number path (link_id != 0) --

# DataFW1_5 is Tier 1, same as PDU type Data -- its own Integrity value just sits at the front of

# leading integrity block is consumed, the GetMultiVariables body behind it must decode normally.

# Edge cases exercising the Data part's own try/catch -- both must degrade to a clear note, never
# a crash or a silently wrong decode. The array-of-Struct case is a regression guard for a real
# bug this project's own code review caught (and fixed) before this decoder was ever built.
add_test(NAME s7commplus_array_of_struct_rejected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(s7commplus_array_of_struct_rejected PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "S7comm-Plus Data part decoding stopped: an array of Struct values was encountered -- this decoder does not support delimiting per-element nested member lists")

add_test(NAME s7commplus_unrecognized_datatype_s7string_rejected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(s7commplus_unrecognized_datatype_s7string_rejected PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "S7comm-Plus Data part decoding stopped: unrecognized S7comm-Plus value datatype 0x19")

# A telegram missing its trailer -- S7comm-Plus's own above-COTP fragmentation signal (NOT COTP's
# own EOT bit). ROADMAP item 147 (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md): this now actually buffers it (via
# S7CommPlusReassemblyState, FlowStateKeying::Session), rather than merely reporting the gap --
# renamed from s7commplus_missing_trailer_fragment_noted to reflect that, mirroring OPC UA item
# 146's own opcua_intermediate_chunk_not_reassembled_noted -> opcua_lone_intermediate_chunk_buffers_noted
# rename. This particular fragment is never followed by a completing one (its flow ends here), so
# it stays in the "buffering" state forever -- the completing case is covered by
# s7commplus_reassembly_completes_across_fragments below.
add_test(NAME s7commplus_lone_missing_trailer_fragment_buffers_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(s7commplus_lone_missing_trailer_fragment_buffers_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Data \\(fragment, awaiting further data\\)[^\n]*\n *note: S7comm-Plus telegram has no trailer in this frame -- it continues in a further TPKT/COTP frame; reassembled once a later frame's trailer completes it.*\n *note: buffering an S7comm-Plus telegram split across TPKT/COTP frames -- 12 byte\\(s\\) buffered across 1 fragment\\(s\\) so far on this TCP session")

# ROADMAP item 147 (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md): above-COTP, trailer-based reassembly actually
# COMPLETING across two physical TPKT/COTP frames (plain Data PDU type) -- the gap this item
# closes. The reassembled GetMultiVariables response decodes its one value (Int=4242) and its
# own tail Integrity block exactly as a single, unfragmented frame would have.
add_test(NAME s7commplus_reassembly_completes_across_fragments

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Data: Response GetMultiVariables \\(seq=20\\) \\(1 value\\(s\\)\\)[^\n]*\n *note: S7comm-Plus telegram reassembled from 2 fragment\\(s\\) across this TCP session, 52 byte\\(s\\) of Data part total")

# Same fixture, --format json: confirms the reassembled value actually decoded correctly (not

# Same fixture, --format json: confirms the reassembled value decoded correctly AND that
