# ROADMAP item 147: a complete telegram of a DIFFERENT PDU type (Connect) arrives while a
# previous above-COTP reassembly (Data) is still in progress on the same TCP session -- the
# in-progress reassembly is abandoned (with a note naming the byte/fragment counts lost), and the
# Connect telegram's own standalone decode is unaffected. A deliberate deviation from the
# reference plugin's own FSM, which doesn't guard against this at all (see s7commplus.hpp's own
# "Chunking" section).
add_test(NAME s7commplus_reassembly_abandoned_on_pdu_type_mismatch
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(s7commplus_reassembly_abandoned_on_pdu_type_mismatch PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Connect[^\n]*\n *note: Connect PDU \\(session establishment handshake\\) is recognized but not decoded.*\n *note: a complete S7comm-Plus telegram \\(PDU type Connect\\) arrived while a previous above-COTP reassembly was in progress \\(12 byte\\(s\\) buffered across 1 fragment\\(s\\)\\) -- abandoned; this telegram's own standalone decode above is unaffected")

# Security-audit-style follow-up (same posture as max_reassembly_bytes/segments_abandons_dnp3_
# fragment_reassembly above): the same two --max-reassembly-* flags, exercised against
# S7comm-Plus's OWN local above-COTP reassembly cap (S7CommPlusReassemblyState, s7commplus.cpp)
# instead of the generic TCP-segment cap. sample_s7commplus.pcap's reasm_port flow (port 50305)
# normally reassembles a 2-fragment, 52-byte telegram cleanly (see
# s7commplus_reassembly_completes_across_fragments above); set low enough, s7commplus.cpp's own

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ROADMAP item 148: S7comm-Plus native symbolic item address (Symbol CRC + LID chain) name
# resolution via an externally-supplied lookup table (symbol_table.hpp/symbol_table.cpp,
# --s7plus-symbols). tests/s7plus_symbols_sample.txt (see its own file header) is the shared
# fixture: it names tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap's own SYM-CRC=ea2db0d9 (LID=M, a bare depth-1
# address -- "-" chain) and SYM-CRC=a9bc66e6 (LID=DB5.10, a one-LID chain -- "10"), leaves
# SYM-CRC=deadbeef (also LID=M) deliberately unlisted as a guaranteed miss, and exercises its own
# tolerant-parsing/last-line-wins rules. All verified against the real built binary's own output
# before being written here, per this project's standing discipline.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

set(S7PLUS_SYMBOLS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/s7plus_symbols_sample.txt")

# Off by default: the raw tag renders exactly as before, no "(name)" annotation at all.

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(s7plus_symbols_off_by_default_no_annotation PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SYM-CRC=ea2db0d9, LID=M\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Motor1_Running")

# decode --format json: both a bare depth-1 ("-" chain) and a one-LID-chain address resolve;
# object-ID-style addresses (never looked up at all) and an unlisted CRC (deadbeef) stay bare.
add_test(NAME s7plus_symbols_decode_json_resolves_matches
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format json
          --s7plus-symbols "${S7PLUS_SYMBOLS}")
set_tests_properties(s7plus_symbols_decode_json_resolves_matches PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SYM-CRC=ea2db0d9, LID=M \\(Motor1_Running_Overridden\\).*SYM-CRC=a9bc66e6, LID=DB5.10 \\(Line2_Speed_Setpoint\\)")

# The guaranteed miss (deadbeef, present in the capture, absent from the table) never gets a
# "(name)" suffix -- an annotation, never a replacement; a miss adds nothing.
add_test(NAME s7plus_symbols_decode_json_miss_stays_unannotated
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap" --format json

set_tests_properties(s7plus_symbols_decode_json_miss_stays_unannotated PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"SYM-CRC=deadbeef, LID=M\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SYM-CRC=deadbeef, LID=M \\(")

# Regression guard for a documented custom --protocol/policy-validate value: "s7comm-plus" must be
# accepted, and --stats confirms the full PDU-type/function/Tier-1 breakdown this fixture is meant
# to exercise (note: the COTP Connection Request/Confirm frames still show up as their own "cotp"
# protocol -- COTP-level framing is always surfaced, matching classic S7comm/MMS's own filters).
# sample_s7commplus.pcap is s7comm-plus-only (plus its own COTP connection framing, always
# surfaced regardless of --protocol), so `--protocol s7comm-plus` (decode-only, no longer
# combinable with --stats) doesn't change what `info` (Auto mode) already reports here --
# confirmed against this build's actual output identical to the below.
add_test(NAME s7commplus_protocol_filter
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7commplus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(s7commplus_protocol_filter PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "protocols:\n *cotp +2\n *parse-error +1\n *s7comm-plus +29.*\ns7comm-plus pdu types:\n *Connect +3\n *Data +21\n *DataFW1_5 +3\n *Keep Alive +2\ns7comm-plus functions:\n *DeleteObject +2\n *Explore +2\n *GetMultiVariables +9\n *SetMultiVariables +4\n *SetVariable +2\ns7comm-plus function bodies fully decoded \\(Tier 1\\): 15")

# Regression guard for a real false positive: non-Modbus traffic (here, bytes that also happen
# to satisfy DNP3's 0x05 0x64 start) whose first four bytes look like transaction_id + a valid
# protocol_id==0, and whose function-code byte is 0x00 -- reserved/never assigned in the Modbus
# spec. Found via a real capture (DNP3 traffic on port 20000 mislabeled as Modbus); must now fall
# through to DNP3 detection instead.
add_test(NAME modbus_function_code_zero_is_not_modbus
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus_false_positive.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(modbus_function_code_zero_is_not_modbus PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[dnp3\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[modbus\\]")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authoritative (MBAP transaction-ID + TCP-session, non-heuristic) Modbus request/response pairing
# (Decoder::pair_modbus_transaction / modbus_pending_), layered on top of -- never replacing --
# modbus.cpp's own payload-shape heuristic. sample_modbus.pcap already incidentally exercises the
# common read-family pairing case and one orphan response; sample_modbus_pairing.pcap covers the
# cases that need their own scenario -- see its own file comment for why.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A) Write Single Register: request and response share the IDENTICAL 4-byte shape per spec -- the
# heuristic alone cannot tell them apart (its own note says so), so this is the strongest
# real-world case for this feature. The response must still be authoritatively paired to packet #1.
add_test(NAME modbus_pairing_write_single_paired_despite_ambiguous_shape
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus_pairing.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(modbus_pairing_write_single_paired_despite_ambiguous_shape PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "authoritative pairing: response to transaction id 500 \\(unit 1\\) -- matches the request seen in packet #1")

# B) A reused transaction ID before its first request is ever answered must be noted, and the
# eventual response must pair to the SECOND (most recently outstanding) request, not the first.
add_test(NAME modbus_pairing_reused_transaction_id_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus_pairing.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(modbus_pairing_reused_transaction_id_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "transaction id 600 reused on this TCP flow before its previous outstanding request \\(packet #3\\) was matched with a response")

add_test(NAME modbus_pairing_reused_transaction_id_pairs_to_latest_request
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus_pairing.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(modbus_pairing_reused_transaction_id_pairs_to_latest_request PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "authoritative pairing: response to transaction id 600 \\(unit 1\\) -- matches the request seen in packet #4 \\(Read Holding Registers: request: read 5 holding register\\(s\\) starting at address 100\\)")

# C) An orphan response (its request never seen on this session) -- already exercised incidentally
# by sample_modbus.pcap's exception-response packet (transaction id 2, no matching request).
add_test(NAME modbus_pairing_orphan_response_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(modbus_pairing_orphan_response_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "no outstanding request found on this TCP session for transaction id 2")

# ModbusFrame::is_request/start_address/quantity (modbus.hpp/modbus.cpp) -- the baseline-engine
# Phase 1 prerequisite (docs/design/baseline-engine.md): the same address/quantity already rendered
# into `summary` text, now also exposed as their own structured fields. Purely additive -- every
# existing modbus_* test above still passes byte-for-byte unmodified; these four are the dedicated

add_test(NAME modbus_json_includes_start_address_and_quantity_for_read_request
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format json)

# A read RESPONSE carries no address at all on the wire -- start_address/quantity must be omitted

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format json)

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"modbus_paired_request_index\": 1,\n *\"modbus_is_request\": false,\n *\"modbus_start_address\"")

# A write-multiple REQUEST and its RESPONSE both carry address+quantity (the response echoes it
# back, real Modbus wire behavior) -- is_request distinguishes which side is which even though both
# populate the same two fields. sample_modbus_pairing.pcap's packet 5/6 (second read-family
# request/response pair) doesn't cover write-multiple, so this uses a purpose-built check against
# sample_baseline_modbus_mutated.pcap's own Write Multiple Registers request instead (packet #2 --
# see build_baseline_modbus_mutated_sample's own comment, tools/make_sample_pcap.py).

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_modbus_mutated.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(modbus_json_write_multiple_request_has_start_address_and_quantity PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"Write Multiple Registers: request: write 2 register\\(s\\) starting at address 5[^\"]*\",\n *\"modbus_is_request\": true,\n *\"modbus_start_address\": 5,\n *\"modbus_quantity\": 2,")

# Write Single Coil/Register is deliberately left out of this addition entirely (see
# ModbusFrame::is_request's own comment, modbus.hpp): request and response share the identical wire
# shape, so is_request stays false and start_address/quantity stay unset on BOTH sides -- not a
# regression, a documented scope boundary.
add_test(NAME modbus_json_write_single_has_no_is_request_address_or_quantity
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus_pairing.pcap" --format json)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"Write Single Register: address=10[^\"]*\",\n *\"modbus_is_request\": false,\n *\"notes\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"Write Single Register: address=10[^\"]*\",\n *\"modbus_is_request\": false,\n *\"modbus_start_address\"")

# SM Identify Rsp on BOTH LinkId branches -- the single trickiest piece of this decoder (see
# ffhse.hpp's own "The LinkId branch" section): LinkId != 0 decodes the trailing list as 2-byte
# H1NodeAddress+VersionNumber pairs; LinkId == 0 decodes it as 4-byte H1LinkId+Reserved+Version
# quads -- same total byte count, different internal shape.
add_test(NAME ffhse_sm_identify_linkid_nonzero_branch
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ffhse.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(ffhse_sm_identify_linkid_nonzero_branch PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"version-number-list\\[0\\].a=h1-node-address=0x01 version=1\", \"version-number-list\\[0\\].b=h1-node-address=0x02 version=1\".*LinkId \\(this PDU's own header FDA Address, upper 16 bits\\) = 0x0005 -- version-number-list decoded as H1NodeAddress\\+VersionNumber pairs")

add_test(NAME ffhse_sm_identify_linkid_zero_branch
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ffhse.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(ffhse_sm_identify_linkid_zero_branch PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"version-number-list\\[0\\]=h1-link-id=0x0005 version=1\", \"version-number-list\\[1\\]=h1-link-id=0x0006 version=2\".*LinkId \\(this PDU's own header FDA Address, upper 16 bits\\) = 0x0000 -- version-number-list decoded as H1LinkId\\+Reserved\\+VersionNumber quads")

# Two FF-HSE PDUs concatenated into ONE UDP datagram -- exercises the wire_length-driven
# coalescing while-loop in decoder.cpp's UDP dispatch.
add_test(NAME ffhse_udp_multi_pdu_coalescing
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ffhse.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(ffhse_udp_multi_pdu_coalescing PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"ffhse_message_name\": \"FDA Idle Req\",.*additional FF-HSE PDU 2 found in the same UDP datagram at byte offset 12: FDA Idle Rsp")

# Fix: Message Length claims a full 52-byte FDA Open Session Req body, but only 20 bytes of it are
# actually present in this UDP datagram (declared 64 total, only 32 available). Originally this
# decoder "explained" that as a truncated-but-recognized FF-HSE message (note + raw-hex fallback,
# still claiming the packet as ffhse) -- repurposed as a regression pin after a user-submitted real
# capture showed the same shape (a Message Length grossly exceeding the actual datagram) was
# actually a systematic false positive from unrelated UDP traffic, not a real truncated FF-HSE
# message. Root-caused against the reference dissector: packet-ff.c's own dissect_ff_udp() already
# does exactly this check -- "/* Make sure the length field is valid */ if ((length >
# tvb_reported_length_remaining(tvb, offset)) || ...) break;" -- and simply declines to dissect a
# PDU whose own declared length exceeds what's actually in the datagram, rather than accepting it
# as truncated. A UDP datagram is delivered whole; there is no reassembly at this layer the way
# there legitimately is for TCP (see ffhse_declared_length), so this can never really be "still
# arriving". FfhseUdpDecoder::decode now matches the reference exactly and declines outright, so
# this packet correctly falls through to the generic "udp" protocol instead.
add_test(NAME ffhse_udp_message_length_exceeding_datagram_not_misdetected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ffhse.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(ffhse_udp_message_length_exceeding_datagram_not_misdetected PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 62,.*\"src_port\": 52200,\n *\"dst_port\": 1089,\n *\"tcp_flags\": null,\n *\"protocol\": \"udp\",\n *\"summary\": \"UDP payload of 32 byte\\(s\\) on port 52200->1089\"")

# Unexpected port: an otherwise perfectly valid SM Identify Req on a port that is none of the 4
# configured FF-HSE ports -- still decodes, but with the "not a configured/standard FF-HSE port"
# note (matches HART-IP's/BACnet's own posture: port is an annotation, never a detection gate).
add_test(NAME ffhse_unexpected_port_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ffhse.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(ffhse_unexpected_port_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"ffhse_message_name\": \"SM Identify Req\",.*seen on UDP port 52200->40000, which is not a configured/standard FF-HSE port \\(1089/1090/1091/3622\\)")

# False-positive regression: an otherwise structurally-valid ProtocolAndType byte, but a Message
# Length (4237566479) far beyond the 16 MiB plausibility ceiling (kMaxPlausibleMessageLength,
# ffhse.cpp) -- must fall through to the generic "udp" protocol, NOT be detected as ffhse. Mirrors
# a real false positive found on a genuine capture: a UDP/443 QUIC/TLS response's essentially-
# random bytes matched this decoder's own weak structural gate before this ceiling existed.
add_test(NAME ffhse_implausible_message_length_not_misdetected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ffhse.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(ffhse_implausible_message_length_not_misdetected PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"src_port\": 443,\n *\"dst_port\": 58201,\n *\"tcp_flags\": null,\n *\"protocol\": \"udp\"")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Beckhoff TwinCAT / ADS over AMS/TCP (TCP port 48898) -- see twincat.hpp's file header comment
# for the exact wire format each assertion below exercises, and tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_twincat_sample for the exact byte layout. TwinCAT is the first protocol in this codebase
# built entirely on the ProtocolDecoder interface (protocol_decoder.hpp) -- see
# docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's "registration-model decoder refactor" entry. Fixture:
# tests/sample_twincat.pcap.

# DeviceNotification is an unsolicited push -- excluded from Invoke-ID pairing entirely (no
# "authoritative pairing"/"no outstanding request" note at all), decoded structurally
# (stamp/sample counts) but not per-sample, with an explicit note saying so.
add_test(NAME twincat_device_notification_structural_only_not_paired
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_twincat.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(twincat_device_notification_structural_only_not_paired PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[twincat\\]  DeviceNotification request: 36 byte\\(s\\), 1 stamp\\(s\\), 2 sample\\(s\\) total \\(values not decoded, see twincat\\.hpp\\)[^\n]*\n *note: DeviceNotification sample values are not decoded"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[twincat\\]  DeviceNotification[^\n]*\n *note: (authoritative pairing|no outstanding request)")

# Invoke ID reused on the same direction before its first request was ever paired -- must not be
# silently overwritten, and the eventual response must pair to the SECOND (most recently
# outstanding) request, not the first, mirroring modbus_pairing's own scenario B.
add_test(NAME twincat_invoke_id_reused_pairs_to_most_recent_request
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_twincat.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(twincat_invoke_id_reused_pairs_to_most_recent_request PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: Invoke ID 9 reused on this AMS session before its previous outstanding request \\(packet #18\\) was matched with a response.*\\[twincat\\]  Read response: result=0x0, 2 byte\\(s\\) of data[^\n]*\n *note: authoritative pairing: response to Invoke ID 9 -- matches the request seen in packet #19")

add_test(NAME twincat_orphan_response_no_outstanding_request_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_twincat.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(twincat_orphan_response_no_outstanding_request_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: no outstanding request found on this AMS session for Invoke ID 999")

# A ReadState response payload too short for its own command's expected shape (decode_payload's
# own internal ParseError catch, distinct from try_parse_twincat's outer structural gate) --
# reported as a note, the frame itself still recognized as TwinCAT (the AMS header decoded fine).
add_test(NAME twincat_payload_truncated_relative_to_command_shape_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_twincat.pcap" --format text --verbose)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[twincat\\]  ReadState response \\(payload shorter than this command's expected shape -- not fully decoded\\).*\n *note: payload truncated or malformed relative to ReadState's expected shape\; only the AMS header was decoded")

# Structural detection gate rejections: an unrecognized Command ID, a missing ADS command State
# Flags bit, and an AMS/TCP-vs-AMS-header Data Length cross-check mismatch must each be rejected
# outright (never misdetected as twincat), falling through to generic "tcp" -- see twincat.hpp's
# STRUCTURAL DETECTION GATE paragraph.

# One AMS/TCP frame split across two TCP segments, the split point deliberately after the full
# 38-byte AMS/TCP+AMS header (see build_twincat_sample's own comment on why) -- exercises
# TwinCatDecoder::tcp_declared_length via Decoder::reassemble_tcp_payload, the same split/rejoin
# shape build_tcp_reassembly_sample already covers for Modbus/DNP3/TPKT, and confirms Invoke-ID
# pairing still resolves correctly once the response is fully reassembled.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MELSEC / MC Protocol (SLMP), Mitsubishi Electric -- TCP port 5001, UDP port 5000 (see
# melsec.hpp's file header comment for the wire format, structural detection gate, and the
# curated security notes). Fixture generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_melsec_sample --
# tests/sample_melsec.pcap (39 packets: 30 TCP request/response pairs and structural variants, 1
# gate-rejection negative control, a 3-packet TCP segment-split reassembly, 4 UDP packets, and a
# UDP declared-length-mismatch negative control). MELSEC is built entirely on the ProtocolDecoder
# registration-model interface from inception, like TwinCAT -- see melsec.hpp's own comment.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME melsec_batch_read_word_and_bit_units_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_melsec.pcap" --format text)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[melsec\\]  Batch Read request: D1000, 3 point\\(s\\), word units.*\\[melsec\\]  Batch Read response: 3 word value\\(s\\).*\\[melsec\\]  Batch Read request: M100, 5 point\\(s\\), bit units.*\\[melsec\\]  Batch Read response: 6 bit value\\(s\\)")

# Proves the bit-units nibble-packing quirk (even-indexed bit in bit 4, odd-indexed in bit 0 of
# the same byte) was unpacked correctly, not just that some bit values came back.
add_test(NAME melsec_bit_units_nibble_packing_correct
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_melsec.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(melsec_bit_units_nibble_packing_correct PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"melsec_bit_values\": \\[1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0\\]")

# The redaction proof (text format): the password's own length is shown, its value never is --
# per Jurgen's own NTLM/Netlogon-style redaction decision (melsec.hpp's file header comment).
add_test(NAME melsec_remote_password_length_shown_value_redacted_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_melsec.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(melsec_remote_password_length_shown_value_redacted_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[melsec\\]  Remote Password UNLOCK request: password present \\(8 byte\\(s\\), value not decoded -- see melsec\\.hpp\\)[^\n]*\n *note: Remote Password UNLOCK/LOCK: the password itself travels as cleartext ASCII"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "S3cr3t")

# The same redaction proof, JSON format -- asserts melsec_remote_password_length IS present while
# the literal password text is absent from the field-level structured output too.
add_test(NAME melsec_remote_password_length_shown_value_redacted_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_melsec.pcap" --format json)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"melsec_remote_password_length\": 8"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "S3cr3t")

# 4E frame variant -- proves the 2-byte Serial No. field (little-endian, immediately after the

# Gate-rejection negative control: leading bytes 0x1234 match none of the four subheader magic

# THE regression proof for the real collision this protocol's own manual smoke test caught:
# HART-IP's own deliberately weak UDP gate (MessageType/MessageID at payload bytes 1/2 both small
# enumerated values, MsgLength >= 8) used to steal this exact MELSEC UDP request before MELSEC's
# own much stronger two-part gate got a chance to run -- see decoder.cpp's MELSEC UDP call-site
# comment for the full analysis. Asserts it decodes as melsec and NEVER as hartip.
add_test(NAME melsec_udp_request_not_misdetected_as_hartip
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_melsec.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(melsec_udp_request_not_misdetected_as_hartip PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53500 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:5000  \\[melsec\\]  Batch Read request: D1700, 1 point\\(s\\), word units"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[hartip\\]")

add_test(NAME melsec_udp_non_standard_port_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_melsec.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(melsec_udp_non_standard_port_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53501 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:15000  \\[melsec\\]  Remote STOP request \\(no arguments\\)[^\n]*\n *note: Remote STOP: no protocol-level authentication[^\n]*\n *note: seen on UDP port 53501->15000, which is not a configured/standard MELSEC port \\(5000\\)")

# UDP declared-length mismatch negative control: subheader magic matches but the length
# accounting doesn't, so the structural gate rejects it and it falls through to generic "udp" --

# THE regression proof for the real MELSEC-vs-Modbus TCP collision Jurgen reported and this session
# fixed (see melsec.hpp's own "POST-DELIVERY FIX" paragraph and decoder.cpp's MELSEC TCP call-site
# comment for the full analysis): Modbus's own weak protocol_id==0 gate used to steal a genuine
# MELSEC request with Network No.==PC No.==0 and a small I/O No. before MELSEC's own much stronger
# two-part gate got a chance to run -- even on MELSEC's own TCP port 5001. Asserts it decodes as
# melsec and NEVER as modbus.
add_test(NAME melsec_tcp_request_not_misdetected_as_modbus

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53400 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:5001  \\[melsec\\]  Batch Read request: D1800, 1 point\\(s\\), word units"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[modbus\\]")

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_melsec.pcap" --melsec-port 15000 --format text)
set_tests_properties(melsec_extra_port_widens_expected_port_annotation PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53501 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:15000  \\[melsec\\]  Remote STOP request \\(no arguments\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "seen on UDP port 53501->15000, which is not a configured/standard MELSEC port")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FINS (Factory Interface Network Service), Omron -- TCP port 9600, UDP port 9600 (see fins.hpp's
# file header comment for the wire format, structural detection gate, and the curated security
# notes). Fixture generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_fins_sample --
# tests/sample_fins.pcap (46 TCP packets -- a handshake pair, 17 commands' request/response pairs
# or structural variants, an unrecognized-command structural fallback, a 2-segment TCP reassembly
# split -- plus 4 UDP packets and 3 UDP gate-rejection negative controls). FINS is built entirely
# on the ProtocolDecoder registration-model interface from inception, like MELSEC -- see fins.hpp's
# own comment. Unlike MELSEC, a FINS response self-describes its own command code, so most of these
# tests need no session-state proof the way melsec_random_read_word_and_dword_decoded does --
# fins_multiple_memory_area_read_matches_request_devices below is the one exception (Multiple
# Memory Area Read, the FINS analogue of MELSEC's own Random Read).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME fins_tcp_handshake_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(fins_tcp_handshake_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[fins\\]  Node Address Data Send \\(client->server\\): requested client node 1.*\\[fins\\]  Node Address Data Send \\(server->client\\): client node 1, server node 1")

add_test(NAME fins_memory_area_read_word_and_bit_units_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(fins_memory_area_read_word_and_bit_units_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[fins\\]  Memory Area Read request: D1000, 3 item\\(s\\), word.*\\[fins\\]  Memory Area Read response: 3 word value\\(s\\).*\\[fins\\]  Memory Area Read request: CIO10\\.05, 4 item\\(s\\), bit.*\\[fins\\]  Memory Area Read response: 4 bit value\\(s\\)")

add_test(NAME fins_memory_area_write_and_fill_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(fins_memory_area_write_and_fill_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[fins\\]  Memory Area Write request: D2000, 2 item\\(s\\), word.*\\[fins\\]  Memory Area Write response \\(no data\\).*\\[fins\\]  Memory Area Fill request: D3000, 5 item\\(s\\) filled with 1234.*\\[fins\\]  Memory Area Fill response \\(no data\\)")

# The FINS analogue of melsec_random_read_word_and_dword_decoded: proves FinsFlowState carries the
# request's own device list (D4000 word + CIO20.03 bit) forward so Multiple Memory Area Read's own
# response -- which carries no per-item type information on the wire at all -- splits its two raw
# values correctly by type. Checked at the JSON field level (fins_devices/fins_device_values line
# up index-for-index), not just the text summary's item count.
add_test(NAME fins_multiple_memory_area_read_matches_request_devices
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(fins_multiple_memory_area_read_matches_request_devices PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"fins_devices\": \\[\"D4000\", \"CIO20\\.03\"\\],\n *\"fins_device_values\": \\[\"4242\", \"1\"\\]")

# Unrecognized command code (0x9999) over TCP: structural fallback, numeric-only -- FINS/TCP's own
# exact "FINS" magic is gate enough on its own, unlike UDP (see fins_udp_unrecognized_command_
# rejected below for the deliberately different UDP posture).
add_test(NAME fins_tcp_unrecognized_command_structural_fallback
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(fins_tcp_unrecognized_command_structural_fallback PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[fins\\]  Unknown command 0x9999 request \\(no further decode -- unrecognized command\\)")

# A Memory Area Read request split across two TCP segments -- the declared-length reassembly gate,
# mirroring melsec_tcp_segment_split_reassembly_still_matches exactly.
add_test(NAME fins_tcp_segment_split_reassembly_still_matches
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(fins_tcp_segment_split_reassembly_still_matches PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[tcp\\]  buffering a FINS/TCP \\(Omron\\) PDU/frame split across TCP segments 53600->9600: 17 of 34 declared byte\\(s\\) seen so far across 1 segment\\(s\\) on this flow, waiting for more.*\\[fins\\]  Memory Area Read request: D5000, 1 item\\(s\\), word[^\n]*\n *note: reassembled a FINS/TCP \\(Omron\\) PDU/frame from 34 byte\\(s\\) spanning 2 TCP segments on this flow")

# THE regression proof for the collision risk fins.hpp's own UDP gate ordering defends against:
# this packet's own GCT byte (0x02, fins_frame's own default -- a real probe's own observed value,
# not the conventional-but-unreliable 0x07) DOES satisfy HART-IP's own weak MessageID-in-{0,1,2,3}
# UDP gate condition, and RSV=0x00 always satisfies its MessageType==0 condition too -- see
# decoder.cpp's FINS UDP call-site comment for the full analysis. Asserts it decodes as fins and
# NEVER as hartip.
add_test(NAME fins_udp_request_not_misdetected_as_hartip
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(fins_udp_request_not_misdetected_as_hartip PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:9600 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:9600  \\[fins\\]  Memory Area Read request: D6000, 2 item\\(s\\), word"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[hartip\\]")

add_test(NAME fins_udp_non_standard_port_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(fins_udp_non_standard_port_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53601 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:15001  \\[fins\\]  Stop request \\(no arguments\\)[^\n]*\n *note: Stop: no protocol-level authentication[^\n]*\n *note: seen on UDP port 53601->15001, which is not a configured/standard FINS port \\(9600\\)")

# UDP negative control: the SAME unrecognized command code (0x9999) fins_tcp_unrecognized_command_
# structural_fallback above proves decodes structurally over TCP -- over UDP it must be REJECTED
# outright, falling through to generic "udp" -- the deliberate departure from MELSEC's own numeric-
# fallback posture forced by FINS/UDP having no other structural anchor to lean on (see fins.hpp).
add_test(NAME fins_udp_unrecognized_command_rejected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(fins_udp_unrecognized_command_rejected PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53602 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:9600  \\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 15 byte\\(s\\) on port 53602->9600")

# UDP structural-gate-rejection negative controls: ICF reserved bits (0x3E mask) set, and RSV !=
# 0x00 -- neither may be recognized as fins at all.
add_test(NAME fins_udp_gate_rejects_reserved_icf_bits
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(fins_udp_gate_rejects_reserved_icf_bits PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53603 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:9600  \\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 12 byte\\(s\\) on port 53603->9600")

add_test(NAME fins_udp_gate_rejects_nonzero_rsv
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fins.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(fins_udp_gate_rejects_nonzero_rsv PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53604 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:9600  \\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 12 byte\\(s\\) on port 53604->9600")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kerberos (RFC 4120), TCP and UDP port 88 -- the first Windows AD-suite protocol (see
# kerberos.hpp's file header comment for the wire format, structural detection gate, and the
# curated attack/monitoring notes). Fixtures generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_kerberos_sample -- tests/sample_kerberos.pcap (UDP, 15 packets) and
# tests/sample_kerberos_tcp.pcap (TCP, 3 packets: one whole frame, one split across two segments).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME kerberos_as_req_no_preauth_standing_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_as_req_no_preauth_standing_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  AS-REQ cname=alice sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM realm=\"EXAMPLE\\.COM\" etype=\\[aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96,aes128-cts-hmac-sha1-96,rc4-hmac\\]\n *note: AS-REQ has no PA-ENC-TIMESTAMP pre-authentication data -- AS-REP-Roasting-style request shape")

# The FLAGSHIP AS-REP-Roasting note: only fires on the successful AS-REP that correlates (by
# cname, on the same session) to an earlier no-preauth AS-REQ -- see kerberos.cpp's
# KerberosFlowState::pending_as_req.
add_test(NAME kerberos_as_rep_roasting_flagship_note_correlated
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_as_rep_roasting_flagship_note_correlated PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  AS-REP cname=alice ticket-sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM enc-part-etype=rc4-hmac\n *note: AS-REP Roasting: this is a successful, crackable AS-REP answering an AS-REQ \\(packet #1\\) that included no pre-authentication proof -- the target account likely has Kerberos pre-authentication disabled")

add_test(NAME kerberos_tgs_req_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_tgs_req_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  TGS-REQ cname=\\(none\\) sname=cifs/fileserver\\.example\\.com realm=\"EXAMPLE\\.COM\"")

# The FLAGSHIP Kerberoasting note: keys off the embedded Ticket's OWN enc-part etype (RC4 here),
# not the response's own outer enc-part etype (deliberately left AES in this fixture to prove the
# two are checked independently -- see kerberos.cpp's Note 2 comment).
add_test(NAME kerberos_kerberoasting_flagship_note_correlated
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_kerberoasting_flagship_note_correlated PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  TGS-REP cname=alice ticket-sname=cifs/fileserver\\.example\\.com enc-part-etype=aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96\n *note: this service ticket's encrypted part uses rc4-hmac -- crackable offline if this SPN's account is compromised via Kerberoasting")

# Kerberoasting must NOT fire on a krbtgt sname (an ordinary TGT, not a service ticket) even with
# an RC4 ticket enc-part -- see kerberos.cpp's own exclusion comment.
add_test(NAME kerberos_kerberoasting_excludes_krbtgt_sname
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_kerberoasting_excludes_krbtgt_sname PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  TGS-REP cname=alice ticket-sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM enc-part-etype=aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ticket-sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM[^\n]*\n *note: this service ticket")

# Kerberoasting negative control: a real (non-krbtgt) SPN whose ticket enc-part is AES (a fully
# patched, AES-only domain) must not be flagged either.
add_test(NAME kerberos_kerberoasting_negative_control_aes_ticket
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_kerberoasting_negative_control_aes_ticket PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  TGS-REP cname=alice ticket-sname=ldap/dc1\\.example\\.com enc-part-etype=aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ticket-sname=ldap/dc1\\.example\\.com[^\n]*\n *note: this service ticket")

# The negative case for the roasting FLAGSHIP note itself: ordinary Windows-style behavior --
# no-preauth AS-REQ, KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED, a RETRY that DOES include PA-ENC-TIMESTAMP, then a
# successful AS-REP -- must NOT get the flagship note. Proves correlation tracks the most recent
# request for a given cname (the retry overwrites the pending entry), not just the first attempt.
add_test(NAME kerberos_as_rep_roasting_negative_case_normal_retry_not_flagged
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_as_rep_roasting_negative_case_normal_retry_not_flagged PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  AS-REP cname=bob ticket-sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM enc-part-etype=aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "cname=bob[^\n]*\n *note: AS-REP Roasting")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LDAP (RFC 4511), TCP/389 and TCP/3268 (Global Catalog) -- the second Windows AD-suite protocol
# (see ldap.hpp's file header comment for the wire format -- IMPLICIT tagging, NOT Kerberos's own
# EXPLICIT convention -- the structural detection gate/collision survey, and the six curated
# attack/monitoring notes). Fixtures generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_ldap_sample()
# -- tests/sample_ldap.pcap (TCP, 62 packets across 17 independent sessions/flows A-Q) and
# tests/sample_ldap_tcp_split.pcap (TCP, 2 packets: one SearchRequest split across two segments).
# All expectations below were captured from the actual built binary's output against these
# fixtures (the same "manual smoke test BEFORE writing CMakeLists.txt tests" discipline the
# Kerberos delivery's own verification step used), not hand-computed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Curated note 3 (SPN sweep) plus the example filter rendering ldap.hpp's own header comment
# cites verbatim -- "(&(objectClass=user)(servicePrincipalName=*))".
add_test(NAME ldap_search_spn_filter_note3
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ldap.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(ldap_search_spn_filter_note3 PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[ldap\\]  SearchRequest id=1 base=\"dc=example,dc=com\" scope=wholeSubtree filter=\\(&\\(objectClass=user\\)\\(servicePrincipalName=\\*\\)\\)[^\n]*\n *note: filter references servicePrincipalName -- the standard Kerberoasting target-discovery step")

# The "keep state across many SearchResultEntry responses, close on the terminal
# SearchResultDone" correlation shape -- genuinely new relative to Kerberos's own strict 1:1
# pairing (see ldap.hpp's own STATE/CORRELATION section).

# Curated note 4 -- AS-REP-Roasting target discovery via the AD bitwise-AND matching rule against

# Note 4/5 NEGATIVE control -- the SAME bitwise-AND mechanism against an unrelated bit

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SMB2/NTLM (MS-SMB2/MS-NLMP), TCP/445 and TCP/139 -- the third Windows AD-suite protocol (see
# smb.hpp's/ntlm.hpp's own file header comments for the wire format -- fixed-width little-endian
# fields, NOT BER like Kerberos/LDAP -- the structural detection gate, compounding, and the six
# curated attack/monitoring notes). Fixtures generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_smb_sample() -- tests/sample_smb.pcap (TCP, 26 packets across 7 independent
# sessions/flows A-G) and tests/sample_smb_tcp_split.pcap (TCP, 2 packets: one NEGOTIATE Request
# split across two segments). All expectations below were captured from the actual built binary's
# output against these fixtures -- confirmed first via an independent, hand-built synthetic
# exchange (the same "manual smoke test BEFORE writing CMakeLists.txt tests" discipline
# Kerberos's/LDAP's own deliveries used), not hand-computed or guessed at.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# NEGOTIATE Request's dialect list (including the 0x02FF multi-protocol wildcard) and Response's
# negotiated dialect, plus curated note 2 POSITIVE -- SecurityMode SIGNING_ENABLED but NOT
# SIGNING_REQUIRED, the ntlmrelayx precondition.
add_test(NAME smb_negotiate_dialects_and_note2_positive
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(smb_negotiate_dialects_and_note2_positive PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Request \\(dialects: SMB 2\\.0\\.2, SMB 2\\.1, SMB 3\\.0, SMB 3\\.0\\.2, SMB 3\\.1\\.1, SMB 2\\.\\?\\?\\? \\(multi-protocol negotiate wildcard\\)\\).*SMB2 NEGOTIATE Response \\(SMB 3\\.1\\.1\\) \\[STATUS_SUCCESS\\][^\n]*\n *note: SMB signing is enabled but NOT required on this session -- the precondition every NTLM-relay tool \\(ntlmrelayx and equivalents\\) checks for")

# Curated note 2 NEGATIVE control -- SecurityMode SIGNING_ENABLED|SIGNING_REQUIRED on the SAME
# NEGOTIATE Response shape (flow D): must NOT fire.
add_test(NAME smb_negotiate_signing_required_note2_negative_control
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(smb_negotiate_signing_required_note2_negative_control PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "52504 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:445 \\(microsoft-ds\\)  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Request \\(dialects: SMB 3\\.1\\.1\\)  \\(client"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.10:445 \\(microsoft-ds\\) -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.50:52504  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Response \\(SMB 3\\.1\\.1\\) \\[STATUS_SUCCESS\\][^\n]*\n *note: SMB signing")

# Full NTLM negotiate/challenge/authenticate handshake -- curated note 3 fires on EVERY
# NTLM-bearing message (not just once), and the terminal SESSION_SETUP Response closes the
# SessionId-keyed multi-leg handshake with a "succeeded" correlation note (the genuinely new
# correlation shape relative to Kerberos's/LDAP's own 1:1/keep-until-terminal pairings).
add_test(NAME smb_ntlm_handshake_note3_and_succeeded_correlation
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(smb_ntlm_handshake_note3_and_succeeded_correlation PROPERTIES

# Security rule (smb.hpp's/ntlm.hpp's own file header comment): LmChallengeResponse/
# NtChallengeResponse/EncryptedRandomSessionKey are NEVER rendered, in any form -- not the raw
# bytes, not even presence/length -- anywhere in this decoder's JSON output, only
# ntlm_user_name/ntlm_domain_name (identity, not proof-of-possession material). Checked against
# the AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE emitted for flow A's own successful handshake.

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"ntlm_message_type\": \"AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE\",\n *\"ntlm_user_name\": \"jdoe\",\n *\"ntlm_domain_name\": \"CORP\","
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "lm_challenge|nt_challenge|LmChallenge|NtChallenge|session_key|\\\\xAA\\\\xAA|\\\\xBB\\\\xBB")

# SMB is GateKind::TcpPortIndependent -- a NEGOTIATE exchange on an arbitrary, non-configured TCP

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Netlogon/DCE-RPC (MS-NRPC/MS-RPCE), carried inside SMB2 WRITE/READ/IOCTL against a tracked
# "\PIPE\netlogon" FileId -- the fourth and final Windows AD-suite protocol (see dcerpc.hpp's/
# netlogon.hpp's own file header comments for the wire format -- the generic DCE/RPC PDU
# envelope, NDR conformant-varying strings, the FileId->bind->call_id correlation depth, and
# the five curated notes). No independent wire gate: this traffic is recognized only via a
# tracked FileId opened against a pipe share whose CREATE Name (after stripping a leading
# \PIPE\ prefix) equals "netlogon". Fixture generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_netlogon_sample() -- tests/sample_netlogon.pcap (TCP, 142 packets across 9 independent
# flows A-I): A) a normal ReqChallenge->NetrServerAuthenticate3 handshake for WIN10-PC$ (note 1
# positive, notes 2/3/4 negative controls); B) an all-zero-ClientChallenge NetrServerReqChallenge
# from "ATTACKER-PC" (note 2 positive -- the Zerologon wire signature); C) a
# NetrServerAuthenticate2 handshake for LEGACY-PC$ (note 3 positive, note 1 positive); D) a
# NetrServerAuthenticate3 handshake with AccountName "WORKSTATION1" not ending in "$" despite a
# WorkstationSecureChannel type (note 4 positive, note 1 positive); E) the same shape with
# AccountName "WORKSTATION1$" (note 4 negative control, note 1 positive); F) a
# NetrServerPasswordSet2 call for WIN10-PC$ (note 5 positive); G) a NetrServerPasswordSet2 call
# sent sealed (RPC_C_AUTHN_LEVEL_PKT_PRIVACY) -- exercises the "sealed, N bytes, not decoded"
# fallback, no notes; H) a bind to a non-Netlogon interface UUID on a netlogon-named pipe --
# exercises the bind-interface-confirmation gate, structural-only, no notes; a bare
# NetrLogonUasLogon-shaped CREATE against pipe name "lsarpc" -- proves an untracked pipe name
# never even reaches the DCE/RPC parser (zero dcerpc_messages emitted); I) the same handshake as
# flow A for WIN10-PC$ but carried over IOCTL/FSCTL_PIPE_TRANSCEIVE instead of WRITE+READ (note 1
# positive, proving both real-world transport shapes decode identically). All expectations below
# were captured from the actual built binary's output against this fixture -- confirmed via
# direct --format text/--format json/--stats inspection (the "manual smoke test BEFORE writing
# CMakeLists.txt tests" discipline every prior phase's delivery used), not hand-computed or
# guessed at.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# CREATE request decodes the pipe Name (stripped of any \PIPE\ prefix); CREATE response decodes
# the 16-byte FileId -- both fields smb.hpp/smb.cpp read for the very first time this phase,
# needed regardless of Netlogon since neither was read at all before.
add_test(NAME netlogon_create_request_and_response_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_create_request_and_response_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"create_name\": \"netlogon\",.*\"file_id\": \"0000000000000002:00000000f00d0002\",")

# NetrServerReqChallenge (opnum 4) request/response field decode -- PrimaryName (unique
# pointer)/ComputerName (ref pointer)/ClientChallenge (presence via client_credential_all_zero
# only, never the raw 8 bytes).
add_test(NAME netlogon_reqchallenge_request_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_reqchallenge_request_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge\",\n *\"call_id\": 3,\n *\"is_response\": false,\n *\"primary_name\": \"DC1\",\n *\"computer_name\": \"WIN10-PC\",\n *\"client_credential_all_zero\": false,\n *\"summary\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge computer=WIN10-PC\"")

add_test(NAME netlogon_reqchallenge_response_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_reqchallenge_response_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge\",\n *\"call_id\": 3,\n *\"is_response\": true,\n *\"status_name\": \"STATUS_SUCCESS\",\n *\"summary\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge response status=STATUS_SUCCESS\"")

# NetrServerAuthenticate3 (opnum 26) request/response field decode -- AccountName/
# SecureChannelType (the 16-bit NDR enum, named)/NegotiateFlags/AccountRid, the fullest-decoded
# opnum this phase has.

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerAuthenticate3\",\n *\"call_id\": 4,\n *\"is_response\": false,\n *\"primary_name\": \"DC1\",\n *\"account_name\": \"WIN10-PC\\$\",\n *\"computer_name\": \"WIN10-PC\",\n *\"secure_channel_type\": \"WorkstationSecureChannel\",\n *\"client_credential_all_zero\": false,\n *\"negotiate_flags\": 1630535679,\n *\"summary\": \"NetrServerAuthenticate3 account=WIN10-PC\\$\"")

add_test(NAME netlogon_authenticate3_response_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerAuthenticate3\",\n *\"call_id\": 4,\n *\"is_response\": true,\n *\"account_rid\": 1105,\n *\"status_name\": \"STATUS_SUCCESS\",\n *\"summary\": \"NetrServerAuthenticate3 response status=STATUS_SUCCESS\"")

# Curated note 1 -- closing correlation on the terminal NetrServerAuthenticate3 response for flow

# Curated note 2 POSITIVE -- an all-zero NetrServerReqChallenge ClientChallenge, the Zerologon

# (client_credential_all_zero: true, never the raw bytes).

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SMB2 WRITE Request  \\(client 192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -- port-heuristic\\)\n *note: Netlogon ClientChallenge is all-zero bytes -- the wire signature of CVE-2020-1472 \\(\"Zerologon\"\\)\; a real challenge is an 8-byte random nonce, so this essentially never occurs in benign traffic, though presence alone does not prove a completed compromise")

add_test(NAME netlogon_zerologon_zero_challenge_json_field

# Curated note 3 POSITIVE -- legacy NetrServerAuthenticate2 (opnum 15) used instead of the modern

# Curated note 5 -- NetrServerPasswordSet2 observed (flow F), the literal post-Zerologon
# password-reset step; deliberately NOT sticky (fires every occurrence, unlike notes 2-4). JSON
# check doubles as the "password material never rendered" test: only authenticator_present (bool)
# and clear_new_password_length (int) are emitted, never the Authenticator/ClearNewPassword bytes
# themselves -- the same posture NTLM's own LmChallengeResponse/NtChallengeResponse test enforces.
add_test(NAME netlogon_password_set2_note5_and_material_never_rendered
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format text --verbose)

# Sealed-call fallback (flow G, RPC_C_AUTHN_LEVEL_PKT_PRIVACY): auth_level and sealed=true are
# read from the sec_trailer's own unencrypted fixed header, but the stub is never parsed as
# plaintext NDR -- an honest "sealed, N bytes, not decoded" summary with no account/credential
# fields at all, and (see the negative-control test below) no curated note fires from it either.
add_test(NAME netlogon_sealed_call_fallback_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_sealed_call_fallback_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": 30,\n *\"auth_level\": \"RPC_C_AUTHN_LEVEL_PKT_PRIVACY\",\n *\"sealed\": true,\n *\"summary\": \"DCE/RPC request \\(opnum 30\\)\"[^\n]*\n *\\}\n *\\],\n *\"netlogon_calls\": \\[\n *\\{\n *\"opnum\": \"NetrServerPasswordSet2\",\n *\"call_id\": 16,\n *\"is_response\": false,\n *\"sealed\": true,\n *\"summary\": \"sealed, 32 bytes, not decoded\"")

add_test(NAME netlogon_sealed_call_produces_no_curated_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_sealed_call_produces_no_curated_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\n#97  [0-9.]+  192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53006 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:445 \\(microsoft-ds\\)  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 WRITE Request  \\(client 192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -- port-heuristic\\)\n#98  "
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "sealed")

# Bind-interface-confirmation gate (flow H): a bind to a non-Netlogon abstract syntax UUID on a
# netlogon-named pipe leaves the context's later request/response pairs structural-only (opnum
# numeric, no netlogon_calls emitted at all) -- the defensive edge case where the pipe NAME alone
# is not trusted as proof of which RPC interface is actually bound.
add_test(NAME netlogon_non_netlogon_interface_bind_structural_only_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_non_netlogon_interface_bind_structural_only_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"bind_contexts\": \\[\\{\"context_id\": 0, \"abstract_syntax_uuid\": \"367abb81-9844-35f1-ad32-98f038001003\", \"is_netlogon\": false\\}\\],\n *\"summary\": \"DCE/RPC bind\".*\"opnum\": 4,\n *\"summary\": \"DCE/RPC request \\(opnum 4\\)\"\n *\\}\n *\\],\n *\"summary\": \"SMB2 WRITE Request\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge\",\n *\"call_id\": 18")

add_test(NAME netlogon_non_netlogon_interface_bind_no_curated_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_non_netlogon_interface_bind_no_curated_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\n#111  [0-9.]+  192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53007 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:445 \\(microsoft-ds\\)  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 WRITE Request  \\(client 192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -- port-heuristic\\)\n#112  ")

# Flow H's own pipe is named "lsarpc" -- since the SAMR/LSARPC batch (this file's own later
# lsarpc_* tests), that name IS now tracked, so this is no longer a never-parsed negative control
# (an earlier revision of this test predates LSARPC support and asserted the opposite). What it
# actually exercises now: flow H's own bind negotiates the NETLOGON interface UUID on this
# "lsarpc"-named pipe (a deliberately mismatched pipe-name/interface-UUID combination), so the
# envelope IS parsed (dcerpc_messages appears, is_netlogon: true on the bind) but LsarpcPipeState's
# own bound_context_is_interface check (is_lsarpc_interface_uuid) never accepts it -- the LSARPC-side
# analog of netlogon_non_netlogon_interface_bind_structural_only_json above, proven by no
# "lsarpc_calls"/"samr_calls" key ever appearing for this FileId.
add_test(NAME lsarpc_pipe_name_netlogon_interface_bind_never_lsarpc_calls_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(lsarpc_pipe_name_netlogon_interface_bind_never_lsarpc_calls_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"create_name\": \"lsarpc\",.*\"file_id\": \"000000000000000a:00000000f00d000a\",\n *\"dcerpc_messages\": \\[\n *\\{\n *\"ptype\": \"bind\",.*\"abstract_syntax_uuid\": \"12345678-1234-abcd-ef00-01234567cffb\", \"is_netlogon\": true"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"(lsarpc|samr)_calls\"")

# Both real-world transport shapes decode identically -- flow I repeats flow A's own

# --stats netlogon opnum counts -- NetrServerAuthenticate2=1 (flow C), NetrServerAuthenticate3=4

# Cross-interface note -- SAMR + LSARPC pipes both open on flow C's own session; fires once,

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_samr_lsarpc.pcap" --format text --verbose)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DRSUAPI (MS-DRSR), phase 3 of the SAMR/LSARPC/SRVSVC/WKSSVC/DRSUAPI batch -- see drsuapi.hpp's
# own file header comment for the wire format, the narrow four-opnum coverage table, and --
# critically -- the EMPIRICALLY-DISCOVERED SCOPE CAVEAT: real DRSUAPI traffic predominantly rides
# a dynamically-negotiated raw TCP connection (resolved via the port-135 endpoint mapper), not an
# SMB named pipe, so this decoder (and the fixture below) only ever demonstrate the narrow "also
# exposed over a named pipe" case, not real-world DCSync traffic as it actually appears on the
# wire. Fixture generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_drsuapi_sample() --
# tests/sample_drsuapi.pcap (TCP, 3 independent flows A-C -- see that function's own doc comment
# for the full per-flow breakdown). All expectations below were captured from the actual built
# binary's output against this fixture -- confirmed via direct --format text/--format json/--stats
# inspection, not hand-computed or guessed at.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# DRSBind (0) request/response -- non-NULL puuidClientDsa (full field decode), and a response whose

# follow it (both are correctly decoded here, not garbage/misaligned).

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "999999")

# DRSBind (0) request again -- NULL puuidClientDsa this time: negative control, no client_dsa_guid
# field at all (the regex below requires is_response/summary to be textually ADJACENT to call_id 4,
# so any intervening client_dsa_guid line would break the match).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# QUIC -- Tier 2, joining HTTPS (see quic.hpp's own file header comment and notable_it_protocols.hpp
# for why). tests/sample_quic.pcap (tools/make_quic_sample_pcap.py) has 13 packets: #1 a genuine
# client Initial, decrypted end to end with its ClientHello SNI extracted; #2 Version Negotiation;
# #3-5 Handshake/0-RTT/Retry, each name-only but each now requiring the per-type structural
# cross-check described below; #6 a short-header (1-RTT) packet, the weakest, port-only fallback;
# #7 an Initial whose AEAD tag doesn't verify (simulating a server's own Initial, which this decoder
# can never decrypt -- see quic.hpp's file header comment); #8 non-QUIC junk on QUIC's own default
# port, proving no false positive; #9 a short-header packet on a non-standard port, proving that
# fallback's own internal port gate; #10 (round-one bug fix regression, see below) a 0-RTT-shaped
# packet whose byte0 satisfies Header Form/Fixed Bit/type bits but whose trailer is NOT structurally
# self-consistent, proving it now falls through to generic "udp" rather than being misdetected;
# #11-12 (round-two bug fix regression, see below) an Initial-shaped packet whose Token-Length/
# Length-field pair both decode to 0, and a Retry-shaped packet whose Version isn't QUIC v1 --
# proving both now fall through to generic "udp" too; #13 (round-two positive control) a genuinely
# truncated real v1 Initial packet (a plausible, large Length field, but far fewer bytes actually
# captured), proving round two's fix didn't also reject legitimate truncated captures. See
# decoder.cpp's own dispatch-ordering comment (just above its HART-IP UDP check) for why QUIC's
# recognition call had to move ahead of HART-IP's: QUIC v1's Version field lands on the exact same
# two payload bytes HART-IP's own MessageType/MessageID gate reads, and is SYSTEMATICALLY 0x00/0x00
# there for every long-header packet type this fixture exercises -- a guaranteed collision, not a
# coincidental one.
#
# Bug fix, round one (post-release, Jurgen's own report): packets #3-5's own Handshake/0-RTT/Retry
# recognition originally accepted ANY long-header packet whose byte0 had the Header Form bit, Fixed
# Bit, and a non-Initial type value set -- only 4 bits of the whole packet, true of roughly 1 in 4
# arbitrary UDP payloads port-independently. A real capture proved this too weak: a busy NBT-NS
# (UDP port 137) broadcast segment's own 2-byte Transaction ID landed on byte0/byte1 often enough to
# misdetect a large fraction of that segment's non-NBT-NS-parsing traffic as QUIC 0-RTT/Handshake
# packets. Fixed by requiring the same kind of self-consistent structural cross-check every other
# long-header type already had (Version Negotiation's own whole-number-of-4-byte-versions check;
# Initial's own Length-field/captured-bytes cross-check): 0-RTT/Handshake now read their own Length
# field (RFC 9000 17.2.3/17.2.4) and require it to describe a byte count that actually fits within
# what was captured and is at least large enough for a 1-byte Packet Number plus a 16-byte AEAD tag;
# Retry now requires its own mandatory 16-byte Retry Integrity Tag (RFC 9000 17.2.5) to actually be
# present. See try_recognize_quic's own comment in quic.cpp for the full writeup, and packet #10
# above/quic_0rtt_type_bits_alone_not_misdetected below for the regression test.
#
# Bug fix, round two (post-release, Jurgen's own SECOND report, against the same real NBT-NS
# capture): round one's own checks were each individually still too weak. Retry's "16 trailing bytes
# exist" check is true of nearly any ordinary-sized UDP payload (Retry has no Length field to
# cross-check at all -- see quic.cpp's own comment for why not), so it now also requires an exact
# QUIC-v1 Version match. Initial's pre-existing Length-field check conflated two different failure
# modes into one tolerant "truncated capture" fallback: `length_field < 17` (structurally impossible
# for a real Initial packet, any capture length) was treated the same as `pn_offset + length_field >
# captured size` (a plausible field that just wasn't fully captured -- genuine truncation); only the
# second one still gets the tolerant match now. See try_recognize_quic's own comment in quic.cpp for
# the full writeup, and packets #11-13 above / the three quic_*_round_two_* tests below.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME quic_client_initial_decrypted_sni
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(quic_client_initial_decrypted_sni PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"protocol\": \"quic\",\n +\"summary\": \"QUIC Initial packet, decrypted \\(RFC 9001 publicly-derivable keys\\) -- ClientHello SNI: scada-vendor-cloud\\.example\\.com\"")

add_test(NAME quic_protocol_filter_isolates_family
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap" --protocol lateral-movement --format text)
set_tests_properties(quic_protocol_filter_isolates_family PROPERTIES
  # Packets #1-7 plus #13 (round two's positive truncated-capture control) are quic under this
  # filter -- 8 total, nothing else in this fixture is Tier 2 -- and since HART-IP's own dispatch is
  # entirely disabled by --protocol lateral-movement (not just reordered), packets #8/#9/#11/#12 fall
  # straight through to generic udp with no [hartip] tag at all.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[quic\\].*\\[quic\\].*\\[quic\\].*\\[quic\\].*\\[quic\\].*\\[quic\\].*\\[quic\\].*\\[quic\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[hartip\\]")

add_test(NAME quic_stats_counted_in_lateral_movement_tier
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap")
set_tests_properties(quic_stats_counted_in_lateral_movement_tier PROPERTIES
  # quic +8 (packet #13, round two's positive truncated-capture control, is the 8th quic match);
  # udp +5, not +3, now that packets #11/#12 (round two's own negative-control regression fixtures)
  # correctly fall through to generic udp too, alongside pre-existing packets #8/#9/#10.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "quic +8\n *udp +5")

add_test(NAME quic_inventory_notable_protocols
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap")
set_tests_properties(quic_inventory_notable_protocols PROPERTIES
  # 8, not 7, now that packet #13 (round two's positive truncated-capture control) is also quic.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "NOTABLE IT PROTOCOLS \\(8\\):\n(.*\n)*.*\\[1\\] quic  \\(lateral-movement\\)")

add_test(NAME quic_0rtt_type_bits_alone_not_misdetected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(quic_0rtt_type_bits_alone_not_misdetected PROPERTIES
  # Bug fix regression test (see this section's own header comment and quic.cpp's comment on
  # try_recognize_quic): packet #10's byte0 alone satisfies Header Form/Fixed Bit/type bits -- the
  # exact shape that used to be misdetected as [quic] -- but its trailer has no self-consistent
  # Length field, so it must now fall through to the generic udp tag instead.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 27 byte\\(s\\) on port 54109->443"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "54109->443  \\[quic\\]")

add_test(NAME quic_initial_zero_length_field_not_misdetected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(quic_initial_zero_length_field_not_misdetected PROPERTIES
  # Bug fix regression test, round two (see this section's own header comment and quic.cpp's comment
  # on try_recognize_quic): packet #11's Token-Length/Length-field pair both decode to 0 -- the exact
  # shape the old combined check used to wave through as "truncated capture" -- so it must now fall
  # through to the generic udp tag instead, the same "not a match" treatment a structurally
  # implausible field already gets on the 0-RTT/Handshake paths.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 25 byte\\(s\\) on port 54110->443"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "54110 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:443  \\[quic\\]")

add_test(NAME quic_retry_wrong_version_not_misdetected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(quic_retry_wrong_version_not_misdetected PROPERTIES
  # Bug fix regression test, round two: packet #12 has a fully self-consistent 16-byte trailer --
  # everything round one's own Retry check required -- but a Version field that isn't QUIC v1, so it
  # must now fall through to the generic udp tag instead of being misdetected as [quic] Retry.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 43 byte\\(s\\) on port 54111->443"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "54111 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:443  \\[quic\\]")

add_test(NAME quic_initial_genuinely_truncated_still_matches
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(quic_initial_genuinely_truncated_still_matches PROPERTIES
  # Positive control, round two: packet #13 is a real QUIC v1 Initial packet whose Length field
  # declares a large, entirely plausible value (1200) that simply wasn't fully captured -- proving
  # round two's fix didn't overcorrect and reject a genuinely truncated capture along with the
  # implausible-length-field case packets #11/#12 above exercise.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "54112 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:443  \\[quic\\]  QUIC Initial packet \\(truncated capture -- not decrypted\\)")
