# Finding 2, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch160.md: a malicious if_tsresol
# byte could declare a units-per-second figure that doesn't fit in a uint64_t, making
# fill_pcapng_timestamp's static_cast<uint64_t>(...) undefined behavior (pcap_reader.cpp). Fixed
# by bounding the exponent before computing it (parse_if_tsresol_option) plus a defense-in-depth
# clamp at the conversion site itself (fill_pcapng_timestamp). sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng
# (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_pcapng_implausible_tsresol_sample) has three interfaces:
# 0 (binary, exponent 127 -- far past the 63 boundary), 1 (decimal, exponent 100 -- far past the
# 19 boundary), both of which must fall back to the same microsecond default this function
# already uses for a malformed option; and 2 (binary, exponent 63 -- exactly the largest power of
# two that still fits in a uint64_t), which must NOT fall back, proving the boundary itself isn't
# off-by-one rejected. The whole point of this test is simply that decoding completes cleanly and
# produces this exact, deterministic output instead of crashing or invoking UB -- a golden-output
# test, the same bar every other exact-value test in this file is held to, confirmed against the
# actual CLI before being written here (not guessed at). Packet 3's own oddly large negative
# relative timestamp is a legitimate, defined consequence of interface 2's own genuinely absurd
# (2^63 units/second) but in-bounds resolution -- not a defect this fix introduces or needs to
# smooth over; only interfaces 0 and 1 (the ones actually being tested for the fallback) need to
# look sane, and they do (a clean 1-microsecond delta between packets 1 and 2, exactly what
# falling back to the 1e6 default on both produces).
add_test(NAME pcapng_implausible_tsresol_falls_back_without_ub
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(pcapng_implausible_tsresol_falls_back_without_ub PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0.000000[^\n]*\n.*\n#2  0.000001[^\n]*\n.*\n.*\n#3  -1699999999.999816")

add_test(NAME pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_completes_all_three_packets
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng" --format json)
set_tests_properties(pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_completes_all_three_packets PROPERTIES
  # Each packet's own index+timestamp pair (adjacent lines, confirmed against the real JSON
  # output first) -- proves all three packets decoded cleanly: interfaces 0/1's implausible
  # exponents both falling back to the same 1e6 default (hence identical whole-second epoch,
  # 1-microsecond apart), interface 2's boundary case computing its own (legitimately odd, see
  # the text-format test above) but still well-defined result. Three independent checks in one
  # regex (rather than one long chain spanning all three packet objects) to avoid depending on
  # every field in between, which is unrelated to what this test is actually confirming.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 1,\n *\"timestamp\": 1700000000.000000,")
add_test(NAME pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_packet2_timestamp
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng" --format json)
set_tests_properties(pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_packet2_timestamp PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 2,\n *\"timestamp\": 1700000000.000001,")
add_test(NAME pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_packet3_timestamp
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng" --format json)
set_tests_properties(pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_packet3_timestamp PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 3,\n *\"timestamp\": 0.000184,")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# terminal_escape (output.cpp, finding 4, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch160.md):
# packet-derived text (here, an MQTT PUBLISH topic straight off the wire) can carry raw C0 control
# bytes, including ESC (0x1B). TextWriter/FieldsWriter used to write such text straight to the
# real terminal -- an attacker-controlled capture could therefore emit real ANSI escape sequences
# (manipulating the analyst's terminal, e.g. faking colored alert text) or raw newlines (forging
# fake extra packet lines). terminal_escape() renders every C0/DEL byte as a literal "\xNN" escape
# instead, in TEXT-mode output only -- JSON/CSV keep their own existing, different, complete
# escaping rules untouched (json_escape already renders ESC as \u001b; CSV is deliberately left
# as-is per the review's own guidance). The fixture's two packets carry a raw ESC-based ANSI
# injection attempt and a raw-newline forgery attempt respectively; both are confirmed against the
# actual CLI output below, not guessed at.
add_test(NAME terminal_escape_ansi_injection_sanitized_in_text_output
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_terminal_escape_injection.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(terminal_escape_ansi_injection_sanitized_in_text_output PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "PUBLISH topic=\"evil\\\\x1b\\[31mFAKE-ALERT\\\\x1b\\[0m\" qos=0")

add_test(NAME terminal_escape_newline_injection_sanitized_in_text_output
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_terminal_escape_injection.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(terminal_escape_newline_injection_sanitized_in_text_output PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "PUBLISH topic=\"evil\\\\x0afake-injected-line\" qos=0")

# FieldsWriter (-T fields) has its own, separate route to the terminal: it round-trips each field
# through a one-shot JSON encode/decode (json_escape then json_unescape_inner) to build the flat
# text representation. json_unescape_inner deliberately restores \n/\t/\r to raw bytes (but leaves
# \uXXXX, including ESC's \u001b, as literal text) -- so FieldsWriter was already safe against the
# ESC-specific attack above, but not against a restored raw newline forging an extra output line.
# This confirms terminal_escape() closes that second, independent gap too.
add_test(NAME terminal_escape_newline_injection_sanitized_in_fields_output
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_terminal_escape_injection.pcap" -T fields -e summary)
set_tests_properties(terminal_escape_newline_injection_sanitized_in_fields_output PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "PUBLISH topic=\"evil\\\\x0afake-injected-line\" qos=0")

# JSON output must be unaffected by terminal_escape (it is never applied to JsonWriter): the raw
# ESC byte still comes through json_escape's own existing \u001b control-character escaping,
# exactly as before this fix.
add_test(NAME terminal_escape_json_output_unaffected_still_uses_u001b
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_terminal_escape_injection.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(terminal_escape_json_output_unaffected_still_uses_u001b PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"PUBLISH topic=\\\\\"evil\\\\u001b\\[31mFAKE-ALERT\\\\u001b\\[0m\\\\\" qos=0")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Resolver (resolver.hpp/resolver.cpp): OUI (MAC vendor) resolution (off by default, --mac-vendor, to
# keep output compact), hostname resolution (off by default, --resolve/--hosts, file-only --
# never live DNS), and service name resolution (on by default, --nn/--services) -- see
# decoder.cpp's src_mac/dst_mac gap-fix and output.cpp's TextWriter/JsonWriter/CsvWriter for how
# these are rendered. All tests below use tests/sample_modbus.pcap, whose two endpoints' MACs
# (00:0c:29:11:22:33/00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc) are both in oui_table.gen.hpp's MA-L table as "VMware",
# and tests/hosts_sample.txt / tests/services_sample.txt (see their own file headers) as the
# --hosts/--services fixtures.
#
# In TEXT output specifically, the entire "eth <src> -> <dst>" line is itself gated behind
# --ether (off by default, mirrors tcpdump's own -e -- see output.hpp/output.cpp's show_mac_;
# --ether has no short alias of its own in this codebase -- -e is reserved for -T fields' own
# --field, tshark's own convention -- see the "-T fields / -e / -f / -c / -a / -w / -x" section
# further down).
# --mac-vendor implies --ether (cli_main.cpp: there'd be nothing to attach a vendor name to
# otherwise), so --mac-vendor alone still shows the full "eth <mac> (<vendor>) -> <mac> (<vendor>)"
# line. --ether alone shows the MAC pair with no vendor annotation. JSON/CSV are NOT gated by
# --ether at all -- src_mac/dst_mac stay unconditional base fields there (like src_ip/dst_ip)
# regardless of --ether; --mac-vendor only ever controls their *_mac_vendor annotation fields, in
# every format.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

set(RESOLVER_HOSTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/hosts_sample.txt")
set(RESOLVER_SERVICES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/services_sample.txt")

# --- --ether (the eth line itself), off by default, text-output only ---------------------

add_test(NAME resolver_mac_and_vendor_hidden_by_default_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_mac_and_vendor_hidden_by_default_text PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29|VMware")

add_test(NAME resolver_ether_flag_shows_mac_without_vendor_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --ether --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_ether_flag_shows_mac_without_vendor_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc\n"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "VMware")

# --- OUI (MAC vendor) vendor annotation, off by default, --mac-vendor opts in (and implies --ether) -----

add_test(NAME resolver_oui_vendor_hidden_by_default_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(resolver_oui_vendor_hidden_by_default_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"src_mac\": \"00:0c:29:11:22:33\","
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "_mac_vendor")

add_test(NAME resolver_oui_flag_shows_vendor_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --mac-vendor --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_oui_flag_shows_vendor_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29:11:22:33 \\(VMware\\) -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc \\(VMware\\)")

# --mac-vendor alone (no explicit --ether) must still show the eth line -- --mac-vendor implies --ether (cli_main.cpp).
add_test(NAME resolver_oui_flag_alone_implies_ether_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --mac-vendor --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_oui_flag_alone_implies_ether_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29:11:22:33")

add_test(NAME resolver_oui_flag_shows_vendor_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --mac-vendor --format json)
set_tests_properties(resolver_oui_flag_shows_vendor_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"src_mac\": \"00:0c:29:11:22:33\",\n *\"dst_mac\": \"00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc\",\n *\"src_mac_vendor\": \"VMware\",\n *\"dst_mac_vendor\": \"VMware\",")

# src_mac/dst_mac themselves (the base gap-fix, independent of OUI resolution and of --ether)
# are always present for an Ethernet-linktype capture in JSON/CSV, even with OUI resolution left
# at its off-by-default posture -- this is the actual base value, not an annotation, so OUI
# resolution only ever adds a vendor name, never gates the MAC itself. --ether only affects
# TEXT output (see this section's own header comment above) -- CSV keeps showing it regardless.
add_test(NAME resolver_base_src_dst_mac_always_present_in_csv_regardless_of_oui_or_ether
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format csv)
set_tests_properties(resolver_base_src_dst_mac_always_present_in_csv_regardless_of_oui_or_ether PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33,00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc,,,")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Gap fix (a necessary, deliberate part of this feature, not scope creep -- see resolver.hpp's
# file header and docs/MANUAL.md): src_mac/dst_mac are now rendered for EVERY protocol on an
# Ethernet-linktype capture, not just the raw-Ethernet ones (GOOSE/SV/EtherCAT/PROFINET/STP) whose
# own MAC-bearing fields (stp_root_mac/etc.) were already shown. sample_enip.pcap is a plain
# IPv4-based protocol (EtherNet/IP explicit messaging over TCP) that never had any MAC output at
# all before this feature.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME resolver_mac_shown_for_plain_ip_protocol_not_just_raw_ethernet
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap" --ether --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_mac_shown_for_plain_ip_protocol_not_just_raw_ethernet PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[enip\\].*\n *eth 00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VLAN ID display (output.cpp's TextWriter/JsonWriter/CsvWriter show_vlan_; --no-vlan in
# cli_main.cpp). DecodedPacket::has_vlan_tag/vlan_id are already unconditionally populated by the
# decoding layer for every Ethernet-linktype packet (link_layer.cpp's parse_ethernet unwraps a
# single 802.1Q tag) -- this is purely a display toggle, shown by default. tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap
# (see build_vlan_zones_sample in tools/make_sample_pcap.py) carries VLAN 100, VLAN 200, and one
# untagged flow, so it exercises both "tagged" and "untagged" in the same capture.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# VLAN display is independent of --ether (show_mac_) -- see output.hpp/output.cpp's own
# comments -- so a VLAN-tagged packet still gets its own "vlan <id>" line by default. Every packet
# in this fixture is non-IP (PROFINET RT/GOOSE/SV/EtherCAT), so its src_mac/dst_mac already appear
# directly on the headline itself (output.cpp's endpoint() -- see that function's own comment) with
# no --ether/--mac-vendor needed at all; there is deliberately no separate "eth <mac> -> <mac>" prefix line for
# a non-IP packet any more (write_packet() suppresses it there specifically, since it would just
# repeat what the headline already shows), so this fixture no longer has one to test.
add_test(NAME vlan_id_shown_by_default_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_shown_by_default_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc[^\n]*\\[profinet\\][^\n]*\n *vlan 100"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\n *eth ")

# --ether is now a no-op for this fixture (every packet is non-IP, so show_mac_'s own separate line
# never applies here regardless -- see this section's own header comment) -- kept as an explicit
# regression check that --ether doesn't reintroduce a combined "eth ... vlan ..." line for a non-IP
# packet the way it did before this behavior changed.
add_test(NAME vlan_id_stays_on_own_line_with_ether_for_non_ip_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --ether --format text)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_stays_on_own_line_with_ether_for_non_ip_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc[^\n]*\\[profinet\\][^\n]*\n *vlan 100"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29")

# The untagged flow (mac pair 00:0c:29:cc:55:66 -> 00:0c:29:dd:77:88) must never get a "vlan ..."
# suffix at all -- has_vlan_tag is false, not vlan_id == 0. No --ether needed any more: the untagged
# packet's own MAC pair is already on its headline by default (see this section's own header
# comment), same as every other packet in this fixture.
add_test(NAME vlan_id_omitted_for_untagged_packet_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_omitted_for_untagged_packet_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:cc:55:66 -> 00:0c:29:dd:77:88[^\n]*\\[ethercat\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:cc:55:66 -> 00:0c:29:dd:77:88[^\n]*\n *vlan")

# The MAC pair fallback itself needs neither --ether nor --mac-vendor -- it's unconditional for any
# non-IP packet (see endpoint()'s own comment) -- but the vendor-name annotation next to it still
# needs --mac-vendor explicitly (Resolver::oui_vendor() self-gates on that flag). Confirms neither flag is
# now accidentally implied by MAC display working out of the box.
add_test(NAME non_ip_mac_shown_by_default_without_vendor_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(non_ip_mac_shown_by_default_without_vendor_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:cc:55:66 -> 00:0c:29:dd:77:88"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29|VMware")

add_test(NAME vlan_id_shown_by_default_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_shown_by_default_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"dst_mac\": \"00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc\",\n *\"has_vlan_tag\": true,\n *\"vlan_id\": 100,")

# The untagged flow gets has_vlan_tag: false / vlan_id: null, never omitted entirely -- unlike an
# annotation, has_vlan_tag/vlan_id are always both present together when the flag is on, regardless
# of whether this particular packet actually carries a tag (mirrors policy_engine.cpp's own
# EthernetFlowReport JSON convention).
add_test(NAME vlan_id_null_for_untagged_packet_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_null_for_untagged_packet_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"has_vlan_tag\": false,\n *\"vlan_id\": null,")

add_test(NAME vlan_id_shown_by_default_csv
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format csv)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_shown_by_default_csv PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "profinet,\"Cyclic RT IO data \\(RT_CLASS_1, unicast\\): 8 byte\\(s\\) IO data, cycle_counter=4660 data_status=\\[Primary,Valid,Run,Ok\\] transfer_status=OK\",,100")

# --no-vlan suppresses the "  vlan 100" suffix; the headline's own MAC pair (unconditional for a
# non-IP packet, see this section's own header comment) is unaffected either way. --ether is included
# here purely as a regression check that it still doesn't reintroduce anything.
add_test(NAME no_vlan_suppresses_display_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text --no-vlan --ether)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_suppresses_display_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc[^\n]*\\[profinet\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "vlan 100|eth 00:0c:29")

# Same, without --ether: the whole vlan line disappears, the MAC pair stays exactly as it was.
add_test(NAME no_vlan_and_no_ether_suppresses_entire_eth_line_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text --no-vlan)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_and_no_ether_suppresses_entire_eth_line_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29|vlan 100")

add_test(NAME no_vlan_suppresses_display_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format json --no-vlan)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_suppresses_display_json PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "has_vlan_tag|vlan_id")

add_test(NAME no_vlan_suppresses_display_csv
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format csv --no-vlan)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_suppresses_display_csv PROPERTIES
  # vlan_id (empty, suppressed by --no-vlan) is immediately followed by the trailing `time` column
  # (see time_format.hpp/output.cpp's `-t`/--time-format/--time-offset) -- relative's default
  # rendering is elapsed-since-first-packet, so this pcap's first packet is asserted literally as
  # 0.000000 here, same "hardcode this sample's known value" style vlan_id_shown_by_default_csv
  # above already uses for its own trailing column. `time` is no longer the row's last column --
  # direction_source/direction_client_ip (empty here: this is a raw PROFINET RT frame, not TCP, so
  # FlowDirectionTracker never touches it -- see CsvWriter::write_packet) now follow it, then
  # decode's own --detect-highlight columns (has_detect_finding=false plus three empty fields --
  # this frame matches none of DetectEngine's always-notable findings), hence the six trailing
  # fields (two empty, "false", three more empty) before the newline.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "profinet,\"Cyclic RT IO data \\(RT_CLASS_1, unicast\\): 8 byte\\(s\\) IO data, cycle_counter=4660 data_status=\\[Primary,Valid,Run,Ok\\] transfer_status=OK\",,,0\\.000000,,,false,,,\n"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "transfer_status=OK\",,100")

# --mac-vendor and --no-vlan are independent toggles -- suppressing VLAN display must not affect the
# vendor annotation either way. --mac-vendor alone (no --ether) is enough here: the vendor name attaches
# directly to the headline's own MAC pair for a non-IP packet like this one, no separate eth line
# involved any more -- see this section's own header comment.
add_test(NAME no_vlan_does_not_affect_oui
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text --no-vlan --mac-vendor)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_does_not_affect_oui PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 \\(VMware\\) -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc \\(VMware\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29|vlan 100")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `-t`/`--time-format` mnemonics (time_format.hpp/time_format.cpp; TextWriter's leading "#<index>
# <time>" header -- see output.cpp's own use of TimeRenderer). sample_modbus.pcap's own 3 packets
# (see tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_modbus_sample) have known, fixed timestamps: 1700000000
# .000000, 1700000001.001000, 1700000002.002000 -- exactly 1.001s / 1.001s apart -- deliberately
# uneven spacing so relative/delta/epoch are all distinguishable from each other in the assertions
# below, not just from zero. This section previously had no dedicated coverage at all (only one
# CSV test elsewhere incidentally hardcoded the epoch-format value of a different pcap's first
# packet) -- added here as part of flipping the default from epoch to relative, so the default
# this project now actually ships is verified, not just the explicit mnemonics.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# r/relative, the default: elapsed since the first packet, so packet 1 is always 0.000000
# regardless of its raw epoch value.
add_test(NAME time_format_relative_is_the_default
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(time_format_relative_is_the_default PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  .*\n.*#2  1\\.001000  .*\n.*#3  2\\.002000  ")

add_test(NAME time_format_r_mnemonic_same_as_relative
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t r)
set_tests_properties(time_format_r_mnemonic_same_as_relative PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  ")

# e/epoch: raw seconds since the Unix epoch, unchanged from the pcap's own timestamp field.
add_test(NAME time_format_epoch_explicit_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t epoch)
set_tests_properties(time_format_epoch_explicit_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  1700000000\\.000000  .*\n.*#2  1700000001\\.001000  ")

add_test(NAME time_format_e_mnemonic_same_as_epoch
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t e)
set_tests_properties(time_format_e_mnemonic_same_as_epoch PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  1700000000\\.000000  ")

# The raw "timestamp" JSON field is always the epoch double, regardless of -t -- only the "time"
# field it sits alongside is affected. Asserted here with the default (relative) -t left in place,
# to prove -t's default change doesn't leak into the machine-parseable raw field.
add_test(NAME time_format_does_not_affect_raw_timestamp_json_field
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(time_format_does_not_affect_raw_timestamp_json_field PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"timestamp\": 1700000000\\.000000,.*\"time\": \"0\\.000000\"")

# d/delta: elapsed since the previous packet -- packet 1 has no previous packet, so it's 0.000000
# same as relative; packets 2 and 3 are both 1.001000 apart despite different relative offsets,
# which is exactly what distinguishes delta from relative.
add_test(NAME time_format_delta_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t delta)
set_tests_properties(time_format_delta_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  .*\n.*#2  1\\.001000  .*\n.*#3  1\\.001000  ")

# a/absolute (HH:MM:SS.ffffff) and ad/absolute-date (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff), UTC by default
# (--time-offset) -- 1700000000 is 2023-11-14 22:13:20 UTC.
add_test(NAME time_format_absolute_utc_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t absolute)
set_tests_properties(time_format_absolute_utc_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  22:13:20\\.000000Z  ")

add_test(NAME time_format_absolute_date_utc_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t ad)
set_tests_properties(time_format_absolute_date_utc_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  2023-11-14 22:13:20\\.000000Z  ")

# --time-offset with a fixed "+HH:MM" shifts absolute/absolute-date's rendered wall-clock time and
# suffix; +02:00 turns 22:13:20 UTC into 00:13:20 the next calendar day.
add_test(NAME time_format_absolute_date_fixed_offset_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t ad --time-offset +02:00)
set_tests_properties(time_format_absolute_date_fixed_offset_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  2023-11-15 00:13:20\\.000000\\+02:00  ")

# --time-offset is meaningless for relative/delta/epoch (only absolute/absolute-date consult it)
# -- given anyway, it's silently ignored rather than rejected, since the flags are independent and
# nothing about the combination is actually invalid.
add_test(NAME time_offset_ignored_for_relative
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t relative --time-offset +02:00)
set_tests_properties(time_offset_ignored_for_relative PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  ")

# An unrecognized -t value is rejected at CLI-parse time (CLI::IsMember), same convention as
# --format's own bad-value handling.
add_test(NAME time_format_bad_value_rejected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t bogus)
set_tests_properties(time_format_bad_value_rejected PROPERTIES
  WILL_FAIL TRUE)

# An attack-pattern packet (DecodedPacket::has_attack_signature/attack_signature_kind, decoder.hpp
# -- set from attack_detect.hpp/ipv6_attack_detect.hpp's own curated notes, see decoder.cpp's six
# observe_*() call sites) used to get its WHOLE head line colored kBoldRed under --color; reverted
# to a narrowly-scoped "[attack: <kind>]" tag (mirroring detect-highlighting's own "[detect: ...]"
# tag, see the color_detect_only_* tests below) after a direct report against a real capture where
# attack_detect.hpp's own flood counters and `decode`'s own detect-highlighting feature both fired
# on overlapping traffic, producing multiple different reasons for a fully red line -- see
# TextWriter::write_packet's own comment (output.cpp) and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md ROADMAP item 99 for
# the full history. Packet #1 of sample_attack_detect.pcap is the LAND attack scenario (TCP SYN,
# identical src/dst -- see attack_detect_land above). The pattern below pins the exact shape: no
# bold-red before "#1", the "[tcp]" tag keeps its own plain kDim protocol_tag_color, the summary is
# unstyled, and bold red starts only at the two spaces immediately before "[attack:" and ends right
# after the tag's own closing "]".
add_test(NAME color_attack_pattern_tag_scoped_not_whole_line
  COMMAND conduitscope --color decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_attack_detect.pcap")
set_tests_properties(color_attack_pattern_tag_scoped_not_whole_line PROPERTIES
  # A lone "." stands in for the raw ESC (0x1B) byte at each point a new SGR escape starts right
  # after the previous one's reset, with no literal text between them (e.g. "\033[0m\033[2m") --
  # CMake's own regex engine matches literal text across that invisible byte, but only if the
  # pattern accounts for it; verified against this exact fixture's real output before being
  # written, matching this project's own "never write a CTest assertion you haven't confirmed
  # against real output" discipline.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  192\\.168\\.1\\.77:4444 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.77:4444  .\\[2m\\[tcp\\].\\[0m  TCP segment 4444 -> 4444 with no payload \\(handshake/ACK/teardown\\).\\[1\;31m  \\[attack: land\\].\\[0m"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1;31m#1")

# Packet #2 (an ordinary TCP segment, no attack signature) must NOT get any tag or color at all --
# proves the coloring/tagging is keyed on DecodedPacket::has_attack_signature, not applied to every
# packet once --color is on, and not "sticky" from packet #1's own tag above it.
add_test(NAME color_non_attack_packet_not_reddened
  COMMAND conduitscope --color decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_attack_detect.pcap")
set_tests_properties(color_non_attack_packet_not_reddened PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1;31m#2|#2  [^\n]*\\[attack:")

# The "[attack: <kind>]" tag itself is plain text, not color-only -- unlike the old whole-line-red
# design (which left an attack-pattern packet with NO visible signal at all under --no-color/piped
# output in default, non-verbose text -- see TextWriter::write_packet's own comment), the tag
# survives --no-color unchanged; only the red emphasis is color-gated.
add_test(NAME color_attack_pattern_tag_survives_no_color
  COMMAND conduitscope --no-color decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_attack_detect.pcap")
set_tests_properties(color_attack_pattern_tag_survives_no_color PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[attack: land\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1;31m")

# The IPv6 attack path (ipv6_attack_detect.hpp, wired through a SEPARATE pair of decoder.cpp call
# sites than the IPv4 one above -- observe_icmpv6/observe_dhcpv6, not observe_tcp/udp/icmp/ipv4)
# gets the identical tag-only treatment. Packet #3 of sample_ipv6_attack_ra_collision.pcap is the
# second, conflicting Router Advertisement identity (see the RA-collision note itself) -- confirms
# has_attack_signature/attack_signature_kind are set correctly from BOTH attack-detection state
# classes, not just the IPv4 one, and that ipv6_attack_detect.cpp's own kind slugs ("ipv6-ra-
# collision") reach the tag correctly.
add_test(NAME color_attack_pattern_tag_scoped_ipv6
  COMMAND conduitscope --color decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_attack_ra_collision.pcap")
set_tests_properties(color_attack_pattern_tag_scoped_ipv6 PROPERTIES
  # See color_attack_pattern_tag_scoped_not_whole_line's own comment above for why the "."
  # placeholders are needed here. Spelled out against the real captured line in full (rather than
  # a "#3  [^\n]*\\." wildcard prefix) -- CMake's own regex engine did not backtrack that wildcard
  # combination correctly against this fixture's real output, confirmed by running the test and
  # seeing it fail even though the literal text is present; verified against real output before
  # being written, per this project's own "never write a CTest assertion you haven't confirmed
  # against real output" rule.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  2\\.002000  fe80::b1 -> ff02::1  .\\[2m\\[icmpv6\\].\\[0m  ICMPv6 Router Advertisement, lifetime=300s, 2 option\\(s\\) \\(SLAAC prefix 2001:db8:bbbb::/64 offered\\).\\[1\;31m  \\[attack: ipv6-ra-collision\\].\\[0m"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1;31m#3")

# A detect-only finding (--detect-highlight, no severe/attack -- see DecodedPacket::has_detect_finding's
# own comment, decoder.hpp) is deliberately NOT treated the same as an attack-pattern packet above:
# reported directly against a real capture (a port scan decoded on Windows) where the WHOLE line,
# IP endpoints included, was turning red on every scanned-port packet and burying the actual
# decode. Fixed in TextWriter::write_packet (output.cpp) so red_line covers only severe/attack;
# the "[detect: ...]" tag gets its own separate, narrowly-scoped kBoldRed/kReset pair instead. This
# pins the exact shape for packet #1 of sample_s7comm_pi_control.pcap (an S7 PLC Stop, detect-only,
# no attack signature): NO bold-red escape appears before "#1" (unlike the attack-pattern tests
# above, which start "\x1b[1;31m#<n>"), the "[s7comm]" tag keeps its own plain
# protocol_tag_color(38;2;0;153;153) as always, the summary "Job: PLC Stop (...)" is plain/unstyled,
# and bold red starts only at the two literal spaces immediately before "[detect:" and ends right
# after the tag's own closing "]". See color_attack_pattern_head_line_red's own comment above for
# why a lone "." stands in for the raw ESC byte between two escapes with no literal text between
# them; verified against this exact command's real output before being written, matching this
# project's own "never write a CTest assertion you haven't confirmed against real output"
# discipline.
add_test(NAME color_detect_only_finding_tag_scoped_not_whole_line
  COMMAND conduitscope --color decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7comm_pi_control.pcap")
set_tests_properties(color_detect_only_finding_tag_scoped_not_whole_line PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  192\\.168\\.1\\.50:49210 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:102 \\(mms\\)  .\\[38\;2\;0\;153\;153m\\[s7comm\\].\\[0m  Job: PLC Stop \\(\"PLC_STOP\"\\).\\[1\;31m  \\[detect: s7-plc-stop\\].\\[0m"
  # The bold-red escape must not appear anywhere before the tag itself -- specifically, not right
  # after "#1  " (where the attack-pattern tests above DO put one) and not right after the
  # "[s7comm]" tag's own reset plus its trailing two spaces (where the previous, buggy version of
  # this same feature DID put one, coloring the summary text red too -- confirmed against this
  # exact fixture's real pre-fix output before being written).
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1;31m#1|\\[0m  \\.\\[1;31mJob")

# Packet #2 of the same capture (an S7 PLC Control command -- also a detect-only finding, different
# kind) gets the identical narrow-tag-only treatment, not a fluke of packet #1's specific fields.
add_test(NAME color_detect_only_finding_tag_scoped_second_packet
  COMMAND conduitscope --color decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7comm_pi_control.pcap")
set_tests_properties(color_detect_only_finding_tag_scoped_second_packet PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2  1\\.001000  192\\.168\\.1\\.50:49211 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:102 \\(mms\\)  .\\[38\;2\;0\;153\;153m\\[s7comm\\].\\[0m  Job: PLC Control \\(_INSE - Activates a PLC module, 2 block\\(s\\): DB100 \\(Passive\\), FC5 \\(Active\\)\\).\\[1\;31m  \\[detect: s7-plc-control\\].\\[0m"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1;31m#2")

# Regression coverage for the patch257 security review's finding 1 ("LEEF export: unescaped tab
# characters can corrupt event boundaries") -- tab_in_zone_name.yaml's own header comment has the
# full vulnerability/fixture rationale. The client zone's own name contains a literal embedded tab
# byte (not a "\t" escape -- yaml_mini doesn't interpret one); CEF/syslog (space-delimited
# extensions, per spec) pass the raw tab through unchanged, exactly like every other unlisted
# character cef_extension_escape doesn't touch, while LEEF (tab-delimited extensions) must render
# it as the literal two-character "\t" via leef_extension_escape -- a raw tab there would silently
# split this one finding into extra, bogus LEEF fields for a downstream SIEM.
add_test(NAME policy_tab_zone_name_cef_format
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/tab_in_zone_name.yaml" --format cef)
set_tests_properties(policy_tab_zone_name_cef_format PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^CEF:0\\|conduitscope\\|conduitscope-policy\\|[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\|policy-violation\\|Zone/Conduit Policy Violation\\|8\\|src=192\\.168\\.1\\.50 dst=192\\.168\\.1\\.10 dpt=502 proto=modbus cat=policy-violation msg=a conduit exists between zone 'hmi\tzone' and zone 'plc_zone', but none permits modbus traffic on port 502 cs1Label=Client Zone cs1=hmi\tzone cs2Label=Server Zone cs2=plc_zone cnt=3\n$")

add_test(NAME policy_tab_zone_name_leef_format
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/tab_in_zone_name.yaml" --format leef)
set_tests_properties(policy_tab_zone_name_leef_format PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^LEEF:2\\.0\\|conduitscope\\|conduitscope-policy\\|[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\|policy-violation\\|src=192\\.168\\.1\\.50\tdst=192\\.168\\.1\\.10\tdpt=502\tproto=modbus\tcat=policy-violation\tmsg=a conduit exists between zone 'hmi\\\\tzone' and zone 'plc_zone', but none permits modbus traffic on port 502\tcs1Label=Client Zone\tcs1=hmi\\\\tzone\tcs2Label=Server Zone\tcs2=plc_zone\tcnt=3\tsev=8\n$")

# An Allowed/Unclassified-only report (no Violation anywhere) produces zero lines in every one of
# the three curated-export formats -- see write_policy_report_cef's own doc comment (policy_engine.hpp)
# for why: an Unclassified flow is "no conduit declared an opinion," not a policy breach.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# --summarize-unclassified (policy_engine.cpp's summarize_unclassified_flows/
# write_unclassified_flow_group_summarized_text) -- added after a real, busy capture produced a
# 37MB/567K-line text report, almost entirely from UNCLASSIFIED TRAFFIC entries for host pairs
# reconnecting thousands of times (a new TCP flow, and so a new report entry, on every reconnect).
# tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_summarize_unclassified_sample) has three flow patterns: A (3 flows, same client/server/
# port, both zone-classified -- the "no recognized protocol" unclassified reason), B (2 flows, same
# client/server as A but a DIFFERENT port, proving the grouping key includes port), and C (2 flows,
# to an address outside every declared zone -- the OTHER unclassified reason, "no declared zone
# contains ..."). See tests/policies/summarize_unclassified.yaml's own header comment for the zones.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_off_by_default
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml")
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_off_by_default PROPERTIES
  # Without the flag, all 7 flows are still listed individually -- proves the flag is opt-in and
  # nothing about the default report changed by adding this feature.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "UNCLASSIFIED TRAFFIC \\(7\\):\n(  \\[[0-9]+\\].*\n)+"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "summarized into")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_collapses_into_three_groups
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_collapses_into_three_groups PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "UNCLASSIFIED TRAFFIC \\(7 flow\\(s\\), summarized into 3 distinct pattern\\(s\\)")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_pattern_a_flow_and_packet_counts
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_pattern_a_flow_and_packet_counts PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:9999  -- 3 flow\\(s\\), 6 packet\\(s\\) total\n *zones: hmi_zone -> plc_zone\n *mac: [0-9a-f:]+ -> [0-9a-f:]+\n *no recognized OT protocol traffic was found on any of these flows")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_pattern_b_kept_separate_by_port
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_pattern_b_kept_separate_by_port PROPERTIES
  # Same client/server IPs as pattern A, but port 8888 not 9999 -- must be its own group (2 flows,
  # 4 packets), not folded into pattern A's.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:8888  -- 2 flow\\(s\\), 4 packet\\(s\\) total")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_pattern_c_zone_reason_reused
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_pattern_c_zone_reason_reused PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 10\\.0\\.0\\.5:7777  -- 2 flow\\(s\\), 4 packet\\(s\\) total\n *zones: hmi_zone -> unclassified\n *mac: [0-9a-f:]+ -> [0-9a-f:]+\n *no declared zone contains 10\\.0\\.0\\.5")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_does_not_affect_violations_or_allowed
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/wrong_port.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)

# Reserved 'read'/'write' function-group keywords (Phase 4 of the policy-engine zoning work, see
# docs/design/policy-engine-zoning.md). 'functions: [read]'/'[write]' expand at parse time into
# that protocol's full Read-/Write-classified function/service name set (see
# modbus/dnp3/s7comm/iec104/enip .hpp/.cpp), combinable with literal names in the same list.
# Fixtures: tests/policies/functions_group_*.yaml and bad_functions_group_keyword_near_miss.yaml.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME policy_functions_group_read_modbus
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus_pairing.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/functions_group_read_modbus.yaml")
set_tests_properties(policy_functions_group_read_modbus PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "function 'Write Single Register' observed\; conduit 'modbus reads only via group keyword' permits only: Read Coils, Read Discrete Inputs, Read Holding Registers, Read Input Registers, Read Exception Status, Report Server ID, Read FIFO Queue, Encapsulated Interface Transport.*matched conduit \"modbus reads only via group keyword\"")

add_test(NAME policy_functions_group_write_modbus

# BACnet/IP is UDP-only in this decoder (see decoder.cpp) and `policy validate` only ever
# evaluates TCP flows -- so a "bacnet" conduit parses and validates fine (this policy file loads
# without error against every fixture) but can never actually be exercised. Read against
# sample_modbus.pcap (which has no BACnet traffic at all, real or otherwise) purely to confirm the
# conduit is accepted and simply never matched.

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Conduits never exercised by this capture \\(6\\):.*BACnet placeholder")

# sample_modbus.pcap (any capture will do -- every one of these errors fires at policy-load time,
# before a single packet is ever decoded); the worked-example fixtures are matched against the
# dedicated tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap (see build_vlan_zones_sample in tools/make_sample_pcap.py).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ROADMAP item 144 (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) -- a DNP3 data-link-address zone model, closing out item
# 13's own deliberately-deferred gap: a serial-to-IP DNP3 gateway multiplexing several outstations
# behind one IP (and typically one TCP session) can now be classified per outstation, by DNP3 link
# address, rather than producing a single IP-based verdict for the whole session. See
# tests/sample_dnp3_gateway.pcap (one TCP session, one master address 1, three outstations --
# 1024, 2048, 4096 -- multiplexed on it) and tests/policies/dnp3_link_zone_*.yaml /
# bad_*dnp3_link*.yaml.
add_test(NAME policy_dnp3_link_zone_mixed_results_text
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3_gateway.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/dnp3_link_zone_mixed_results.yaml")
set_tests_properties(policy_dnp3_link_zone_mixed_results_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: NON-COMPLIANT \\(0 violation\\(s\\), 3 unclassified flow\\(s\\)\\).*DNP3 LINK flows evaluated: 3 \\(1 allowed, 0 violation\\(s\\), 2 unclassified\\).*DNP3 LINK UNCLASSIFIED TRAFFIC \\(2\\):.*master 1 -> outstation 2048.*no declared Dnp3Link zone contains outstation address 2048.*master 1 -> outstation 4096.*no declared Dnp3Link zone contains outstation address 4096.*DNP3 LINK ALLOWED \\(1\\):.*master 1 -> outstation 1024.*zones: master_station -> outstation_1024, matched conduit \"Master polls outstation 1024 via DNP3\"")

add_test(NAME policy_dnp3_link_zone_mixed_results_json
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3_gateway.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/dnp3_link_zone_mixed_results.yaml" --format json)
set_tests_properties(policy_dnp3_link_zone_mixed_results_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"dnp3_link_flows\": \\[\n *\\{\n *\"protocol\": \"dnp3\",.*\"master_link_address\": 1,\n *\"outstation_link_address\": 1024,\n *\"master_zone\": \"master_station\",\n *\"outstation_zone\": \"outstation_1024\",.*\"verdict\": \"allowed\",\n *\"matched_conduit\": \"Master polls outstation 1024 via DNP3\",.*\\},\n *\\{\n *\"protocol\": \"dnp3\",.*\"master_link_address\": 1,\n *\"outstation_link_address\": 2048,.*\"outstation_zone\": \"unclassified\",.*\"verdict\": \"unclassified\",.*\\},\n *\\{\n *\"protocol\": \"dnp3\",.*\"outstation_link_address\": 4096,.*\"verdict\": \"unclassified\"")

# Proves a Dnp3Link conduit's 'functions' allow-list is checked per outstation, not once for the
# whole session -- outstation 1024 Allowed (both observed functions permitted), outstation 2048 a
# Violation (its own conduit disallows "Read"), outstation 4096 Unclassified (undeclared).
add_test(NAME policy_dnp3_link_zone_functions
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3_gateway.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/dnp3_link_zone_functions.yaml")
set_tests_properties(policy_dnp3_link_zone_functions PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "DNP3 LINK flows evaluated: 3 \\(1 allowed, 1 violation\\(s\\), 1 unclassified\\).*DNP3 LINK VIOLATIONS \\(1\\):.*master 1 -> outstation 2048.*function 'Read' observed; conduit 'Master polls outstation 2048, Response only -- Read is not permitted' permits only: Response")

add_test(NAME policy_error_zone_both_networks_and_dnp3_link

add_test(NAME policy_error_zone_dnp3_link_reserved_address

# sample_dnp3_gateway.pcap carries three distinct (master, outstation) DNP3 link sub-flows --
# --max-policy-dnp3-link-flows 1 forces every sub-flow after the first to be refused on
# dnp3_link_flows_, mirroring the tcp/udp/ethernet/notable-protocol resource-limit tests below.
add_test(NAME policy_engine_limits_dnp3_link_flows_cap_marks_validate_incomplete
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' policy validate --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3_gateway.pcap' --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/dnp3_link_zone_mixed_results.yaml' --max-policy-dnp3-link-flows 1; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(policy_engine_limits_dnp3_link_flows_cap_marks_validate_incomplete PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "OBSERVATION INCOMPLETE.*tracked-key limit \\(1\\) reached on dnp3_link_flows_.*--max-policy-dnp3-link-flows.*EXITCODE=6")

# compliant.yaml names neither "bacnet" nor "enip" (nor "any") on any conduit, so

# "policy validate: support UDP flows" finishing pass -- Phase 3 above shipped BACnet/IP + CIP I/O
# first; this closes the two protocols it left for later, HART-IP's UDP form and FF-HSE's UDP
# form, on the SAME policy-wide opt-in gate (Policy::has_udp_eligible_conduit()) and the same
# CIDR/hostname-zone UdpFlowReport machinery -- just two more protocol names. Direction is decided
# from each protocol's own request/response signal (HartIpFrame::message_type,
# FfhseHeader::type), mirroring BACnet's own content-based precedent (CIP I/O has no such signal
# and stays port-heuristic-only). See tests/sample_policy_udp_hartip_ffhse.pcap (one HART-IP
# Pass-Through request/response exchange plus one FF-HSE FMS Status request/response exchange,
# same HMI_IP<->PLC_IP pair) and tests/policies/udp_hartip_*.yaml.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `inventory` (asset_inventory.hpp/cpp) -- passive OT asset inventory: pcap -> zones and conduits,
# ROADMAP item 17. Runs the opposite direction from `policy validate`: infers a first-draft
# zone/conduit model from observed traffic instead of checking traffic against a hand-written one.
# tests/sample_inventory.pcap (build_inventory_sample in tools/make_sample_pcap.py) is the primary
# fixture -- unlike every other sample pcap, it deliberately spans TWO /24 subnets so the
# cross-zone conduit-inference path (not just same-subnet grouping) is actually exercised; see that
# builder's own comment for the full asset/zone/conduit layout it produces.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME inventory_text_report_assets_communications_zones_conduits

# docs/DEVELOPMENT.md ROADMAP item 125 (patch282 security review finding 8): the loud, all-caps
# "*** CONDUITSCOPE GENERATED DRAFT -- NOT VALIDATED ***" / "*** NOT SAFE FOR DIRECT DEPLOYMENT --
# REVIEW BEFORE USE ***" banner write_acl_draft_header (asset_inventory.cpp) now puts at the very
# top of every --acl-out dialect. Deliberately a DEDICATED test, not folded only into
# inventory_diagram_and_policy_out_smoke above -- that combined test's own regex uses `.*` to skip
# past whatever comes between each "=== acl-out (...) ===" marker and the pre-existing "Auto-
# generated by" sentence, which TOLERATES this banner's presence but would not actually catch its
# removal; this test is the one that positively proves it's there, in all three dialects.
add_test(NAME inventory_acl_out_has_loud_not_validated_banner
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' inventory --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_inventory.pcap' --acl-out '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/acl_banner_check_cisco.txt' --output /dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' inventory --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_inventory.pcap' --acl-out '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/acl_banner_check_fortinet.txt' --acl-format fortinet --output /dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' inventory --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_inventory.pcap' --acl-out '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/acl_banner_check_paloalto.txt' --acl-format paloalto --output /dev/null && echo === cisco === && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/acl_banner_check_cisco.txt' && echo === fortinet === && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/acl_banner_check_fortinet.txt' && echo === paloalto === && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/acl_banner_check_paloalto.txt'")
set_tests_properties(inventory_acl_out_has_loud_not_validated_banner PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "=== cisco ===\n! \\*\\*\\* CONDUITSCOPE GENERATED DRAFT -- NOT VALIDATED \\*\\*\\*\n! \\*\\*\\* NOT SAFE FOR DIRECT DEPLOYMENT -- REVIEW BEFORE USE \\*\\*\\*\n!\n! Auto-generated.*=== fortinet ===\n# \\*\\*\\* CONDUITSCOPE GENERATED DRAFT -- NOT VALIDATED \\*\\*\\*\n# \\*\\*\\* NOT SAFE FOR DIRECT DEPLOYMENT -- REVIEW BEFORE USE \\*\\*\\*\n#\n# Auto-generated.*=== paloalto ===\n# \\*\\*\\* CONDUITSCOPE GENERATED DRAFT -- NOT VALIDATED \\*\\*\\*\n# \\*\\*\\* NOT SAFE FOR DIRECT DEPLOYMENT -- REVIEW BEFORE USE \\*\\*\\*\n#\n# Auto-generated")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Widened protocol scope (asset_inventory.hpp/cpp) -- `inventory` originally only recognized five
# protocols (modbus/dnp3/s7comm/enip/bacnet); it now recognizes the same ten PolicyEngine::observe
# itself evaluates over TCP, adding iec104/hartip/opcua/mms/mqtt/ffhse -- see asset_inventory.hpp's
# own header comment for the full rationale, and why HART-IP/FF-HSE are deliberately TCP-only here
# even though decoder.cpp can also recognize both over UDP (a UDP conduit for either could never be
# exercised by `policy validate`, which only ever evaluates TCP flows).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME inventory_iec104_recognized
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_iec104.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_iec104_recognized PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50 .*\\[client\\]  iec104.*192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:2404 \\(iec104\\)  iec104.*zone_192_168_1_0_24 -> zone_192_168_1_0_24  \\(iec104/2404\\)  1 edge\\(s\\)")

# Closes the discover-then-enforce loop for real, for one of the newly-widened protocols -- the same
# "generate a policy from this capture, then validate the same capture against it" round trip the
# existing inventory_diagram_and_policy_out_smoke test already proves for the original five
# protocols (modbus/dnp3/s7comm/enip/bacnet), now proven for iec104 too.
add_test(NAME inventory_iec104_policy_out_round_trips_compliant
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' inventory --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_iec104.pcap' --policy-out '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/iec104_inferred.yaml' --output /dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' policy validate --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_iec104.pcap' --policy '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/iec104_inferred.yaml'")
set_tests_properties(inventory_iec104_policy_out_round_trips_compliant PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: COMPLIANT\n\nFlows evaluated: 1 \\(1 allowed, 0 violation\\(s\\), 0 unclassified\\)")

# HART-IP rides over both TCP and UDP in this fixture (67 total packets, only 3 of them TCP-carried
# hartip) -- proves BOTH halves of the TCP-only carve-out at once: the TCP-carried packets ARE
# counted (as an asset/edge), and the UDP-carried majority fold into skipped_packets instead of
# silently producing an inferred conduit `policy validate` could never check.
add_test(NAME inventory_hartip_recognized_tcp_only_udp_skipped
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_hartip_recognized_tcp_only_udp_skipped PROPERTIES
  # 68 total / 65 skipped, not 67/64: packet #68's own fabricated TLS Application Data record (see
  # hartip_tls_record_not_misdetected_as_hartip) is correctly skipped as "not one of the ten
  # recognized protocols" now that it's no longer misclassified as hartip.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "2 asset\\(s\\) observed, 68 total packet\\(s\\) in capture, 65 skipped.*192\\.168\\.1\\.10 .*\\[server\\]  hartip  \\(3 packet\\(s\\)\\)")

add_test(NAME inventory_opcua_recognized
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_opcua.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_opcua_recognized PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.10 .*\\[server\\]  opcua.*192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:4840 \\(opcua\\)  opcua")

# A COTP-only control packet on this same session still folds into "s7comm" (same convention
# PolicyEngine::observe uses -- see this feature's own header comment), while the actual MMS PDUs

# coexist as distinct edges (edge_key includes protocol) rather than one clobbering the other.

# FF-HSE, like HART-IP above, rides over both TCP and UDP in this fixture (70 total packets, only 4

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Grok gap #2 phase 0/1: last-seen (free -- DecodedPacket::timestamp already exists) and
# EtherNet/IP CIP Identity wiring (free -- EnipFrame::has_identity/identity_* are already fully
# decoded, see enip.hpp) into InventoryAsset. tests/sample_enip.pcap's own ListIdentity response
# (built for this exact purpose -- see build_enip_sample's own docstring) carries vendor=1,
# device_type=0x0C, product_code=54, revision 2.1, serial 0x001337AB, name "Conduit-ENIP-Sample" --
# sent BY 192.168.1.10 (the PLC/server side), so identity binds to that IP, not the HMI/client.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME inventory_enip_identity_wired_into_asset_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_enip_identity_wired_into_asset_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.10 .*\\[server\\]  enip.*first seen: 2023-11-14 22:46:40.*last seen: 2023-11-14 22:46:48.*identity:  vendor=Vendor ID 1  product=\"Conduit-ENIP-Sample\"  firmware=2.1  serial=0x1337ab")

add_test(NAME inventory_enip_identity_wired_into_asset_json
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_enip_identity_wired_into_asset_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"ip\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.10\",.*\"packet_count\": 9,\n *\"first_seen\": 1700002000.000000,\n *\"first_seen_text\": \"2023-11-14 22:46:40.000000Z\",\n *\"last_seen\": 1700002008.008000,\n *\"last_seen_text\": \"2023-11-14 22:46:48.008000Z\",\n *\"vendor\": \"Vendor ID 1\",\n *\"product\": \"Conduit-ENIP-Sample\",\n *\"firmware_revision\": \"2.1\",\n *\"serial_number\": \"0x1337ab\"")

# The client (HMI) side has no identity of its own -- never sent a ListIdentity response -- so its
# vendor/product/firmware_revision/serial_number fields must be omitted entirely (never emitted as
# empty strings or null), same "omit, never null, on a miss" convention hostname/mac_vendor above
# already follow.
add_test(NAME inventory_enip_no_identity_fields_omitted_for_client_json
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_enip_no_identity_fields_omitted_for_client_json PROPERTIES
  # Updated for Phase 6 of Grok gap #2 (InventoryAsset::inferred_role): every asset's JSON object
  # unconditionally gets an "inferred_role" field after last_seen_text now (see that field's own
  # comment, asset_inventory.hpp, for why it's never omitted the way vendor/product/etc. are) -- this
  # anchor pattern's "nothing else follows" assertion has to include it, not stop at last_seen_text.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"ip\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.50\",.*\"last_seen_text\": \"2023-11-14 22:46:48.008000Z\",\n *\"inferred_role\": \"Unknown\"\n *\\}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Grok gap #2 phase 7: InventoryEdge::top_touched_addresses -- tag/point/DB touch summarization
# (see that field's own comment in asset_inventory.hpp for the full per-protocol key design and the
# two-tier cap). tests/sample_touch_summarization.pcap (build_touch_summarization_sample in
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py) puts one concern on its own isolated client/server IP pair -- see that
# function's own docstring for the full per-edge reasoning behind each expected key/count below.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# modbus, basic key-format coverage: 5 distinct addresses, sorted by count (desc) then address
# (asc) -- hreg:00201-00202 was touched by BOTH the Write Multiple Registers request AND its
# response (real wire behavior echoes address+quantity on both sides -- see ModbusFrame::
# start_address's own comment, modbus.hpp), so it's the only 2-touch entry and sorts first.
add_test(NAME inventory_touch_modbus_basic_key_formats_and_sort_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_touch_summarization.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_touch_modbus_basic_key_formats_and_sort_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.240 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.241.*top touched addresses \\(1-based Modicon-style addressing\\) \\(5 distinct address\\(es\\) touched\\):\n *hreg:00201-00202  \\(2 touch\\(es\\)\\)\n *coil:00006-00008  \\(1 touch\\(es\\)\\)\n *discrete:00001  \\(1 touch\\(es\\)\\)\n *hreg:00001-00010  \\(1 touch\\(es\\)\\)\n *ireg:00100  \\(1 touch\\(es\\)\\)")

# modbus, truncation + deterministic sort: 35 distinct single-register reads, every count tied at
# 1 -- the top 32 SHOWN are exactly the 32 lexically/numerically smallest addresses (hreg:00001
# through hreg:00032); hreg:00033/00034/00035 exist (touched_addresses_total_distinct=35) but are
# NOT among the top 32 shown, proving kMaxShownTouchedAddressesPerEdge's cutoff and the
# (count desc, address asc) tie-break both actually fire, not just documented.
add_test(NAME inventory_touch_modbus_truncated_to_top_32_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_touch_summarization.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_touch_modbus_truncated_to_top_32_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.242 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.243.*top touched addresses \\(1-based Modicon-style addressing\\) \\(top 32 of 35 distinct addresses touched, by touch count\\):\n *hreg:00001  \\(1 touch\\(es\\)\\).*hreg:00032  \\(1 touch\\(es\\)\\)\n")

add_test(NAME inventory_touch_modbus_truncated_excludes_beyond_top_32_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_touch_summarization.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_touch_modbus_truncated_excludes_beyond_top_32_text PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "hreg:00033")

add_test(NAME inventory_touch_modbus_truncated_json_fields

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"client_ip\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.242\",.*\"touched_addresses_total_distinct\": 35,\n *\"touched_addresses_truncated\": true")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Loopback self-talk (AssetInventoryEngine::update_asset's own doc comment, asset_inventory.hpp)
# and the TCP-control-segment skip breakdown (AssetInventoryReport::skipped_tcp_control_packets'
# own comment). tests/sample_inventory_loopback_self_talk.pcap is Jurgen's own real capture,
# cross-validating conduitgate (his separate read-only Modbus proxy) against conduitscope: a
# single client script talking Modbus/TCP to 127.0.0.1:5020 (the real device) AND 127.0.0.1:5502
# (conduitgate's own listener, which decodes and re-issues UMAS/diagnostics operations against the
# real device) -- 103 packets total, 56 Modbus PDUs, 47 bare TCP segments (46 of them genuinely
# no-payload handshake/ACK/teardown; the 47th -- packet #73 -- is a TCP segment carrying the FIRST
# 7 of a 12-byte Modbus/TCP PDU split across segments, so it's non-empty and dp.tcp_no_payload
# correctly stays false for it, proving the fix reads the structured field rather than just
# checking dp.protocol == "tcp", which is also "tcp" here -- see decoder.cpp's own "buffering a ..."
# branch. The one packet that keeps skipped_tcp_control_packets from equaling skipped_packets
# exactly).
#
# Both bugs were invisible on every pre-existing two-host fixture (client_ip != server_ip there,
# so each update_asset call always landed on a DIFFERENT asset) and only surfaced on a real
# loopback capture -- see update_asset's own doc comment for why this dedicated fixture, not a
# synthetic two-host one, is what's needed to actually exercise the fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The headline bug: 26 + 30 = 56 packets recognized as modbus for 127.0.0.1, not 112 (the old
# "count once as client, once as server, even when they're the same asset" double-count). Anchored
# on the full ASSETS-section line so a regression back to 112 -- or any other drift -- fails this
# even if some other field on the same line also changed.
add_test(NAME inventory_loopback_self_talk_packet_count_not_doubled_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_inventory_loopback_self_talk.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_loopback_self_talk_packet_count_not_doubled_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "127\\.0\\.0\\.1  00:00:00:00:00:00  \\[client\\+server\\]  modbus  \\(56 packet\\(s\\)\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "112 packet")

add_test(NAME inventory_loopback_self_talk_packet_count_json
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_inventory_loopback_self_talk.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_loopback_self_talk_packet_count_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"ip\": \"127\\.0\\.0\\.1\",.*\"packet_count\": 56,"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"packet_count\": 112")

# The report header's own top-line total: 103 total, 47 skipped -- never exceeding total_packets
# (the exact "impossible number" shape Jurgen's report flagged), regardless of the breakdown below.
add_test(NAME inventory_loopback_self_talk_total_and_skipped_not_impossible_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_inventory_loopback_self_talk.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_loopback_self_talk_total_and_skipped_not_impossible_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "1 asset\\(s\\) observed, 103 total packet\\(s\\) in capture, 47 skipped")

# The skipped-packet breakdown: 46 bare TCP control segments (SYN/ACK/FIN, no application payload)
# broken out from the 1 remaining packet that's genuinely unrecognized -- see
# AssetInventoryReport::skipped_tcp_control_packets' own comment for why folding all 47 into
# "not one of the eleven recognized protocols" (the pre-existing wording, still used verbatim for
# the 1 that actually is that) overstated how much of this capture was genuinely opaque.
add_test(NAME inventory_skipped_tcp_control_breakdown_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_inventory_loopback_self_talk.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_skipped_tcp_control_breakdown_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "47 skipped \\(46 TCP control segment\\(s\\) with no application payload -- SYN/ACK/FIN traffic, not itself evidence of an unrecognized protocol\; 1 not one of the eleven recognized protocols, no IPv4 layer, or HART-IP/FF-HSE seen over UDP\\)")

add_test(NAME inventory_skipped_tcp_control_breakdown_json
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_inventory_loopback_self_talk.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_skipped_tcp_control_breakdown_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"skipped_packets\": 47,.*\"skipped_tcp_control_packets\": 46")

# Regression guard: a capture with ZERO bare-TCP-control skips (every packet is either recognized
# or a genuinely unrecognized payload) must read EXACTLY as it did before this feature existed --
# no "0 TCP control segment(s)..." noise, same pre-existing wording verbatim. sample_modbus.pcap is
# a normal two-host, fully-recognized, zero-skip capture -- confirms the omit-when-zero branch.
add_test(NAME inventory_skipped_tcp_control_omitted_when_zero_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_skipped_tcp_control_omitted_when_zero_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "0 skipped \\(not one of the eleven recognized protocols, no IPv4 layer, or HART-IP/FF-HSE seen over UDP\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "TCP control segment")

# s7comm: three well-established S7ANY tags (S7Item::tag verbatim) plus one EXPERIMENTAL 0xB2 item

# mqtt: MqttMessage::topic verbatim, PUBLISH only -- CONNECT/CONNACK on this same edge contribute
# nothing (no topic field of their own), and one of the two topics was published twice.
add_test(NAME inventory_touch_mqtt_publish_topics_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_touch_summarization.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_touch_mqtt_publish_topics_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.252 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.253.*top touched addresses \\(2 distinct address\\(es\\) touched\\):\n *line1/pump1/speed  \\(2 touch\\(es\\)\\)\n *line1/pump1/status  \\(1 touch\\(es\\)\\)")

# opcua: deliberately out of scope this phase (see InventoryEdge::top_touched_addresses' own
# comment for why) -- a GetEndpoints exchange on this edge must produce NO "top touched addresses"
# line at all in the text report (omitted entirely, same "don't print a header for nothing"
# convention the identity/security lines already follow), not an empty one.
add_test(NAME inventory_touch_opcua_out_of_scope_produces_no_section_text
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_touch_summarization.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_touch_opcua_out_of_scope_produces_no_section_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.254 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.1.*direction: port-heuristic\\)\n *first seen: [^\n]*\n\nINFERRED ZONES")

# Same opcua out-of-scope check in JSON: the array is present but empty (unconditional emission,
# same "always an array, never an omitted field" convention observed_functions already follows --
# see InventoryEdge::top_touched_addresses' own comment for why this differs from vendor/product's
# own "omit when empty" convention), never omitted or null.
add_test(NAME inventory_touch_opcua_out_of_scope_empty_array_json
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_touch_summarization.pcap")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"client_ip\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.254\",.*\"top_touched_addresses\": \\[\\],\n *\"touched_addresses_total_distinct\": 0,\n *\"touched_addresses_truncated\": false")

# JSON shape for a populated edge: address+count object pairs, matching the enip edge's own
# hand-verified text-mode expectation above.
add_test(NAME inventory_touch_json_address_count_object_shape

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tier 1 "IT protocols an OT auditor flags" recognition (it_protocols.hpp/cpp) -- RDP, VNC,
# TeamViewer, AnyDesk, and Zoom. See docs/MANUAL.md's ROADMAP item 18 for the full "why this
# matters to an OT auditor" framing. Name-only recognition, deliberately: no decoding past
# identifying which of the five a flow most likely is. tests/sample_remote_access.pcap (8 packets,
# built with scapy, see its own construction notes in git history) covers every one of this
# family's distinct confidence tiers:
#   #1 RDP, genuine X.224 Connection Request over TPKT/COTP, standard port 3389 (strong signal)
#   #2 RDP, port-only fallback, standard port 3389 (an already-established, encrypted session)
#   #3 VNC, genuine RFB protocol-version banner, standard port 5900 (strong signal)
#   #4 VNC, genuine RFB banner on a NON-standard port (still confidently identified -- port-
#      independent structural check, see it_protocols.hpp)
#   #5 TeamViewer, port-only, standard port 5938 (weakest tier -- no structural signal exists)
#   #6 AnyDesk, port-only, standard port 7070 (weakest tier)
#   #7 Zoom, port-only, UDP client range 8801-8810 (weakest tier)
#   #8 Zoom, port-only, UDP STUN range 3478-3479 (weakest tier, explicitly non-exclusive-to-Zoom)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME remote_access_rdp_connection_request_recognized
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_remote_access.pcap")
set_tests_properties(remote_access_rdp_connection_request_recognized PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"src_port\": 52100,\n *\"dst_port\": 3389,.*\"protocol\": \"rdp\",\n *\"summary\": \"RDP X.224 Connection Request \\(CR\\)\",\n *\"notes\": \\[\\]")

add_test(NAME remote_access_rdp_port_only_fallback_noted_weak
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_remote_access.pcap")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[rdp\\]  RDP \\(TCP port 3389\\) -- port match only, not confirmed by an X.224 Connection Request/Confirm in this packet")
