# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tier 2 "IT protocols an OT auditor flags" recognition (SSH/HTTP/HTTPS/SNMPv1v2c/Telnet/FTP/
# TFTP -- see it_protocols.hpp's own Tier 2 file header comment and docs/MANUAL.md's ROADMAP item
# 18). Fixture built by tools/make_sample_pcap.py-style scapy script (not itself checked in as a
# generator -- see tests/sample_remote_access.pcap's own precedent from Tier 1), 21 packets. SMB
# (packets 1-2) was originally an eighth Tier 2 protocol here, recognized only by its own 4-byte
# magic via it_protocols.hpp's own (now-removed) Tier 2 branches; it has since been upgraded to its
# own full dedicated decoder (smb.hpp, AD suite phase 3) -- see that file's own file header comment.
# That decoder enforces the genuine, verified [MS-SMB2]/RFC 1002 wire framing (a mandatory 4-byte
# Zero+StreamProtocolLength prefix before the magic on EITHER port, see smb.hpp's own FRAMING
# paragraph) more strictly than the old Tier 2 heuristic ever did, which is what these two packets
# (built for that older, less strict check, before smb.hpp existed) now expose:
#   1  TCP 52400->445   SMB2 magic (0xFE"SMB") with NO 4-byte prefix                 -> tcp (no
#                        longer recognized -- see lateral_movement_smb_missing_prefix_no_longer_
#                        misdetected below: this packet was never genuine SMB2 wire framing, only
#                        the old Tier 2 check's own less strict "magic at offset 0" heuristic ever
#                        accepted it)
#   2  TCP 52401->139   SMB1 magic (0xFF"SMB") behind a valid-looking 4-byte prefix  -> smb (still
#                        correctly recognized, now by smb.hpp -- see
#                        lateral_movement_smb_netbios_wrapper_recognized below)
#   3  TCP 52402->22    SSH banner, standard port                                    -> ssh
#   4  TCP 59022->52403 SSH banner, non-standard port                                -> ssh (noted)
#   5  TCP 52404->8080  HTTP request-line, curated port                              -> http
#   6  TCP 52405->34567 HTTP request-line, arbitrary vendor-web-UI port              -> http (noted)
#   7  TCP 34567->52405 HTTP status-line response, same arbitrary port               -> http (noted)
#   8  TCP 52407->443   TLS ClientHello, SNI + ALPN http/1.1                         -> https (ALPN-confirmed)
#   9  TCP 52408->443   TLS ClientHello, SNI, no ALPN                                -> https (port-only confirmed)
#  10  TCP 52409->8443  opaque byte, no ClientHello                                  -> https (weak port fallback)
#  11  TCP 52410->23    Telnet IAC negotiation                                       -> telnet
#  12  TCP 52411->23    opaque byte, no IAC negotiation                              -> telnet (weak fallback)
#  13  TCP 21->52412    FTP reply code 220                                           -> ftp
#  14  TCP 52413->21    FTP command USER                                             -> ftp
#  15  TCP 52414->21    opaque byte, no reply code/verb                              -> ftp (weak fallback)
#  16  UDP 52415->161   SNMPv2c GetRequest, community "public"                       -> snmp
#  17  UDP 52416->162   SNMPv1 Trap, community "private"                             -> snmp
#  18  UDP 52417->161   2 arbitrary bytes, not valid SNMP BER                        -> snmp (weak fallback)
#  19  UDP 52418->69    TFTP RRQ "firmware.bin" mode octet                           -> tftp
#  20  UDP 52419->69    TFTP WRQ "config.cfg" mode netascii                          -> tftp
#  21  UDP 52420->69    TFTP DATA opcode, no RRQ/WRQ structure                       -> tftp (weak fallback)
# Confirms smb.hpp's own, stricter, wire-verified gate -- not smb_tcp_declared_length's own weaker
# cousin, since this fixture's packet doesn't reach the declared-length cascade with a plausible
# length at all -- correctly does NOT misdetect this old Tier 2-era packet (magic at offset 0, no
# 4-byte Zero+StreamProtocolLength prefix) as SMB, since real [MS-SMB2]/RFC 1002 wire traffic always
# carries that prefix on both ports. See this fixture's own updated packet-1 comment above.
add_test(NAME lateral_movement_smb_missing_prefix_no_longer_misdetected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_lateral_movement.pcap")
set_tests_properties(lateral_movement_smb_missing_prefix_no_longer_misdetected PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:52400 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:445 \\(microsoft-ds\\)  \\[tcp\\]")

add_test(NAME lateral_movement_smb_netbios_wrapper_recognized
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_lateral_movement.pcap" --verbose)
set_tests_properties(lateral_movement_smb_netbios_wrapper_recognized PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[smb\\]  SMB1 \\(CIFS\\) message[^\n]*\n *note: SMB1 \\(CIFS\\) traffic observed on this session")

add_test(NAME lateral_movement_ssh_banner_standard_port_no_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_lateral_movement.pcap")
set_tests_properties(lateral_movement_ssh_banner_standard_port_no_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"protocol\": \"ssh\",\n *\"summary\": \"SSH version-exchange banner \\\\\"SSH-2\\.0-OpenSSH_9\\.6\\\\\"\",\n *\"notes\": \\[\\]")

# smb is 1, not 2 -- packet 1 no longer decodes as smb at all (see this fixture's own updated
# packet-1 comment above and lateral_movement_smb_missing_prefix_no_longer_misdetected); it counts
# under "tcp" here instead, one of the reasons this test no longer tries to assert every line's own
# protocol tag (that's lateral_movement_protocol_filter_isolates_family's job, immediately below).
add_test(NAME lateral_movement_stats_counted
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_lateral_movement.pcap")
# "tcp +1" appears between ssh and telnet because packet #1 (port 52400->445, no genuine SMB2
# Direct-TCP/NBSS 4-byte prefix -- see this fixture's own updated packet-1 comment above) falls
# through to generic tcp under the new, stricter smb.hpp gate rather than being counted as smb.
set_tests_properties(lateral_movement_stats_counted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ftp +3\n *http +3\n *https +3\n *smb +1\n *snmp +3\n *ssh +2\n *tcp +1\n *telnet +2\n *tftp +3")

# SMB no longer appears at all under --protocol lateral-movement (it has its own dedicated SmbOnly
# filter now, see decoder.hpp/smb.hpp) -- both former SMB packets fall to generic "tcp" here instead
# (packet 1 was never genuine SMB2 framing to begin with, see this fixture's own updated packet-1
# comment above; packet 2 IS genuine SMB1 traffic, but --protocol lateral-movement's own want_smb
# gate is simply off). The same "name the excluded protocol, don't blanket-fail on tcp/udp" pattern
# enterprise_trust_protocol_filter_isolates_port_based_family already established once LDAP made
# this identical move out of its own tier.
add_test(NAME lateral_movement_protocol_filter_isolates_family
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --protocol lateral-movement --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_lateral_movement.pcap")
set_tests_properties(lateral_movement_protocol_filter_isolates_family PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[ssh\\].*\\[ssh\\].*\\[http\\].*\\[http\\].*\\[http\\].*\\[https\\].*\\[https\\].*\\[https\\].*\\[telnet\\].*\\[telnet\\].*\\[ftp\\].*\\[ftp\\].*\\[ftp\\].*\\[snmp\\].*\\[snmp\\].*\\[snmp\\].*\\[tftp\\].*\\[tftp\\].*\\[tftp\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[smb\\]|\\[udp\\]")

add_test(NAME lateral_movement_extra_port_widens_expected_range

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tier 3 "IT protocols an OT auditor flags" recognition (NTP/DHCP/LDAP/LDAPS/RADIUS/TACACS+/EAPOL --
# see it_protocols.hpp's/eapol.hpp's own Tier 3 file header comments and docs/MANUAL.md's ROADMAP
# item 18). Fixture built by a scapy script (not itself checked in as a generator -- see tests/
# sample_lateral_movement.pcap's own precedent from Tier 2), 26 packets:
#    1  UDP 52500->123   NTPv4 client (VN=4 Mode=3)                          -> ntp
#    2  UDP 123->52500   NTPv4 server (VN=4 Mode=4)                          -> ntp
#    3  UDP 52501->123   3 bytes, too short to be a plausible NTP header     -> ntp (weak fallback)
#    4  UDP 68->67       DHCP DISCOVER (op=1, option 53=1)                  -> dhcp
#    5  UDP 67->68       DHCP OFFER (op=2, option 53=2)                     -> dhcp
#    6  UDP 15067->15068 DHCP REQUEST, non-standard port pair               -> dhcp (noted)
#    7  TCP 52502->389   LDAP anonymous BindRequest                          -> ldap (noted)
#    8  TCP 52503->3268  14 bytes, not a complete 8-field SearchRequest      -> tcp (not recognized --
#                        plain LDAP is its own full ProtocolDecoder now, see ldap.hpp; this packet
#                        satisfied the old shallow op-tag-only check but not a genuine full decode)
#    9  TCP 52504->389   3 bytes, not a recognizable LDAPMessage shape       -> tcp (not recognized)
#   10  TCP 52520->5000  LDAP bindRequest on an arbitrary, non-configured
#                        port -- RECOGNIZED as ldap regardless (ldap.hpp's own decoder is
#                        GateKind::TcpPortIndependent, tried before MQTT in decoder.cpp's own
#                        cascade), with a "not a configured/standard LDAP port" note;
#                        --ldap-port 5000 suppresses just that note, not detection itself          -> ldap (noted)
#   11  TCP 52505->636   LDAPS ClientHello, no ALPN, standard port           -> ldaps
#   12  TCP 52506->3269  LDAPS ClientHello, no ALPN, Global Catalog-over-TLS -> ldaps
#   13  TCP 52507->636   opaque byte, no ClientHello                        -> ldaps (weak fallback)
#   14  TCP 52521->636   ClientHello WITH ALPN http/1.1 on the LDAPS port    -> https (ALPN wins)
#   15  UDP 52508->1812  RADIUS Access-Request, current standard port        -> radius
#   16  UDP 1813->52509  RADIUS Accounting-Response, current standard port   -> radius
#   17  UDP 52510->1645  RADIUS Access-Request, legacy port                  -> radius
#   18  UDP 52511->1812  3 bytes, not a plausible Code/Length header         -> radius (weak fallback)
#   19  TCP 52512->49    TACACS+ Authentication, unencrypted flag set        -> tacacs-plus (noted)
#   20  TCP 52513->49    TACACS+ Authorization                               -> tacacs-plus
#   21  TCP 52514->49    invalid version byte                                -> tacacs-plus (weak fallback)
#   22  EAPOL            EAPOL-Start (Type 1, Length 0)                      -> eapol
#   23  EAPOL            EAP-Request/Identity (Type 0)                       -> eapol
#   24  EAPOL            EAP-Response/Identity (Type 0)                      -> eapol
#   25  EAPOL            EAPOL-Key, RSN/WPA2 Key Descriptor Type (Type 3)    -> eapol
#   26  EAPOL            EAPOL-Logoff (Type 2, Length 0)                     -> eapol
add_test(NAME enterprise_trust_ntp_client_recognized
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enterprise_trust.pcap")
set_tests_properties(enterprise_trust_ntp_client_recognized PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[ntp\\]  NTPv4 client \\(UDP port 123\\)")

add_test(NAME enterprise_trust_ntp_server_recognized

# Tier 4 "IT protocols an OT auditor flags" recognition (CAPWAP control/data, LWAPP control/data,
# GTP-U, PPPoE -- see it_protocols.hpp's/pppoe.hpp's own Tier 4 file header comments and
# docs/MANUAL.md's ROADMAP item 18). Fixture built by a scapy script (not itself checked in as a
# generator -- see tests/sample_enterprise_trust.pcap's own precedent from Tier 3), 23 packets:
#    1  UDP 52600->5246   CAPWAP control, Discovery Request (msg type 1)     -> capwap-control
#    2  UDP 52601->5246   CAPWAP control, DTLS-protected (Preamble Type=1)   -> capwap-control
#    3  UDP 52602->5246   CAPWAP control, Preamble ok, too short for HLEN    -> capwap-control (weak fallback)
#    4  UDP 52603->5246   CAPWAP control, Version nibble != 0                -> capwap-control (port-only fallback)
#    5  UDP 52604->5247   CAPWAP data, plaintext Preamble                    -> capwap-data
#    6  UDP 52605->5247   CAPWAP data, DTLS-protected                        -> capwap-data
#    7  UDP 52606->5247   CAPWAP data, not a plausible Preamble              -> capwap-data (port-only fallback)
#    8  UDP 52607->12222  LWAPP control, arbitrary bytes                     -> lwapp-control (port only)
#    9  UDP 52608->12223  LWAPP data, arbitrary bytes                        -> lwapp-data (port only)
#   10  UDP 52609->2152   GTP-U G-PDU (msg type 255), TEID=0x12345678        -> gtp-u (noted)
#   11  UDP 52610->2152   GTP-U Echo Request (msg type 1)                    -> gtp-u
#   12  UDP 52611->2152   GTP-U, Version/PT nibble != 0x3                    -> gtp-u (port-only fallback)
#   13  UDP 52612->6000   CAPWAP control Echo Request on a NON-standard
#                         port -- not recognized without widening; fixed
#                         by --wireless-backhaul-port below                 -> udp
#   14  PPPoE Discovery   PADI (code 0x09)                                   -> pppoe
#   15  PPPoE Discovery   PADO (code 0x07)                                   -> pppoe
#   16  PPPoE Discovery   PADR (code 0x19)                                   -> pppoe
#   17  PPPoE Discovery   PADS (code 0x65), session=0x1234                   -> pppoe
#   18  PPPoE Discovery   PADT (code 0xA7), session=0x1234                   -> pppoe
#   19  PPPoE Session     Session Data, PPP protocol=LCP (0xC021)            -> pppoe
#   20  PPPoE Session     Session Data, PPP protocol=PAP (0xC023)            -> pppoe (noted)
#   21  PPPoE Session     Session Data, PPP protocol=IP (0x0021)             -> pppoe
#   22  PPPoE Session     PADT (code 0xA7) mid-session                      -> pppoe
#   23  PPPoE Session     malformed (Ver/Type nibbles wrong)                 -> non-ip
add_test(NAME wireless_backhaul_capwap_control_discovery_request_recognized
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_wireless_backhaul.pcap")
set_tests_properties(wireless_backhaul_capwap_control_discovery_request_recognized PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[capwap-control\\]  CAPWAP control Discovery Request \\(UDP port 5246\\)")

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_wireless_backhaul.pcap")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tier 5 "IT protocols an OT auditor flags" recognition (GRE/NVGRE/EoIP, ESP, AH, IP-in-IP, 6in4,
# L2TP, IKE, VXLAN, Geneve, WireGuard, OpenVPN, dtls-tunnel, STT, MPLS -- see tunnel_vpn.hpp's/
# mpls.hpp's own Tier 5 file header comments and docs/MANUAL.md's ROADMAP item 18). Fixture built
# by a scapy script (not itself checked in as a generator -- see tests/sample_wireless_backhaul
# .pcap's own precedent from Tier 4), 28 packets:
#    1  IP proto 47   GRE, Protocol Type 0x0800 (IPv4)                    -> gre
#    2  IP proto 47   GRE, Protocol Type 0x6558, Key flag set             -> nvgre (noted)
#    3  IP proto 47   GRE, Protocol Type 0x6400 (Mikrotik)                -> eoip
#    4  IP proto 47   GRE, Version nibble != 0                            -> non-tcp (fallback)
#    5  IP proto 50   ESP, SPI=0x12345678                                 -> esp
#    6  IP proto 51   AH, Next Header=6 (TCP), SPI=0x87654321             -> ah
#    7  IP proto 4    IP-in-IP, valid inner IPv4 header                   -> ip-in-ip (inner addrs)
#    8  IP proto 4    IP-in-IP, first nibble != 4                         -> non-tcp (fallback)
#    9  IP proto 41   6in4, first nibble == 6                             -> 6in4
#   10  IP proto 115  L2TPv3 direct-IP, Session ID=0xAABBCCDD             -> l2tp
#   11  UDP 52700->500    IKEv2 IKE_SA_INIT                               -> ike
#   12  UDP 52701->4500   IKEv2 NAT-T (zero marker) INFORMATIONAL         -> ike
#   13  UDP 52702->4500   ESP NAT-Traversed (no marker), SPI=0x99887766   -> esp
#   14  UDP 52703->1701   L2TPv2 data message (Version=2, reserved clear) -> l2tp
#   15  UDP 52704->1701   L2TP, Version nibble=3 (not v2 shape)           -> l2tp (weak fallback)
#   16  UDP 52705->4789   VXLAN, Flags=0x08, VNI=0x00A1B2                 -> vxlan
#   17  UDP 52706->4789   VXLAN, malformed Flags byte                    -> udp (fallback)
#   18  UDP 52707->6081   Geneve, Version=0, Protocol Type=0x6558         -> geneve
#   19  UDP 52708->51820  WireGuard Handshake Initiation (148 bytes)      -> wireguard
#   20  UDP 52709->51820  WireGuard Transport Data (32 bytes)             -> wireguard
#   21  UDP 52710->1194   OpenVPN P_CONTROL_HARD_RESET_CLIENT_V2          -> openvpn
#   22  TCP 52711->1194   OpenVPN P_DATA_V2, 2-byte length prefix         -> openvpn
#   23  TCP 52712->7878   STT, arbitrary bytes                            -> stt (port only)
#   24  UDP 52713->9999   DTLS 1.2 Application Data record                -> dtls-tunnel
#   25  MPLS unicast (0x8847), 1 label, Bottom-of-Stack set               -> mpls
#   26  MPLS multicast (0x8848), 1 label                                  -> mpls
#   27  MPLS unicast, 2-label stack                                       -> mpls
#   28  MPLS unicast, 4 bytes only, Bottom-of-Stack NOT set               -> mpls (truncated)
add_test(NAME tunnel_vpn_gre_plain_recognized
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tunnel_vpn.pcap")
set_tests_properties(tunnel_vpn_gre_plain_recognized PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[gre\\]  GRE tunnel carrying 0x800 \\(IPv4\\)")

add_test(NAME tunnel_vpn_gre_nvgre_ambiguity_noted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tunnel_vpn.pcap" --verbose)
set_tests_properties(tunnel_vpn_gre_nvgre_ambiguity_noted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[nvgre\\]  NVGRE \\(or plain Ethernet-bridging-over-GRE.*\n.*note: Protocol Type 0x6558 with the Key flag set matches BOTH NVGRE")

add_test(NAME tunnel_vpn_gre_eoip_recognized

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# direction_source: which tier (handshake/content/port-heuristic) decided a flow's client/server
# side, across all three surfaces that make that call -- `decode` (FlowDirectionTracker, see
# flow_direction.hpp), `policy validate` (PolicyEngine::FlowReport), and `inventory`
# (AssetInventoryEngine::InventoryEdge). See DirectionSource's own comment (decoder.hpp) and
# docs/MANUAL.md's ROADMAP item 19 for the full three-tier design record. sample_policy_engine.pcap
# supplies both a captured-handshake flow and a mid-capture (no-handshake) flow in one fixture (see
# its own use above under "sample_policy_engine.pcap: client/server (initiator) determination and
# cotp->s7comm folding"); sample_modbus.pcap starts mid-session, giving a pure port-heuristic case;
# sample_inventory.pcap's BACnet edge is this codebase's only content-based case.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME decode_direction_source_handshake_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_policy_engine.pcap" --format json)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"tcp_flags\": \"SYN\",[^}]*\"direction_source\": \"handshake\",\n *\"direction_client_ip\": \"192.168.1.50\"")

add_test(NAME decode_direction_source_port_heuristic_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(decode_direction_source_port_heuristic_json PROPERTIES
  # sample_modbus.pcap's session starts mid-capture (no SYN ever seen), so every packet on it falls
  # back to the known-port/lower-port-number guess -- server_port 502 is Modbus's registered port,
  # so 192.168.1.50 (the other, unrecognized-port side) is (correctly, here) assumed to be the client.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"direction_source\": \"port-heuristic\",\n *\"direction_client_ip\": \"192.168.1.50\"")

# Proves the STATEFUL-IMMEDIATE and WINDOWED-THRESHOLD always-notable categories highlight live
# through `decode` too, not just the trivial STATELESS-IMMEDIATE case the tests just above cover --
# reusing detect_snort_patterns_batch5_all_findings's own fixture (see that test's own comment for
# the full first-seen-order finding list this pcap produces via `detect` itself).
#
# modbus-write-without-read-registers (STATEFUL-IMMEDIATE: needs to remember whether a prior read
# ever covered this address range, but resolves the instant the write itself is seen -- no
# threshold/window) fires on packet #30 (the FIRST write on the .170/.172 conduit) AND again on
# packets #34/#35/#36 (three separate writes on the .176/.177 conduit, each its own occurrence) --
# proving every individual occurrence is flagged live, not just a first-ever-seen one the way
# DetectEngine's own report-facing dedup works (see AlwaysNotableHit's own comment,
# detect_engine.hpp).
#
# port-scan (WINDOWED-THRESHOLD: a running count within a time window) fires ONLY on packet #16 --
# the 10th distinct destination port that crosses this engine's own threshold -- never on packets
# #7-#15, the nine SYNs leading up to it that are real traffic on the same (src,dst) pair but don't
# yet cross the threshold; the FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION below confirms none of those nine packets
# were also tagged (a bug here would tag every packet in the window, not just the triggering one).
#
# modbus-rogue-master/dnp3-rogue-master (NEW-VS-KNOWN, resolved only in finish() against a baseline
# or whole-capture first-occurrence -- see this file's own header comment) never appear via `decode`
# at all -- confirmed by the same FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION, since novelty-shaped findings are
# structurally out of AlwaysNotableHit's scope (see that struct's own comment) and `decode` has no
# way to resolve them live regardless.
add_test(NAME decode_detect_highlight_stateful_and_windowed_live
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_detect_snort_patterns_batch5.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(decode_detect_highlight_stateful_and_windowed_live PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#16  -0\\.100000  192\\.168\\.1\\.164:49016 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.165:23 \\(telnet\\)[^\n]*\\[detect: port-scan\\].*#30  [^\n]*192\\.168\\.1\\.170:49900 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.172:502 \\(modbus\\)[^\n]*\\[detect: modbus-write-without-read-registers\\].*#34  [^\n]*192\\.168\\.1\\.176:49910 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.177:502 \\(modbus\\)[^\n]*\\[detect: modbus-write-without-read-registers\\].*#35  [^\n]*192\\.168\\.1\\.176:49910 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.177:502 \\(modbus\\)[^\n]*\\[detect: modbus-write-without-read-registers\\].*#36  [^\n]*192\\.168\\.1\\.176:49910 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.177:502 \\(modbus\\)[^\n]*\\[detect: modbus-write-without-read-registers\\]"
  # Each of packets #7-#15 (the nine SYNs leading up to the port-scan threshold, real traffic on
  # the same (src,dst) pair) must NOT be individually tagged -- only #16, the 10th distinct port,
  # crosses the threshold. [^\n]* keeps each alternative scoped to its own line (this file's own
  # regex dialect lets a bare .* span newlines, matching the whole multi-line output -- see e.g.
  # this file's own "direction_client_ip":[^\n]*\n anchors elsewhere -- so an unscoped #7 .*port-scan
  # would wrongly match all the way forward into #16's own real, correct tag).
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "rogue-master|#7  [^\n]*\\[detect:|#8  [^\n]*\\[detect:|#9  [^\n]*\\[detect:|#10  [^\n]*\\[detect:|#11  [^\n]*\\[detect:|#12  [^\n]*\\[detect:|#13  [^\n]*\\[detect:|#14  [^\n]*\\[detect:|#15  [^\n]*\\[detect:")

  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_policy_engine.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/policy_engine_sample.yaml" --format json)
set_tests_properties(policy_validate_direction_source_handshake_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"client_ip\": \"192.168.1.50\",[^}]*\"server_port\": 502,[^}]*\"direction_source\": \"handshake\"")

add_test(NAME policy_validate_direction_source_port_heuristic_json

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Live capture (live_capture.hpp/cpp) -- an optional, build-time-detected libpcap (Linux) / Npcap
# (Windows) dependency; see CMakeLists.txt's CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP detection above. The CLI
# surface (-i/--interface, --filter, --duration, --snaplen, --no-promiscuous, `interfaces`) exists
# unconditionally -- only the runtime behavior behind it depends on CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP -- so
# argument-validation tests below run regardless. Tests that actually open an interface are gated
# on CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP (nothing to open otherwise) and, since this project has no CI configured
# yet and has only been exercised in a Linux dev sandbox so far, further gated on UNIX and scoped to
# loopback ("lo"), which every Linux/macOS host has; a Windows loopback interface has a different,
# non-portable name (see docs/MANUAL.md's LIVE CAPTURE section), so the Windows path is currently
# validated only by the argument-parsing tests, same honesty-about-scope convention as this
# project's other platform-specific caveats (e.g. the S7comm-Plus/DNP3 real-capture notes above).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME live_capture_requires_exactly_one_source_decode
  COMMAND conduitscope decode)
set_tests_properties(live_capture_requires_exactly_one_source_decode PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "needs exactly one of -r/--read.*or -i/--interface")

add_test(NAME live_capture_input_and_interface_are_mutually_exclusive_decode
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --interface lo)
set_tests_properties(live_capture_input_and_interface_are_mutually_exclusive_decode PROPERTIES
  WILL_FAIL TRUE)

add_test(NAME live_capture_requires_exactly_one_source_policy_validate
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml")
set_tests_properties(live_capture_requires_exactly_one_source_policy_validate PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "needs exactly one of -r/--read.*or -i/--interface")

add_test(NAME live_capture_input_and_interface_are_mutually_exclusive_policy_validate
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --interface lo --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml")
set_tests_properties(live_capture_input_and_interface_are_mutually_exclusive_policy_validate PROPERTIES
  WILL_FAIL TRUE)

add_test(NAME live_capture_requires_exactly_one_source_inventory
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory)
set_tests_properties(live_capture_requires_exactly_one_source_inventory PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "needs exactly one of -r/--read.*or -i/--interface")

add_test(NAME live_capture_input_and_interface_are_mutually_exclusive_inventory
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --interface lo)
set_tests_properties(live_capture_input_and_interface_are_mutually_exclusive_inventory PROPERTIES
  WILL_FAIL TRUE)

add_test(NAME live_capture_version_reports_support
  COMMAND conduitscope version)
if(CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP)
  set_tests_properties(live_capture_version_reports_support PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "live capture: libpcap/Npcap")
else()
  set_tests_properties(live_capture_version_reports_support PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "live capture: not built in")
endif()

if(NOT CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP)
  # This build was configured with CONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_LIVE_CAPTURE=OFF, or simply didn't find
  # libpcap/Npcap -- confirm the stub path (live_capture.cpp's #else branch) gives a clear,
  # actionable error rather than a crash or a silent no-op, for both entry points.
  add_test(NAME live_capture_unavailable_interfaces_command
    COMMAND conduitscope interfaces)
  set_tests_properties(live_capture_unavailable_interfaces_command PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "live capture is not available.*libpcap.*Npcap")

  add_test(NAME live_capture_unavailable_decode_interface
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --interface lo --duration 1)
  set_tests_properties(live_capture_unavailable_decode_interface PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "live capture is not available.*libpcap.*Npcap")

  # --filter on an offline read (-r) needs libpcap/Npcap too (bpf_filter.hpp/cpp's own stub path,
  # same posture as live_capture.cpp's) -- confirm that's also a clear, actionable error here,
  # not a crash or a silent no-op that quietly ignores the filter.
  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_unavailable_decode_read
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --filter "tcp port 502")
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_unavailable_decode_read PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "BPF filtering .*requires this build to have been compiled with libpcap/Npcap")
else()
  # This build actually found libpcap/Npcap. A bad/nonexistent interface name is portable (no real
  # interface needs to exist on either platform for this to fail the way it's supposed to), so it
  # runs regardless of OS; everything else here opens "lo" specifically, which only exists (under
  # that name) on Linux/macOS -- Windows' loopback interface has a different, non-portable name
  # (see docs/MANUAL.md's LIVE CAPTURE section) -- so those are further gated on UNIX. This project
  # has no CI configured yet and has only actually been run on Linux so far; the Windows path is
  # validated only by the argument-parsing and bad-interface-name tests until that changes.
  add_test(NAME live_capture_bad_interface_name_reports_clearly
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --interface this_interface_does_not_exist --duration 1)
  # Two legitimate failure messages are possible here, and both count as "reports clearly": on a
  # machine with the Npcap/libpcap RUNTIME actually present, pcap itself rejects the unknown
  # interface name ("cannot open/activate ... this_interface_does_not_exist"); on Windows CI (SDK
  # only, no Npcap runtime -- see live_capture.cpp's ensure_pcap_runtime_available and the
  # /DELAYLOAD comment in this file above), the runtime-missing check fires first instead. Either
  # one is the correct, actionable error for its environment.
  set_tests_properties(live_capture_bad_interface_name_reports_clearly PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(cannot (open|activate) .*this_interface_does_not_exist|live capture requires the Npcap RUNTIME to be installed)")

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # --filter on an offline read (-r), not just live capture (-i) -- bpf_filter.hpp/bpf_filter.cpp.
  # sample_modbus.pcap's 3 packets (see build_modbus_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py):
  #   #1 192.168.1.50:51000 -> 192.168.1.10:502  (HMI's request)
  #   #2 192.168.1.10:502 -> 192.168.1.50:51000  (PLC's response)
  #   #3 192.168.1.10:502 -> 192.168.1.50:51000  (PLC's exception response)
  # Runs on every platform this whole `else()` branch already runs on (unlike the `if(UNIX)` live
  # -i tests below, this needs no real interface at all, just libpcap linked in for its BPF
  # compiler -- see bpf_filter.cpp's own file header for why an offline read needs libpcap the
  # same way live capture does, despite PcapReader itself having no such dependency).
  #
  # Every PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION below also accepts bpf_filter.cpp's own "Npcap RUNTIME" error
  # text, the same dual-acceptance pattern live_capture_bad_interface_name_reports_clearly above
  # already established for the identical situation: on Windows CI (SDK only, no Npcap runtime
  # actually installed -- see bpf_filter.cpp's own pcap_runtime_available() guard, added after
  # these 7 tests were first found crashing the release-windows job outright with a raw Windows
  # delay-load structured exception, 0xc06d007e, instead of failing cleanly), compiling ANY BPF
  # filter -- even just to read an offline file, even one that would otherwise match nothing --
  # now fails fast with that clear CaptureError before ever reaching pcap_open_dead(). A machine
  # that genuinely has the runtime (every Linux CI leg, or a real Windows box with Npcap
  # installed) still exercises the real filtering behavior each test's own regex checks for;
  # bpf_filter_read_invalid_syntax_reports_clearly's own invalid-syntax message is simply never
  # reached in the runtime-missing case (the missing-runtime check fires first, regardless of
  # whether the filter text itself is valid), which is why its own PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION needs
  # the same alternation despite testing a specifically DIFFERENT failure mode.
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_read_matches_all_three_packets
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --filter "tcp port 502" --format text)
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_read_matches_all_three_packets PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(#1 .*\n.*#2 .*\n.*#3 |Npcap RUNTIME)"
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#4 ")

  # No PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION originally (a real "0 packets matched" run produces zero bytes of
  # output, exit 0 -- nothing positive to match against) -- but once a second, alternate "correct"
  # outcome (the Npcap RUNTIME error, exit nonzero) also needs accepting, CTest's exit-code-based
  # pass/fail check has to be replaced entirely (setting PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION at all disables
  # it -- see this section's own header comment), not merely supplemented. "^$" anchors to
  # genuinely empty output specifically, rather than a blanket "match anything" pattern that would
  # silently stop this test from ever being able to fail on the exit-code axis again.
  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_read_matches_no_packets
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --filter "tcp port 9999" --format text)
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_read_matches_no_packets PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(^$|Npcap RUNTIME)"
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1 ")

  # src host narrows to just the HMI's own request (#1) -- proves the filter genuinely inspects
  # packet content (source IP), not just "matches everything/matches nothing".
  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_read_src_host_narrows_correctly
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --filter "src host 192.168.1.50" --format text)
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_read_src_host_narrows_correctly PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(#1 |Npcap RUNTIME)"
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2 |#3 ")

  # dst host narrows to the PLC's two responses (packets #2 and #3 in the unfiltered file), not
  # the HMI's request (#1) -- the complementary direction from the src-host test above. Also
  # doubles as the first half of the "preserve original packet numbering" check below: the PASS
  # regex pins the two surviving packets to their real "#2"/"#3" file positions, not a renumbering
  # to "#1"/"#2" -- see bpf_filter_read_preserves_original_packet_numbering's own comment for why
  # that distinction matters and PacketSource::next()'s own comment (cli_main.cpp) for the fix.
  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_read_dst_host_narrows_correctly
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --filter "dst host 192.168.1.50" --format text --verbose)
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_read_dst_host_narrows_correctly PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(#2 .*response: 20 data byte\\(s\\).*\n.*\n.*\n#3 .*exception response|Npcap RUNTIME)"
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "request: read 10 holding register|^#1 ")

  # Dedicated regression test for the fix itself: a `--filter`ed offline (`-r`) read must report
  # each surviving packet under its own position in the UNFILTERED file -- the same convention
  # Wireshark's own display filter follows (frame numbers are stable positions in the capture) --
  # not renumber sequentially from 1 within just the matches, which is what this tool used to do
  # (and what a real capture-filter, or this tool's own `-i`/`--filter` live-capture path, still
  # does -- there, the discarded packets were genuinely never captured at all, so there is no
  # original position to preserve). "src host" alone matches only packet #1, unaffected either
  # way; "dst host" is the case that actually distinguishes the two conventions, since packets #2
  # and #3 would collapse to #1/#2 under the old, buggy renumbering-from-1 behavior.
  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_read_preserves_original_packet_numbering
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --filter "dst host 192.168.1.50" --format text)
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_read_preserves_original_packet_numbering PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(^#2 |Npcap RUNTIME)"
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 ")

  # An invalid filter expression is reported clearly and fails the run, exactly like the existing
  # live-capture equivalent (live_capture_invalid_filter_reports_clearly below) -- same error
  # message shape, since bpf_filter.cpp's own error text deliberately mirrors live_capture.cpp's.
  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_read_invalid_syntax_reports_clearly
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --filter "this is not valid bpf syntax {{{")
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_read_invalid_syntax_reports_clearly PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(invalid capture filter|Npcap RUNTIME)")

  # `--filter` is wired identically into `policy validate -r` and `inventory -r` (both funnel
  # through cli_main.cpp's own open_packet_source, same as decode -- see its own file comment).
  # "Flows evaluated" is printed on every real (runtime-present) run regardless of how many flows
  # the filter actually leaves -- unlike decode's own text format, `policy validate` always has a
  # non-empty report to match against, so this can stay PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION-based without
  # `bpf_filter_read_matches_no_packets`'s own "empty output" wrinkle.
  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_policy_validate_read_narrows_flows
    COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml" --filter "tcp port 9999")
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_policy_validate_read_narrows_flows PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(Flows evaluated|Npcap RUNTIME)"
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.10")

  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_inventory_read_narrows_assets
    COMMAND conduitscope inventory --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --filter "tcp port 9999")
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_inventory_read_narrows_assets PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(0 asset\\(s\\) observed|Npcap RUNTIME)")

  # -f is `decode`'s own short alias for --filter (mirrors tshark's own -f) -- same
  # "src host narrows to just packet #1" behavior bpf_filter_read_src_host_narrows_correctly
  # already proves for the long form, now proven for -f too; same runtime-missing alternation
  # every other filter test in this block needs, for the same reason.
  add_test(NAME bpf_filter_dash_f_alias_narrows_correctly
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -f "src host 192.168.1.50" --format text)
  set_tests_properties(bpf_filter_dash_f_alias_narrows_correctly PROPERTIES
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "(#1 |Npcap RUNTIME)"
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2 |#3 ")

  if(UNIX)
    # None of these depend on any traffic actually existing on "lo" during the run (--duration
    # alone must be enough to stop cleanly), so they don't need a traffic generator and stay
    # fast/deterministic.
    add_test(NAME live_capture_interfaces_command_lists_loopback
      COMMAND conduitscope interfaces)
    set_tests_properties(live_capture_interfaces_command_lists_loopback PROPERTIES
      PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "lo  \\[loopback\\]")

    add_test(NAME live_capture_invalid_filter_reports_clearly
      COMMAND conduitscope decode --interface lo --filter "this is not valid bpf syntax {{{" --duration 1)
    set_tests_properties(live_capture_invalid_filter_reports_clearly PROPERTIES
      PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "invalid capture filter")

    add_test(NAME live_capture_duration_stops_cleanly_with_no_traffic
      COMMAND conduitscope decode --interface lo --duration 1 --format text)
    set_tests_properties(live_capture_duration_stops_cleanly_with_no_traffic PROPERTIES
      TIMEOUT 10
      FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error:")

    add_test(NAME live_capture_policy_validate_duration_stops_cleanly
      COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --interface lo --duration 1 --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml")
    set_tests_properties(live_capture_policy_validate_duration_stops_cleanly PROPERTIES
      TIMEOUT 10
      PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "capture: live:lo")

    # Every test above deliberately relies on "lo" carrying NO traffic, for determinism -- which
    # means none of them prove --max-packets actually bounds a live capture, or that live capture
    # decodes something real rather than just opening/closing cleanly. This one does: it generates
    # one real loopback TCP handshake attempt concurrently with a --max-packets=2 capture. See the
    # script's own header comment for exactly how, and why a bug here would hang (TIMEOUT) rather
    # than silently pass.
    add_test(NAME live_capture_max_packets_stops_capture_early_with_real_traffic
      COMMAND bash "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/live_capture_max_packets_smoke.sh" "$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>")
    set_tests_properties(live_capture_max_packets_stops_capture_early_with_real_traffic PROPERTIES
      TIMEOUT 20)
  endif()
endif()

# docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch282.md finding 5 (item 122, DEVELOPMENT.md):
# --max-inventory-file-bytes, the same shape as --max-baseline-file-bytes (item 68), rejects an
# oversized input report BEFORE it's read into memory rather than silently allocating without a
# ceiling. tests/merge_inventory_oversize_smoke.sh generates one real 'inventory --format json'
# report with the CLI itself (so this doesn't depend on a checked-in fixture staying in sync with
# the report schema), then proves: (1) merging it still succeeds under the default 256 MiB
# ceiling, and (2) a --max-inventory-file-bytes set below that report's own real size is rejected
# with a clear error naming the byte count/limit/override flag, and exits non-zero, before any
# "merged:"/report output is produced.

  TIMEOUT 20)

# docs/reviews/2026-10-chatgpt-security-review-patch295.md finding F1 fix (item 133,
# DEVELOPMENT.md): the per-file ceiling above says nothing about the AGGREGATE across however
# many input files one merge names -- these four new ceilings (input-file count, combined byte
# total, combined asset count, combined edge count) close that gap. See
# tests/merge_inventory_aggregate_limits_smoke.sh's own file header for exactly what each of the
# four proves and why (in particular: the asset/edge ceilings are proven to trip DURING a file's
# own array parsing, not only after it finishes, which is what actually matters against F1's own
# "second-order amplification" concern).
add_test(NAME merge_inventory_aggregate_limits_enforced

# docs/reviews/2026-10-chatgpt-security-review-patch295.md finding F2 fix (item 134,
# DEVELOPMENT.md): the JSON parser behind `merge inventory` now validates several fields
# SEMANTICALLY (not just syntactically) before trusting them -- a negative packet_count/
# total_packets/skipped_packets, an out-of-range server_port, a malformed IPv4 address string, and
# first_seen after last_seen are all rejected now instead of silently becoming corrupted/
# nonsensical data (or, for an out-of-range integer literal, crashing the process -- a bug found
# incidentally while making this same fix). See tests/merge_inventory_semantic_validation_smoke.sh's
# own file header for the full list of cases and why this one test file deliberately hand-authors
# its JSON fixtures rather than generating them with the CLI (every case it proves is a value the
# CLI itself can never produce).

          "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests")
set_tests_properties(merge_inventory_semantic_validation_rejects_crafted_values PROPERTIES
  TIMEOUT 20)

# docs/reviews/2026-10-chatgpt-security-review-patch295.md finding F3 fix (item 135,
# DEVELOPMENT.md): the per-file BYTE ceiling above bounds how much JSON text there can be, but
# says nothing about how DEEPLY NESTED it is -- skip_value() (inventory_merge.cpp's one genuinely
# recursive parser function) used to recurse once per nesting level with no depth tracking at all,
# so a tiny, compact, well-under-the-ceiling file shaped like {"x":{"x":{"x": ... }}} could still
# crash the whole process (a real stack overflow, confirmed by testing before this fix). See
# tests/merge_inventory_nesting_depth_smoke.sh's own file header for the full crash repro and why
# this is another deliberate exception to this project's own "generate every fixture with the real
# CLI" rule.

  TIMEOUT 30)

# DEVELOPMENT.md): the JSON parser behind `merge inventory` (JsonCursor::parse_string,
# inventory_merge.cpp) is now strict about two things RFC 8259 itself requires instead of silently
# accepting the malformed shape or corrupting the value -- an unescaped control character inside a

# UTF-16-decoded (including surrogate pairs) and UTF-8-encoded rather than truncated to its own low
# byte. See tests/merge_inventory_json_strictness_smoke.sh's own file header for the full case list
# (including why it hand-builds its fixtures rather than generating them with the CLI) and item

# ROADMAP item 18, second half: `policy validate`/`inventory` surfacing the mere PRESENCE of any
# of the 42 "IT protocols an OT auditor flags" (notable_it_protocols.hpp) as their own finding --
# PolicyReport::notable_protocols / AssetInventoryReport::notable_protocols -- independent of, and
# never changing, either report's existing Allowed/Violation/Unclassified verdicts or skipped-
# packet counts. The naming/recognition half of this item (all 42 protocol values themselves) has
# its own extensive test coverage already, under each tier's own decode section above; these tests
# are only for the NEW finding this adds on top, reusing those same five fixture pcaps
# (sample_remote_access/lateral_movement/enterprise_trust/wireless_backhaul/tunnel_vpn.pcap),
# which until now were only ever exercised by `decode` tests.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Tier 1 (remote-access): all 8 packets in this fixture are one of the five Tier 1 protocols, so
# every one becomes its own notable_protocols entry -- proves the text report's own section header,
# a representative line for each of the five protocol names, and that this section renders even
# though every flow above it is Unclassified (no conduit in compliant.yaml even mentions "rdp").
add_test(NAME notable_protocols_remote_access_text
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_remote_access.pcap"
          --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml")
set_tests_properties(notable_protocols_remote_access_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "NOTABLE IT PROTOCOLS \\(8\\):\n.*\\[1\\] rdp  \\(remote-access\\).*vnc  \\(remote-access\\).*teamviewer  \\(remote-access\\).*anydesk  \\(remote-access\\).*zoom  \\(remote-access\\)")

add_test(NAME notable_protocols_remote_access_json
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_remote_access.pcap"
          --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml")
set_tests_properties(notable_protocols_remote_access_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"notable_protocols\": \\[\n    \\{\n      \"protocol\": \"rdp\",\n      \"tier\": \"remote-access\",\n      \"client_ip\"")

# Tier 2 (lateral-movement), 19 of this fixture's packets recognized as one of the seven Tier 2
# it_protocols.hpp protocols or smb.hpp's own dedicated SMB decoder (still mapped to the
# "lateral-movement" tier by notable_it_protocols.cpp regardless of which decoder produced the
# "smb" protocol tag) -- the rest of the 26-packet fixture is negative-control/collision-check
# traffic (see this tier's own decode section above) that correctly produces no notable_protocols
# entry. Was 20 of 21 before smb.hpp's own stricter, wire-verified gate stopped misdetecting this
# fixture's packet 1 (built for the old, less strict Tier 2 heuristic, never genuine SMB2 framing --
# see this tier's own decode section's updated packet-1 comment); packet 2's genuine SMB1 traffic is
# still counted, so this drops by exactly one, not two. The text report's own
# "NOTABLE IT PROTOCOLS (N):" header count IS the assertion that exactly 19 were found (the same
# "let the tool's own printed count do the counting" convention every other cardinality assertion in
# this file already uses, e.g. "8 asset(s) observed" above) -- every line in the fixture is Tier 2,
# so this also confirms no other tier's protocol leaked in.
add_test(NAME notable_protocols_lateral_movement_count
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_lateral_movement.pcap"
          --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml")
set_tests_properties(notable_protocols_lateral_movement_count PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "NOTABLE IT PROTOCOLS \\(19\\):"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\(remote-access\\)|\\(enterprise-trust\\)|\\(wireless-backhaul\\)|\\(tunnel-vpn\\)")

# QUIC's own fixture (tests/sample_quic.pcap) is exercised separately from sample_lateral_movement.pcap
# above -- see this tier's own decode section for why it needed its own dedicated pcap -- so it gets
# its own notable_protocols check here too: 7 quic packets (#1-7) become entries; #8/#9 (generic udp,
# deliberate negative controls) do not.
add_test(NAME quic_notable_protocols_lateral_movement_tier
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap"
          --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml")
set_tests_properties(quic_notable_protocols_lateral_movement_tier PROPERTIES
  # 8, not 7, now that packet #13 (round two's positive truncated-capture control) is also quic.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "NOTABLE IT PROTOCOLS \\(8\\):\n(.*\n)*.*\\[1\\] quic  \\(lateral-movement\\)")

# Tier 3 (enterprise-trust): the one tier whose fixture also contains a Tier-2 "https" packet (a
# deliberate negative control proving LDAPS-vs-HTTPS ALPN disambiguation -- see this tier's own
# decode section above), so this is the one fixture that proves notable_protocols spans more than
# one tier in a single report, and its own EAPOL packets (no IP layer at all) render by MAC pair
# rather than IP.
add_test(NAME notable_protocols_enterprise_trust_multi_tier_and_eapol_mac
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enterprise_trust.pcap"
          --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml")
set_tests_properties(notable_protocols_enterprise_trust_multi_tier_and_eapol_mac PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[[0-9]+\\] https  \\(lateral-movement\\).*\\[[0-9]+\\] eapol  \\(enterprise-trust\\)  00:0c:29:11:22:33 <-> 01:80:c2:00:00:03  \\([0-9]+ packet\\(s\\)\\)")

# Tier 4 (wireless-backhaul): all five of this tier's own protocols (capwap-control/-data, lwapp-
# control/-data, gtp-u) are UDP-only, and PPPoE (also this tier) is EtherType-keyed -- so this
# fixture's own flows/ethernet_flows are BOTH empty (0 TCP flows, no VLAN-zoned L2 traffic either),
# making compliant.yaml's own verdict trivially COMPLIANT -- exactly the case that proves
# `--strict-it-protocols` is what's deciding the exit code below, not this report's own existing

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: COMPLIANT\n\nFlows evaluated: 0 .*NOTABLE IT PROTOCOLS \\(14\\):")

# WILL_FAIL alone (no PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION alongside it -- CTest inverts a regex match's
# contribution to pass/fail together with the exit code when both are set on the same test, which
# would make this assert the OPPOSITE of what it means to check; the sibling test above already
# pins this exact command's "Result: COMPLIANT" text, this one only needs the exit code).
add_test(NAME notable_protocols_strict_it_protocols_flips_exit_code

          --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml" --strict-it-protocols)
set_tests_properties(notable_protocols_strict_it_protocols_flips_exit_code PROPERTIES
  WILL_FAIL TRUE)

# Without --strict-it-protocols, the exact same capture/policy pair still exits 0 (COMPLIANT) --

add_test(NAME notable_protocols_without_strict_flag_stays_compliant

set_tests_properties(notable_protocols_without_strict_flag_stays_compliant PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: COMPLIANT")

# ============================================================================================
# CLI-configurable resource-exhaustion limits (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's "External code review and
# engineering priorities" item 7 -- see resource_limits.hpp for the full design). Five grouped
# `--max-*` flags, each overriding a whole category of the ~60-odd individually-named DoS-
# protection constants scattered across decoder.cpp and the protocol files. 0/unset (never
# passed) means every site keeps its own compile-time default -- already proven byte-identical
# to this feature's absence by the fact that every other test in this file above, none of which
# passes any of these five flags, still passes unchanged. The tests below instead demonstrate
# each flag's actual effect: set low enough, it visibly and correctly changes decode behavior.
# ============================================================================================

# --max-reassembly-bytes: sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap's first split (Modbus/TCP, 29 bytes across
# 2 TCP segments) normally reassembles cleanly (see tcp_reassembly_completes_and_decodes below/
# above); set low enough, decoder.cpp's general TCP reassembly path now abandons it instead.
add_test(NAME max_reassembly_bytes_abandons_normally_successful_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --max-reassembly-bytes 5 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_reassembly_bytes_abandons_normally_successful_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "TCP segment reassembly on this flow exceeded its safety cap \\(29 byte\\(s\\) across 2 segment\\(s\\)\\) -- abandoning it\; this segment's own payload is tried fresh instead")

# --max-reassembly-segments: same fixture/flow, same effect via the segment-count half of the
# same cap instead of the byte-count half -- confirms both halves of decoder.cpp's `if` are
# independently reachable through their own flag.
add_test(NAME max_reassembly_segments_abandons_normally_successful_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --max-reassembly-segments 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_reassembly_segments_abandons_normally_successful_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "TCP segment reassembly on this flow exceeded its safety cap \\(29 byte\\(s\\) across 2 segment\\(s\\)\\) -- abandoning it\; this segment's own payload is tried fresh instead")

# Security audit follow-up (docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch257.md's own "4.
# OT-specific security risks", item 3, "Protocol reassembly"): the same two --max-reassembly-*
# flags above, exercised against DNP3's OWN local fragment-reassembly cap (Dnp3ReassemblyState,
# dnp3.cpp) instead of the generic TCP-segment cap -- sample_dnp3.pcap's packets 8-9 normally
# reassemble a 2-frame, 18-byte fragment cleanly (see dnp3_reassembly_completes_across_packets
# below); set low enough, dnp3.cpp's own cap abandons it instead, with the application layer
# left undecoded.
add_test(NAME max_reassembly_bytes_abandons_dnp3_fragment_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --max-reassembly-bytes 5 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_reassembly_bytes_abandons_dnp3_fragment_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "DNP3 fragment reassembly on this TCP flow exceeded its safety cap \\(18 byte\\(s\\) across 2 frame\\(s\\)\\) -- abandoning it\; application layer not decoded")

add_test(NAME max_reassembly_segments_abandons_dnp3_fragment_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --max-reassembly-segments 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_reassembly_segments_abandons_dnp3_fragment_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "DNP3 fragment reassembly on this TCP flow exceeded its safety cap \\(18 byte\\(s\\) across 2 frame\\(s\\)\\) -- abandoning it\; application layer not decoded")

# Same audit, BACnet's own local segment-reassembly cap (BacnetReassemblyState, bacnet.cpp)
# instead -- sample_bacnet.pcap's invoke-id=60 exchange normally reassembles a 2-segment,
# 18-byte Confirmed-Request cleanly (see
# bacnet_segment_reassembly_confirmed_request_completes_and_decodes below). Unlike DNP3, BACnet's
# cap check is reachable from BOTH the starting and continuing segment branches (they fall
# through to shared code rather than the starting branch returning early), so the two flags trip
# at DIFFERENT points here: --max-reassembly-segments 1 still only trips once the second segment
# arrives (18 byte(s) across 2 segment(s), matching DNP3's shape), but --max-reassembly-bytes 5
# trips immediately on the FIRST segment alone, since that segment's own 9 bytes already exceed
# the cap before a second segment ever arrives.
add_test(NAME max_reassembly_segments_abandons_bacnet_segment_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet.pcap" --format text --max-reassembly-segments 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_reassembly_segments_abandons_bacnet_segment_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "segmented BACnet APDU reassembly for this \\(flow, invoke-id\\) exceeded its safety cap \\(18 byte\\(s\\) across 2 segment\\(s\\)\\) -- abandoning it\; service data not reassembled")

add_test(NAME max_reassembly_bytes_abandons_bacnet_segment_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet.pcap" --format text --max-reassembly-bytes 5 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_reassembly_bytes_abandons_bacnet_segment_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "segmented BACnet APDU reassembly for this \\(flow, invoke-id\\) exceeded its safety cap \\(9 byte\\(s\\) across 1 segment\\(s\\)\\) -- abandoning it\; service data not reassembled")

# --max-recursion-depth: tests/sample_goose_deep_nesting.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's own
# build_goose_deep_nesting_sample -- see its docstring) is a GOOSE allData structure nested three
# levels deep specifically so this flag has something to truncate; every other GOOSE fixture's
# allData is at most one level deep, too shallow to demonstrate this flag at any CLI-
# representable value (0 means "unset/default", not "a cap of zero").
add_test(NAME max_recursion_depth_goose_truncates
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_goose_deep_nesting.pcap" --format text --max-recursion-depth 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_recursion_depth_goose_truncates PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: allData\\[0.0\\]: nesting exceeds max depth \\(1\\) -- not decoded further")

# --max-decoded-objects: sample_dnp3.pcap's first Response frame carries two object headers
# (g1v2 with 3 points, g30v1) -- set low enough, both dnp3.cpp's per-fragment object-header cap
# and its per-header point-value cap visibly truncate, in the same decoded frame.
add_test(NAME max_decoded_objects_dnp3_truncates_headers_and_points
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --max-decoded-objects 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_decoded_objects_dnp3_truncates_headers_and_points PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "objects: \\[g1v2\\][^\n]*\n *note: object header 0: only the first 1 of 3 point value\\(s\\) were decoded \\(safety cap\\)[^\n]*\n *note: stopped after 1 object header\\(s\\), more may remain \\(safety cap\\)")

# --max-coalesced-messages: sample_hartip.pcap's Keep Alive flow normally decodes 2 HART-IP
# messages coalesced in one TCP payload (see hartip_tcp_coalesced_keep_alive_decoded above);
# set to 1, only the first is decoded and the existing "stopped after N" note style fires at the
# configured N instead of the compile-time default.
add_test(NAME max_coalesced_messages_hartip_stops_at_one
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip.pcap" --format text --max-coalesced-messages 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_coalesced_messages_hartip_stops_at_one PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.1.50:52150 -> 192.168.1.10:5094 \\(hart-ip\\)  \\[hartip\\]  Request Keep Alive[^\n]*\n *note: stopped after 1 HART-IP message\\(s\\) in this one TCP payload, more may remain \\(safety cap\\)")

# All eight flags are registered identically on all three subcommands (unlike the --modbus-port-
# style port-list flags, which remain decode-only) -- confirmed here via --help rather than only
# by cli_main.cpp's own add_resource_limit_options call sites, so a future accidental removal
# from one subcommand's wiring is actually caught by the test suite. (ROADMAP item 102 added the
# eighth, --max-active-fragment-groups.)
add_test(NAME resource_limit_flags_present_in_decode_help
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --help)
set_tests_properties(resource_limit_flags_present_in_decode_help PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "--max-reassembly-bytes[^\n]*\n.*--max-reassembly-segments[^\n]*\n.*--max-recursion-depth[^\n]*\n.*--max-decoded-objects[^\n]*\n.*--max-coalesced-messages[^\n]*\n.*--max-active-flows[^\n]*\n.*--max-flow-state-entries[^\n]*\n.*--max-active-fragment-groups")

add_test(NAME resource_limit_flags_present_in_policy_validate_help
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --help)
set_tests_properties(resource_limit_flags_present_in_policy_validate_help PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "--max-reassembly-bytes[^\n]*\n.*--max-reassembly-segments[^\n]*\n.*--max-recursion-depth[^\n]*\n.*--max-decoded-objects[^\n]*\n.*--max-coalesced-messages[^\n]*\n.*--max-active-flows[^\n]*\n.*--max-flow-state-entries[^\n]*\n.*--max-active-fragment-groups")

add_test(NAME resource_limit_flags_present_in_inventory_help
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --help)
set_tests_properties(resource_limit_flags_present_in_inventory_help PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "--max-reassembly-bytes[^\n]*\n.*--max-reassembly-segments[^\n]*\n.*--max-recursion-depth[^\n]*\n.*--max-decoded-objects[^\n]*\n.*--max-coalesced-messages[^\n]*\n.*--max-active-flows[^\n]*\n.*--max-flow-state-entries[^\n]*\n.*--max-active-fragment-groups")

# ============================================================================================
# --max-active-flows / --max-flow-state-entries (docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-
# patch160.md finding 1: "Unbounded lifetime of TCP/decoder flow state"). A different category
# from the five flags above: those bound the COST of any one flow/reassembly/message; these two
# bound the COUNT of distinct flows/sessions tracked at once, regardless of a capture's total
# flow count. See resource_limits.hpp's own comments on both fields and
# Decoder::reassemble_tcp_payload's/DecodeContext::flow_state<T>()'s (protocol_decoder.hpp) own
# fix comments for the full rationale.
# ============================================================================================

# --max-active-flows: sample_resource_exhaustion_active_flows.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_resource_exhaustion_active_flows_sample) has two DISTINCT TCP flows, each left "waiting
# for more" mid-reassembly. Uncapped, both entries coexist in Decoder::tcp_reassembly_ with no
# interaction; capped to 1, the second flow's own still-incomplete segment must evict the first
# flow's entry to make room.
add_test(NAME max_active_flows_evicts_other_flow_entry
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_active_flows.pcap" --format text --max-active-flows 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_active_flows_evicts_other_flow_entry PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2[^\n]*51701[^\n]*waiting for more[^\n]*\n *note: active TCP flow-reassembly limit \\(1\\) reached -- evicted an existing in-progress reassembly on another flow to make room for this one \\(--max-active-flows\\)")

# Unset (the default): both flows' entries coexist, no eviction note anywhere -- byte-identical
# to this feature's absence, the same bar every other resource_limits() field is held to.
add_test(NAME max_active_flows_unset_no_eviction
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_active_flows.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_active_flows_unset_no_eviction PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "waiting for more"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "active TCP flow-reassembly limit")

# --max-flow-state-entries: sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap (build_resource_
# exhaustion_flow_state_sample) has two DISTINCT Modbus TCP sessions, each opening with a
# request (creating a ModbusFlowState entry in Decoder::registry_flow_state_). Capped to 1,
# session 2's own request must evict session 1's entry; session 1's later response (matching
# transaction id, same session) then finds no pending request -- modbus.cpp's own "no
# outstanding request found" note -- proving the eviction actually happened, not merely that the
# flag was accepted. Contrast with modbus_authoritative_transaction_pairing-style tests
# elsewhere in this file, which show the SAME response correctly paired when nothing evicted it.
add_test(NAME max_flow_state_entries_evicts_other_session_state
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap" --format text --max-flow-state-entries 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_flow_state_entries_evicts_other_session_state PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: no outstanding request found on this TCP session for transaction id 100"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "authoritative pairing")

# Unset (the default): session 1's response still pairs authoritatively -- byte-identical to
# this feature's absence.
add_test(NAME max_flow_state_entries_unset_still_pairs
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_flow_state_entries_unset_still_pairs PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "authoritative pairing: response to transaction id 100"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "no outstanding request found")

# patch282 security review finding F4 ("resource limits are much better, but eviction can damage
# analytical correctness"): the flow-state eviction `decode --max-flow-state-entries 1` already
# proves above (session 2's request evicting session 1's ModbusFlowState) must ALSO surface as a
# persistent, run-level OBSERVATION INCOMPLETE condition on every one of the four report engines
# (DetectEngine/BaselineEngine/PolicyEngine/AssetInventoryEngine) -- not just as decode()'s own
# per-session "no outstanding request found" symptom -- because an evicted session's next packet
# looks exactly like a brand-new one to whichever of these engines is watching: a false "new
# originator"/"new conduit" finding, a baseline/policy verdict that can't be trusted. Reusing
# sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap (build_resource_exhaustion_flow_state_sample,
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py) rather than a new fixture -- same "evict session 1's state, then
# session 1's own response re-creates and evicts session 2's state" cascade --max-flow-state-
# entries 1 already produces above, which is why the eviction COUNT below is 2, not 1 (confirmed
# against the real built binary, not assumed -- see append_flow_state_eviction_reason's own
# comment, resource_limits.hpp, for why this is a single, centrally-worded reason line shared by
# every call site below, so the wording can never drift between engines).
#
# `bash -c "...; echo EXITCODE=$?"` plus a PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION spanning from "OBSERVATION
# INCOMPLETE" through to "EXITCODE=<N>" is this codebase's own established pattern for proving a
# resource-limit ceiling's exit code (see detect_engine_limits_tracked_keys_cap_marks_detect_
# incomplete and its siblings above) -- reused here rather than invented fresh.

add_test(NAME detect_flow_state_eviction_marks_observation_incomplete
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' detect --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap' --max-flow-state-entries 1; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(detect_flow_state_eviction_marks_observation_incomplete PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "OBSERVATION INCOMPLETE.*categories: flow_state_eviction.*flow-state eviction limit reached -- 2 state entries evicted.*--max-flow-state-entries.*EXITCODE=6")

add_test(NAME detect_flow_state_eviction_in_json_report
  COMMAND conduitscope detect --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap" --max-flow-state-entries 1 --format json)
set_tests_properties(detect_flow_state_eviction_in_json_report PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"observation_truncated\": true,\n *\"observation_status\": \"incomplete\",\n *\"observation_reasons\": \\[\"flow_state_eviction\"\\],\n *\"truncation_reasons\": \\[\"flow-state eviction limit reached -- 2 state entries evicted")

# F4 fix: before this, write_detection_report_cef (and its LEEF/syslog siblings) only ever emitted
# one line per curated finding -- a truncated run with zero findings (exactly this fixture's own
# case: eviction, not a detection technique, is what's being reported) would otherwise emit
# NOTHING here at all, indistinguishable from a genuinely clean, complete run to anything watching
# only this export stream. See observation_incomplete_extension_fields' own comment
# (security_event_format.hpp).
add_test(NAME detect_flow_state_eviction_in_cef_report
  COMMAND conduitscope detect --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap" --max-flow-state-entries 1 --format cef)
set_tests_properties(detect_flow_state_eviction_in_cef_report PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "CEF:0\\|conduitscope\\|conduitscope-detect\\|[^|]+\\|ObservationIncomplete\\|Observation incomplete\\|5\\|msg=flow-state eviction limit reached -- 2 state entries evicted.*reasonCount=1 cat=flow_state_eviction")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_flow_state_eviction_marks_observation_incomplete
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap' --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/empty_baseline.json' --max-flow-state-entries 1 2>&1; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_flow_state_eviction_marks_observation_incomplete PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "OBSERVATION INCOMPLETE.*categories: flow_state_eviction.*flow-state eviction limit reached -- 2 state entries evicted.*--max-flow-state-entries.*EXITCODE=5")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_flow_state_eviction_in_leef_report
  COMMAND conduitscope baseline check "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap" --baseline-file "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/empty_baseline.json" --max-flow-state-entries 1 --format leef)
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_flow_state_eviction_in_leef_report PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "LEEF:2\\.0\\|conduitscope\\|conduitscope-baseline\\|[^|]+\\|ObservationIncomplete\\|msg=flow-state eviction limit reached -- 2 state entries evicted.*reasonCount=1	cat=flow_state_eviction")

# `baseline learn` has no Report struct of its own to attach observation_truncated/
# truncation_reasons to (it absorbs best-effort and writes the merged baseline file either way,
# same Item 64 fix posture as engine.truncated() already has for its OWN three growth ceilings --
# see run_baseline_learn's own comment, cli_main.cpp) -- so this is a diagnostic warning on
# stderr, not an exit-code/report-field change, proven here against the identical wording the
# other four engines share.
add_test(NAME baseline_learn_flow_state_eviction_warns_diagnostically
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/flow_state_eviction_baseline_learn_scratch.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap' --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/flow_state_eviction_baseline_learn_scratch.json' --max-flow-state-entries 1")
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_flow_state_eviction_warns_diagnostically PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "warning: baseline observation of '.*' is INCOMPLETE.*flow-state eviction limit reached -- 2 state entries evicted")

set_tests_properties(policy_validate_flow_state_eviction_marks_observation_incomplete PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "OBSERVATION INCOMPLETE.*flow-state eviction limit reached -- 2 state entries evicted.*--max-flow-state-entries.*EXITCODE=6")

add_test(NAME policy_validate_flow_state_eviction_in_syslog_report

# Unset (the default), across all four report engines: no eviction occurred, so none of them may
