# -w writes every packet reaching this run to a new classic-pcap file, raw and unmodified --
# proven end to end by round-tripping: write sample_arp.pcap's own 6 packets out through -w, then
# read the written file straight back in and diff its --format json output against the
# original's own --format json output. Byte-identical JSON (same src_mac/dst_mac/summary/etc.
# for all 6 packets, in the same order) is only possible if -w genuinely wrote real, complete,
# correctly-ordered packet records rather than truncating, reordering, or corrupting anything --
# see pcap_writer.cpp's own file header for the classic-pcap format itself. Uses `diff` (not a
# PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION, which can't compare two command outputs against each other) via the
# same `bash -c` two-command pattern inventory_iec104_policy_out_round_trips_compliant already
# established elsewhere in this file for an analogous write-then-reread proof.
add_test(NAME pcap_write_dash_w_round_trips_byte_identical_json
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap' --write '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_roundtrip.pcap' --output /dev/null && diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap' --format json) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_roundtrip.pcap' --format json)")
set_tests_properties(pcap_write_dash_w_round_trips_byte_identical_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^$")

# `info` (its own dedicated summary command, distinct from `decode --stats`) reads the written
# file's own pcap global header back -- confirms -w wrote a genuinely well-formed 24-byte classic
# pcap header (correct magic/version, and the right link type/packet count), not just something
# `conduitscope decode` alone happens to tolerate.
add_test(NAME pcap_write_dash_w_produces_valid_pcap_header
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap' -w '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_header_check.pcap' --output /dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_header_check.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(pcap_write_dash_w_produces_valid_pcap_header PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "pcap version: +2\\.4\nlink type: +Ethernet\nsnaplen: .*\npackets: +6")

# Regression test for a real-world bug report: `-w` against a PCAPNG source (not classic pcap --
# see sample_arp.pcap's own test just above, which never exercised this) wrote a classic-pcap
# output file with link type 0 (LINKTYPE_NULL) instead of the source interface's real declared
# link type (Ethernet here), because PcapWriter is constructed from source.linktype() once,
# before the main packet loop's first next() call -- and, before pcap_reader.cpp's
# prefetch_first_interface_linktype() fix, a pcapng PcapReader's info().linktype wasn't populated
# from the file's own Interface Description Block until the first PACKET had actually been read.
# The practical symptom this reached the user as: Wireshark opening a `decode -w`-written file and
# showing every frame as unrecognized "Null/Loopback" raw data instead of Ethernet/IP/TCP/Modbus.
# sample_modbus.pcapng is a real pcapng fixture (build_pcapng_basic_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py)
# with a single Ethernet-linked interface, matching the single-interface shape of the real capture
# that surfaced this bug.
add_test(NAME pcap_write_dash_w_from_pcapng_source_produces_correct_linktype
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcapng' -w '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_pcapng_header_check.pcap' --output /dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_pcapng_header_check.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(pcap_write_dash_w_from_pcapng_source_produces_correct_linktype PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "pcap version: +2\\.4\nlink type: +Ethernet\nsnaplen: .*\npackets: +3")

# Same bug, but for a multi-interface pcapng source (sample_pcapng_multi_interface.pcapng,
# build_pcapng_multi_interface_sample -- interface 0: Ethernet, interface 1: Raw IP, both
# Interface Description Blocks declared before either packet): proves
# prefetch_first_interface_linktype() correctly picks up the FIRST declared interface (Ethernet)
# specifically, matching PcapReader's own class-level doc comment ("initially the first interface
# declared in the file"), not e.g. the last IDB parsed or some other value. Classic pcap has
# exactly one link type for the whole file, so -w against a genuinely multi-linktype pcapng source
# necessarily reinterprets every packet under this one chosen type -- see this test's own
# surrounding comment for why that's an inherent classic-pcap format limitation, not something
# this fix does or could address, and docs/USER_GUIDE.md's LIMITATIONS entry for the same.
add_test(NAME pcap_write_dash_w_from_multi_interface_pcapng_uses_first_interface_linktype
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_pcapng_multi_interface.pcapng' -w '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_pcapng_multi_header_check.pcap' --output /dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_pcapng_multi_header_check.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(pcap_write_dash_w_from_multi_interface_pcapng_uses_first_interface_linktype PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "pcap version: +2\\.4\nlink type: +Ethernet\nsnaplen: .*\npackets: +2")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IPv6 support (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md ROADMAP item 24) -- ipv6.hpp/ipv6.cpp's own base-header and
# RFC 8200 extension-header-chain parsing, format_ipv6's RFC 5952 canonical rendering, and
# decoder.cpp's shared version-sniffing dispatch (Decoder::decode_ip_payload, reached from either
# the IPv4 or the IPv6 branch), all exercised through real Modbus/TCP and plain UDP traffic --
# tests/sample_ipv6.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_ipv6_sample). Every regex below was
# confirmed against the real CLI output first, not guessed at.

# Packet 1: Modbus/TCP request over IPv6, no extension headers -- proves the whole upper-layer
# cascade (TCP dispatch, port-based Modbus recognition) is reachable over IPv6 at all, and that
# both addresses (each with one compressible zero run) render in RFC 5952 canonical form.
add_test(NAME ipv6_modbus_over_tcp_decodes_with_canonical_zero_run_compression
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_modbus_over_tcp_decodes_with_canonical_zero_run_compression PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  2001:db8::50:51000 -> 2001:db8::10:502")

# Packet 2: the response, paired to packet 1 via tcp_session_key/DecodeContext::session_key --
# proves the '#' flow-key/session-key separator fix (decoder.cpp's format_flow_endpoint, added
# alongside this same IPv6 work to remove a latent collision now that an IP address string can
# itself contain colons) didn't break authoritative TCP-session+transaction-ID pairing, the one
# existing feature that most directly depends on session_key uniqueness.
add_test(NAME ipv6_modbus_tcp_session_pairing_works_across_ipv6_addresses
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_modbus_tcp_session_pairing_works_across_ipv6_addresses PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "authoritative pairing: response to transaction id 1")

# Packet 3: a plain UDP datagram over IPv6 between two link-local addresses -- proves has_udp/
# src_port/dst_port populate correctly off an IPv6 outer header.
add_test(NAME ipv6_udp_datagram_decodes_with_link_local_addresses
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_udp_datagram_decodes_with_link_local_addresses PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  2\\.002000  fe80::1:34567 -> fe80::2:44444")

# Packet 4: the same Modbus request as packet 1, preceded by a chained Hop-by-Hop Options header
# and a Destination Options header -- proves parse_ipv6's extension-header walk correctly reaches
# the real upper-layer protocol AND the real payload past two extension headers (the request's own
# "read 4 holding register" text, unique to this packet, only decodes correctly if the walk landed
# exactly on the start of the TCP segment, not a few bytes short or long). Also exercises
# NO_COMPRESSION_ADDR (no zero run at all) to prove format_ipv6 renders plain colon-separated
# groups, with no "::", when there's nothing to compress.
add_test(NAME ipv6_extension_header_chain_walked_to_reach_modbus_payload
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_extension_header_chain_walked_to_reach_modbus_payload PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#4  3\\.003000  2001:db8:1:2:3:4:5:6:51001 -> 2001:db8::10:502.*read 4 holding register")

# Packet 5: next_header == ESP directly off the base header, no extension headers at all -- proves
# parse_ipv6 deliberately does NOT walk past ESP (its payload is encrypted, the same opaque-
# regardless-of-IP-version limit ESP already has over IPv4): it must surface as a recognized-but-
# undecoded ESP packet via decoder.cpp's existing GRE/ESP/AH/IPIP/6in4/L2TPv3 tunnel_vpn
# recognition, now reachable over IPv6 with no new code of its own.
add_test(NAME ipv6_esp_next_header_not_walked_past_reaches_tunnel_vpn_recognition
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_esp_next_header_not_walked_past_reaches_tunnel_vpn_recognition PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#5  4\\.004000  2001:db8::50 -> 2001:db8::10.*SPI=0x12345678")

# A raw-IP link type (no Ethernet framing, no ethertype field at all) carrying an IPv6 packet --
# proves decoder.cpp's version-sniff (peeking the IP version nibble directly) works with no
# ethertype hint to lean on at all, the scenario ROADMAP item 24 specifically calls out.
# tests/sample_ipv6_raw_link.pcapng (build_ipv6_raw_link_sample).
add_test(NAME ipv6_over_raw_ip_link_type_decodes_via_version_sniff
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_raw_link.pcapng" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_over_raw_ip_link_type_decodes_via_version_sniff PROPERTIES

# GE SRTP (Service Request Transport Protocol), GE Fanuc/GE Intelligent Platforms PLC families

# against the existing TPKT/COTP decoder found and fixed while building this decoder.
# tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap (build_ge_srtp_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py). Packet #2 (INIT_ACK)
# reuses real captured bytes from automayt/ICS-pcap's GE-SRTP/Notes.txt; every other packet is
# synthetic (no real public GE SRTP pcap capture is known to exist).

# EXTENDED_ACK response -- THE COLLISION-FIX REGRESSION TEST. Before the fix, GE SRTP's own
# declared-length function returned nullopt for EXTENDED_ACK (its body layout past the common
# header is not independently verified by any source, so no length was claimed), which let
# TPKT/COTP's weaker structural gate opportunistically claim this packet instead (GE SRTP's own
# Packet Type 3 supplies TPKT's magic version byte 0x03 by coincidence) and corrupt every
# subsequent server->client packet on the flow into a bogus ongoing TPKT reassembly. This packet
# must show [ge-srtp] with its honestly-undecoded body, NOT [tcp] buffering a TPKT/COTP PDU.
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_extended_ack_undecoded_body_and_tpkt_collision_fix
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ge_srtp_extended_ack_undecoded_body_and_tpkt_collision_fix PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#18  [^\n]*\\[ge-srtp\\]  EXTENDED_ACK response \\(14 byte\\(s\\) from byte 42 onward, layout not independently verified -- see ge_srtp\\.hpp\\)[^\n]*\n *note: matched to the write task memory request seen in packet #17"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#18[^\n]*TPKT")

# UNKNOWN (Packet Type 8) -- structural recognition of a packet type this decoder cannot further
# classify, honestly undecoded rather than guessed at.
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_unknown_packet_type_structural_recognition
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ge_srtp_unknown_packet_type_structural_recognition PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#19  [^\n]*UNKNOWN / Unrecognized message type 0xAB \\(not otherwise decoded\\)")

# NEGATIVE CONTROL: an orphan response (sequence number with no matching prior request on this

# service request.
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_orphan_response_no_outstanding_request_note

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#20[^\n]*\n *note: matched to")

# NEGATIVE CONTROL: a payload whose Packet Type (256) is not one of GE SRTP's own recognized
# values {0,1,2,3,8} must be REJECTED by GE SRTP's own gate and must NOT be misclassified as any
# other opportunistic protocol either (this exact payload's leading byte, chosen deliberately,
# would otherwise satisfy MQTT's own intentionally weak single-byte gate).
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_gate_rejects_invalid_packet_type_and_falls_through_cleanly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ge_srtp_gate_rejects_invalid_packet_type_and_falls_through_cleanly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#21  [^\n]*\\[tcp\\]  TCP payload of 56 byte\\(s\\) on port 53600->18245"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#21[^\n]*\\[(ge-srtp|mqtt)\\]")

# THE OTHER COLLISION-FIX REGRESSION TEST: a SHORT request's response split across two TCP
# segments, first segment only 20 of 56 bytes. Before the two-phase declared-length fix, GE
# SRTP's own function required the full 56 bytes before it could read Message Type (byte 31) and
# determine shape, so on this short first segment it returned nullopt unconditionally --
# letting TPKT/COTP's weaker gate win the race and misclassify the buffering state. Must show
# "buffering a GE SRTP message PDU/frame", not "buffering a TPKT/COTP PDU/frame".
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_short_first_segment_reassembly_two_phase_declaration_fix
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ge_srtp_short_first_segment_reassembly_two_phase_declaration_fix PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#23  [^\n]*buffering a GE SRTP message PDU/frame split across TCP segments 18245->53600: 20 of 56 declared byte\\(s\\) seen so far across 1 segment\\(s\\) on this flow, waiting for more"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#23[^\n]*TPKT")
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_reassembled_from_two_tcp_segments
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ge_srtp_reassembled_from_two_tcp_segments PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#24  [^\n]*\\[ge-srtp\\]  SHORT_ACK response: No error[^\n]*\n *note: reassembled a GE SRTP message PDU/frame from 56 byte\\(s\\) spanning 2 TCP segments on this flow\n *note: matched to the read system memory request seen in packet #22")

# Non-standard port (9999, not 18245) in Auto (port-gated) mode: GE SRTP's own GateKind::TcpPort
# means it does NOT claim traffic on an unconfigured port here -- the packet stays generic [tcp]

add_test(NAME ge_srtp_non_standard_port_not_claimed_in_auto_mode

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#25[^\n]*\\[ge-srtp\\]")

# The same non-standard-port exchange DOES decode correctly when GE SRTP is explicitly forced

# BSAP (Bristol Standard Asynchronous/Synchronous Protocol, Bristol Babcock/Emerson RTU protocol)
# recognition -- see bsap.hpp's own file header comment for the full sourcing writeup (including
# why this decoder treats the "BSAAP" name Jurgen pointed at as a naming variant of BSAP), the
# honestly-stated sourcing gap (no numeric RDB function-code table found anywhere, not even in the
# reference open-source Zeek parser this project cross-checked the header layout against), and the
# real dispatch-ordering collision (against both HART-IP's and FF-HSE's own fully opportunistic
# UDP checks) found and fixed via this project's own mandatory manual-CLI-verification-before-
# writing-any-CTest-regex discipline. tests/sample_bsap.pcap (build_bsap_sample,
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py) is entirely synthetic -- the pcap Jurgen pointed at
# (github.com/EmreEkin/ICS-Pcaps/tree/master/BSAAP) could not be browsed by this session's web
# tools (GitHub's robots.txt blocks directory listings).

# Serial-tunneled Local POLL -- structural recognition, decoded ADDR/SER/SEQ, and the one
# confirmed numeric link-function-code table (Emerson's own official document).
add_test(NAME bsap_serial_local_poll_recognized

set_tests_properties(bsap_serial_local_poll_recognized PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^\n]*\\[bsap\\]  BSAP serial-tunneled Local message: addr=5 ser=1 seq=100 dfun=POLL sfun=0x00")

# Serial-tunneled Local ACK/DOWN-ACK response, carrying an opaque trailing RDB-shaped body this
# decoder honestly does not further interpret -- confirmed via --format json that the trailing
# byte count is decoded even though its content is not.

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2  [^\n]*\\[bsap\\]  BSAP serial-tunneled Local message: addr=5 ser=1 seq=100 dfun=ACK / DOWN-ACK sfun=0x00")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"bsap_dfun\": \"ACK / DOWN-ACK\",\n *\"bsap_trailing_data_bytes\": 7,")

# Serial-tunneled Global message -- DADD/SADD/CTL decode, a different local address, and a

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bsap.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(bsap_serial_global_message_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"bsap_dadd\": 5,\n *\"bsap_sadd\": 1,")

# A Local message whose DFUN is NAK -- the one curated note this decoder adds (a directly
# observable link-layer failure signal, not a guess -- see bsap.hpp's SECURITY CONTEXT section for
# why this decoder does not add a note to every single frame the way GE SRTP's own per-operation
# notes do).
add_test(NAME bsap_serial_nak_curated_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bsap.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(bsap_serial_nak_curated_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#4  [^\n]*\\[bsap\\]  BSAP serial-tunneled Local message: addr=5 ser=3 seq=102 dfun=NAK sfun=0x00[^\n]*\n *note: NAK observed -- a negative acknowledgment at BSAP's own link layer")

# BSAP-IP-native framing: leading_value/message_func recognized structurally, trailing body shown
# as a byte count only (not descended into -- see bsap.hpp's BSAP-IP-NATIVE FRAMING section).
add_test(NAME bsap_ip_native_structural_recognition
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bsap.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(bsap_ip_native_structural_recognition PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#5  [^\n]*\\[bsap\\]  BSAP-IP-native message: leading_value=8 message_func=0x1 \\(8 byte\\(s\\) of body, not further decoded -- see bsap\\.hpp\\)")

# NEGATIVE CONTROL: a single byte -- too short even to read the 2-byte leading field this
# decoder's own gate depends on entirely. Must fall through to a plain, unclassified "udp" result,
# not "bsap" -- and, since BSAP now runs BEFORE HART-IP's/FF-HSE's own fully opportunistic checks
# (see decoder.cpp's own BSAP call site comment for the real collision that ordering fixes), also
# confirms this one-byte payload doesn't get misclassified as either of those either.
add_test(NAME bsap_gate_rejects_too_short_payload_falls_through_cleanly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bsap.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(bsap_gate_rejects_too_short_payload_falls_through_cleanly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#6  [^\n]*\\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 1 byte\\(s\\) on port 1234->1234"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#6[^\n]*\\[(bsap|hartip|ffhse)\\]")

# Non-standard port (9999, not 1234) in Auto (port-gated) mode: BSAP's own GateKind::UdpPort means

# CC-Link IE Field Network Basic (CCIEFB) -- see cclink_ie.hpp's own file header for the full

# 61450, SLMP node search/set-IP-address on UDP 61451) plus the critical MELSEC-coexistence design:
# a genuine MELSEC command riding the same 3E framing must not be swallowed (packet #8 below), and

# Orphan response, no session-tracked request (fresh 4-tuple) -- MUST fall through to MELSEC's own
# generic response handling, not be claimed/misattributed as cclink-ie. This is the direct proof of
# cclink_ie.hpp's own "RESPONSES CARRY NO COMMAND FIELD" design.
add_test(NAME cclink_ie_orphan_response_falls_through_to_melsec
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cclink_ie.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_orphan_response_falls_through_to_melsec PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#7  [^\n]*\\[melsec\\]  MELSEC response: Normal completion[^\n]*\n *note: no outstanding request found on this session"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#7  [^\n]*\\[cclink-ie\\]")

# A genuine MELSEC command (Batch Read, command 0x0401) riding the exact same 3E framing and port
# this decoder is tried on -- the direct zero-regression proof: 0x0401 is not one of this decoder's
# own 3 known commands, so it must still decode [melsec], never [cclink-ie].
add_test(NAME cclink_ie_genuine_melsec_command_not_swallowed
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cclink_ie.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_genuine_melsec_command_not_swallowed PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#8  [^\n]*\\[melsec\\]  Batch Read request: D100, 1 point\\(s\\), word units"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#8  [^\n]*\\[cclink-ie\\]")

# Same genuine MELSEC command, but with --protocol cclink-ie forced -- the sharpest proof of all:
# this decoder's own gate rejects it outright (command 0x0401 doesn't match 0x0E70/0x0E30/0x0E31),
# so forcing cclink-ie still correctly falls through to generic [udp], never fabricating a match.
add_test(NAME cclink_ie_forced_protocol_still_rejects_genuine_melsec_command
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cclink_ie.pcap" --protocol cclink-ie --format text)
set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_forced_protocol_still_rejects_genuine_melsec_command PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#8  [^\n]*\\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 21 byte\\(s\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#8  [^\n]*\\[cclink-ie\\]")

add_test(NAME cclink_ie_cyclic_response_non_success_end_code
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cclink_ie.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_cyclic_response_non_success_end_code PROPERTIES

add_test(NAME cclink_ie_non_standard_port_note

set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_non_standard_port_note PROPERTIES

# NEGATIVE CONTROL: a 2-byte payload carrying only the 3E-frame request magic -- too short for

# attack_detect.hpp -- classic network-layer DoS/reconnaissance attack signatures (see its own

# NOT sized into this fixture -- see attack_detect.hpp's own DEFAULT_FLOOD_THRESHOLD comment for

# NEGATIVE CONTROL: a flood targeting a broadcast-looking destination is never flagged, even at

# codesys.hpp/.cpp -- CODESYS V3 (3S-Smart/CODESYS GmbH's PLC runtime protocol), added at Jurgen's
# request. See codesys.hpp's own file header for the full sourcing (a public Wireshark dissector
# plus Kaspersky ICS-CERT's own reverse-engineering research), scoping (decided via
# AskUserQuestion: V3 only, structural-only beyond CmpDevice's own Login/AUTH exchange), and wire
# format writeup. sample_codesys.pcap (build_codesys_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py) carries 8
# TCP messages (OPEN_CHANNEL req/resp, Login/AUTH req/resp, a structural-only CmpApp command, a
# non-validating BLK continuation-block fallback, a non-standard-port variant, and a negative
# control) plus 4 UDP datagrams (Address Service, Channel Service GET_INFO on a standard and a
# non-standard port, and a negative control).
add_test(NAME codesys_tcp_open_channel_request_and_response
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_codesys.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(codesys_tcp_open_channel_request_and_response PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^\n]*\\[codesys\\]  CODESYS TCP Channel Service\; channel OPEN_CHANNEL ch=1[^\n]*\n#2  [^\n]*\\[codesys\\]  CODESYS TCP Channel Service\; channel OPEN_CHANNEL response ch=1")

# Login/AUTH request: username decoded, password field NEVER rendered (presence/length only),
# regardless of Kaspersky's own "encrypted" characterization -- mirrors this codebase's own
# NL_TRUST_PASSWORD/SAMR-style never-render-credential-bytes convention. FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION
# checks the raw password bytes never leak into the text output in any form.
add_test(NAME codesys_tcp_login_auth_username_decoded_password_never_rendered
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_codesys.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(codesys_tcp_login_auth_username_decoded_password_never_rendered PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  [^\n]*\\[codesys\\]  CODESYS TCP Channel Service\; channel BLK ch=1\; CmpDevice::Login \\(AUTH\\) session=0 user=\"engineer\"[^\n]*\n *note: Login/AUTH request carries a password field \\(10 byte\\(s\\)\\) -- never rendered by this decoder regardless of whether it is genuinely encrypted on the wire"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "s3cr3t")

add_test(NAME codesys_tcp_login_auth_response_session_id
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_codesys.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(codesys_tcp_login_auth_response_session_id PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#4  [^\n]*\\[codesys\\]  CODESYS TCP Channel Service\; channel BLK ch=1\; CmpDevice::Login \\(AUTH\\) session=0 new_session=1245391901")

add_test(NAME codesys_json_fields_auth_request

# GateKind::UdpPort -- CoAP is only attempted on a configured/expected port in Auto mode (unlike
# CC-Link IE/CODESYS's own UdpPortIndependent posture), so packet 9's own non-standard port

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#9[^\n]*\\[coap\\]")

# --coap-port WIDENS which port(s) are actually attempted in Auto mode (unlike --bsap-port's own
# sibling behavior of only widening the "expected" annotation -- CoAP's own gate is real port
# gating, not opportunistic-with-an-annotation) -- packet 9 now decodes as coap, no "non-standard"
# note since 6683 is now itself an expected port for this run.

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_coap.pcap" --coap-port 6683 --format text -v)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#9  [^\n]*\\[coap\\]  CoAP CON GET Message-ID=4103 Token=01 /sensors/temperature\n#10"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "not a configured/standard CoAP port")

# Forced --protocol coap tries every port regardless (like every other explicit protocol filter in

# SECURITY (headline finding): the BMC's own Open Session Response ACCEPTS Cipher Suite 0 -- the
# actual exploitable authentication-bypass condition (CVE-2013-4786-class).
add_test(NAME ipmi_cipher_suite_zero_open_session_response_accepted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipmi.pcap" --format text -v)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#12  [^\n]*\\[ipmi\\]  IPMI2\\.0/RMCP\\+ Open Session Response tag=2 status=No errors auth=RAKP-none \\[CIPHER SUITE 0 ACCEPTED\\][^\n]*\n *note: SECURITY: this Open Session Response ACCEPTS Cipher Suite 0 \\(Authentication Algorithm = RAKP-none, status = No errors\\) -- RAKP's own key-exchange authentication check will never happen for the rest of this session\; ANY password, including a nonexistent one, will complete this handshake")

# The sticky per-session note: RAKP Message 1 carries no algorithm field of its own, but this
# session's own earlier Open Session exchange already proposed/accepted Cipher Suite 0 -- see
# rmcp.hpp's own STATEFULNESS section (IpmiFlowState).

# ieee802154.hpp/.cpp + zigbee.hpp/.cpp -- IEEE 802.15.4 MAC framing (LINKTYPE_IEEE802_15_4_WITHFCS
# 195 and LINKTYPE_IEEE802_15_4_TAP 283) plus Zigbee NWK/APS/full ZDP. See both headers' own file
# header comments for the full sourcing/scoping/wire-format writeup. sample_zigbee.pcap
# (build_zigbee_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py, WITHFCS-framed) carries 13 named ZDP
# cluster request/response pairs, a broadcast Device_annce (no response), a curated
# Mgmt_Permit_Joining INDEFINITE-duration security note, an NWK-layer-security-enabled frame, an
# APS-layer-security-enabled frame (NWK security NOT enabled), an application-profile/ZCL frame
# (Profile ID != 0x0000, correctly not decoded), an APS Command frame, an NWK Command frame, a
# non-Data MAC frame type (Ack), and a MALFORMED/truncated (1-byte) frame. sample_zigbee_tap.pcap
# (build_zigbee_tap_sample, TAP-framed) exercises all three TAP FCS_TYPE variants (16-bit/none/
# 32-bit).

# NWK-layer security enabled: the NWK header (frame type/addressing/routing) decodes fully, but

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `baseline learn`/`baseline check` (baseline.hpp/baseline.cpp, roadmap item 41 -- see
# docs/design/baseline-engine.md). Reuses tests/sample_modbus.pcap/tests/sample_s7comm.pcap as the
# "known-good" baseline seed (per the design doc's own testing plan), plus the two deliberately
# mutated fixtures above (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_baseline_modbus_mutated_sample/
# build_baseline_two_conduit_sample) for the anomaly-detection cases those two unmodified captures
# can't exercise on their own. Every baseline file here is written under CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR
# (never tests/, which is source-controlled), one distinct filename per test so parallel `ctest -j`
# runs never race on the same file.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME baseline_learn_produces_expected_json
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_learn_expected.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_learn_expected.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7comm.pcap' && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_learn_expected.json'")
# "Write Var/Merkers/Flags (M)/bit" is the exact scenario Jurgen originally reported (a Merker
# bit-write showing up with has_target_range: false and no range at all) -- see extract_s7comm_
# operations' own comment for why a BIT-transport-size item now gets its own "/bit"-suffixed
# operation_key with a real bit_address-unit range ([0, 1) here: a single write to M0.0), instead of
# being excluded from range tracking the way it was before this feature. The store's own JSON schema
# is otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged (no s7_area_letter/s7_db_number/s7_range_unit fields --
# deliberately not persisted, see OperationBaseline's own comment, baseline.hpp), confirmed here by
# "Read Var/Data Block (DB)/DB10"'s own entry rendering identically to before this feature.
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_produces_expected_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"protocol\": \"modbus\",\n *\"server_port\": 502,\n *\"packet_count\": 1,.*\"operation_key\": \"Read Holding Registers\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[0, 10\\]\\].*\"protocol\": \"s7comm\",\n *\"server_port\": 102,\n *\"packet_count\": 2,.*\"operation_key\": \"Read Var/Data Block \\(DB\\)/DB10\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[100, 110\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Write Var/Merkers/Flags \\(M\\)/bit\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[0, 1\\]\\]")

# `learn` never emits a pass/fail verdict -- see baseline.hpp's own file header comment. Its own
# diagnostic summary line ("learned from N capture(s)...") is the only thing printed to stderr;
# nothing that looks like a compliance/anomaly verdict.
add_test(NAME baseline_learn_never_prints_a_verdict
  COMMAND conduitscope baseline learn --baseline-file "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_learn_no_verdict.json" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_never_prints_a_verdict PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "learned from 1 capture\\(s\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result:|ANOMAL|CLEAN")

# `check` against the deliberately mutated fixture -> exactly one NewOperation finding (Write

# `learn` run TWICE (two separate captures) merges into one cumulative baseline rather than the
# second run clobbering the first -- the first run's [0, 10) range must still be present alongside
# the second run's own new operation/range afterward.

  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_learn_twice.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_learn_twice.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_learn_twice.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_modbus_mutated.pcap' && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_learn_twice.json'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_twice_merges_ranges_rather_than_clobbering PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"first_seen_capture\": \".*sample_modbus\\.pcap\",\n *\"last_seen_capture\": \".*sample_baseline_modbus_mutated\\.pcap\".*\"operation_key\": \"Read Holding Registers\",\n *\"packet_count\": 3,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[0, 10\\], \\[200, 205\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Write Multiple Registers\"")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `baseline check --policy` -- zone-awareness follow-up (roadmap item 41's second deferred
# question, docs/design/baseline-engine.md's own "Follow-up" section: "does a new IP in an
# already-trusted zone count as NewConduit or not?"). Every test below independently `rm -f`s and
# re-`learn`s its own baseline file from tests/sample_modbus.pcap (HMI_IP=192.168.1.50 doing Read
# Holding Registers only -- the same fixture/one-liner-chaining convention every other
# baseline_check_* test above already uses), then `check`s against
# tests/policies/baseline_zone.yaml, whose "engineering_ws_zone" declares HMI_IP plus a second,
# never-learned workstation, 192.168.1.77.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(BASELINE_ZONE_POLICY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/policies/baseline_zone.yaml")

# Positive case: a SECOND, previously-unseen client (192.168.1.77) in the SAME declared zone as
# the learned host (HMI_IP), doing the EXACT SAME operation (Read Holding Registers, address 0,
# quantity 10) -- with --policy, this must be new-conduit-known-zone, naming both the zone and
# the vouching client IP (192.168.1.50), not plain new-conduit.
add_test(NAME baseline_check_zone_known_zone_new_host_text
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_new_host_text.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_new_host_text.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_new_host_text.json' --policy '${BASELINE_ZONE_POLICY}' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_zone_new_host.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_zone_known_zone_new_host_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1\\] new-conduit-known-zone  192\\.168\\.1\\.77 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:502  modbus  operation=\"Read Holding Registers\"  \\(1 packet\\(s\\)\\)\n *zone: engineering_ws_zone\n *already known in this zone: 192\\.168\\.1\\.50")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_zone_known_zone_new_host_json
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_new_host_json.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_new_host_json.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_new_host_json.json' --policy '${BASELINE_ZONE_POLICY}' --format json '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_zone_new_host.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_zone_known_zone_new_host_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"verdict\": \"new-conduit-known-zone\",\n *\"client_ip\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.77\",\n *\"server_ip\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.10\",\n *\"protocol\": \"modbus\",\n *\"server_port\": 502,\n *\"operation_key\": \"Read Holding Registers\",\n *\"zone\": \"engineering_ws_zone\",\n *\"zone_known_client_ips\": \\[\"192\\.168\\.1\\.50\"\\]")

# Negative control, same capture/baseline, --policy simply omitted: must be plain new-conduit,
# proving the flag itself (not some incidental property of the fixture) gates the behavior --
# exit code 4 (kExitBaselineAnomaly) either way, since a plain new-conduit finding is still
# non-compliant on its own.
add_test(NAME baseline_check_zone_flag_absent_is_plain_new_conduit
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_flag_absent.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_flag_absent.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_flag_absent.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_zone_new_host.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_zone_flag_absent_is_plain_new_conduit PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1\\] new-conduit  192\\.168\\.1\\.77 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:502  modbus  operation=\"Read Holding Registers\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "new-conduit-known-zone|\n *zone:")

# A client IP that --policy's own zones don't cover AT ALL (192.168.1.99, in neither
# engineering_ws_zone nor plc_zone) must stay plain new-conduit even with --policy given --
# zone_for() returning nullptr is exactly the "not in any declared zone" case.
add_test(NAME baseline_check_zone_client_not_in_any_zone_stays_new_conduit
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_unknown_host.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_unknown_host.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_unknown_host.json' --policy '${BASELINE_ZONE_POLICY}' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_zone_unknown_host.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_zone_client_not_in_any_zone_stays_new_conduit PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1\\] new-conduit  192\\.168\\.1\\.99 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:502  modbus  operation=\"Read Holding Registers\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "new-conduit-known-zone|\n *zone:")

# The conservative core of this whole feature: the second workstation IS in the same declared
# zone as the learned host, but doing Write Multiple Registers -- a function code NOBODY in the
# zone (not even HMI_IP) has ever been baselined doing (the learned baseline only ever taught
# Read Holding Registers). A known zone never vouches for an operation nobody in it has actually
# done -- this must stay full new-conduit even with --policy given.
add_test(NAME baseline_check_zone_known_zone_unprecedented_operation_stays_new_conduit
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_new_operation.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_new_operation.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_new_operation.json' --policy '${BASELINE_ZONE_POLICY}' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_zone_new_operation.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_zone_known_zone_unprecedented_operation_stays_new_conduit PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[1\\] new-conduit  192\\.168\\.1\\.77 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:502  modbus  operation=\"Write Multiple Registers\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "new-conduit-known-zone|\n *zone:")

# `baseline check` against sample_modbus.pcap's own already-known conduit/operation, --policy
# given: an EXACT baseline match must stay KnownOperation regardless of --policy -- zone
# awareness only ever applies to the "no exact conduit match" case, never overrides an
# already-known conduit. Zero findings, exit 0.
add_test(NAME baseline_check_zone_known_conduit_unaffected_by_policy
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_known_conduit.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_known_conduit.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_known_conduit.json' --policy '${BASELINE_ZONE_POLICY}' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_zone_known_conduit_unaffected_by_policy PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: CLEAN\n\n1 conduit\\(s\\) observed, 1 distinct operation\\(s\\) observed, 1 matched the baseline, 0 did not\n\nFINDINGS \\(0\\):\n *\\(none\\)")

# `baseline check --policy` with a policy file that exists but fails to parse (reusing the exact
# same PolicyError `policy validate --policy` already surfaces): caught by run_baseline_check's
# own PolicyError handler, exit code 1, not the baseline-anomaly exit code 4 -- a policy-file
# problem is a fatal setup error, not an anomaly finding. (A --policy path that doesn't exist at
# all is instead caught earlier, at the CLI layer, by ->check(CLI::ExistingFile) on the option
# itself -- see baseline_check_cmd's own --policy definition, cli_main.cpp.)
add_test(NAME baseline_check_zone_malformed_policy_file_is_a_fatal_error
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_malformed_policy.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_malformed_policy.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_zone_malformed_policy.json' --policy '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/policies/bad_missing_zones.yaml' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_zone_malformed_policy_file_is_a_fatal_error PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error:.*bad_missing_zones\\.yaml")

# `baseline check` against a nonexistent/never-learned-from baseline file: --baseline-file is
# ->check(CLI::ExistingFile)'d at the CLI layer (unlike `learn`'s own --baseline-file, which must
# accept a not-yet-existing path -- see baseline_learn_cmd's own option definition, cli_main.cpp),
# so this is a CLI11 argument-validation error, not a BaselineStoreError.
add_test(NAME baseline_check_missing_baseline_file_is_an_error
  COMMAND conduitscope baseline check --baseline-file "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/does_not_exist_baseline.json" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_missing_baseline_file_is_an_error PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "does_not_exist_baseline\\.json")

# `learn` against a not-yet-existing baseline file path is NOT an error -- it's exactly how a
# baseline gets created in the first place (see load_baseline_store's own comment, baseline.hpp).
# Removes any leftover file from a previous run of this same test in this same build directory
# first, so the assertion is about THIS run creating the file, not about it merely still existing
# from last time.
add_test(NAME baseline_learn_creates_a_new_baseline_file
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_fresh_create.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_fresh_create.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_fresh_create.json'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_creates_a_new_baseline_file PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"schema_version\": 1,\n *\"conduits\": \\[\n *\\{\n *\"client_ip\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.50\"")

# Item 68 (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md; finding 5, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-
# patch209.md): load_baseline_store now rejects a baseline file larger than --max-baseline-
# file-bytes BEFORE reading it into memory, rather than reading an arbitrarily large file
# unconditionally. A real 256 MiB+ fixture isn't practical to check into this repo, so this proves
# the enforcement path itself by learning a normal, small baseline file first, then pointing
# `learn`/`check` at it with a deliberately tiny override (1 byte) -- guaranteed to be smaller than
# any real baseline file's content, so this only tests the size-ceiling check firing correctly, not
# some coincidental fixture-size boundary. Each test below is fully self-contained (its own
# freshly (re-)learned baseline file, own filename) rather than depending on another test's file --
# this codebase has no CTest DEPENDS precedent anywhere else, and ctest -j runs tests in parallel by
# default, so sharing one file across separate add_test entries would be a real race. No
# WILL_FAIL on any of these: PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION alone already determines pass/fail regardless
# of exit code (see notable_protocols_strict_it_protocols_flips_exit_code's own comment above for
# why combining the two would invert the assertion), matching baseline_check_missing_baseline_
# file_is_an_error's own precedent for a deliberately-failing baseline command.
add_test(NAME baseline_max_file_bytes_learn_rejects_oversized_file
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_max_bytes_learn.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_max_bytes_learn.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_max_bytes_learn.json' --max-baseline-file-bytes 1 '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_max_file_bytes_learn_rejects_oversized_file PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "baseline file '.*baseline_max_bytes_learn\\.json': [0-9]+ byte\\(s\\) exceeds the 1 byte limit \\(--max-baseline-file-bytes to override\\)")

add_test(NAME baseline_max_file_bytes_check_rejects_oversized_file
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_max_bytes_check.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_max_bytes_check.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_max_bytes_check.json' --max-baseline-file-bytes 1 '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_max_file_bytes_check_rejects_oversized_file PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "baseline file '.*baseline_max_bytes_check\\.json': [0-9]+ byte\\(s\\) exceeds the 1 byte limit \\(--max-baseline-file-bytes to override\\)")

# The default (no --max-baseline-file-bytes at all) must NOT reject that same small, legitimate
# file -- proves kDefaultMaxBaselineFileBytes (256 MiB) is generous enough for ordinary use, not
# just that the override mechanism works.
add_test(NAME baseline_max_file_bytes_default_does_not_reject_a_normal_file
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_max_bytes_default.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_max_bytes_default.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_max_bytes_default.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_max_file_bytes_default_does_not_reject_a_normal_file PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: CLEAN")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Item 64 (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch209.md finding 1):
# BaselineEngine's own four internal growth ceilings (tracked TCP sessions, conduits, operations
# per conduit, ranges per operation) -- each --max-baseline-* flag actually engages its own cap,
# `baseline check` never exits 0/kExitBaselineAnomaly while the observation is truncated (always
# kExitBaselineIncomplete=5 instead, checked here via the "; echo EXITCODE=$?" idiom -- neither
# WILL_FAIL nor a bare nonzero-exit check can distinguish 5 from 1/4, and combining WILL_FAIL with
# PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION on the same test inverts the regex's own contribution to pass/fail in
# this codebase, see notable_protocols_strict_it_protocols_flips_exit_code's own comment above --
# so this appends a harmless trailing `echo`, making the test's own exit code always 0 and letting
# PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION alone decide, exactly like every other baseline_max_file_bytes_* test
# above), `baseline learn` still merges what it could observe but says so on stderr rather than
# silently writing an incomplete baseline, and the compiled defaults (50,000/20,000/5,000/1,000)
# never trip on any of this codebase's own small fixtures.
#
# tests/sample_baseline_two_conduit.pcap (used by baseline_check_two_conduit_isolation above) has
# exactly 2 distinct conduits -- --max-baseline-conduits 1 forces the second one to be refused.
add_test(NAME baseline_engine_limits_conduit_cap_marks_check_incomplete
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_conduit.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_conduit.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' >/dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_conduit.json' --max-baseline-conduits 1 '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_two_conduit.pcap'; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(baseline_engine_limits_conduit_cap_marks_check_incomplete PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "OBSERVATION INCOMPLETE.*categories: resource_limit.*conduit limit \\(1\\) reached.*--max-baseline-conduits.*EXITCODE=5")

# Same scenario, --format json: observation_truncated/truncation_reasons both populated, compliant
# still reads true (no findings -- the whole point is that a caller must check BOTH fields, not
# "compliant" alone, per observation_truncated's own comment, baseline.hpp).
add_test(NAME baseline_engine_limits_conduit_cap_json_fields
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_conduit_json.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_conduit_json.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' >/dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_conduit_json.json' --format json --max-baseline-conduits 1 '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_two_conduit.pcap'; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(baseline_engine_limits_conduit_cap_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"compliant\": true,\n *\"observation_truncated\": true,\n *\"observation_status\": \"incomplete\",\n *\"observation_reasons\": \\[\"resource_limit\"\\],\n *\"truncation_reasons\": \\[\"conduit limit \\(1\\) reached.*EXITCODE=5")

# tests/sample_baseline_modbus_mutated.pcap (used by the *_mutated_* tests above) has 2 distinct
# operation_keys on its one conduit ("Read Holding Registers", "Write Multiple Registers") --
# --max-baseline-operations-per-conduit 1 forces the second one to be refused. `learn` still
# writes a (partial) baseline rather than erroring out, but must say INCOMPLETE on stderr.
add_test(NAME baseline_engine_limits_operations_cap_marks_learn_incomplete
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_ops.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_ops.json' --max-baseline-operations-per-conduit 1 '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_modbus_mutated.pcap'; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(baseline_engine_limits_operations_cap_marks_learn_incomplete PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "warning: baseline observation of '.*' is INCOMPLETE.*operations-per-conduit limit \\(1\\) reached.*--max-baseline-operations-per-conduit.*EXITCODE=0")

# The compiled defaults (50,000/20,000/5,000/1,000) must never trip on this codebase's own small
# fixtures -- mirrors baseline_max_file_bytes_default_does_not_reject_a_normal_file's own role for
# item 68's ceiling. Reuses sample_baseline_two_conduit.pcap (2 conduits, still far under 20,000).
add_test(NAME baseline_engine_limits_defaults_do_not_trip_on_a_normal_capture
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_defaults.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_engine_limits_defaults.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_two_conduit.pcap'; echo EXITCODE=$?")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "EXITCODE=0"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "INCOMPLETE")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# S7comm bit-level range tracking + `baseline check --symbolic-addresses` (small follow-up to
# Phase 1/Phase 2 above, docs/design/baseline-engine.md's own "Follow-up" section): a BIT-transport-
# size S7 item now gets a real bit_address-unit range under its own "/bit"-suffixed operation_key
# (extract_s7comm_operations, baseline.cpp) instead of being excluded from range tracking, and
# `baseline check`'s new opt-in --symbolic-addresses flag renders Step7 byte/bit notation
# (s7_range_notation, s7comm.hpp/.cpp) alongside the existing raw numeric fields for S7comm
# NewTargetRange findings. tests/sample_baseline_s7comm_symbolic.pcap (build_baseline_s7comm_
# symbolic_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py) exercises both a byte-unit AND a bit-unit range on the
# SAME area (Merkers) on one conduit, plus one of each in a DB area, specifically to prove the
# mixed-access/never-merged property below.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# `learn` spot-check: mixed byte + bit access to the SAME area (Merkers) produces TWO separate
# OperationBaseline rows ("Read Var/Merkers/Flags (M)" byte-unit, "Write Var/Merkers/Flags (M)/bit"
# bit-unit) -- never one row with byte-unit and bit-unit numbers merged into the same
# observed_ranges vector. Also pins the DB-area byte/bit siblings ("Read Var/Data Block (DB)/DB5",
# "Write Var/Data Block (DB)/DB5/bit") and confirms the store's own JSON schema carries no
# s7_area_letter/s7_db_number/s7_range_unit fields (deliberately not persisted -- see
# OperationBaseline's own comment, baseline.hpp).
add_test(NAME baseline_learn_s7comm_bit_and_byte_are_separate_operations
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_s7comm_symbolic_learn.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_s7comm_symbolic_learn.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_s7comm_symbolic.pcap' && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_s7comm_symbolic_learn.json'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_s7comm_bit_and_byte_are_separate_operations PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"operation_key\": \"Read Var/Merkers/Flags \\(M\\)\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[20, 25\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Read Var/Data Block \\(DB\\)/DB5\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[10, 11\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Write Var/Merkers/Flags \\(M\\)/bit\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[99, 100\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Write Var/Data Block \\(DB\\)/DB5/bit\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[83, 84\\]\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "s7_area_letter|s7_db_number|s7_range_unit")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_s7comm_symbolic_unmodified_zero_findings

# Smaller follow-up (same release, docs/design/baseline-engine.md's "Follow-up" section, 0xB2/
# TIA1200SYM sub-case): Jurgen's own real 4SICS capture (4SICS-GeekLounge-151021.pcap) showed 36
# Merker-write packets landing with NO range at all, not even a "/bit" one -- the is_experimental
# (0xB2) branch in extract_s7comm_operations (baseline.cpp) did nothing, since item.count is always
# unset for a 0xB2 item. Fixed by tracking a single-point [bit_address, bit_address+1) observation
# under a new "/bit-symbolic"-suffixed operation_key -- distinct from the classic-BIT "/bit" key,
# since a 0xB2 item's range is a best-effort reconstruction (S7Item::is_experimental), never a
# item.count-confirmed span. tests/sample_s7comm_1200sym.pcap now also carries two synthetic
# DB-area 0xB2 items (DB5, DB10) proving db_number is correctly folded into this key too (item.area
# itself is never set for a 0xB2 item, so it can't be relied on for that the way a classic DB item's
# key already is -- see extract_s7comm_operations' own comment).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# `learn` spot-check: the five real Merker items (M2.0-M2.4, bit addresses 16-20) coalesce into ONE
# merged "Read Var/Merkers/Flags (M)/bit-symbolic" row spanning [16, 21) -- observed_ranges is a
# merged/coalesced set of intervals by design (OperationBaseline's own comment), not a per-packet
# list, so five adjacent single-bit observations legitimately merge into one contiguous span here,
# same as they would for a classic "/bit" item reading a run of adjacent bits. The two DB-area items
# (DB5, DB10) get their own separate rows, proving they don't collide onto one "Data Block (DB)/
# bit-symbolic" key despite sharing an area_name. The two synthetic decode-fallback edge cases
# (unrecognized area1, multi-LID) still correctly produce ONLY key-only, has_target_range:false
# entries ("Read Var/" and "Read Var/Merkers/Flags (M)" with no bit-symbolic suffix at all) -- proof
# this follow-up didn't change what those already-failing decodes contribute.

  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_1200sym_learn.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_1200sym_learn.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_s7comm_1200sym.pcap' && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_1200sym_learn.json'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_s7comm_1200sym_bit_symbolic PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"operation_key\": \"Read Var/Merkers/Flags \\(M\\)/bit-symbolic\",\n *\"packet_count\": 5,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[16, 21\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Read Var/\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": false,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Read Var/Merkers/Flags \\(M\\)\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": false,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Read Var/Data Block \\(DB\\)/DB5/bit-symbolic\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[58, 59\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Read Var/Data Block \\(DB\\)/DB10/bit-symbolic\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[165, 166\\]\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "s7_area_letter|s7_db_number|s7_range_unit")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Phase 2 (roadmap item 41, docs/design/baseline-engine.md): baseline coverage for the six
# protocols beyond S7comm/Modbus -- EtherNet/IP, DNP3, BACnet, OPC UA, MELSEC, FINS. Reuses each
# protocol's own existing sample pcap (no new fixtures created -- every one of the six already had
# enough real operation diversity to exercise this). Three tests per protocol, mirroring the
# Modbus/S7comm tests above:
#   - a `learn` spot-check that at least one full operation entry (key, has_target_range, and its
#     observed_ranges when range-tracked) comes out exactly as extract_<protocol>_operations
#     (baseline.cpp) is expected to produce;
#   - `check` against an UNMODIFIED copy of the same fixture -> CLEAN, proving the full learn/check
#     round-trip is stable for real per-protocol operation_key/range data, not just the synthetic
#     Modbus/S7comm cases above;
#   - `check` against a baseline that was NEVER learned from this conduit at all (a hand-written
#     empty store, `{"schema_version": 1, "conduits": []}` -- baseline files are plain, reviewable
#     JSON by design, see the design doc's own "Baseline state and persistence" section, so writing
#     one inline here is not a departure from how this file is meant to be handled) -> every
#     operation this capture observed becomes its own new-conduit finding, proving extraction feeds
#     correctly into check_baseline's own verdict machinery (already exhaustively tested against
#     Modbus/S7comm above -- this is per-protocol proof the SAME shared code path receives usable
#     operation_key/range data from each of the six, not a second copy of check_baseline's own
#     logic tests).
# For the three full-range-tracking protocols (DNP3, MELSEC, FINS) a fourth test additionally
# proves NewTargetRange fires correctly: `learn` normally, then shrink ONE already-learned range by
# a single unit with `sed` (baseline files are meant to be hand-edited/reviewed, per the design
# doc), then `check` the ORIGINAL, unmodified fixture against that shrunk baseline -- the capture's
# own real range no longer fits inside the (now smaller) baseline range, so NewTargetRange must
# fire with the exact observed/baseline bounds this test pins. EtherNet/IP, BACnet, and OPC UA have
# no range-tracking to exercise this way at all (see baseline.cpp's own per-protocol comments for
# why each is key-only), so they only get the three tests above.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- EtherNet/IP (CIP) -- key-only: see extract_enip_operations' own comment (baseline.cpp) -----

add_test(NAME baseline_learn_enip_produces_expected_operations
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_enip_learn.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_enip_learn.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap' && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_enip_learn.json'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_enip_produces_expected_operations PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"protocol\": \"enip\",\n *\"server_port\": 44818,.*\"operation_key\": \"Read_Tag\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": false,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\].*\"operation_key\": \"Write_Tag\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": false,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\]")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_enip_unmodified_zero_findings
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_enip_clean.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_enip_clean.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_enip_clean.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_enip_unmodified_zero_findings PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: CLEAN\n\n1 conduit\\(s\\) observed, 2 distinct operation\\(s\\) observed, 2 matched the baseline, 0 did not\n\nFINDINGS \\(0\\):\n *\\(none\\)")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_enip_empty_baseline_finds_new_conduit
  COMMAND bash -c "printf '{\"schema_version\": 1, \"conduits\": []}' > '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_enip_empty.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_enip_empty.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_enip_empty_baseline_finds_new_conduit PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: ANOMALIES FOUND \\(2 finding\\(s\\)\\).*\\[1\\] new-conduit  192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:44818  enip  operation=\"Read_Tag\".*\\[2\\] new-conduit  192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:44818  enip  operation=\"Write_Tag\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "new-operation|new-target-range")

# Shrinks the already-learned [0, 3) range for "Response/Binary Input/v2" down to [0, 2) with sed,
# then checks the SAME, unmodified fixture against that shrunk baseline -- the capture's own real
# range no longer fits, so this must produce exactly one NewTargetRange finding with the capture's
# real bounds ([0, 3)) and the (now shrunk) baseline's own bounds ([0, 2)) for context.
add_test(NAME baseline_check_dnp3_shrunk_range_finds_new_target_range
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_dnp3_shrunk.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_dnp3_shrunk.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap' && sed -i 's/\\[\\[0, 3\\]\\]/[[0, 2]]/' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_dnp3_shrunk.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_dnp3_shrunk.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_dnp3_shrunk_range_finds_new_target_range PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: ANOMALIES FOUND \\(1 finding\\(s\\)\\).*\\[1\\] new-target-range  192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:20000  dnp3  operation=\"Response/Binary Input/v2\".*observed range: \\[0, 3\\).*baseline ranges: \\[0, 2\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "new-conduit|new-operation")

# --- OPC UA -- key-only for every service except Read/Write/Call, which get one Operation PER
# addressed NodeId instead (Grok review item 3's OPC UA sub-item -- see extract_opcua_operations'
# own comment, baseline.cpp, and OpcUaMessage::node_ids' own comment, opcua.hpp) --------------------

# tests/sample_opcua.pcap's own ReadRequest/CallRequest each address exactly one NodeId, and its two
# WriteRequest packets address TWO DIFFERENT NodeIds (ns=2;i=1002 and ns=2;i=1003) -- proving the
# split actually happens: before this follow-up both WriteRequest packets collapsed into one shared
# "WriteRequest" operation_key (packet_count 2); now they're two distinct rows, each packet_count 1,
# which is the entire point of this sub-item (a conduit that only ever writes ns=2;i=1002 suddenly
# writing ns=2;i=1003 is exactly the kind of thing this engine exists to flag, and the old key would
# have hidden it entirely).
add_test(NAME baseline_learn_opcua_produces_expected_operations
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_learn.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_learn.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_opcua.pcap' && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_learn.json'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_opcua_produces_expected_operations PROPERTIES
  # ROADMAP item 146 (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md): ReadRequest/ns=2;i=1001's own packet_count is now 2,
  # not 1 -- the cross-packet chunk-reassembly fixture (tools/make_sample_pcap.py, packets 66-67)
  # reuses that same NodeId for its own reassembled ReadRequest, on the same client/server conduit.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"protocol\": \"opcua\",\n *\"server_port\": 4840,.*\"operation_key\": \"ReadRequest/ns=2\;i=1001\",\n *\"packet_count\": 2,\n *\"has_target_range\": false,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\].*\"operation_key\": \"WriteRequest/ns=2\;i=1002\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": false,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\].*\"operation_key\": \"CallRequest/object=ns=2\;i=2000 method=ns=2\;i=2001\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": false,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\].*\"operation_key\": \"WriteRequest/ns=2\;i=1003\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": false,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"operation_key\": \"WriteRequest\"|\"operation_key\": \"ReadRequest\"|\"operation_key\": \"CallRequest\"")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_opcua_unmodified_zero_findings
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_clean.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_clean.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_opcua.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_clean.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_opcua.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_opcua_unmodified_zero_findings PROPERTIES
  # 23 distinct operations, not 11 -- ROADMAP item 146's own Browse/subscriptions-group/
  # HistoryRead/chunk-reassembly fixtures (appended to the end of build_opcua_sample) add 12 more
  # distinct (conduit, operation_key) pairs on top of the pre-existing 11 (see this section's own
  # comment above for why the two WriteRequest packets key separately).
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: CLEAN\n\n1 conduit\\(s\\) observed, 23 distinct operation\\(s\\) observed, 23 matched the baseline, 0 did not\n\nFINDINGS \\(0\\):\n *\\(none\\)")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_opcua_empty_baseline_finds_new_conduit
  COMMAND bash -c "printf '{\"schema_version\": 1, \"conduits\": []}' > '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_empty.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_empty.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_opcua.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_opcua_empty_baseline_finds_new_conduit PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: ANOMALIES FOUND \\(23 finding\\(s\\)\\).*\\[6\\] new-conduit  192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:4840  opcua  operation=\"ReadRequest/ns=2\;i=1001\".*\\[7\\] new-conduit  192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:4840  opcua  operation=\"WriteRequest/ns=2\;i=1002\".*\\[8\\] new-conduit  192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:4840  opcua  operation=\"CallRequest/object=ns=2\;i=2000 method=ns=2\;i=2001\".*\\[9\\] new-conduit  192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:4840  opcua  operation=\"WriteRequest/ns=2\;i=1003\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "new-operation|new-target-range")

# The NEW behavior's own dedicated positive case: `learn` from the fixture, then `check` a SECOND
# capture on the SAME conduit that writes a NodeId (ns=2;i=9999) the baseline has never seen --
# must be NewOperation (the conduit and the OTHER NodeId are both already known; only this specific
# NodeId is new), never silently folded into the already-known "WriteRequest" behavior the old
# service-name-only key would have produced.
add_test(NAME baseline_check_opcua_new_nodeid_on_known_conduit_is_new_operation
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_new_nodeid.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_new_nodeid.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_opcua.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_opcua_new_nodeid.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_opcua_new_nodeid.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_opcua_new_nodeid_on_known_conduit_is_new_operation PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: ANOMALIES FOUND \\(1 finding\\(s\\)\\).*\\[1\\] new-operation  192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:4840  opcua  operation=\"WriteRequest/ns=2\;i=9999\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "new-conduit|WriteRequest/ns=2\\;i=1002|WriteRequest/ns=2\\;i=1003")

# response.md, "baseline process behavior, not just ports"), deferred from the S7comm/OPC UA
# follow-ups above until Iec104Result carried per-ASDU structured data -- see
# extract_iec104_operations' own comment, baseline.cpp, and Iec104AsduInfo's own comment,
# iec104.hpp, for the full "type/COT folded into the key, sq-driven range tracking" design ---------

add_test(NAME baseline_learn_iec104_produces_expected_operations
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_learn.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_learn.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_iec104.pcap' && cat '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_learn.json'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_iec104_produces_expected_operations PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"protocol\": \"iec104\",\n *\"server_port\": 2404,.*\"operation_key\": \"C_IC_NA_1/activation\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[0, 1\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"M_SP_NA_1/interrogated by station interrogation\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[100, 103\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"M_ME_TD_1/spontaneous\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[200, 201\\]\\].*\"operation_key\": \"C_DC_NA_1/activation\",\n *\"packet_count\": 1,\n *\"has_target_range\": true,\n *\"observed_ranges\": \\[\\[300, 301\\]\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"operation_key\": \"M_SP_NA_1\",|\"operation_key\": \"M_ME_TD_1\",|\"operation_key\": \"C_DC_NA_1\",|\"operation_key\": \"C_IC_NA_1\",")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_iec104_unmodified_zero_findings
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_clean.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_clean.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_iec104.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_clean.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_iec104.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_iec104_unmodified_zero_findings PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: CLEAN\n\n1 conduit\\(s\\) observed, 6 distinct operation\\(s\\) observed, 6 matched the baseline, 0 did not\n\nFINDINGS \\(0\\):\n *\\(none\\)")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_iec104_empty_baseline_finds_new_conduit
  COMMAND bash -c "printf '{\"schema_version\": 1, \"conduits\": []}' > '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_empty.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_empty.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_iec104.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_iec104_empty_baseline_finds_new_conduit PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: ANOMALIES FOUND \\(6 finding\\(s\\)\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "new-operation|new-target-range")

# The NEW behavior's own dedicated positive case: `learn` from the fixture, then `check` a SECOND,
# standalone capture on the SAME conduit reporting a spontaneous M_ME_TD_1 value at IOA 999 -- a
# point the learned baseline's own [200,201) range for "M_ME_TD_1/spontaneous" doesn't cover. Both
# the conduit AND the operation_key (type AND COT) are already known -- only the address itself is
# new -- so this must be new-target-range, never new-conduit/new-operation.
add_test(NAME baseline_check_iec104_new_ioa_on_known_conduit_is_new_target_range
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_new_ioa.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_new_ioa.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_iec104.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_iec104_new_ioa.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_baseline_iec104_new_ioa.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_iec104_new_ioa_on_known_conduit_is_new_target_range PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: ANOMALIES FOUND \\(1 finding\\(s\\)\\).*\\[1\\] new-target-range  192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:2404  iec104  operation=\"M_ME_TD_1/spontaneous\".*observed range: \\[999, 1000\\).*baseline ranges: \\[200, 201\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "new-conduit|new-operation")

# AMQP 0-9-1 and AMQP 1.0 (amqp091.hpp/amqp10.hpp, amqp_common.hpp) -- two wire-INCOMPATIBLE
# protocols that share TCP port 5672 by convention. tests/sample_amqp091.pcap and
# tests/sample_amqp10.pcap (build_amqp091_sample/build_amqp10_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py)
# are entirely synthetic, built directly against this feature's own byte-exact sourcing pass (see
# amqp091.hpp's/amqp10.hpp's own SOURCING notes) -- no real-capture corpus for either protocol was
# available to this session. See amqp_common.hpp's own file header comment for the shared 8-byte
# preamble detection posture (sticky per-session, decline-to-classify when never captured) these
# two fixtures both exercise.

# --- AMQP 0-9-1 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME amqp091_preamble_and_connection_start_recognized
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_amqp091.pcap" --format text -v)

# Headline finding: a PLAIN Connection.Start-Ok is a real cleartext credential exchange -- AND the
# redaction proof: the literal password ("S3cr3tPLC!99") must never appear in this format's own
# output, only the username and the frame's own byte-length.

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_amqp091.pcap" --format text -v)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  [^\n]*\\[amqp091\\]  AMQP 0-9-1 METHOD \\(channel 0\\): Connection\\.Start-Ok \\(mechanism=PLAIN\\)[^\n]*\n *note: cleartext credential exchange: SASL mechanism \"PLAIN\" carries the password in the clear on this connection \\(username: \"scada_svc\"\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "S3cr3tPLC!99")

add_test(NAME amqp091_start_ok_json_redaction_proof

# HEARTBEAT frame -- decodes correctly when AMQP 0-9-1 is explicitly forced (see amqp091.hpp's own

# this exact byte pattern first -- a narrow, honestly-documented ambiguity unique to this one frame
# shape, not a general 0-9-1-vs-Modbus collision).
