# Regression: an array (0xf0) whose shared element constructor is a zero-width AMQP 1.0
# primitive (null=0x40) previously drove read_amqp10_array's element loop with the
# attacker-declared `count` alone (each iteration consumed zero bytes from the array's byte
# region), causing unbounded std::vector<Amqp10Value> growth and an out-of-memory abort -- a
# real crash libFuzzer's fuzz_amqp10 harness found. A count of 0xFFFFFFFF must now decode as a
# bounded, capped array with no crash.

# --- DICOM (dicom.hpp) ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# tests/sample_dicom.pcap (build_dicom_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py) is entirely synthetic,
# built directly against this feature's own byte-exact sourcing pass (PS3.7/PS3.8/PS3.5/PS3.15 and
# Wireshark's packet-dcm.c dissector -- see dicom.hpp's own SOURCING notes). It covers seven
# associations across seven distinct TCP sessions on ports 61000-61006, checked against BOTH
# standard DICOM ports (11112 for most, 104 for the sixth) plus one non-standard port (9999, for the
# seventh) to prove Auto-mode's port gating.

# Full A-ASSOCIATE-RQ/AC handshake, three Presentation Contexts (Verification/C-ECHO, CT Storage
# offering two transfer syntaxes, Study Root Q/R-FIND), each accepted in the AC with its own
# negotiated transfer syntax -- proves the fixed-field layout, Application Context, and nested
# Abstract/Transfer Syntax sub-item parsing for both the RQ and AC forms.
add_test(NAME dicom_associate_rq_recognized
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dicom.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(dicom_associate_rq_recognized PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^\n]*\\[dicom\\]  A-ASSOCIATE-RQ \\(called=\"PACS_AE\", calling=\"CT_MODALITY1\"\\)")

add_test(NAME dicom_associate_rq_json_presentation_contexts_and_transfer_syntax_offer
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dicom.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dicom_associate_rq_json_presentation_contexts_and_transfer_syntax_offer PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"dicom_application_context_uid\": \"1\\.2\\.840\\.10008\\.3\\.1\\.1\\.1\",\n *\"dicom_presentation_contexts\": \\[\\{\"id\": 1, \"abstract_syntax\": \"Verification SOP Class\", \"transfer_syntaxes\": \\[\"Implicit VR Little Endian\"\\]\\}, \\{\"id\": 3, \"abstract_syntax\": \"CT Image Storage\", \"transfer_syntaxes\": \\[\"Implicit VR Little Endian\", \"Explicit VR Little Endian\"\\]\\}, \\{\"id\": 5, \"abstract_syntax\": \"Study Root Query/Retrieve Information Model - FIND\", \"transfer_syntaxes\": \\[\"Implicit VR Little Endian\"\\]\\}\\]")

add_test(NAME dicom_associate_ac_json_accepted_transfer_syntax_per_context
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dicom.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(dicom_associate_ac_json_accepted_transfer_syntax_per_context PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"dicom_presentation_contexts\": \\[\\{\"id\": 1, \"result\": \"Acceptance\", \"transfer_syntax\": \"Implicit VR Little Endian\"\\}, \\{\"id\": 3, \"result\": \"Acceptance\", \"transfer_syntax\": \"Explicit VR Little Endian\"\\}, \\{\"id\": 5, \"result\": \"Acceptance\", \"transfer_syntax\": \"Implicit VR Little Endian\"\\}\\]")

# --- Tridium Niagara Fox (fox.hpp) ----------------------------------------------------------------
# tests/sample_fox.pcap (build_fox_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py) is ENTIRELY SYNTHETIC -- this
# feature's own research pass (fox-info.nse / MartinoTommasini's third-party Wireshark dissector)
# could source the field-name/grammar SHAPE of real Fox traffic, but not a literal byte-exact
# capture to reproduce verbatim (see fox.hpp's own SOURCING section for the full confidence-tier
# breakdown). Covers a `fox hello` request/reply pair (packets #1/#2, the headline unauthenticated-
# identity-disclosure finding), a generic non-hello frame exercising every documented tuple type tag
# (packet #3), a frame split across two TCP segments (packets #4/#5, proving
# FoxDecoder::tcp_declared_length's terminator-scan reassembly), a second hello pair whose reply's
# own hostAddress deliberately differs from the observed TCP peer IP (packets #6/#7, the secondary
# finding), a non-standard-port hello pair (packets #8/#9, port 9999 -- proves Auto-mode's port
# gating and --protocol fox/--fox-port), and a FOXS (Fox-over-TLS, port 4911) ClientHello-only
# packet (#10, detection only).

# The fox hello request itself -- proves the header-line grammar (frame type/seq/reply/channel/
# command) and the curated FoxHelloFields extraction, plus the headline unauthenticated-exchange
# note firing on the REQUEST side too (not just the reply).
add_test(NAME fox_hello_request_recognized_and_curated_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fox.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(fox_hello_request_recognized_and_curated_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^\n]*\\[fox\\]  Fox hello request: hostName=\"ENGINEER-LAPTOP\", hostAddress=\"192\\.168\\.1\\.50\", id=\"1\", app\\.name=\"Workbench\", app\\.version=\"4\\.10\\.0\\.16\", os\\.name=\"Windows 10\"[^\n]*\n *note: unauthenticated Fox hello exchange")

# The fox hello reply -- the station answering with its OWN identity, unauthenticated -- plus the
# JSON structured-field proof (every curated FoxHelloFields member, not just a generic tuple dump).
add_test(NAME fox_hello_reply_json_curated_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fox.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(fox_hello_reply_json_curated_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"fox_is_hello\": true,\n *\"fox_hello_fox_version\": \"1\\.0\",\n *\"fox_hello_id\": \"1\",\n *\"fox_hello_host_name\": \"NIAGARA-STATION-A\",\n *\"fox_hello_host_address\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.10\",\n *\"fox_hello_app_name\": \"Station\",\n *\"fox_hello_app_version\": \"4\\.10\\.0\\.16\",\n *\"fox_hello_vm_name\": \"Java HotSpot\\(TM\\) Embedded Client VM\",\n *\"fox_hello_vm_version\": \"1\\.8\\.0_202\",\n *\"fox_hello_os_name\": \"QNX\",\n *\"fox_hello_os_version\": \"6\\.5\\.0\",\n *\"fox_hello_lang\": \"en\",\n *\"fox_hello_time_zone\": \"America/New_York\",\n *\"fox_hello_host_id\": \"Niagara-JACE8000-0042\",\n *\"fox_hello_vm_uuid\": \"b2c3d4e5-1111-2222-3333-445566778899\",\n *\"fox_hello_brand_id\": \"tridium\"")

# The generic (non-hello) frame -- proves the fully generic key=type:value tuple grammar decodes
# every documented type tag (s/i/f/t/z/b/o/m, including a recursive nested 'm' message) correctly,
# independent of any hello-specific field handling.
add_test(NAME fox_generic_frame_all_tuple_types_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fox.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(fox_generic_frame_all_tuple_types_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"fox_channel\": \"test\",\n *\"fox_command\": \"echo\",\n *\"fox_is_hello\": false,\n *\"fox_tuples\": \\[\\{\"key\": \"greeting\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"hello world\"\\}, \\{\"key\": \"count\", \"type\": \"int\", \"value\": \"42\"\\}, \\{\"key\": \"ratio\", \"type\": \"float\", \"value\": \"3\\.14\"\\}, \\{\"key\": \"lastBoot\", \"type\": \"time\", \"value\": \"0xbc614e[^\"]*\"\\}, \\{\"key\": \"enabled\", \"type\": \"bool\", \"value\": \"true\"\\}, \\{\"key\": \"payload\", \"type\": \"blob\", \"value\": \"5 byte\\(s\\) \\(blob\\)\"\\}, \\{\"key\": \"cert\", \"type\": \"object\", \"value\": \"type=\\\\\"javax\\.security\\.cert\\.X509Certificate\\\\\", 3 byte\\(s\\) \\(object\\)\"\\}, \\{\"key\": \"nestedGroup\", \"type\": \"message\", \"nested\": \\[\\{\"key\": \"subKey\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"nested value\"\\}, \\{\"key\": \"subCount\", \"type\": \"int\", \"value\": \"3\"\\}\\]\\}\\]")

# A Fox frame split across two TCP segments -- packet #4 must show the buffering-in-progress note
# (never a premature/garbled decode), and packet #5 must show the completed, reassembled frame with
# its own "reassembled ... spanning 2 TCP segments" note -- proving
# FoxDecoder::tcp_declared_length's terminator-scan reassembly works, not just the single-segment
# common case.
add_test(NAME fox_split_across_two_tcp_segments_reassembled
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fox.pcap" --format text -v)

# Secondary finding: a hello reply whose own hostAddress ("10.99.99.99") differs from the actual

# --stats aggregation: frame type counts, the headline unauthenticated-hello-exchange finding (4:
# both request+reply on BOTH standard-port hello sessions, packets #1/#2 and #6/#7 -- the
# non-standard-port session #8/#9 is NOT counted here since Auto mode never claims it as fox at all,
# proving this isn't a blind total-packet count), and the secondary hostAddress-mismatch finding (1).

  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fox.pcap")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "fox frame type counts:\n *Asynchronous *3[^\n]*\n *Keep-alive *1[^\n]*\n *Reply *2[^\\*]*\\*\\*\\* Fox hello exchanges observed \\(unauthenticated system-identity disclosure\\) 4 \\*\\*\\*\nfox hello exchanges with hostAddress differing from the observed TCP peer IP \\(internal-topology leakage signal\\) observed: 1")

# Regression (packet #11): a 'b' (blob) tuple with a 34-digit size field -- more digits than
# std::stoull's unsigned-long-long range can hold. libFuzzer's fuzz_fox harness found this as a
# real crash: the uncaught std::out_of_range std::stoull throws took the whole process down via
# std::terminate/abort, not just a ParseError this decoder already knows how to report. Fixed by
# catching it in parse_fox_tuples and re-throwing as a ParseError, exactly like the existing
# seq/reply guard two lines below in parse_one_fox_frame ("Fox frame: malformed seq/reply
# number") already does for the identical failure mode on a different field -- so this pins the
# CORRECT post-fix behavior: the frame is silently NOT claimed as fox (try_parse_fox_pdu's own
# catch(ParseError) returns std::nullopt) and falls through to the generic TCP summary, the same
# as any other structurally malformed Fox frame, instead of crashing.
add_test(NAME fox_oversized_blob_size_field_does_not_crash
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_fox.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(fox_oversized_blob_size_field_does_not_crash PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#11  [^\n]*\\[tcp\\]  TCP payload of 70 byte\\(s\\) on port 61106->1911")

# --- ICMPv6/NDP (icmpv6.hpp) and DHCPv6 (dhcpv6.hpp) -- roadmap item 45 --------------------------
# tests/sample_icmpv6_ndp.pcap (build_icmpv6_ndp_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py) covers RFC
# 4443/4861/4862/8106/4191: RS+SLLA (#1), RA with Prefix Information (A-flag/SLAAC), MTU, RDNSS and
# RIO options (#2), NS (#3), solicited NA with TLLA (#4), Redirect (#5), an Echo Request/Reply pair
# with a real pseudo-header checksum (#6/#7), a name-only error type (Destination Unreachable, #8),
# a deliberately checksum-mismatched Echo Request (#9), an unknown NDP option type that must be
# skipped gracefully rather than misparsed (#10), and a malformed Length==0 NDP option that must stop
# the option walk rather than hang or misparse (#11).

# JSON: every RA option decoded (SLLA, Prefix Information with A-flag/on-link/lifetimes, MTU, RDNSS

# --protocol icmpv6 filters out everything else; --protocol dhcpv6 on an ICMPv6-only capture claims

# tests/sample_dhcpv6.pcap (build_dhcpv6_sample) covers RFC 8415: SOLICIT with DUID-LLT/ORO/Elapsed
# Time/Rapid Commit (#1), ADVERTISE with DUID-LL server + IA_NA/IA Address/Status Code Success (#2),
# a REQUEST/REPLY pair (#3/#4), a REPLY with a non-success Status Code (NoAddrsAvail, #5), a REPLY
# exercising DUID-EN (client) + DUID-UUID (server) + IA_PD/IA Prefix (#6, which also happens to be
# this fixture's own second distinct Server DUID -- see the rogue-server note it triggers below), and
# a RELAY-FORW wrapping an inner SOLICIT (#7, inner message deliberately not decoded).

add_test(NAME dhcpv6_solicit_and_advertise
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dhcpv6.pcap" --format text -v)

# --- IPv6 attack-detection sibling (ipv6_attack_detect.hpp) -- roadmap item 45 -------------------
# Each fixture below pairs a positive case with a negative/control case in the SAME capture, so a
# false positive on ordinary traffic is caught the same way a missed detection would be.

# tests/sample_ipv6_attack_ra_collision.pcap: packets #1/#2 are the SAME router repeating an
# IDENTICAL RA (negative control -- must NOT flag a collision); packet #3 is a second router
# advertising conflicting default-router information (positive case).
add_test(NAME ipv6_attack_ra_collision_negative_control_consistent_router
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_attack_ra_collision.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_attack_ra_collision_negative_control_consistent_router PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^\n]*\\[icmpv6\\]  ICMPv6 Router Advertisement[^\n]*\n#2  [^\n]*\\[icmpv6\\]  ICMPv6 Router Advertisement"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1[^\n]*\n *note: multiple Router Advertisement identities|#2[^\n]*\n *note: multiple Router Advertisement identities")
add_test(NAME ipv6_attack_ra_collision_positive_conflicting_router
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_attack_ra_collision.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_attack_ra_collision_positive_conflicting_router PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  [^\n]*\\[icmpv6\\]  ICMPv6 Router Advertisement[^\n]*\n *note: multiple Router Advertisement identities observed advertising conflicting default-router information[^\n]*worth investigating[^\n]*RFC 6104")

# tests/sample_ipv6_attack_na_spoof.pcap: two distinct link-layer addresses both send NA for the
# same target address -- the IPv6 analogue of ARP spoofing.
add_test(NAME ipv6_attack_na_spoof_distinct_link_layer_addresses
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_attack_na_spoof.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_attack_na_spoof_distinct_link_layer_addresses PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^\n]*\\[icmpv6\\]  ICMPv6 Neighbor Advertisement[^\n]*\n#2  [^\n]*\\[icmpv6\\]  ICMPv6 Neighbor Advertisement[^\n]*\n *note: Neighbor Advertisement spoofing suspected: 2 distinct link-layer addresses observed claiming the same target address \\(2001:db8::99\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1[^\n]*\n *note:")

# tests/sample_ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion.pcap, run with a small --flood-threshold 5 so the
# fixture doesn't need thousands of packets: packets #1/#2 are ONE client legitimately retrying
# (byte-identical DUID -- same MAC AND same DUID Time value, only the transaction ID differs, the
# same shape a real SOLICIT retransmit has on the wire -- negative control, must NOT count as 2
# distinct identities), packets #3-#7 are 5 further DISTINCT client DUIDs -- 6 distinct DUIDs
# total, crossing a --flood-threshold of 5 on packet #6 (see the fixture's own comment in
# make_sample_pcap.py for the exact count breakdown).
add_test(NAME ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion_negative_control_single_retry
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion.pcap" --flood-threshold 5 --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion_negative_control_single_retry PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^\n]*\\[dhcpv6\\]  DHCPv6 SOLICIT[^\n]*\n#2  [^\n]*\\[dhcpv6\\]  DHCPv6 SOLICIT"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1[^\n]*\n *note: DHCPv6 exhaustion|#2[^\n]*\n *note: DHCPv6 exhaustion")
# A genuinely dedup-SENSITIVE negative control: --flood-threshold 2 is low enough that if the two
# retry packets were (wrongly) counted as 2 distinct DUIDs instead of 1, this would false-positive
# on packet #2 -- unlike the --flood-threshold 5 test above, which stays silent on packets #1/#2
# whether or not deduplication actually works (5 is never reached that early either way), so it
# alone can't catch a broken dedup. This test can, and does: the note must stay silent through
# packet #2 and only start firing once the FIRST distinct-from-the-retry client (packet #3) pushes
# the count to 2.
add_test(NAME ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion_negative_control_dedup_sensitive
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion.pcap" --flood-threshold 2 --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion_negative_control_dedup_sensitive PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  [^\n]*\n *note: DHCPv6 exhaustion suspected: 2 DISTINCT Client DUIDs"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1[^\n]*\n *note: DHCPv6 exhaustion|#2[^\n]*\n *note: DHCPv6 exhaustion")
add_test(NAME ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion_positive_distinct_duids
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion.pcap" --flood-threshold 5 --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion_positive_distinct_duids PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#6  [^\n]*\n *note: DHCPv6 exhaustion suspected: 5 DISTINCT Client DUIDs observed sending SOLICIT/REQUEST in this capture \\(threshold: 5\\)[^\n]*flood_dhcpc6[^\n]*counted by distinct identity, not raw packet count, so one legitimate client retrying does not trip this")
# At the DEFAULT threshold (100), this fixture's 6 distinct DUIDs must NOT trip exhaustion at all --
# proves --flood-threshold genuinely governs this counter rather than a hardcoded small constant.
add_test(NAME ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion_default_threshold_not_tripped
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_attack_dhcpv6_exhaustion_default_threshold_not_tripped PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: DHCPv6 exhaustion suspected")

# tests/sample_ipv6_attack_rogue_dhcpv6_server.pcap: two distinct Server DUIDs both answer with
# REPLY -- the multi-server note (also independently exercised as a side effect within
# sample_dhcpv6.pcap's own packet #6, see dhcpv6_duid_en_and_uuid_with_ia_pd_prefix above).
add_test(NAME ipv6_attack_rogue_dhcpv6_server_distinct_server_duids
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_attack_rogue_dhcpv6_server.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_attack_rogue_dhcpv6_server_distinct_server_duids PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^\n]*\\[dhcpv6\\]  DHCPv6 REPLY[^\n]*\n#2  [^\n]*\\[dhcpv6\\]  DHCPv6 REPLY[^\n]*\n *note: multiple DHCPv6 server identities observed \\(2 distinct Server DUIDs answering ADVERTISE/REPLY in this capture\\)[^\n]*worth investigating[^\n]*fake_dhcps6[^\n]*T1557\\.003"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1[^\n]*\n *note:")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `-d`/`--decode-as` (Wireshark/tshark-style "force a decoder onto traffic that wouldn't
# otherwise be recognized as it") -- see decoder.hpp's DecodeAsRule/DecodeOptions::decode_as
# comment, cli_main.cpp's parse_decode_as_rules, and tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_decode_as_sample for the full design and fixture writeup. Deliberately scoped to
# PORT-GATED protocols only (see those same comments for why the opportunistic ICS protocols and
# the tunnel-vpn tier's IP-protocol-number-gated names are out of scope).

add_test(NAME decode_as_absent_reproduces_prior_behavior
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_decode_as.pcap")
set_tests_properties(decode_as_absent_reproduces_prior_behavior PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 12 byte\\(s\\) on port 33001->55901.*\\[tcp\\]  TCP payload of 16 byte\\(s\\) on port 33002->55902.*\\[tcp\\]  TCP payload of 16 byte\\(s\\) on port 33003->55903.*\\[ssh\\]  SSH version-exchange banner \"SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[dns\\]|\\[ldaps\\]|\\[tacacs-plus\\]")

add_test(NAME decode_as_group_a_name_matches_its_own_dedicated_port_option
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --dns-port 55901 --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_decode_as.pcap")
set_tests_properties(decode_as_group_a_name_matches_its_own_dedicated_port_option PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[dns\\]  DNS query id=0x0000 Query, 0 question\\(s\\), 0 answer\\(s\\), 0 authority\\(-ies\\), 0 additional\\(s\\)")

add_test(NAME decode_as_group_a_rule_has_identical_effect_to_its_dedicated_port_option
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text -d udp.port==55901,dns --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_decode_as.pcap")
set_tests_properties(decode_as_group_a_rule_has_identical_effect_to_its_dedicated_port_option PROPERTIES

# Each of the five error-path tests below asserts BOTH a specific exit code (1) AND a specific
# error message on the same invocation. WILL_FAIL alongside PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION on one test
# inverts the regex's contribution to pass/fail in this codebase's CTest setup (see
# notable_protocols_strict_it_protocols_flips_exit_code's own comment above), so -- same
# established idiom as the baseline_engine_limits_*_marks_*_incomplete tests -- these wrap the
# invocation in `bash -c "...; echo EXITCODE=$?"`, keeping the wrapper's OWN exit code 0 (so
# PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION alone decides pass/fail) while asserting the real exit code via the
# echoed value.
add_test(NAME decode_as_rejects_malformed_selector_syntax
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --format text -d bogus --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_decode_as.pcap'; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(decode_as_rejects_malformed_selector_syntax PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: -d/--decode-as 'bogus' must start with 'tcp\\.port==' or 'udp\\.port=='.*EXITCODE=1")

add_test(NAME decode_as_rejects_unrecognized_protocol_name
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --format text -d 'tcp.port==55902,modbus' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_decode_as.pcap'; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(decode_as_rejects_unrecognized_protocol_name PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: -d/--decode-as 'tcp\\.port==55902,modbus': unrecognized protocol name 'modbus'.*EXITCODE=1")

add_test(NAME decode_as_rejects_transport_name_mismatch_group_a
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --format text -d 'tcp.port==55901,dns' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_decode_as.pcap'; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(decode_as_rejects_transport_name_mismatch_group_a PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: -d/--decode-as 'tcp\\.port==55901,dns': 'dns' is a UDP-only protocol, not TCP.*EXITCODE=1")

add_test(NAME decode_as_rejects_transport_name_mismatch_group_bc
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --format text -d 'udp.port==55902,ldaps' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_decode_as.pcap'; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(decode_as_rejects_transport_name_mismatch_group_bc PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: -d/--decode-as 'udp\\.port==55902,ldaps': 'ldaps' \\(tier \"enterprise-trust\"\\) is TCP-only, not UDP.*EXITCODE=1")

add_test(NAME decode_as_rejects_out_of_range_port
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --format text -d 'tcp.port==99999,ldaps' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_decode_as.pcap'; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(decode_as_rejects_out_of_range_port PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: -d/--decode-as 'tcp\\.port==99999,ldaps' has an invalid port '99999'.*EXITCODE=1")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Grok gap #2 phase 9: STIX/TAXII-lite export (`inventory --format stix`) -- see
# write_inventory_stix_json's own doc comment (asset_inventory.hpp) for the exact bundle/SDO
# shape, the deterministic-UUID design (FNV-1a, RFC 9562 version 8, NOT sha256.hpp -- see that
# comment for why), and why this is a plain STIX 2.1 bundle file with no TAXII transport (confirmed
# with Jurgen). Reuses the same two fixtures phase 8's tests do, for the same reason (a new
# rendering of already-tested asset data).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# CMake/CTest's own regex engine has no {n} bounded-repetition support (see every other regex in
# this file -- none use it either), so each hex group is spelled out one character class at a time
# rather than "[0-9a-f]{8}" and similar. The bundle id itself is deliberately NOT asserted against
# an exact expected value here (unlike the infrastructure object id test below, whose id depends
# only on the asset's IP): the bundle id is derived from "bundle:" + capture_path
# (deterministic_uuid's own comment), and capture_path is this fixture's own absolute filesystem
# path as CTest invokes it (CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR) -- a value that legitimately differs between
# checkouts/CI runners, so pinning to one machine's derived UUID here would be a flaky test, not a
# real assertion. Determinism itself (same input, re-run twice, byte-identical bundle) was verified
# manually during development, matching this project's own "manual CLI verification before writing
# CTest assertions" discipline; this test's job is only to confirm the id's *shape* is a valid,
# version-8, variant-correct UUID -- shape is stable across machines, the literal digits are not.
add_test(NAME inventory_stix_bundle_shape
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format stix --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_stix_bundle_shape PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"type\": \"bundle\",\n *\"id\": \"bundle--[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]-[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]-8[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]-[89ab][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]-[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]\",\n *\"objects\": \\[")

add_test(NAME inventory_stix_enip_identity_object
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format stix --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_stix_enip_identity_object PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"id\": \"infrastructure--151c5cd9-4a77-8131-9376-6fb94d6ee481\",\n *\"created\": \"2023-11-14T22:46:40\\.000Z\",\n *\"modified\": \"2023-11-14T22:46:48\\.008Z\",\n *\"name\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.10\",\n *\"infrastructure_types\": \\[\"unknown\"\\],\n *\"x_conduitscope_ip\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.10\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_mac\": \"00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_vendor\": \"Vendor ID 1\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_product\": \"Conduit-ENIP-Sample\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_firmware_revision\": \"2\\.1\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_serial_number\": \"0x1337ab\"")

# The client (HMI) side never sent a ListIdentity response -- vendor/product/firmware_revision/
# serial_number/plant_identification/security_posture custom properties must be omitted entirely
# (never emitted as "" or null), same omit-never-null convention the JSON/CSV writers already
# establish -- proven here by x_conduitscope_mac being followed immediately by
# x_conduitscope_inferred_role, with nothing in between.
add_test(NAME inventory_stix_no_identity_fields_omitted_for_client
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format stix --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_stix_no_identity_fields_omitted_for_client PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"name\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.50\",\n *\"infrastructure_types\": \\[\"unknown\"\\],\n *\"x_conduitscope_ip\": \"192\\.168\\.1\\.50\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_mac\": \"00:0c:29:11:22:33\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_inferred_role\": \"Unknown\"")

# x_conduitscope_protocols renders as a real JSON array (not a joined string the way CSV's
# 'protocols' column has to be) -- exercised with the same multi-protocol asset phase 8's CSV

add_test(NAME inventory_stix_protocols_is_json_array
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format stix --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_role_classification.pcap")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"x_conduitscope_protocols\": \\[\"dnp3\", \"modbus\", \"s7comm\"\\]")

# stix never includes zone/conduit data (renamed from this test's original "..._is_asset_only_..."
# name, which stopped being accurate once relationship SROs -- derived from report.edges, see below

# asset-only, but it still never carries a literal "edges"/"zones"/"conduits" JSON key, and never

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Follow-up to Grok gap #2 phases 8/9, added after initial delivery at Jurgen's request: a SEPARATE
# edges CSV (`--edges-csv`) and conduits CSV (`--conduits-csv`) -- phase 8's own `--format csv`
# stayed deliberately asset-only (see write_inventory_report_csv's own doc comment) -- plus
# `relationship` SROs added to `--format stix`'s bundle, one per InventoryEdge, linking the
# `infrastructure` SDOs into a graph a STIX consumer can traverse (see write_inventory_stix_json's
# own doc comment, asset_inventory.hpp, for the full design, including exactly how incoming/outgoing
# is encoded via source_ref/target_ref). Reuses the same fixtures already used above, for the same
# "new rendering of already-tested data" reasoning.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME inventory_stix_relationship_shape
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format stix --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_stix_relationship_shape PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"type\": \"relationship\",\n *\"spec_version\": \"2\\.1\",\n *\"id\": \"relationship--[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]-[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]-8[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]-[89ab][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]-[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]\",\n *\"created\":.*\"relationship_type\": \"communicates-with\",\n *\"source_ref\": \"infrastructure--.*\",\n *\"target_ref\": \"infrastructure--.*\"")

# Exact values are safe to pin here (unlike the bundle id): the relationship id is derived from
# `edge_key(protocol, client_ip, server_ip, server_port)`, which -- unlike the bundle id's own
# "bundle:" + capture_path key -- never includes the capture's filesystem path, so it's identical
# across checkouts/CI runners. source_ref/target_ref reuse the SAME infrastructure ids
# inventory_stix_enip_identity_object above already pins (151c5cd9... for .10, the server) --
# .50 (the client) resolves to 152a54d9..., confirmed by manual verification during development.
add_test(NAME inventory_stix_relationship_exact_values
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format stix --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_stix_relationship_exact_values PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"id\": \"relationship--148352bf-ec49-85d3-b99d-527615770043\",\n *\"created\": \"2023-11-14T22:46:40\\.000Z\",\n *\"modified\": \"2023-11-14T22:46:48\\.008Z\",\n *\"relationship_type\": \"communicates-with\",\n *\"source_ref\": \"infrastructure--152a54d9-4a83-80f5-9383-e7b94d7a3ac5\",\n *\"target_ref\": \"infrastructure--151c5cd9-4a77-8131-9376-6fb94d6ee481\",\n *\"description\": \"enip \\(port 44818\\)\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_protocol\": \"enip\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_server_port\": 44818,\n *\"x_conduitscope_server_port_service\": \"enip\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_packet_count\": 9,\n *\"x_conduitscope_direction_source\": \"port-heuristic\",\n *\"x_conduitscope_observed_functions\": \\[\"Read_Tag\", \"Write_Tag\"\\]")

# One relationship per InventoryEdge -- sample_inventory.pcap has 5 edges (see the COMMUNICATIONS
# section in inventory_zone_prefix_override_regroups_zones's own fixture output above), so the
# bundle must carry exactly 5 relationship objects alongside its 9 infrastructure objects, and every
# source_ref/target_ref must resolve to an infrastructure id actually present in this same bundle
# (proven with a small Python check during manual verification, not re-litigated here -- this CTest
# assertion just pins the object-count shape, which is what would actually regress if a future
# change dropped or duplicated edges).
add_test(NAME inventory_stix_relationship_count_matches_edges

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `detect` (detect_engine.hpp/cpp, mitre_attack_ics.hpp/cpp) -- "Detection that OT IR teams
# recognize" (Grok gap #4, docs/reviews/2026-09-grok-ics-ot-improvement-areas.md item 4,
# docs/design/detection-engine.md's own design record). Phases 1-4 of that plan: subcommand
# scaffolding, always-notable control-plane/firmware findings from already-decoded fields, and
# new-vs-known remote-access/CIP-originator findings. Phases 5-6 (the new UMAS decoder and its
# wiring into this engine) land in a later phase of work -- see detect_engine.hpp's own header
# comment for the full always-notable-vs-new-vs-known design this engine implements.
#
# tests/sample_detect.pcap (build_detect_sample in tools/make_sample_pcap.py) is the primary
# fixture -- purpose-built (no pre-existing fixture pcap happened to contain this specific mix of
# traffic shapes) to exercise every Phase 2-4 finding source in one capture: an S7comm Request
# Download, a DNP3 Cold Restart, a DNP3 Enable-Unsolicited-then-matching-Unsolicited-Response pair
# (must NOT flag) plus a second outstation's Unsolicited Response with no prior Enable seen at all
# (must flag), an IEC 104 ASDU with an out-of-range/"unknown" cause-of-transmission, an IEC 104
# Reset Process command, a BACnet ReinitializeDevice request, a BACnet DeviceCommunicationControl
# request, two CIP Forward_Open requests from two different originators against the same target
# (only the second is new-relative-to-this-capture), and one RDP (remote-access) session -- 12
# packets total, 9 findings. See that builder's own docstring for the full scenario list.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- --baseline-file: resolves new-vs-known findings against real history (baseline.hpp's own
# --- load_baseline_store/BaselineStore, reused read-only -- see detect_engine.hpp's own header
# --- comment). Learns from sample_detect.pcap itself so the baseline genuinely contains the CIP
# --- conduit both originators used (192.168.1.66->.65 and 192.168.1.67->.65 -- `baseline learn`
# --- tracks enip Forward_Open as a conduit operation, confirmed via manual verification during
# --- development) but never learns an rdp conduit at all (rdp carries no baseline-trackable
# --- operations -- is_baseline_protocol() (baseline.cpp) doesn't include it), so this one baseline
# --- file exercises BOTH new-vs-known outcomes in a single run: the CIP finding (novelty
# --- FirstOccurrence with no baseline) is genuinely present in it and drops out of the report
# --- entirely; the rdp finding (also FirstOccurrence with no baseline) is genuinely absent and
# --- upgrades to DetectionNovelty::ConfirmedNew -- its severity stays Moderate throughout, since a
# --- baseline only ever resolves novelty, never severity or evidence (see NewConduitCandidate's own
# --- comment, detect_engine.hpp).
add_test(NAME detect_baseline_file_suppresses_known_and_upgrades_absent_to_confirmed_new
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/detect_baseline_smoke.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/detect_baseline_smoke.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_detect.pcap' >/dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' detect --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_detect.pcap' --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/detect_baseline_smoke.json'")
set_tests_properties(detect_baseline_file_suppresses_known_and_upgrades_absent_to_confirmed_new PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "findings: 8 \\(Critical 5, Moderate 3, Informational 0\\).*Protocol Misuse: 3.*\\[Remote-Access Channel\\] T0886 \\(Remote Services\\)\n  evidence: Heuristic  novelty: Confirmed New  severity: Moderate\n  192\\.168\\.1\\.68 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.69:3389 \\(rdp\\)\n  New rdp \\(remote-access\\) session 192\\.168\\.1\\.68 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.69:3389 -- confirmed absent from the supplied baseline"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "CIP Forward_Open from a new originator")

# --- --policy: resolves a RemoteAccessChannel finding's technique between T0886 (Remote Services,

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Six Snort-style pattern extensions to `detect` (docs/design/detection-engine.md's own "Snort-
# style pattern extensions" section has the full research/scoping record for each pattern --
# Jurgen's own follow-up ask after gap #4 shipped, "how do I add more detection patterns like
# those of Snort"). tests/sample_detect_snort_patterns.pcap (build_detect_snort_patterns_sample,
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py) covers five of the six in one 16-packet capture, each on its own
# conduit, each paired with a negative/contrast conduit proving the pattern does NOT fire when its
# own condition isn't met: CIP Set_Attribute_Single write to the Identity object; DNP3 Operate with
# no prior Select (contrasted with a Select-then-Operate conduit that must NOT flag); Modbus Write
# Multiple Registers outside every prior read (contrasted with a fully-covered write that must NOT
# flag); S7comm Setup Communication probing, resolved in finish() (contrasted with a pair that also
# does a PLC Stop, whose OWN T0858 finding fires but the probing finding must NOT); and the
# download-then-restart composite (an S7 Request Download and PLC Stop against the same server,
# 10s apart, producing the two individual findings PLUS one T0831 composite). The sixth -- a BACnet
# Who-Is volumetric flood -- is in its OWN fixture, tests/sample_detect_bacnet_who_is_flood.pcap
# (build_detect_bacnet_who_is_flood_sample): it genuinely needs kBacnetWhoIsFloodThreshold-worth of
# packets (100, detect_engine.cpp), which would make the other five scenarios' exact packet-count
# assertions brittle to that threshold constant if interleaved into the same capture.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Every finding source in sample_detect_snort_patterns.pcap, pinned in first-seen order (see this
# section's own header comment for what each scenario is) -- one large regex, same style as
# detect_sample_detect_text_all_findings above, rather than one add_test per finding: these 8
# findings are one coherent, order-dependent report, and the exact "findings: 8" total is itself
# what proves none of the four negative/contrast conduits (DNP3 Select-then-Operate, Modbus fully-
# covered write, S7 probing-pair-that-also-did-real-work) produced an extra finding.
add_test(NAME detect_snort_patterns_all_findings
  COMMAND conduitscope detect --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_detect_snort_patterns.pcap")
set_tests_properties(detect_snort_patterns_all_findings PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "total packets: 16.*findings: 8 \\(Critical 6, Moderate 0, Informational 2\\).*evidence: Confirmed 8, Heuristic 0.*  Engineering-Station Activity: 3.*  Firmware/Logic Change: 2.*  Remote-Access Channel: 0.*  Protocol Misuse: 3.*\\[Protocol Misuse\\] T0855 \\(Unauthorized Command Message\\).*evidence: Confirmed  novelty: N/A  severity: Critical.*192\\.168\\.1\\.70 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.71:44818 \\(enip\\).*CIP Set_Attribute_Single write to the Identity object \\(class 0x01\\) -- broadened-scope stand-in for a ControlLogix-style remote run/program/remote mode change: this engine cannot confirm which specific Identity attribute was written \\(no citable primary source for that wire format\\), so every write to this object is flagged rather than guessing at one.*\\[Protocol Misuse\\] T0855 \\(Unauthorized Command Message\\).*evidence: Confirmed  novelty: N/A  severity: Critical.*192\\.168\\.1\\.70 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.72:20000 \\(dnp3\\).*DNP3 Operate \\(0x04\\) with no matching Select \\(0x03\\) ever seen for this master/outstation pair in this capture -- either the Select happened before this capture began, or the outstation is accepting Operate without requiring Select-before-Operate first \\(not the same thing as Direct Operate 0x05, which this engine never flags -- Direct Operate is a legitimate, intentional bypass of Select-before-Operate, not a violation of it\\).*\\[Protocol Misuse\\] T0831 \\(Manipulation of Control\\).*evidence: Confirmed  novelty: N/A  severity: Informational.*192\\.168\\.1\\.70 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.74:502 \\(modbus\\).*Modbus Write Multiple Registers to address range \\[100, 105\\) not fully covered by any prior read \\(same conduit, same address table\\) in this capture -- a genuinely weak signal on its own \\(many legitimate deployments write setpoints without reading them back first\\): treat as a prompt to check this range's purpose, not as confirmed misuse.*\\[Engineering-Station Activity\\] T0858 \\(Change Operating Mode\\).*evidence: Confirmed  novelty: N/A  severity: Critical.*192\\.168\\.1\\.70 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.77:102 \\(s7comm\\).*S7comm PLC Stop command -- CPU commanded to STOP from the process network.*\\[Firmware/Logic Change\\] T0843 \\(Program Download\\).*evidence: Confirmed  novelty: N/A  severity: Critical.*192\\.168\\.1\\.70 # ROADMAP item 119 (patch257 section 3.B, "Four-axis detection model"): CEF/LEEF/syslog format
# coverage for sample_detect_snort_patterns.pcap -- unlike sample_detect.pcap's own CEF/LEEF/
# syslog tests above (which cover Critical/Moderate severity and Confirmed/Heuristic evidence, but
# never Informational severity -- this capture's own 2 Informational findings, T0831/T0888, were
# never exercised in any of the three SIEM export formats before this item), checked here via the
# first finding (T0855, Critical, CEF/LEEF severity 9, syslog PRI 106) and the first Informational
# one (T0831, CEF/LEEF severity 2, syslog PRI 109) -- proving CEF's numeric severity and syslog's

# ROADMAP item 119: the same --baseline-file run text format already pins above

# SIEM export format before this item, only in text. This one RDP finding happens to combine all

# Batch 5 -- four more `detect` patterns sourced from the live MITRE ATT&CK for ICS matrix itself
# (docs/research/2026-09-detect-pattern-candidates-batch2.md's own Batch 5 section). All 11 findings
# this fixture produces, first-seen order: s7-upload, umas-upload, port-scan, THEN four collateral,
# correctly-fired pre-existing "write outside every range ever read" (T0831) findings -- every one of
# this fixture's four distinct Modbus Write Multiple Registers conduits triggers this pre-existing
# pattern once each, since none of them is ever preceded by a matching read; accepted and documented
# here rather than suppressed, the same "generic pattern plus a specific tool fingerprint" collateral
# acceptance Batch 4 scenario 5's own enip-new-originator-discovery collateral already established --
# THEN modbus-write-burst, modbus-rogue-master, dnp3-write-burst, dnp3-rogue-master. The regex below
# only anchors the eight NEW-pattern findings (skipping over the four T0831 collateral findings via
# its own "." wildcards, the same technique used throughout this file), plus a FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION
# proving none of the three negative-only conduits (.166/.167 three well-known ports under threshold,
# .168/.169 the windowed port-scan reset, .182/.183 two DNP3 writes under the burst threshold)
# produced any finding at all. (.178/.179, the Modbus write-burst UNDER-threshold negative, is
# deliberately NOT in this list -- it correctly still produces its own T0831 collateral finding, just

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# patch257 section 4.5 false-positive validation pass: "commissioning" and "maintenance" fixtures
# (the other two named scenarios, "firmware upgrades" and "redundant-controller behavior", are
# already exercised by detect_snort_patterns_all_findings/detect_umas_all_findings's own Composite
# finding and by detect_snort_patterns_batch5_all_findings/real_dnp3_detect_batch2_findings's own
# Rogue Master/DNP3-broadcast findings -- see build_detect_legitimate_operations_sample's own
# docstring, tools/make_sample_pcap.py, for the full reasoning). None of these five findings got new
# caveat text (their descriptions were already honestly scoped, and none share the Rogue Master/
# Composite/broadcast findings' own "could-easily-be-misread-as-an-attack-signature" shape) -- this
# test instead proves the existing findings still fire honestly on ordinary commissioning/
# maintenance traffic, and that the one plausibly-confusable signal (a burst of BACnet Who-Is during
# device discovery) genuinely needs volume, not just presence, to fire.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# UMAS-over-Modbus/TCP (umas.hpp/cpp, Grok gap #4 Phase 5 -- "Unity Pro/UMAS is in scope as new
# decode work", docs/design/detection-engine.md's own UMAS research section). Dispatched from
# modbus.cpp's own function-code switch on 0x5A/90 (ModbusFrame::umas) -- see umas.hpp's header
# comment for the two primary sources this first-pass, function-code-level-only decoder is built
# from (UMAS has no official public specification). tests/sample_umas.pcap (build_umas_sample,
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py) exercises TAKE_PLC_RESERVATION, START_PLC/STOP_PLC (one success, one
# failure response, to exercise both response_success values), the INITIALIZE_DOWNLOAD/
# DOWNLOAD_BLOCK/END_STRATEGY_DOWNLOAD sequence, READ_ID/READ_PROJECT_INFO/READ_PLC_INFO, and one
# undocumented function code (0x99) to exercise umas_function_name's own "Unknown (0x..)"
# fallback -- 13 packets, all ENG_IP (192.168.1.50) <-> PLC_IP (192.168.1.10) over port 502.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME umas_decode_all_function_codes_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_umas.pcap")
set_tests_properties(umas_decode_all_function_codes_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "UMAS: request \\(session key 0x1\\): TAKE_PLC_RESERVATION, 0 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: response \\(session key 0x1\\): success, 2 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: request \\(session key 0x2\\): START_PLC, 0 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: response \\(session key 0x2\\): success, 0 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: request \\(session key 0x3\\): STOP_PLC, 0 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: response \\(session key 0x3\\): failure, 0 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: request \\(session key 0x4\\): INITIALIZE_DOWNLOAD, 4 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: request \\(session key 0x4\\): DOWNLOAD_BLOCK, 16 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: request \\(session key 0x4\\): END_STRATEGY_DOWNLOAD, 0 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: request \\(session key 0x5\\): READ_ID, 0 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: request \\(session key 0x5\\): READ_PROJECT_INFO, 0 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: request \\(session key 0x5\\): READ_PLC_INFO, 0 data byte\\(s\\).*UMAS: request \\(session key 0x6\\): Unknown \\(0x99\\), 1 data byte\\(s\\)")

# -v/--verbose notes: the request/response heuristic explanation (every UMAS packet gets one --
# see decode_umas's own comment) and the authoritative MBAP transaction-ID pairing note (same
# pairing mechanism as ordinary Modbus, see modbus.cpp's own ModbusDecoder::decode -- UMAS is
# still Modbus/TCP at the wire level).
add_test(NAME umas_decode_verbose_notes_heuristic_and_pairing
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_umas.pcap" -v)
set_tests_properties(umas_decode_verbose_notes_heuristic_and_pairing PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: classified as a request because the byte after the session key is not 0xFE/0xFD.*note: classified as a response because the byte after the session key is 0xFE/0xFD.*note: authoritative pairing: response to transaction id 101 \\(unit 0\\) -- matches the request seen in packet #1")

# JSON field shape -- a request (umas_function_code/umas_function_name present, umas_is_response
# false, no umas_response_success key at all -- this project's own "omit, never null" convention),
# a success response, and a failure response (umas_response_success: false).
add_test(NAME umas_decode_json_request_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_umas.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(umas_decode_json_request_fields PROPERTIES
  # The exact adjacent field sequence pinned below (umas_is_response immediately followed by
  # umas_function_code, with no umas_response_success line between them) is itself the proof that
  # a request's own JSON object never carries umas_response_success -- a whole-capture
  # FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION for that key isn't usable here since OTHER packets in this same JSON
  # array (the response packets) legitimately carry it.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"UMAS: request \\(session key 0x1\\): TAKE_PLC_RESERVATION, 0 data byte\\(s\\)\",\n *\"modbus_is_request\": false,\n *\"umas_session_key\": \"0x1\",\n *\"umas_is_response\": false,\n *\"umas_function_code\": \"0x10\",\n *\"umas_function_name\": \"TAKE_PLC_RESERVATION\",\n *\"umas_data_byte_count\": 0,")

add_test(NAME umas_decode_json_success_response_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_umas.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(umas_decode_json_success_response_fields PROPERTIES

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# -Y/--display-filter (display_filter.hpp/cpp, decode -Y only -- see Jurgen's own request: a
# Wireshark-style display-filter language applied post-decode, e.g.
# `modbus.func_code == 16 && ip.src == 10.1.2.3`, `s7comm.param.func == 0x05`,
# `goose.simulation == 1`). sample_modbus.pcap's own three packets (all function_code==3 "Read
# Holding Registers": #1 request from 192.168.1.50, #2 response, #3 exception response) already
# cover most of the grammar; sample_display_filter_mixed.pcap (build_display_filter_mixed_sample,
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py) is the one genuinely mixed-protocol capture (one Modbus, one DNP3, one
# IEC104 packet) needed to prove a filter actually excludes a non-matching protocol's packets, not
# just narrows within an all-one-protocol capture.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_modbus_func_code_match
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -Y "modbus.func_code == 3")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_modbus_func_code_match PROPERTIES
  # Only #1/#2 -- #3 is packet 3's OWN exception response, whose function_code on the wire carries
  # the 0x80 exception bit (function_code == 0x83, "as seen on the wire" -- see ModbusFrame's own
  # comment, modbus.hpp), so it does not match a plain == 3. No --stats any more (decode lost it --
  # see docs/DEVELOPMENT.md ROADMAP item 105), so this asserts directly against decode's own
  # default per-packet `#N ` index markers instead -- same technique as
  # decode_display_filter_max_packets_counts_post_filter below.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 (.*\n)*#2 "
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3 ")

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_modbus_func_code_no_match
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -Y "modbus.func_code == 99")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_modbus_func_code_no_match PROPERTIES
  # No packet matches -- decode prints nothing at all (no `#N ` marker for any of the 3 packets).
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1 |#2 |#3 ")

# && combines a numeric field match with an ip.src match -- only packet #1 (the request) has
# src_ip 192.168.1.50; #2/#3 are the PLC's own responses, src_ip 192.168.1.10.
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_and_operator
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.func_code == 3 && ip.src == 192.168.1.50")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_and_operator PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 .*request: read 10 holding register\\(s\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2 |#3 ")

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_or_operator
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.exception == true || ip.src == 192.168.1.50")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_or_operator PROPERTIES
  # #1 (ip.src==.50) and #3 (exception==true) match; #2 (the PLC's own non-exception response) is
  # the only one of the three that satisfies neither side of the ||.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 (.*\n)*#3 "
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2 ")

# A bare boolean field name (e.g. `modbus.exception` alone) is a field-EXISTENCE test --
# present-and-non-null, not "value is true" -- see display_filter.hpp's own file header comment.
# modbus.exception is present (true or false) on every decoded Modbus packet, so `!modbus.exception`
# (negated existence) matches nothing here; `modbus.exception == false` is the correct way to test
# the value, matching #1/#2 (non-exception) and excluding #3 (the exception response).
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_not_operator_is_existence_not_value
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "!modbus.exception")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_not_operator_is_existence_not_value PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1 |#2 |#3 ")

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_bool_equality
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.exception == false")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_bool_equality PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 (.*\n)*#2 "
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3 ")

# Parentheses genuinely change which packets match: `!` > comparisons > && > ||, so
# "A || B && C" groups as "A || (B && C)", giving #1 (via B&&C) and #3 (via A) -- but
# "(A || B) && C" groups differently, giving only #1 (every packet satisfies A||B here since B
# -- func_code==3 -- is always true, but only #1 also satisfies C, the ip.src match).
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_parens_change_grouping
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "(modbus.exception == true || modbus.func_code == 3) && ip.src == 192.168.1.50")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_parens_change_grouping PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 "
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2 |#3 ")

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_in_set_match
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.func_code in {3,4,16}")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_in_set_match PROPERTIES
  # Same 0x80-exception-bit caveat as decode_display_filter_modbus_func_code_match above -- #3's
  # own function_code is 0x83, not 3, so only #1/#2 are in {3,4,16}.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 (.*\n)*#2 "
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3 ")

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_in_set_no_match
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.func_code in {4,16}")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_in_set_no_match PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1 |#2 |#3 ")

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_contains
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.func_name contains \"Read\"")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_contains PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 (.*\n)*#2 (.*\n)*#3 ")

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_contains_no_match

    -Y "modbus.func_name contains \"Write\"")

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1 |#2 |#3 ")

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_matches_regex

    -Y "modbus.func_name matches \"^Read\"")

# Malformed-expression tests -- each a CLI error (nonzero exit) before any packet is processed,
# following this project's own "error: <context> '<offending>' <what's wrong> (expected <hint>)"

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_error_unknown_field

add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_error_unterminated_string
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -Y "modbus.func_name contains \"abc")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_error_unterminated_string PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: display filter '.*' '.*abc' has an unterminated string literal")

# patch-282 security review finding F2's own second half ("regex syntax isn't validated during
# compilation... reject invalid regex syntax before opening the capture"): an invalid regex now
# fails compile_display_filter() itself -- the same "fail fast, once, before the loop" pass that
# already catches an unknown field/type mismatch above -- rather than surviving compilation and
# then silently failing (no match, no error) on every single packet for the rest of the run, which
# is what it did before this fix (see the Matches case's own std::regex_error catch that used to
# live in evaluate(), now removed). "[abc" is an unterminated character class, invalid in
# std::regex's own ECMAScript grammar (the default, and this codebase's choice -- see
# display_filter_parser.cpp's own Matches case in type_check()).
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_error_invalid_regex_rejected_at_compile_time
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -Y "modbus.func_name matches \"[abc\"")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_error_invalid_regex_rejected_at_compile_time PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: display filter '.*' 'modbus\\.func_name' matches \"\\[abc\" is not a valid regular expression")

# The identical compile-time rejection applies whether the filter will run against an offline read
# (-r, above) or a live interface (-i) -- proving this by reaching for -i lo specifically (rather
# than asserting on ordering with -r alone) confirms the invalid regex is caught before `capture`'s
# own libpcap interface-open step ever runs at all, not merely before the packet loop starts: if
# compile_display_filter() ran AFTER opening the interface, this exact command line would instead
# either hang waiting for loopback traffic (no --duration/--max-packets given) or, without root/
# CAP_NET_RAW, fail with a permissions error first -- neither of which this regex error could ever
# be confused with. Unconditional (no CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP/UNIX gate, unlike every actual-capture
# test elsewhere in this file) because this never reaches libpcap at all if the fix is correct.
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_error_invalid_regex_rejected_before_live_interface_opens
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --interface lo -Y "modbus.func_name matches \"[abc\"")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_error_invalid_regex_rejected_before_live_interface_opens PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: display filter '.*' 'modbus\\.func_name' matches \"\\[abc\" is not a valid regular expression"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "live capture is not available|requires root|Operation not permitted|no such device")

# patch-282 security review finding F3 ("Display-filter parser has no explicit complexity
# limits"): fixed, non-CLI-configurable ceilings on a -Y expression's own size/shape -- each
# checked once at compile time, the same "fail before packet processing, before a live -i
# interface ever opens" posture every other display-filter validation above already has. See
# display_filter_parser.cpp's own kMaxExpressionLength/kMaxAstNodes/kMaxNestingDepth/
# kMaxSetMembers/kMaxRegexLength comment for the exact values and the trust-boundary reasoning
# (a -Y expression is operator-authored CLI input, the same boundary -f/BPF and --policy YAML
# already sit inside -- not attacker-controlled network traffic). The pathological expressions
# below are built at CMake configure time (string(REPEAT)/string(JOIN)/list(APPEND)) rather than
# hand-typed, since several are multiple kilobytes long. Each limit gets two tests: one proving
# the limit fires with the expected error, one proving an expression safely under that same limit
# still compiles AND evaluates correctly (no false-positive rejection of legitimate, if verbose,
# -Y expressions).

# 1. kMaxExpressionLength (65536 bytes). Content is irrelevant, only size -- a 65537-byte
# nonsense expression is rejected before the parser sees a single token of it. (No "still works
# under the limit" twin for this one -- every other test below already is an under-the-limit
# expression that compiles, and a 65536-byte *meaningful* expression would be unreadable here.)
#
# Written to a file and passed as -Y "@<path>" rather than embedded directly in COMMAND: a 65537-
# byte single argv entry is fine on Linux/macOS, but blows straight through Windows' own
# CreateProcess ~32767-character TOTAL command-line length limit (every argument combined, not
# per-argument) -- CTest cannot even launch the process at all in that case (observed in CI as
# this test going "Not Run" with a "name too long"-style launch failure, not as a normal test
# failure). -Y's own '@<path>' file-reading support (cli_main.cpp) exists specifically so this
# exact scenario -- and any real multi-kilobyte -Y expression an operator might have -- never has
# to touch the OS command-line length limit at all.
string(REPEAT "x" 65537 f3_too_long_expr)
set(f3_too_long_expr_file "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/f3_too_long_display_filter_expr.txt")
file(WRITE "${f3_too_long_expr_file}" "${f3_too_long_expr}")
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_error_expression_too_long
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -Y "@${f3_too_long_expr_file}")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_error_expression_too_long PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: display filter is 65537 bytes long, more than the 65536-byte limit -- simplify the expression \\(it starts with: 'xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx\\.\\.\\.'\\)")

# The '@<path>' file-reading mechanism itself, independent of the length-limit scenario above:
# a trailing newline (as a real file saved by an editor, or `file(WRITE ...)` with an explicit
# "\n", would have) must be trimmed, not counted as part of the expression -- proven by checking
# the compiled filter actually matches (a bare 'modbus' existence test on a known-Modbus capture),
# which would fail if the trailing '\n' were still part of the expression text being parsed as a
# field/keyword token.
set(f3_at_file_with_trailing_newline "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/f3_at_file_trailing_newline.txt")
file(WRITE "${f3_at_file_with_trailing_newline}" "modbus\n")
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_at_file_trims_trailing_newline
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -Y "@${f3_at_file_with_trailing_newline}")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_at_file_trims_trailing_newline PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Read Holding Registers"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^error:")

# A missing '@<path>' file is a clean CLI error, not an unhandled exception/crash.
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_at_file_missing_is_clean_error
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -Y "@${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/does_not_exist_f3_display_filter.txt")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_at_file_missing_is_clean_error PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: cannot open display filter file '.*does_not_exist_f3_display_filter\\.txt' for reading")

# 2. kMaxAstNodes (4096): N bare `modbus` existence tests joined by `or` parse into 2N-1
# FilterNode instances (N Exists nodes + N-1 Or nodes -- parse_or_expr()'s repeated-operator loop
# is iterative, not recursive, so this grows node_count_ without growing depth_). N=2100 gives
# 4199 nodes, over the ceiling, while the expression text itself (~21 KB) stays well under
# kMaxExpressionLength, so this test isolates the AST-node ceiling specifically.
string(REPEAT "modbus or " 2099 f3_many_nodes_expr)
string(APPEND f3_many_nodes_expr "modbus")
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_error_too_many_ast_nodes

# patch295 security review finding F4 ("std::regex remains a potential CPU-amplification
# mechanism", item 136, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md): a `matches` pattern containing a quantified group
# whose own content is itself quantified (e.g. (a+)+) is a classic catastrophic-backtracking
# shape -- std::regex_search against it can take seconds or more on an adversarial input, and
# this filter runs on every packet. Unlike every other display-filter validation above, this one
# is a WARNING, not a rejection (looks_like_nested_quantifier_redos's own comment in
# display_filter_parser.cpp explains why: it's a syntactic heuristic, not a proof the pattern is
# actually unsafe, and the review itself says this is a Low/Medium finding not worth a correctness
# trade-off over). The filter still compiles and still runs; a "note:" is printed the same way
# resolver_notes already are, respecting --quiet the same way.
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_f4_redos_heuristic_warns
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.func_name matches \"(a+)+$\"")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_f4_redos_heuristic_warns PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: 'modbus\\.func_name' matches \"\\(a\\+\\)\\+\\$\" contains a quantified group whose own content is itself quantified"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^error:")

# An ordinary, non-pathological pattern -- including one with an unrelated quantifier -- never
# trips the heuristic: no false-positive warning noise on everyday -Y expressions.
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_f4_redos_heuristic_silent_for_benign_pattern
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.func_name matches \"^Read.*\"")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_f4_redos_heuristic_silent_for_benign_pattern PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Read Holding Registers"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note:|^error:")

# --quiet suppresses the note exactly like every other resolver/compile-time note in this
# codebase -- the global flag has to precede the subcommand (see rewrite_subcommand_alias's own
# leading-global-flags scan in cli_main.cpp), matching
# resolver_resolve_with_no_hosts_file_noop_note_respects_quiet's own command shape above.
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_f4_redos_heuristic_respects_quiet
  COMMAND conduitscope --quiet decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.func_name matches \"(a+)+$\"")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_f4_redos_heuristic_respects_quiet PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note:|^error:")

# UMAS is nested under Modbus (ModbusFrame::umas), not its own top-level protocol -- see

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 (.*\n)*#15 ")

# --max-packets counts only filter-MATCHING packets -- matches Wireshark's own display-filter
# semantics, where a non-matching packet is invisible to every downstream consumer including a
# count-based stop condition. modbus.exception == false matches #1/#2 only (#3 is the exception);
# --max-packets 1 must yield #1 alone, not "the first packet scanned regardless of match".
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_max_packets_counts_post_filter
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap"
    -Y "modbus.exception == false" --max-packets 1)
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_max_packets_counts_post_filter PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^#1 "
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2 |#3 ")

# -w/--write stays PRE-filter -- raw capture passthrough, governed by -f/--filter only, unaffected
# by -Y/--display-filter (see cli_main.cpp's own comment at the loop's insertion point). Writing
# with a narrowing -Y, then reading the written pcap back with no filter at all, must reproduce
# every packet from the original capture, not just the -Y-matching subset.
add_test(NAME decode_display_filter_write_unaffected_by_filter
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/display_filter_write_test.pcap' && \
    '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' \
      -Y 'modbus.exception == false' --write '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/display_filter_write_test.pcap' --format json >/dev/null && \
    '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/display_filter_write_test.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(decode_display_filter_write_unaffected_by_filter PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packets: *3")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conversations/Endpoints tables (tshark's own `-z conv,ip`/`-z endpoints,ip`/`-z conv,eth`/
# `-z endpoints,eth` as design precedent) -- see StatsWriter's own file-header comment
# (output.hpp) and print_conversations'/print_endpoints' comments (output.cpp) for the
# A/B-assignment, byte-counting, sort-order, and truncation conventions this section exercises.
# `-z` is `info`-only now, and explicit opt-in (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md ROADMAP item 105) -- none of
# the four tables are tracked OR printed unless its own `-z` value is given -- so every case below
# passes the specific `-z` value(s) it needs, and a new test just below confirms a table is
# genuinely absent (not just unprinted) when its `-z` value isn't given at all.

# sample_modbus.pcap (3 packets: 1 request 192.168.1.50->192.168.1.10, 2 responses the other way --
# see the pre-existing bacnet_stats_counted-style tests above for this fixture's own shape) gives
# an exact, hand-verifiable A->B/B->A split for both the IPv4 and (same two hosts) Ethernet tables.
add_test(NAME info_ipv4_conversations_both_directions_counted
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -z conv,ip)
set_tests_properties(info_ipv4_conversations_both_directions_counted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ipv4 conversations \\(1, ranked by total bytes\\):\n *192\\.168\\.1\\.50 <-> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10 +3 frame\\(s\\), 212 byte\\(s\\) total +\\(A->B: 1 frame\\(s\\)/66 byte\\(s\\), B->A: 2 frame\\(s\\)/146 byte\\(s\\), duration [0-9.]+s\\)")

add_test(NAME info_ipv4_endpoints_tx_rx_split
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -z endpoints,ip)
set_tests_properties(info_ipv4_endpoints_tx_rx_split PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ipv4 endpoints \\(2, ranked by total bytes\\):\n *192\\.168\\.1\\.50 +3 frame\\(s\\), 212 byte\\(s\\) total +\\(tx: 1 frame\\(s\\)/66 byte\\(s\\), rx: 2 frame\\(s\\)/146 byte\\(s\\)\\)\n *192\\.168\\.1\\.10 +3 frame\\(s\\), 212 byte\\(s\\) total +\\(tx: 2 frame\\(s\\)/146 byte\\(s\\), rx: 1 frame\\(s\\)/66 byte\\(s\\)\\)")

add_test(NAME info_ethernet_conversations_and_endpoints_counted
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -z conv,eth -z endpoints,eth)
set_tests_properties(info_ethernet_conversations_and_endpoints_counted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ethernet conversations \\(1, ranked by total bytes\\):\n *00:0c:29:11:22:33 <-> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc +3 frame\\(s\\), 212 byte\\(s\\) total.*\nethernet endpoints \\(2, ranked by total bytes\\):")

# The actual new capability -- an EtherType this decoder doesn't name (raw-Ethernet POWERLINK on a
# VLAN, ROADMAP item 103's own fixture) has no IP layer at all, so it's invisible to an IPv4-only
# table by construction. Confirms the Ethernet/MAC table sees it (proving the L2 blind spot an
# IP-only conversations table would have is actually closed) AND that no "ipv4 conversations"
# section is printed even when BOTH conv,ip and conv,eth are requested together (every section is
# a no-op when its own map is empty, matching every other conditional block in print_summary).
add_test(NAME info_ethernet_only_traffic_visible_with_no_ip_layer
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_policy_l2_ethertype_powerlink.pcap" -z conv,ip -z conv,eth)
set_tests_properties(info_ethernet_only_traffic_visible_with_no_ip_layer PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ethernet conversations \\(1, ranked by total bytes\\):\n *00:0c:29:11:22:33 <-> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc +4 frame\\(s\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ipv4 conversations")

# The default-off behavior itself: none of the four tables are tracked, let alone printed, when
# `-z` isn't given at all -- not just "info doesn't show them", but genuinely never accumulated
# (see StatsWriter::write_packet's own per-table tables_ gate, output.cpp) -- this fixture has
# traffic that WOULD populate all four tables if any -z value were given (see the tests just
# above), so their total absence here is a real behavioral check, not a vacuous one.
add_test(NAME info_no_conversations_or_endpoints_tables_without_z
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(info_no_conversations_or_endpoints_tables_without_z PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ipv4 conversations|ipv4 endpoints|ethernet conversations|ethernet endpoints")

# -z value validation: an unrecognized stat name is rejected up front by CLI11's own IsMember
# check, the same "reject before any packet is read" posture every other validated-enum option in
# this tool already has (-T/--format, --decode-as's own protocol names, etc).
add_test(NAME info_z_rejects_unrecognized_value
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -z bogus)
set_tests_properties(info_z_rejects_unrecognized_value PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "'bogus' not in \\{conv,ip, endpoints,ip, conv,eth, endpoints,eth, conv,tcp, follow,tcp,stream,<N>, follow,udp,stream,<N>\\}")

# ROADMAP item 108 ("Follow stream as a first-class object") -- a follow,tcp/follow,udp value with
# a non-numeric (or missing) stream index is rejected with its own, more specific message rather

# (cli_main.cpp).

set_tests_properties(info_z_follow_rejects_missing_stream_index PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "'follow,udp,stream,' must end with a non-negative integer stream index")

# An unsupported transport name after "follow," (tshark itself supports follow,http/follow,tls/
# follow,http2/follow,quic too -- this tool deliberately doesn't, see FollowStreamWriter's own file

# --max-conversations/--max-endpoints: sample_bacnet.pcap has 2 distinct IPv4 conversations and 4
