# Not reaching the cap: no warning line at all, on the same fixture with a generous limit --
# guards against the warning firing unconditionally regardless of whether the cap was actually hit.
add_test(NAME info_conversations_no_warning_when_cap_not_reached
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bacnet.pcap" -z conv,ip --max-conversations 200)
set_tests_properties(info_conversations_no_warning_when_cap_not_reached PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "limit of [0-9]+ reached")

# --max-conversations/--max-endpoints are `info`-only now (decode lost --stats and everything that
# went with it, ROADMAP item 105) -- documented in `info --help`, same "flags are discoverable
# from --help" regression guard as resource_limit_flags_present_in_decode_help above -- and
# confirmed genuinely GONE from `decode --help` (there is no longer a decode-side counterpart of
# this test).
add_test(NAME conversation_stats_flags_present_in_info_help
  COMMAND conduitscope info --help)
set_tests_properties(conversation_stats_flags_present_in_info_help PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "--max-conversations(.*\n)*.*--max-endpoints")

add_test(NAME conversation_stats_flags_absent_from_decode_help
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --help)
set_tests_properties(conversation_stats_flags_absent_from_decode_help PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "--max-conversations|--max-endpoints|-z,--stat|--stats|--max-follow-bytes")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ROADMAP item 108 ("Follow stream as a first-class object") -- `info`'s own `-z conv,tcp` and
# `-z follow,tcp,stream,<N>`/`-z follow,udp,stream,<N>`, tshark's own `-z conv,tcp`/Follow Stream
# as design precedent. tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_follow_stream_sample) lays out five independent sessions, each scenario's own comment
# there explaining exactly what it proves and which tcp.stream/udp.stream index it lands on.

# Scenario A (tcp.stream 0) -- an ordinary in-order exchange. Also the base case for --max-follow-
# bytes truncation, below.
add_test(NAME info_follow_tcp_simple_in_order
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z follow,tcp,stream,0)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_tcp_simple_in_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "follow tcp stream 0: 192.168.1.50:56000 <-> 192.168.1.10:502\n  192.168.1.50:56000 -> 192.168.1.10:502 \\(1 segment\\(s\\), 11 byte\\(s\\)\\):\n.*GET STATUS.*\n  192.168.1.10:502 -> 192.168.1.50:56000 \\(1 segment\\(s\\), 19 byte\\(s\\)\\):\n.*STATUS=OK TEMP")
# (the 19-byte B->A payload wraps onto a second 16-bytes-per-line hex dump row -- asserting on
# "STATUS=OK TEMP" alone, which fits entirely within the first row, avoids depending on exactly
# where write_hex_ascii_dump's own fixed 16-byte wrap boundary falls)

# Scenario B (tcp.stream 1) -- "HIJ" is captured BEFORE "CDEFG", the segment that actually closes
# the gap between the direction's first segment ("AB") and it -- must still reconstruct in
# SEQUENCE order, not capture order, with the gap fully closed.
add_test(NAME info_follow_tcp_out_of_order_reassembles_in_sequence_order
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z follow,tcp,stream,1)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_tcp_out_of_order_reassembles_in_sequence_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.1.50:56001 -> 192.168.1.10:502 \\(3 segment\\(s\\), 10 byte\\(s\\)\\):\n.*ABCDEFGHIJ")
set_tests_properties(info_follow_tcp_out_of_order_reassembles_in_sequence_order PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "never became contiguous")

# Scenario C (tcp.stream 2) -- an exact-duplicate retransmission of "HELLO" must be ignored (not
# appended twice, not flagged as a conflict), leaving a clean "HELLOWORLD".
add_test(NAME info_follow_tcp_identical_retransmission_deduplicated
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z follow,tcp,stream,2)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_tcp_identical_retransmission_deduplicated PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.1.50:56002 -> 192.168.1.10:502 \\(3 segment\\(s\\), 10 byte\\(s\\)\\):\n.*HELLOWORLD")
set_tests_properties(info_follow_tcp_identical_retransmission_deduplicated PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "disagreed with what was already captured")

# Scenario D (tcp.stream 3) -- security-relevant: a retransmission at the same seq whose content
# actively DISAGREES ("XXXXX" vs the real "AAAAA") must resolve first-received-wins (the real
# bytes survive), with the conflict flagged once, matching decoder.cpp's own reassemble_tcp_payload
# overlap policy (ROADMAP item 107).
add_test(NAME info_follow_tcp_conflicting_overlap_first_received_wins
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z follow,tcp,stream,3)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_tcp_conflicting_overlap_first_received_wins PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.1.50:56003 -> 192.168.1.10:502 \\(3 segment\\(s\\), 10 byte\\(s\\)\\):\n.*AAAAABBBBB(.*\n)*.*disagreed with what was already captured -- first-received bytes were kept")
set_tests_properties(info_follow_tcp_conflicting_overlap_first_received_wins PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "XXXXX")

# Scenario E (udp.stream 0) -- UDP has no sequence number: two same-direction datagrams
# ("UDPQUERY1" then "UDPQUERY2") must simply concatenate in CAPTURE order.
add_test(NAME info_follow_udp_concatenates_in_capture_order
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z follow,udp,stream,0)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_udp_concatenates_in_capture_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "follow udp stream 0: 192.168.1.50:56010 <-> 192.168.1.10:47900\n  192.168.1.50:56010 -> 192.168.1.10:47900 \\(2 datagram\\(s\\), 18 byte\\(s\\)\\):\n.*UDPQUERY1UDPQUER(.*\n)*.*192.168.1.10:47900 -> 192.168.1.50:56010 \\(1 datagram\\(s\\), 9 byte\\(s\\)\\):\n.*UDPREPLY1")
# (18 bytes wraps the same way -- "UDPQUERY1UDPQUER" is the full first 16-byte row, proving both
# datagrams concatenated back-to-back with nothing dropped, without depending on the wrap point)

# Repeatable `-z`, several follow requests in one run, printed back in the order asked (not a
# fixed table order) -- also proves TCP and UDP index spaces are independent (tcp.stream 0 and
# udp.stream 0 are unrelated sessions).
add_test(NAME info_follow_multiple_requests_printed_in_flag_order
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z follow,udp,stream,0 -z follow,tcp,stream,0)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_multiple_requests_printed_in_flag_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "follow udp stream 0:(.*\n)*follow tcp stream 0:")

# A repeated, IDENTICAL follow request is de-duplicated -- printed once, not twice.
add_test(NAME info_follow_duplicate_request_deduplicated
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z follow,tcp,stream,0 -z follow,tcp,stream,0)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_duplicate_request_deduplicated PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "follow tcp stream 0:")
# Counts occurrences via a trick: FAIL if the header line appears a second time anywhere.
set_tests_properties(info_follow_duplicate_request_deduplicated PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "follow tcp stream 0:(.*\n)*follow tcp stream 0:")

# A stream index past what the capture actually has -- an explicit, actionable diagnostic rather
# than silence (this fixture's highest tcp.stream index is 3).
add_test(NAME info_follow_tcp_stream_not_found
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z follow,tcp,stream,99)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_tcp_stream_not_found PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "follow tcp stream 99: no such stream in this capture \\(highest tcp.stream index seen: 3\\)")

add_test(NAME info_follow_udp_stream_not_found_when_no_udp_at_all
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -z follow,udp,stream,0)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_udp_stream_not_found_when_no_udp_at_all PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "follow udp stream 0: no such stream in this capture \\(no UDP streams observed\\)")

# --max-follow-bytes: scenario A's own B->A direction is 19 bytes -- capping at 5 forces
# truncation of THAT direction only (the smaller A->B direction, 11 bytes, is untouched since its
# own cap isn't reached -- each direction's budget is independent, see TcpDirection's own comment,
# output.hpp).
add_test(NAME info_follow_max_follow_bytes_truncates_and_warns
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z follow,tcp,stream,0 --max-follow-bytes 5)
set_tests_properties(info_follow_max_follow_bytes_truncates_and_warns PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.1.10:502 -> 192.168.1.50:56000 \\(1 segment\\(s\\), 5 byte\\(s\\)\\):\n.*STATU(.*\n)*.*--max-follow-bytes limit of 5 reached for this direction; stream truncated")
set_tests_properties(info_follow_max_follow_bytes_truncates_and_warns PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "GET STATUS(.*\n)*.*--max-follow-bytes limit")  # A->B (11 bytes) must NOT be truncated

# `-z conv,tcp`: four TCP sessions in this fixture, each with its own address:port pair and
# tcp.stream index -- the same index a `-z follow,tcp,stream,<N>` above asks for.
add_test(NAME info_conv_tcp_lists_sessions_with_stream_index
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z conv,tcp)
set_tests_properties(info_conv_tcp_lists_sessions_with_stream_index PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "tcp conversations \\(4, ranked by total bytes\\):(.*\n)*.*192.168.1.50:56000 <-> 192.168.1.10:502  \\(tcp.stream 0\\)")

# conv,tcp is independent of conv,ip -- requesting one does not accumulate (or print) the other,
# same "nothing requested, nothing tracked" posture conv,ip/conv,eth/endpoints,ip/endpoints,eth
# already established.
add_test(NAME info_conv_tcp_does_not_imply_conv_ip
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z conv,tcp)
set_tests_properties(info_conv_tcp_does_not_imply_conv_ip PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ipv4 conversations")

add_test(NAME info_max_conversations_caps_tcp_conversations_table_too
  COMMAND conduitscope info --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap" -z conv,tcp --max-conversations 1)
set_tests_properties(info_max_conversations_caps_tcp_conversations_table_too PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "tcp conversations \\(1, ranked by total bytes\\):\n(.*\n){1} *\\(--max-conversations limit of 1 reached; some conversations are not shown -- rerun with a higher --max-conversations to see them all\\)")

# --max-follow-bytes is discoverable from `info --help`, same "flags are discoverable from --help"
# regression guard --max-conversations/--max-endpoints already have above; -z's own help text also
# names conv,tcp/follow,tcp,stream,<N>/follow,udp,stream,<N> so they're never only discoverable by
# reading source.
add_test(NAME follow_stream_flags_present_in_info_help
  COMMAND conduitscope info --help)
set_tests_properties(follow_stream_flags_present_in_info_help PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "'conv,tcp'.*'follow,tcp,stream,<N>'(.*\n)*.*--max-follow-bytes")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subcommand-alias flags (--decode/--info/--interfaces/--policy/--inventory/--detect/--baseline/
# --capture/--merge, each selectable as a double-dashed flag of the subcommand's own name,
# ROADMAP item 105) -- rewrite_subcommand_alias's own comment (cli_main.cpp) has the full
# position-aware, single-substitution design. `diff <(...) <(...)` is this file's own established
# idiom for "these two invocations must produce byte-identical output" (see e.g.
# dash_w_roundtrip's own test above) -- no PASS/FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION needed, ctest already
# fails a test whose COMMAND exits nonzero, and diff exits nonzero on any difference.

add_test(NAME decode_alias_flag_matches_classic_subcommand
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap') <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

add_test(NAME info_alias_flag_matches_classic_subcommand
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap') <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

add_test(NAME interfaces_alias_flag_matches_classic_subcommand
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --interfaces) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' interfaces)")

add_test(NAME detect_alias_flag_matches_classic_subcommand
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --detect --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap') <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' detect --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

# A global flag (-q here) legally precedes the subcommand-position token -- rewrite_subcommand_
# alias must skip over it, not mistake -q for the subcommand candidate, and still resolve --info
# right after it.
add_test(NAME info_alias_flag_after_global_quiet_flag
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' -q --info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap') <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' -q info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

# --version already behaves like the `version` subcommand via CLI11's own set_version_flag -- not
# part of rewrite_subcommand_alias's own rewrite table (see that function's own comment) -- so this
# confirms the two remain byte-identical (including the "conduitscope " prefix both now share).
add_test(NAME version_flag_matches_version_subcommand
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --version) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' version)")

# The critical collision-safety case: --policy is ALSO a real option name inside `policy
# validate`/`detect`/`baseline check` (--policy FILE) -- rewrite_subcommand_alias must resolve only
# the FIRST (subcommand-position) --policy token and stop, leaving this second, option-position
# --policy completely untouched. Confirms `conduitscope --policy validate --policy FILE ...`
# behaves identically to `conduitscope policy validate --policy FILE ...`, not corrupted into
# `policy validate policy FILE ...`.
add_test(NAME policy_alias_flag_collision_safe_with_policy_option
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --policy validate --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap') <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' policy validate --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

# Same collision-safety proof for `detect --policy FILE` and `baseline check --policy FILE`, the
# other two subcommands with their own unrelated --policy option.
add_test(NAME detect_alias_flag_collision_safe_with_policy_option
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --detect --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap') <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' detect --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_alias_flag_collision_safe_with_policy_option
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_alias_check.json' && \
    '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_alias_check.json' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' >/dev/null && \
    diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --baseline check --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml' --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_alias_check.json' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap') <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline check --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml' --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/baseline_alias_check.json' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

# Order independence (Jurgen's own direct follow-up: these flags were meant to be usable like any
# other flag, not only as a same-position substitute for the bare subcommand word): an alias flag
# appearing AFTER other subcommand-specific tokens -- not just leading the line -- still resolves
# and produces identical output to the classic form. Eight of the nine aliases (every one except
# --policy, which stays candidate-position-only -- see the collision-safety tests above and
# rewrite_subcommand_alias's own comment) support this.
add_test(NAME decode_alias_flag_order_independent_after_options
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' --decode) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

add_test(NAME info_alias_flag_order_independent_after_options
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' --info) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

# Combines a leading global flag (-q, which must still lead) with an alias resolved from several
# tokens further down the line -- proves the two mechanisms compose rather than only one at a time.
add_test(NAME detect_alias_flag_order_independent_after_global_and_options
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' -q --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' --detect) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' -q detect --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

# --policy specifically does NOT gain order independence (see the comment above) -- confirms it
# still falls back to CLI11's own honest \"subcommand required\" error rather than silently
# misparsing when it appears anywhere but the candidate position, exactly as before this round.
add_test(NAME policy_alias_flag_still_requires_leading_position
  COMMAND conduitscope --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --policy validate)
set_tests_properties(policy_alias_flag_still_requires_leading_position PROPERTIES
  WILL_FAIL TRUE)

add_test(NAME baseline_learn_dash_r_matches_positional_form

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No-subcommand default (ROADMAP item 109) -- Jurgen's own direct request: `-z` usable without
# ever typing `info`, and no subcommand at all now defaults to `decode` UNLESS `-z`/`--stat`
# appears anywhere on the line, in which case it defaults to `info` instead. See
# inject_default_subcommand's own comment (cli_main.cpp) for the full design; this section proves
# it end to end, at the real-binary argv level, the same `diff <(...) <(...)` "byte-identical
# output" idiom the item 105 alias-flag section above already established for an identical kind of
# pre-parse argv rewrite.

# No subcommand + no -z: identical output to the classic `decode` form.
add_test(NAME no_subcommand_defaults_to_decode
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap') <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap')")

# No subcommand + -z: identical output to explicit `info -z ...` (which item 109 also changed --
# see the stat_output_only tests below -- so this is comparing two invocations of the NEW
# behavior, not the old one).
add_test(NAME no_subcommand_with_stat_flag_defaults_to_info
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap' -z conv,tcp) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap' -z conv,tcp)")

# --stat (long form of -z) triggers the same default as -z itself.
add_test(NAME no_subcommand_with_long_form_stat_flag_defaults_to_info
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap' --stat conv,tcp) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap' -z conv,tcp)")

# A leading global flag (-q) before -z is still correctly detected -- the default-subcommand scan
# must skip past it the same way rewrite_subcommand_alias's own candidate_start scan does (kept in
# sync with it, see inject_default_subcommand's own comment) rather than mistaking -q's own
# position for where -z would have to be.
add_test(NAME no_subcommand_global_flag_before_stat_flag_still_defaults_to_info
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' -q --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap' -z conv,tcp) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' -q info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap' -z conv,tcp)")

# follow,tcp,stream,<N> works the same way with no subcommand typed, not just conv,tcp.
add_test(NAME no_subcommand_follow_stream_matches_explicit_info
  COMMAND bash -c "diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap' -z follow,tcp,stream,0) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_follow_stream.pcap' -z follow,tcp,stream,0)")

# A bare invocation with no arguments at all now prints the top-level --help and exits cleanly
# (Jurgen's own direct request -- this used to default-inject `decode`, same as item 109's other
# cases, and then immediately fail with decode's own "needs exactly one of -r/--read or
# -i/--interface" error: a confusing first impression for anyone who ran the bare executable with
# nothing else typed, e.g. by double-clicking conduitscope.exe from Explorer on Windows, expecting
# to see what the tool does). main()'s own `argc == 1` short-circuit (cli_main.cpp) deliberately
# sits before item 109's default-subcommand injection and only ever fires on this exact case.
add_test(NAME bare_invocation_prints_top_level_help
  COMMAND conduitscope)
set_tests_properties(bare_invocation_prints_top_level_help PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Usage: conduitscope \\[OPTIONS\\] SUBCOMMAND"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "needs exactly one of -r/--read")

# Confirms the bare-invocation case above exits 0 (a genuine --help display, not an error that
# happens to also print usage text) -- distinct from the regex check above, which only inspects
# stdout content and would equally pass whether the process exited 0 or non-zero.
add_test(NAME bare_invocation_exits_zero
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' >/dev/null; exit $?")

# A bare invocation plus one explicit global flag (no subcommand, but something WAS typed) is
# unaffected by the argc==1 short-circuit above -- item 109's own default-subcommand injection
# still applies and decode's own specific missing-source error is still the right diagnosis,
# since the operator did type something on the line.
add_test(NAME bare_invocation_with_explicit_flag_still_reports_decode_missing_source_error

set_tests_properties(bare_invocation_with_explicit_flag_still_reports_decode_missing_source_error PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "'decode' needs exactly one of -r/--read.*or -i/--interface")

# --decode/--info alias flags (already resolved to a bare subcommand word by

# `-z`-only output (ROADMAP item 109) -- Jurgen's own direct request: "If the -z option is used,
# no output is expected except of the -z option output." Exercised through the classic `info -z
# ...` form (the no-subcommand form above already proved byte-identical to this), so these are the
# real regression guards for StatsWriter::stat_output_only_ itself (output.hpp/.cpp).

# None of `info`'s own always-on metadata/histogram lines appear once any -z value was given --
# this fixture has both IP and protocol-histogram content that WOULD show up here (see the
# existing info_ipv4_conversations_both_directions_counted-style tests elsewhere in this file,

# The pre-item-109 behavior is unchanged when `-z` is never given at all -- `info` alone still

# A -z value that happens to match nothing in this particular capture (no UDP traffic in
# sample_modbus.pcap, so follow,udp,stream,0 finds no such stream) still suppresses the classic
# metadata/histogram output -- stat_output_only is keyed on whether -z was GIVEN, never on whether

# ============================================================================================
# Friendlier --help (Jurgen's direct request: "make the output of --help way more friendlier to
# read"). Two separate, pre-existing readability problems were found and fixed in cli_main.cpp,
# neither one touching a single option's own description TEXT (no information removed or
# reworded, only how it's laid out -- see WrappingHelpFormatter's own comment, above
# stdout_is_terminal() in cli_main.cpp, for the full writeup):
#
#   1. CLI11's own stock Formatter::make_option/make_subcommand/make_description (detail::
#      format_help, CLI11.hpp) never word-wrap a description to any width at all -- a long one
#      (and this file deliberately writes long, complete ones, matching docs/USER_GUIDE.md's own
#      depth) printed as one single unbroken line that just ran off the terminal. A new
#      WrappingHelpFormatter (cli_main.cpp) overrides all three to wrap to terminal_width() (real
#      terminal size via ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)/GetConsoleScreenBufferInfo, a COLUMNS env var override
#      when not a terminal, clamped to [60, 200]) while reusing every other CLI11 building block
#      unchanged.
#   2. Every option in every subcommand previously shared CLI11's single default "Options" group
#      -- `decode --help` alone dumped ~190 options in one flat list, with no separation between
#      "used every time" (-r/-i/-f/-o/-T) and "advanced, rarely touched" (the ~45 `--*-port`
#      protocol-port overrides, the dozen `--max-*` resource-limit flags). Every add_option()/
#      add_flag() call across every subcommand in cli_main.cpp now carries an explicit
#      ->group("...") sorting it into one of a small, consistent, reused-by-name set of sections
#      ("Input/output", "Filtering", "Output format", "Protocol port overrides (rarely needed)",
#      "Resource limits (advanced)", "Name resolution", and a few subcommand-specific ones) --
#      CLI11 buckets and labels each group as its own section automatically (Formatter::
#      make_groups) once options declare different group names.
#
# Both are proven below: group-header presence/order per subcommand (one test each, the eight
# subcommands with enough options to be grouped at all), the line-count explosion a genuinely
# wrapped --help produces versus a flat one, the exact wrap-width clamp floor/ceiling, and the
# `--protocol` choice-list's own comma-boundary wrapping (the one name/opts-column case long
# enough, with no whitespace anywhere in it, that plain word-wrapping alone can't help it).
#
# `bash -c "COLUMNS=<n> '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' ..."` is required (not plain `COMMAND
# conduitscope ...`) everywhere a specific width matters: CTest itself runs this binary with
# stdout piped (never a real terminal), so terminal_width() would otherwise fall through straight
# to its own COLUMNS-env-var/fallback path regardless -- setting COLUMNS explicitly in the same
# subshell is what actually controls which width is exercised.

add_test(NAME decode_help_group_headers_present_in_order
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --help)
set_tests_properties(decode_help_group_headers_present_in_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Input/output:.*Filtering:.*Live capture \\(-i only\\):.*Output format:.*Protocol selection:.*Protocol port overrides \\(rarely needed\\):.*Resource limits \\(advanced\\):.*Display options:.*Name resolution:"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Zone & conduit output:|Capture rotation:|Policy & baseline inputs")

add_test(NAME policy_validate_help_group_headers_present_in_order
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --help)
set_tests_properties(policy_validate_help_group_headers_present_in_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Input/output:.*Filtering:.*Live capture \\(-i only\\):.*Output format:.*Display options:.*Resource limits \\(advanced\\):.*Name resolution:"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Protocol port overrides|Zone & conduit output:|Capture rotation:")

add_test(NAME inventory_help_group_headers_present_in_order
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --help)
set_tests_properties(inventory_help_group_headers_present_in_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Input/output:.*Filtering:.*Live capture \\(-i only\\):.*Output format:.*Display options:.*Resource limits \\(advanced\\):.*Zone & conduit output:.*Name resolution:"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Protocol port overrides|Capture rotation:|Policy & baseline inputs")

add_test(NAME detect_help_group_headers_present_in_order
  COMMAND conduitscope detect --help)
set_tests_properties(detect_help_group_headers_present_in_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Input/output:.*Filtering:.*Live capture \\(-i only\\):.*Output format:.*Display options:.*Resource limits \\(advanced\\):.*Policy & baseline inputs \\(optional\\):.*Name resolution:"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Protocol port overrides|Zone & conduit output:|Capture rotation:")

add_test(NAME baseline_learn_help_group_headers_present_in_order
  COMMAND conduitscope baseline learn --help)
set_tests_properties(baseline_learn_help_group_headers_present_in_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Input/output:.*Resource limits \\(advanced\\):.*Display options:"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Protocol port overrides|Zone & conduit output:|Capture rotation:|Policy & baseline inputs")

add_test(NAME baseline_check_help_group_headers_present_in_order
  COMMAND conduitscope baseline check --help)
set_tests_properties(baseline_check_help_group_headers_present_in_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Input/output:.*Resource limits \\(advanced\\):.*Output format:.*Display options:.*Policy & baseline inputs \\(optional\\):"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Protocol port overrides|Zone & conduit output:|Capture rotation:")

add_test(NAME capture_help_group_headers_present_in_order
  COMMAND conduitscope capture --help)
set_tests_properties(capture_help_group_headers_present_in_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Input/output:.*Filtering:.*Live capture \\(-i only\\):.*Capture rotation:"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Protocol port overrides|Zone & conduit output:|Policy & baseline inputs|Name resolution:")

add_test(NAME merge_inventory_help_group_headers_present_in_order
  COMMAND conduitscope merge inventory --help)
set_tests_properties(merge_inventory_help_group_headers_present_in_order PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Input/output:.*Output format:.*Zone & conduit output:.*Name resolution:"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Protocol port overrides|Capture rotation:|Policy & baseline inputs")

# decode --help has ~190 options; printed as CLI11's own stock flat, one-group, no-wrap list
# this would be on the order of 115-130 lines (confirmed against this project's own pre-fix
# output). Wrapped to a deliberately narrow 80-column terminal, the same content runs past 500
# lines -- proving real word-wrapping is actually happening at scale, not just on one or two
# hand-picked options.
add_test(NAME decode_help_wraps_into_far_more_lines_at_narrow_terminal_width
  COMMAND bash -c "COLUMNS=80 '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --help | wc -l")
set_tests_properties(decode_help_wraps_into_far_more_lines_at_narrow_terminal_width PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^[5-9][0-9][0-9]|^[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]")

# make_subcommand (the "Subcommands:" listing under e.g. `baseline --help`) gets the identical
# wrapping fix make_option does -- proven separately here since it's a different override with
# its own previously-missing word-wrap, not exercised by any of the make_option-focused tests
# above. `learn`'s own description is long enough to still require 5+ wrapped lines even at a
# narrow 60-column width.
add_test(NAME baseline_help_subcommand_listing_wraps_at_narrow_terminal_width
  COMMAND bash -c "COLUMNS=60 '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline --help | wc -l")
set_tests_properties(baseline_help_subcommand_listing_wraps_at_narrow_terminal_width PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^[3-9][0-9]|^[0-9][0-9][0-9]")

# terminal_width()'s own documented clamp floor: a COLUMNS/terminal size far below 60 (5, here)
# must still wrap exactly as if it were 60, not attempt an unreadably narrow actual wrap -- this
# exact two-line split ("...classic pcap or" / 30-space-padded "pcapng, auto-detected)") was
# confirmed to appear byte-for-byte identically at COLUMNS=5 and COLUMNS=60 against the real
# built binary before being pinned here.
add_test(NAME decode_help_clamps_tiny_terminal_width_to_60_column_floor
  COMMAND bash -c "COLUMNS=5 '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --help")
set_tests_properties(decode_help_clamps_tiny_terminal_width_to_60_column_floor PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Input capture file \\(classic pcap or\n                              pcapng, auto-detected\\)")

# terminal_width()'s own documented clamp ceiling: a COLUMNS/terminal size far above 200 (99999,
# here) must still wrap exactly as if it were 200, not run the whole description out as one
# arbitrarily long unbroken line again (the very problem this entire mechanism exists to fix) --
# this exact phrase was confirmed to stay on one unbroken line at COLUMNS=200/99999 but split
# across multiple lines at COLUMNS=100, against the real built binary, before being pinned here.
add_test(NAME decode_help_clamps_huge_terminal_width_to_200_column_ceiling
  COMMAND bash -c "COLUMNS=99999 '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --help")
set_tests_properties(decode_help_clamps_huge_terminal_width_to_200_column_ceiling PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "this network interface instead of reading a file \\(see 'conduitscope interfaces'\\); requires this build to have been compiled with libpcap/Npcap support")

# --protocol's own `{auto,modbus,dnp3,...,homeplug-av}` choice list (CLI11's own rendering of a
# CLI::IsMember validator) is close to 500 characters with no whitespace anywhere in it at all --
# wrap_text()'s plain whitespace-only breaking can't help here, which is exactly why
# wrap_name_opts() separately loosens ',' into an equally valid break point (see its own comment,
# cli_main.cpp). Proven at a narrow 90-column width: the choice list must actually split across
# multiple comma-bounded lines (not stay one unbroken line), every wrapped continuation line must
# carry the fixed 4-space indent, and both the first ("auto") and last ("homeplug-av") protocol
# names must still be present -- content preserved, only re-flowed.
add_test(NAME decode_help_protocol_choice_list_wraps_on_commas_at_narrow_terminal_width
  COMMAND bash -c "COLUMNS=90 '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --help")
set_tests_properties(decode_help_protocol_choice_list_wraps_on_commas_at_narrow_terminal_width PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "--protocol TEXT:\\{auto, modbus.*\n    [a-z0-9,. -]*homeplug-av\\} \\[auto\\]")

# ROADMAP item 117: `evidence` subcommand -- a single-command 62443/NIS2/CIP-007/CIP-015 audit
# evidence pack. Every test below pins output confirmed against the real built binary first, not
# assumed -- same discipline as every other subcommand's own test suite -- and every
# PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION below is a single bare ".*" between literal anchors with no nested
# repeated group, per this codebase's own established cmsys-regex-engine lesson (chained
# "(.*\n)*" groups hang ctest; `{n}` interval quantifiers are not supported at all).
#
# The very first test below is also this feature's own regression test for a real bug caught
# during development: `rewrite_subcommand_alias`'s own `kBareSubcommands` set did not originally
# include "evidence", so `conduitscope evidence -r <file>` would have been silently mis-parsed by
# `inject_default_subcommand`, which would have wrongly injected `decode` in front of it. The
# FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION guards against that exact regression: if it ever reappears, this run
# would print decode's own "needs exactly one of -r/--read ... or -i/--interface" error instead of
# an evidence pack.
add_test(NAME evidence_kbaresubcommands_fix_no_spurious_decode_injection
  COMMAND conduitscope evidence -r "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(evidence_kbaresubcommands_fix_no_spurious_decode_injection PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ConduitScope Evidence Pack"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "needs exactly one of -r/--read")

# Integrity / signing: --sign-key produces a verifiable HMAC-SHA256 line; omitted says so plainly.
add_test(NAME evidence_sign_key_produces_signature_line
  COMMAND conduitscope evidence -r "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --sign-key "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/empty_baseline.json")
set_tests_properties(evidence_sign_key_produces_signature_line PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "signature: HMAC-SHA256 [0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]")

add_test(NAME evidence_without_sign_key_signature_none
  COMMAND conduitscope evidence -r "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(evidence_without_sign_key_signature_none PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "signature: none \\(no --sign-key given")

# -T json: well-shaped, with every optional section correctly null when its input is omitted...
add_test(NAME evidence_json_format_sections_null_when_inputs_omitted
  COMMAND conduitscope evidence -r "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(evidence_json_format_sections_null_when_inputs_omitted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"policy_compliance\": null.*\"baseline_anomalies\": null.*\"cip_monitoring_coverage\": null.*\"policy_file\": null.*\"signed\": false")

# ...and correctly populated when every optional input is supplied.
add_test(NAME evidence_json_format_sections_populated_when_inputs_supplied
  COMMAND bash -c "rm -f '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/evidence_baseline_json.json' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' baseline learn --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/evidence_baseline_json.json' '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' evidence -r '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml' --baseline-file '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/evidence_baseline_json.json' --cip-monitoring-window --sign-key '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/empty_baseline.json' --format json")
set_tests_properties(evidence_json_format_sections_populated_when_inputs_supplied PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"policy_compliance\": \\{.*\"baseline_anomalies\": \\{.*\"cip_monitoring_coverage\": \\{.*\"policy_file\": \\{.*\"signed\": true")

add_test(NAME evidence_json_format_is_syntactically_valid_json
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' evidence -r '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml' --cip-monitoring-window --format json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; json.load(sys.stdin); print(\"VALID_JSON\")'")
set_tests_properties(evidence_json_format_is_syntactically_valid_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "VALID_JSON")

# Clean run (compliant policy, no baseline anomalies) exits 0; a nonexistent capture and a missing
# required --read both fail the way every other subcommand's own CLI11-validated options do.
add_test(NAME evidence_clean_run_exits_zero
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' evidence -r '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap' --policy '${POLICY_DIR}/compliant.yaml' >/dev/null 2>&1; echo EXITCODE=$?")
set_tests_properties(evidence_clean_run_exits_zero PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "EXITCODE=0")

set_tests_properties(evidence_output_flag_writes_report_to_file PROPERTIES

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ROADMAP item 118: "Detection completeness: distinguish clean from degraded"
# (docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch257.md section 4, item 2, High priority --
# "Packet loss, unsupported protocols, truncated captures, and resource-limit exhaustion must be
# distinguishable from a clean capture with no findings. An empty report must not imply that the
# network is safe."). See DetectionReport::parse_error_packets' own comment (detect_engine.hpp)
# and live_capture.hpp's own LiveCaptureStats/format_live_capture_drop_reason comments for the
# full design. The pure logic half of the live-capture-drop-stats fix is covered by
# tools/live_capture_stats_selftest.cpp's own 6 checks (see live_capture_drop_statistics_self_test
# above) -- the tests below cover the `detect`-report-level parse_error_packets addition
# (deterministic, offline, no live capture needed) plus a handful of real-live-capture
# false-positive checks (does the new drop-warning code path stay silent on an ordinary, driver-
# level-loss-free run -- the live-capture counterpart to crypto_selftest's own "happy path costs
# nothing" check).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# tests/sample_modbus.pcap: 3 packets, 0 parse errors, 0 findings -- confirmed against the real
# built binary (not assumed) before being pinned here. The genuinely clean case: parse_error_packets
# must be present and zero, and the "no findings" line must stay the original bare wording (no
# caveat text) when there is nothing to caveat about.
add_test(NAME detect_parse_error_packets_zero_on_clean_capture_text
  COMMAND conduitscope detect -r "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(detect_parse_error_packets_zero_on_clean_capture_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packets this tool could not decode at all \\(parse errors\\): 0 \\(0.0%\\).*\nno findings\n"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "NOT evidence of absence")

add_test(NAME detect_parse_error_packets_zero_on_clean_capture_json
  COMMAND conduitscope detect -r "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" -T json)
set_tests_properties(detect_parse_error_packets_zero_on_clean_capture_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"total_packets\": 3,\n  \"parse_error_packets\": 0,")

# tests/sample_zigbee.pcap: 32 packets, 1 parse error, 0 findings -- confirmed against the real
# built binary before being pinned here. The degraded-but-looks-clean case this whole item exists
# for: "findings: 0" alone would misleadingly read as "capture is clean" without the caveat text
# below it.
add_test(NAME detect_parse_error_packets_nonzero_adds_no_findings_caveat
  COMMAND conduitscope detect -r "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_zigbee.pcap")
set_tests_properties(detect_parse_error_packets_nonzero_adds_no_findings_caveat PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packets this tool could not decode at all \\(parse errors\\): 1 \\(3.1%\\).*no findings in the packets this tool could analyze -- but 1 of 32 packet\\(s\\).*NOT evidence of absence")

add_test(NAME detect_parse_error_packets_nonzero_json
  COMMAND conduitscope detect -r "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_zigbee.pcap" -T json)
set_tests_properties(detect_parse_error_packets_nonzero_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"total_packets\": 32,\n  \"parse_error_packets\": 1,")

if(CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP AND UNIX)
  # Real-live-capture false-positive checks: an ordinary idle "lo" run (same determinism
  # conventions as live_capture_duration_stops_cleanly_with_no_traffic above -- no traffic
  # generator, --duration alone stops it) must never print the new drop-warning text or flip
  # observation_truncated, since pcap_stats() has nothing to report here. These are the
  # integration-level counterpart to live_capture_stats_selftest's own unit-level "zero drops ->
  # nullopt" check -- proving the real cli_main.cpp wiring (not just the pure formatter function)
  # stays silent on the overwhelmingly common case.
  add_test(NAME live_capture_decode_no_spurious_drop_warning_with_no_traffic
    COMMAND conduitscope decode --interface lo --duration 1)
  set_tests_properties(live_capture_decode_no_spurious_drop_warning_with_no_traffic PROPERTIES
    TIMEOUT 10
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packet\\(s\\) dropped|error:")

  add_test(NAME live_capture_detect_no_spurious_drop_warning_with_no_traffic
    COMMAND conduitscope detect --interface lo --duration 1 --format json)
  set_tests_properties(live_capture_detect_no_spurious_drop_warning_with_no_traffic PROPERTIES
    TIMEOUT 10
    PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"observation_truncated\": false"
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packet\\(s\\) dropped")

  add_test(NAME live_capture_capture_no_spurious_drop_warning_with_no_traffic
    COMMAND conduitscope capture --interface lo --directory "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}" --prefix
            live_capture_drop_stats_smoke --duration 1)
  set_tests_properties(live_capture_capture_no_spurious_drop_warning_with_no_traffic PROPERTIES
    TIMEOUT 10
    FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packet\\(s\\) dropped|error:")
endif()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# tools/generate_build_manifest.sh smoke test -- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md ROADMAP item 124 (patch282
# security review finding 7). Deliberately NOT a test of tools/verify_reproducible_build.sh
# (that script runs two full nested `cmake`/`cmake --build` invocations of its own -- real build
# time that belongs in its own dedicated CI job, `reproducible-build-check` in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml, not inside the default CTest suite that this project's own
# verification convention runs repeatedly end-to-end). generate_build_manifest.sh does no nested
# build at all -- it only inspects the already-built $<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope> and the already-
# present third_party/CLI11/README.md -- so it's cheap enough to cover here directly. The
# script's own last action is to `cat` the manifest it just wrote, so PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION
# below matches directly against that stdout rather than needing a second step to read the file
# back.
add_test(NAME generate_build_manifest_produces_expected_fields
  COMMAND bash "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/generate_build_manifest.sh" "$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>"
          "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/build_manifest_smoke_test_output.json")
set_tests_properties(generate_build_manifest_produces_expected_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\{\n  \"schema\": \"conduitscope-build-manifest/1\",\n  \"generated_at_utc\": \"[0-9]+-[0-9]+-[0-9]+T[0-9]+:[0-9]+:[0-9]+Z\",\n  \"conduitscope_version\": \"[^\"]+\",\n  \"built_from_commit\": \"[^\"]+\",\n  \"compiler\": \"[^\"]+\",\n  \"target_os\": \"[^\"]+\",\n  \"build_type\": \"[^\"]+\",\n  \"build_host_kernel\": \"[^\"]+\",\n  \"dependencies\": \\{\n    \"libpcap_dev_package_version\": \"[^\"]+\",\n    \"cli11_vendored_version\": \"2\\.4\\.2\"\n  \\},")
